# Aster codebase audit — 2026-11-22

Tree audited: `main` at `d30ead9` (v0.4.2, clean apart from the untracked `docs/audits/`), packages rebuilt with `pnpm build` before any measurement. Nothing in the repository was modified apart from this file; it is left uncommitted.

**Result: 766 findings — 7 Critical, 79 High, 296 Medium, 384 Low.** 50 further reports were the same defect found independently by a second lane and are folded into the finding they confirm. Status: 205 CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead), 381 CONFIRMED (run), 4 CONFIRMED (traced; lines re-read by lead), 170 CONFIRMED (traced), 6 PLAUSIBLE.

<!-- resolution-progress -->
**Resolution progress:** 594 of 766 findings resolved (579 fixed, 12 already fixed on main, 3 disputed with evidence); 172 open. Each resolved row names the PR; each finding's section carries a **Resolution** line.
<!-- /resolution-progress -->

## Bottom line

The ports are good and the glue is not. Every owned re-implementation that has a live differential against its upstream (scales, formats, time, colour, curves, path parsing, geo projection and clipping, hierarchy/force/voronoi/contour numerics, the event-selector grammar, selection tests, guide layout) came back equal to Vega/d3 over several hundred thousand generated cases run by this audit. The defects sit in four places those differentials do not reach:

1. **The untrusted-spec boundary has holes on its default paths.** A spec can inject DOM through the patcher (C1), keep a policy-refused URL in later scenes (C2), write a `javascript:` link (C3), read page secrets through the native event (C4), pollute `Object.prototype` at compile (C5), and kill or hang the process with a ~150-byte spec in more than a dozen ways that the documented ceilings and `maxTimeMs` do not stop (C10, C9, C29, C15, C16, C17, C12, C19).
2. **Incremental evaluation is not always the fresh evaluation.** The headline guarantee fails for a signal holding a dataset past 512 values (C24), for marks in group items reading another dataset (C26), for fitted projections (C42), and a rejected evaluation leaks its rows into the last accepted scene (C30). The oracle that states the guarantee does not generate any of these inputs, and is itself incremental-vs-incremental for `identifier` specs (C85).
3. **Accepted-and-ignored input.** The stated policy is "no silent wrong charts". In practice Vega features (`encode.hover`, colour objects, item `zindex`, mark `key`, data triggers, `config.locale`, `config.events`, object-form field parameters, `{signal}` padding/background) and Vega-Lite features (layer `resolve`, wrapped-facet headers, `config.style.<mark>`, layer child sizes) are validated or parsed and then dropped. The Vega-Lite compiler additionally mis-compiles a facet of layers, double binning and unstacked `normalize` with no error (C6, C53, C54).
4. **The verification system over-reports.** One browser gate cannot fail (C64); the sweeps hand Aster a spec the oracle has already written its answers onto (C61); the scene differential compares nothing for grouped marks (C62); several gates pass on zero cases; pixel tolerances pass missing marks. This is why groups 1–3 were invisible to a green `pnpm check`.

5. **The tests and the corpus were then read in full, and they explain the rest.** The second wave rendered all 1,063 corpus specs through both engines and found no new mismatch (one explained `clipPath` count difference), so the corpus gate's verdict is true for what the corpus contains. What it contains is narrower than its count: 140 files in 54 groups give byte-identical reference output (C318), composite specs pinned to `autosize: none` draw into a 10-pixel root (C255), and dozens of specs do not contain the feature their name states (C313). The incremental oracle runs 33 of its 58 pipelines by default and never generates a mark drawn from another mark (C75); reading it for what it omits found a seventh Critical, a stale dependent mark on every same-length data update through a session (C7). The old-versus-new geometry differential shares modules, a cache slot and item numbering with the code it checks (C67, C106), so defects present in both copies pass (C198).

6. **Reading the remaining test files line by line found four more Vega-Lite compiler defects the differentials cannot see.** `scale.rangeMin`/`rangeMax` are applied to quantize, threshold, quantile and ordinal scales where vega-lite drops them (C223); an explicit `reverse` on a discrete `theta`/`radius` is deleted (C224); an area over a measure and a pre-binned position with no second channel draws nothing (C221); a ranged mark from a datum to a field loses its axis title (C222). Each sits behind a comparator that normalises the difference away or a case space that omits it (C358, C220, C219). The recorded oracle vectors, lockfile, raster fixtures and gallery lists are correct against their pinned upstreams: every recorded value was re-derived and matched; what those lanes found is what the recordings cannot detect (C359, C698).

7. **The official example galleries pass their gate on the first frame only.** The 720 upstream Vega and Vega-Lite gallery specs (fetched inputs of the nightly gallery gate, not tracked in the repository) were also read in full. The gate is green, and its green is real for the frame it compares; what it never does is move a pointer, press a key or change a bound widget, on examples most of which exist to show an interaction. Driving them found: a signal holding an event's `datum` is never identical to a row afterwards, which silently disables `reorderable-matrix` (C68); a brushed crossfilter re-bins because a layer's unit bins after its own transforms where vega-lite bins before (C69); one legend click collapses a legend the example exists to keep constant (C70); a size signal's `update` loses to the top-level number (C225); an array-valued `select` option renders as "undefined" (C227); and the earlier findings about `encode.hover`, triggers and item `zindex` each disable the headline behaviour of several official examples (C76, C73, C28). One example is counted as passing while both engines fail on it (C360).

The React layer has its own cluster: errors that escape `onError` by being thrown from render (C47), identity-keyed inputs that loop or refetch forever (C48, C72, C50), worker-stream backpressure that bounds nothing (C77), and interaction math that is linear and number-typed while `log` and `time` are documented as supported (C44, C155).

## How this audit was done

- **Coverage.** The non-test source of all three published packages, the conformance harness and its scripts, root tooling, CI workflows, benchmarks, the demo app and every reader-facing document were read in full by 26 parallel lanes, each owning a disjoint file list. A second wave of 23 lanes then read in full what the first had only inventoried: every `*.test.*`, `*.testlib.*` and `*.testkit.*` file of the three packages and the conformance package, the generators and case tables, all 1,063 corpus specs (each also rendered through Aster and through real Vega, with a coarse signature compared), and the leftovers (the whole `CHANGELOG.md`, notices and licences, bundle budgets, declaration files, demo data, gallery lists). Four further lanes read the 720 upstream gallery specs line by line from that cache. A third wave of 16 lanes then read, line by line with recorded page ranges, everything the first two had checked only by script or named only in abbreviated form: the 4,716-line lockfile, all seven recorded oracle-vector files (about 70,000 lines), the 561 kB raster fixture character range by character range, the gallery manifest and passing lists, and about 160 smaller files. The lead read the last 39 files whose ledger entries were ambiguous. Appendix A opens with a per-file table, generated from the ledgers, naming for each of the 2,094 tracked files the lane whose ledger records a full read and quoting the ledger text; a script credits a file only when the ledger states its true line count (or contiguous ranges to its end) and fails on any gap. Because that table rests on what lanes reported, the lead also measured coverage from the session recordings themselves: the text of every tracked file was looked up in the output of the tool calls that displayed it. That check found a handful of real gaps the ledgers had hidden (one core test file half displayed, a list checked only by script, 54 corpus specs read through a lossy dump), which the lead then read in full; Appendix A.0 gives the method and the final figures. Every lane stated how its area should behave, then read to refute, then wrote repro scripts against the built `dist` and, where an oracle exists, against real Vega 6.3.1 / Vega-Lite 6.4.3 / d3.
- **Lead verification.** Per the repository's rule that a subagent's claim is not accepted unverified, the lead re-ran the headline repro scripts of every lane (205 CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead), 381 CONFIRMED (run), 4 CONFIRMED (traced; lines re-read by lead), 170 CONFIRMED (traced), 6 PLAUSIBLE). A finding marked "re-run by lead" printed the claimed output on the lead's run; "lines re-read by lead" means the cited lines were re-opened and say what the finding says. Nothing a lead re-run contradicted is in this report. Three memory-heavy repros were deliberately not re-run and are marked in their findings. For the second and third waves the lead re-ran the headline scripts of each lane the same way; Appendix B lists what was and was not re-run.
- **Gate baseline.** After all lanes had finished, the lead ran `pnpm check` once (Node 26.13, `TZ=UTC`, alone on the machine, Chromium installed): all 26 PR gates passed, exit 0, including the unit suite (465 files, 42,332 tests), the time-zone matrix, the three corpus gates (1063/1063), the six browser gates and the bundle budgets. Every finding in this report therefore describes a tree on which the project's own PR gate is green; the findings about gates that cannot fail, or that compare less than they report, are about exactly this green result. The nightly-only checks the lead also ran are listed in Appendix B with their results.
- **Nightly steps.** The lead also ran every step of the nightly workflow once (schema and value sweeps, the gallery gate against a previously fetched and manifest-verified cache, 3,000 fuzz seeds, Firefox and WebKit canvas parity, the nightly benchmarks): all passed; Appendix B has the figures. Lanes did not run gates; their claims about what a gate *would* do are traced from its code and say so.
- **Repro scripts** live outside the repository, under `~/.cache/aster-review/audit-2026-11-22/<lane>/`; each finding names its lane directory and script. They are plain `node` ESM against `packages/*/dist` and must be run with the `timeout` (and, for the amplification cases, the `--max-old-space-size`) the finding quotes.

**Status labels.** `CONFIRMED (run)` — reproduced with a script by the auditing lane. `CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)` — and reproduced again by the lead. `CONFIRMED (traced)` — traced end to end by reading, lines quoted. `PLAUSIBLE` — suspected, not driven.

**Severity.** Critical — security hole, or silently wrong output on a default or documented path. High — wrong output, hang or crash on a common or documented path; a gate, guarantee or documented claim that does not hold. Medium — wrong on a less common path, missing safeguard, misleading doc or API shape. Low — hygiene, dead code, minor drift.

**Relation to the earlier audits.** `codebase-audit-2026-10-22.md` and `docs-audit-2026-11-06.md` were checked for each file; their findings are overwhelmingly fixed (Appendix D lists the ones that continue). This report does not repeat a fixed finding.

## 2. System map

### 2.1 Architecture as it runs

Three published packages, no `vega-*`/`d3-*`/`topojson-*` import in their `src` or `dist` (verified), real Vega and Vega-Lite as test oracle only.

| Package | What it is | Real entry points |
|---|---|---|
| `@aster-charts/vl` | Vega-Lite → Vega compiler. One 9.1k-line `compile.ts` plus validate/optimize/selection/transform modules. Does not import core. | `compile` → `withRows` → `compileTwice` → `compileOnce`: clone → `validateSpec` → normalise → `compileView` (layer / facet / repeat / concat / unit) → `finalizeData` → `optimizeData` → naming. A second full pass runs for forward selection references. |
| `@aster-charts/core` | The engine. `compileChart` → `CompiledChart` IR → `evaluateChart` (8k-line `runtime.ts`) → `SceneRoot` → SVG string / DOM patch / canvas. 17 export subpaths, six of them `lean*` entries that differ by the `browser` export condition. | `renderSpec`/`getChartInfo` → `evaluateOnce` (no state). `evaluateChart` → `evaluateChartPending(engine, …)` + immediate commit. `createChartSession` → same, commit after limit checks. `createChartStream` → queue/fold → `session.evaluate`. `bindSceneSignals` → the event loop. `loadSpecData` → fetch + inline. |
| `@aster-charts/react` | One implementation (`ChartCore.tsx`, 1.9k lines) behind `<Chart>` and `<SvgChart>`; hooks; stream components; worker protocol. | `forwardRef` → `AsyncChart` (`React.use(spec)`) or `SpecChart` → `ChartView`, keyed by a string skeleton of the spec. |

### 2.2 The evaluation path (core)

1. **Compile** (`compiler.ts:33`): depth check → list normalisation → config merge → `checkExpressions` (walks the spec in vega-parser's order, refuses syntax errors, unknown functions and undeclared signals) → a *shallow structural copy* into the IR. It validates names and expressions, not shapes or types: an unknown mark type, a `{signal}` padding or an object-form field parameter passes (C238, C36, C35). Inline `values`, `format`, guide `encode` and transform parameter values in the IR are the spec's own objects.
2. **Evaluate** (`evaluateChartPending`, `runtime.ts:3337`): `beginTxn` reads the committed `IncrementalState` (one per `CompiledChart`, in a module `WeakMap`) unless it is stale. Up to four content builds share one transaction: a signed-size padding build, the first build, a fit second build, and inside each a second pass cut at the earliest abort point.
   - **Signals and datasets** are resolved by a bounded round loop (`prepareChartCtx`, `runtime.ts:981-998`), not a dataflow graph: resolve signal updates → build scales → rebuild datasets if anything changed → resolve again. The exit test is taken before the first scales exist (C23); `init` latches on its first non-undefined value (C25); a cycle yields the round count instead of an error (C113).
   - **Datasets** (`buildDatasetsOf`): per dataset in rank order — input → row-count check → kept copy, kept build, pulse path (claim + `incremental-engine.ts`) or `runPipeline` with kept steps. Row ownership is sound: no transform writes a host, spec or upstream row (tested with frozen rows over 43 pipelines).
   - **Scales** (`buildScales`): stamp → memo → unaffected → census → settings equality → rebuild. Options are applied by reflection on the scale function object (C18).
   - **Marks**: `evaluateMark` → `evaluateMarkItems`. Only `encode.update` is ever evaluated; `enter` is folded into it at compile and `hover`/`exit` are carried but unread (C76, C117). Three encode paths exist (pulse splice, channel re-encode, full). The append/same-length fast path writes the previous scene group's own `items` array in place and re-points the old group at a lazy snapshot afterwards.
   - **Guides**: definitions built once per spec/config; tick generation, label formatting and signal resolution for guide properties live in `runtime.ts`, not in the guide modules.
3. **Commit**: the draft becomes the committed state once, after success (or after the session's limit checks). A fast path that writes in place first "claims" the structure, which flags the committed state stale. Claims exist for a dataset's state and the two scale censuses only; the mark-items append is unclaimed (C2).
4. **Render**: `render.ts` defines one `*Attrs(item, sink)` per element; the string renderer and the DOM descriptor builder share it. The canvas painter has its own paint code. The DOM patcher caches each item's descriptor *on the scene item* (`__domDesc`) — an object whose keys a spec's encode channel names choose (C1).

### 2.3 The reuse machinery

About 29 distinct reuse mechanisms, each with its own key and its own "refused when" list (signal-scoped scale/mark reuse, kept steps, kept builds, kept copies, censuses, instance marks, kept group marks, channel re-encode, marks drawn from marks, kept guides, shared nodes, derived structures keyed on nodes). Correctness rests on each key being a superset of what the result reads. The recurring key ingredients:

- **Array identity** as proof of content — sound only together with "not named as changed", because the pulse path advances pipeline arrays in place. One site omits the second half (C26); published scenes hold the same live arrays (C30).
- **`valueKey` fingerprints** — content up to 512 nodes, then object identity. Safe only for objects nobody writes (C24, C265).
- **Process-wide inputs** — the expression registry and default locale are in every key; the text measurer set by `setTextMetricsProvider` is in the guide key only, and a channel key omits the URL policy the mark key holds (C217, C478).
- **"Not under `limits`"** — nearly every reuse path refuses when limits are set, so the configuration recommended for untrusted specs is also the from-scratch one (C277).

### 2.4 Limits

`withLimits` installs an ambient meter. There are three kinds of call site, and which one a site uses decides whether it is safe when the host passes no limits: `meterX`/`ceiling` (built-in ceiling or the host's budget), `checkGeneratedRows` (ceiling plus `maxRows` only), and `boundedCount`/`checkRowCount`/`meterTick` (a no-op without a meter). `maxTimeMs` is cooperative: it is seen only where a loop ticks. The layout, geo, raster, contour, label, regex-screen and several transform loops do not tick. `docs/LIMITS.md` is honest that the killable worker is the hard guarantee; the React hooks own neither a deadline nor a restart for that worker (C244).

### 2.5 The event loop (`signals.ts`)

One binding per scene; hosts bind again per render. Per binding: scopes, runtime, streams, the propagation graph, DOM listeners. Per *owner element* (module `WeakMap`s, keyed by handler text, not by chart): between/throttle/debounce state, timers, `{signal}`-handler memory (C40). Handlers receive the native DOM event; sources may be `window` or any `document.querySelectorAll` selector; `config.events` permits are not read (C4, C78). A signal write is a fresh render (ADR 0005).

### 2.6 React

- **Render phase does real work**: Vega-Lite compile, add-on/part detection (may suspend), `session.evaluate`, a second session for base domains, SVG serialisation, the a11y tree. Correctness under discarded renders rests on the session being identity-cached and pure.
- **DOM ownership**: the first commit is a string through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; afterwards `patchSceneDom` owns the `<svg>`. "The DOM equals the last drawn scene" is assumed from provenance, with separate branches for hydration, dense marks, `incremental={false}`, streams and renderer switches (C43, C45).
- **Lean vs full engine**: the shells import `@aster-charts/core/lean*`; under the `browser` export condition engine parts (legend, aggregate, time, colour, curves, …) load on demand through a Suspense wait. Any React module on the shell path that imports a synchronous core entry silently flips the app to the full engine (C82).
- **Errors have four exits**: `onError` + `role="alert"`, thrown from render, `onStreamError`, and the logger/console.
- **Input identity has three regimes**: spec by content (`<Chart>`, `useChart`, streams); spec by object identity (`useSpecData`); option functions and `signals`/`data` by identity in some hooks and by content in others.

### 2.7 Verification system

- **Strong**: the in-process vitest differentials (generated cases, exact comparison, non-vacuity floors), `verify-publish` with planted faults, the SVG canonicalizer (rewritten since the last audit; it flags paint, order and structure).
- **Weak**: the corpus (949 of 1,063 specs pin `autosize: none`; none contains `zindex`, an encode `hover`, a colour object, `blend`, or a datum-sorted mark); sweeps that vary one property with one uniform literal; the scene differential; pixel gates with global scalar tolerances; gates with no floor on cases compared; no test of any gate's own failure path except the sweeps and `verify-publish`.
- **What reading every test and spec added** (second wave). All 1,063 corpus specs were rendered through both engines by the corpus lanes and agree on a coarse signature, so the gate's verdict is true; its *count* overstates: 140 files in 54 groups have byte-identical reference output (C318), composite specs under `autosize: none` draw into a 10-pixel root so pixel gates see none of the chart (C255), and several families do not contain the feature in their name (C313, C314, C256). The incremental oracle draws 33 of its 58 pipelines in the default sweep and generates no mark drawn from a mark (C75, C7). The legacy "frozen copy" differential follows product fixes, shares leaf modules and the `__domDesc` cache slot with the code under test, and numbers hit items separately on each side (C67, C106). Corpus loops in core tests skip 42 of 391 specs through a bare `catch { continue }` (C334); the attack-kit helper counts a crashed child as a clean return (C199).
- **PR vs nightly**: schema sweeps, value sweep, gallery, seeded fuzzing and cross-browser canvas run nightly only; a release is not gated on them.

### 2.8 Key invariants — enforced or assumed

| Invariant | State |
|---|---|
| No scene value reaches SVG text unescaped | **Enforced** in `StringAttrSink` (22,752 hostile renders, 0 problems) |
| No element or attribute *name* comes from a spec | **Assumed**; false through `__domDesc` (C1) |
| Item fields starting `_`/`__` are the engine's | **Assumed**; encode copies any channel name onto the item |
| Every URL in the output passed the policy | **Per call site**; titles, `image` channel, `cursor` are outside (C8, C20, C97) |
| A refused evaluation leaves nothing behind | **False** for in-place appends (C2, C30) |
| Incremental result = fresh result | **Enforced by oracle** only over the inputs it generates; false for a mark drawn from a mark (C7) |
| A reuse record never holds an array the engine advances in place | **Assumed**; `recordOverMarkItems` stores the live items array (C7) |
| A fast path claims before it writes | **Enforced** for dataset state and censuses; **not** for mark items |
| Every expression is read at compile | **True for the sites the walk knows**; root `layout`/`encode`, facet expressions are not (C126) |
| Spec-set counts are bounded without `limits` | **Per call site**; legends, interval ranges, scale `bins`, grids from data, `cross`/`fold`/`graticule` are not |
| Dictionaries keyed by user strings ignore `Object.prototype` | **Enforced** widely in core (Maps, `Object.hasOwn`); missed in `vl/selection.ts`, scale options, a few tables |
| Each engine sees pristine input in the harness | **Assumed**; false in sweeps, probe, gallery-static (C61) |
| A passing gate compared something | **Assumed** in a dozen gates |
| Only compiler-written expressions are renamed (vl) | **Assumed**; user `labelExpr` is rewritten (C299) |
| "Validated" means "implemented" (vl) | **Assumed**; `validate.ts` and `compile.ts` are separate allow-lists |

## 3. Findings by category

Each finding is filed under its primary category and listed in severity (ID) order. The text is the auditing lane's own write-up; `packages/core/src/` (or the lane's package) is implied where a file is named bare. "Scripts" names the directory under `~/.cache/aster-review/audit-2026-11-22/` that holds the repro scripts a finding cites.

### 3.1 Correctness (256)

#### C6 — Critical — A facet of layers draws every facet's rows in every cell when no layer needs a cast dataset

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:2022-2024`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #202 (b378034). facet of layers: cells read their facet; layer casts as base; assertCellsReadTheirFacet invariant; vl-facet-layer-data.test.ts (352)
- **Area:** vl / composition
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c1-1` — `vl-c1/`

**A facet of layers draws every facet's rows in every cell when no layer needs a cast dataset.**

- **Cause:** `baseName = layeredInner ? (innerData[1]?.source === srcName ? innerData[1]!.name : srcName)` assumes `innerData[1]` is the shared casts dataset. When no cast is needed (every encoded measure is produced by a transform such as `calculate`), `innerData[1]` is layer 0's own pipeline.
- **Consequence:** the loop at 2052-2059 re-derives in the cell only datasets whose `source` is in `cellMap`. The other layers' pipelines have `source === srcName` and are skipped, so their marks keep reading the root dataset.
- **Input:** 5 rows; `transform: [{calculate: "datum.b / 100", as: "pct"}]`; `facet: {column: {field: "c"}}`; `spec: {layer: [bar(x: a, y: pct), text(x: a, y: pct, text: pct)]}`.
- **Observed:** `cell.from.facet.data = "data_0"`, no `cell.data`, marks read `["facet", "data_1"]`. 15 text marks are drawn; vega-lite draws 5.
- **Also reproduced:** a wrapped facet, the transform on the layer spec instead of the facet, and `joinaggregate` plus a rule (`t9-facetlayer2.mjs` cases 3, 4, 7; `t4-facet.mjs` `facet-layer-transform`).
- **Unaffected:** the same specs when any layer needs a cast, which is why the gallery passes. `t17.mjs` shows which transforms trigger it.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `repro-facet-layer-leak.mjs` prints `text marks drawn: ours 15  vega-lite 5` and `ours cell: from.facet.data = data_0 | cell.data = [] | marks read ["facet","data_1"]`.
- **Direction:** have `compileLayered` hand back each group's casts and source names instead of inferring by position. When there is no casts dataset, the base is the source and every layer pipeline is re-derived in the cell. Add an invariant that no mark inside `cell` reads a root dataset except through `facet`. `row_domain` is also derived from layer 0's pipeline (`source: baseName`).

#### C7 — Critical — A top-level mark drawn from another mark (`from: {data: <mark name>}`) keeps its previous items when the source rows are edited or reordered in place

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:2961`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (feddea0). Fixed: a mark drawn from a mark records a copy of the source items and every reuse compares engine arrays by content stamp (content-stamp.ts); incremental-shapes.test.ts generates text/rule/voronoi/label over a mark, top level and nested, under every delivery.
- **Area:** tests / core (incremental oracle, legacy copies I)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core3-1` — `tests-core3/`
- **Lead's note:** Found by reading the incremental oracle's generator for what it never produces. The lead re-ran `r1c-scope.mjs` and `r1d-cause.mjs`: real Vega and a fresh Aster evaluation agree, the session keeps the old items for an edit, a move and a swap. Reached by hand-written Vega (labels, `label` transforms, voronoi or rules over a top-level mark); the lane found Vega-Lite `nearest` output unaffected and did not trace why. If "default path" is read as Vega-Lite output only, this is High.

`packages/core/src/runtime.ts:2961` (record), `:2922-2924` (compare), reached from `:3120-3124`.

**Scenario.** Symbol mark `pts` over dataset `t`, plus a text mark `from: {data: 'pts'}` with `text: {signal: "datum.datum.g + '@' + datum.x"}`. Rows A/B/C at x 1/5/9. Evaluate, then give a same-length change through `createChartSession().evaluate` (the default `<Chart>` path) or through `evaluateChart` with a truthful `dataChanges` / `dataPulse`.

Observed (`r1c-scope.mjs`, real Vega 6.3.1 alongside):

| Update | Vega | Aster fresh | Aster session |
|---|---|---|---|
| edit a label field (g) | `A@20 ZZZ@100 C@180` | same as Vega | `A@20 B@100 C@180` (stale) |
| move a point (x) | `A@20 B@140 C@180` | same as Vega | `A@20 B@100 C@180` (stale) |
| swap two rows | `B@100 A@20 C@180` | same as Vega | `A@20 B@100 C@180` (stale) |
| append a row | ok | ok | ok |
| remove a row | ok | ok | ok |

`r1-mark-from-mark.mjs` shows `evaluateChart` with no hint or with `changedDatasets` is correct; `dataChanges` and `dataPulse` are stale. The dependent group is the very same object as before, and its items' `datum.datum` is the old row.

`e4c-more.mjs` (10 seeds each, session and chart+`dataChanges`) fails 10/10 for each of:
- a text mark from a mark;
- a `voronoi` path over a mark;
- a `label` transform over a mark;
- a rule from a mark.

The same marks inside a group pass.

**Root cause** (`r1d-cause.mjs`, run):
- `recordOverMarkItems` stores the source mark's items array by reference: `ctx.draft.markSources.set(mark, { key, items, … })` (`:2961`).
- A `dataChanges`/`dataPulse` evaluation advances that same array in place. The script prints "new group holds the SAME items array: true" and "slot 1 was replaced in place: true".
- `keptOverMarkItems` then runs `const a = record.items[i]; const b = items[i]; if (a === b) continue` (`:2922-2924`). It compares the array with itself, returns `'same'`, and the old group is reused whole.

**Why no test saw it.**
- The oracle generates no mark-from-mark (see `C252 (tests-core3-4)`).
- `channel-reuse.test.ts:105-155`, which pins `keptOverMarkItems`, only changes the store and signals; its source dataset is the constant `ROWS`.

**Scope note.** Vega-Lite `nearest: true` (voronoi from `marks`) came out correct in `r2-vl-nearest.mjs`. Its pipeline has an `identifier`, which appears to keep it off the in-place path; I did not trace that. The exposed class is hand-written Vega with reactive geometry (labels over bars or points, `label` transforms, voronoi). If the lead reads "default path" as Vega-Lite output only, this is High.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`r1-mark-from-mark.mjs`, `r1b-debug.mjs`, `r1c-scope.mjs`, `r1d-cause.mjs`, `e4c-more.mjs`).

**Direction.** Record a copy of the source items (or the item-generation stamp), never the live array. Add a mark-from-mark shape to the oracle generator and a data-edit step to `channel-reuse.test.ts`.

#### C23 — High — The fixed point stops before the scales exist

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:981-998`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (feddea0 409b2fd 557ff2d). Fixed: each round resolves signals after its scales exist and rebuilds datasets when a signal they read moved, bounded by chart size; signal-order-generated-vs-vega.test.ts chains depth 1..8 vs vega.
- **Area:** core / runtime: state, signals, reuse keys
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt1-2` — `core-rt1/`

`runtime.ts:981-998`

- **Issue.** The exit test is taken before the first `buildScales`:
  ```
  changed = resolveSignalUpdates(ctx) || geoStale || (rounds === 0 && readsScales) || ctx.setData.changed   // :987
  buildScales(ctx)                                                                                         // :989
  if (changed) { ... buildDatasets ... }                                                                   // :990
  resolveSignalUpdates(ctx)   // :997  the signal gets its value here
  buildScales(ctx)            // :998  no dataset is built again
  ```
  In round 0 `domain('x0')[1]` is `undefined`, so `changed` is false and the loop ends. `readsScales` only covers dataset transforms that call a scale function themselves.
- **Scenario** (`s7b-fixed-point-variants.mjs`; `d0=[{v:1},{v:2}]`, `s = domain('x0')[1]`, `d1 = d0 + formula datum.v + s`):
  ```
  DIFFERENT formula reads the signal: vega [3,4] evaluateChart [NaN,NaN] session [NaN,NaN]
  DIFFERENT formula reads the signal, signal has an initial value: vega [3,4] evaluateChart [101,102] session [101,102]
  DIFFERENT filter reads the signal: vega [1] evaluateChart [] session []
  same      formula reads the scale itself (control): vega [3,4] evaluateChart [3,4] session [3,4]
  ```
  `s7-fixed-point.mjs`: the same at every chain depth 1–8 (Vega 4…512, Aster `NaN`).
- **Docs.** `ARCHITECTURE.md:312` and `API.md:374` say "resolved to a fixed point". Not under "Deviations from Vega".
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-RUN against Vega 6.
- **Direction.** Decide `changed` after the round's scales exist, and rebuild datasets when the resolve at :997 moves a signal a dataset reads.

#### C24 — High — A signal holding a dataset array is identity-keyed past 512 values

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/fingerprint.ts:36-37`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (feddea0). Fixed: valueKey keys a published dataset array past the 512 budget by its content stamp (identity + in-place write count), so data('t') signals see pulses; large-signal shape in incremental-shapes.test.ts.
- **Area:** core / runtime: state, signals, reuse keys
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt1-3` — `core-rt1/`

`fingerprint.ts:36-37,51,56`; `runtime.ts:1578`, `:2508-2524` (`readsKey`), `:2618-2619` (`canReuseMarkGroup`)

- **Issue.** `valueKey` falls back to `#refId` past 512 nodes. The header calls that "always the safe direction (a miss, never a stale hit)", which holds only for objects nobody writes. The pulse path advances a dataset's rows array in place, so a signal `update: "data('t')"` has the same key and is `Object.is`-equal before and after. The fingerprint is unchanged, the mark names no dataset, and it is kept.
- **Scenario** (`s2b-session-variants.mjs`; `t` with one `formula` step, text mark `s[1].v + ':' + length(s)`, host gives a NEW array):
  ```
  ok       N=170 session.change NEW array + dataChanges text=777:170
  MISMATCH N=171 evaluateChart NEW array + dataChanges  text=1:171 :: fresh "777:171" incremental "1:171"
  MISMATCH N=171 session.change NEW array + dataChanges text=1:171
  MISMATCH N=171 session.change append dataPulse        text=1:171 :: fresh "777:172" incremental "1:171"
  ```
  171 rows × 3 = 513 nodes, exactly the bound. `s2-signal-holds-dataset.mjs` shows it with no hint at all (`session.evaluate`, auto-diff) for a `formula` pipeline (edit and append) and a `filter` pipeline (append). A dataset with no transforms is not affected.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-RUN. The session reproduces only with the pulse part loaded.
- **Direction.** Never key an engine-written array by identity alone: key it like `datasetKey`, or add the datasets a signal's expression reads to the dependencies of whatever reads the signal. Fix the header claim.

#### C26 — High — A leaf mark inside a group item that reads another pipeline dataset by expression goes permanently stale after an append

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:5644`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (feddea0). Fixed: instance-mark deps are pinned (array + version) instead of compared by identity; group-scoped reads shape in incremental-shapes.test.ts (length/indata/data()[0], 2..600 rows).
- **Area:** core / runtime: datasets, scales, fit (also categories 3)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt2-1` — `core-rt2/`

**`runtime.ts:5644`, `:5651` (`evaluateInstanceMark`)**: a leaf mark inside a group item is kept when the other datasets it reads are "the same objects", but a pulse advances a pipeline dataset's array in place.

Every other reuse in the range pairs array identity with `!ctx.affected.has(name)` (`sameRows` `:2567`, `keptCopy` `:4149`, `reusableRuns` `:4173`, `runScopedData` `:4542`, `datasetKey` `:4454`). This one does not:
```ts
5644  const deps = [...new Set([...named.names, ...named.exprData])].filter((n) => n !== source).sort().map((n) => [n, ctx.datasets.get(n)] as const)
5651    && prev.deps.length === deps.length && prev.deps.every(([n, d], i) => deps[i]![0] === n && deps[i]![1] === d)
```
The comment at `:5642` states the false premise: "as arrays, which an edit makes anew".

- **Scenario** (default session, auto-diff, no limits): facet over `t`; each cell has a text mark with `text: {signal: "datum.k + length(data('other'))"}`; `other` is `source: src2` plus one `formula` or `filter`. The host replaces `src2` with `[...rows, newRow]`.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**, `repro-instance-deps.mjs` (15 of 18 steps BAD).
Direction: one helper for "this dataset holds the rows it held" (`sameRows` or `datasetKey`), never a bare `===` on a dataset array. Add a nested mark reading a pipeline dataset by expression to `incremental-oracle.test.ts`.

#### C29 — High — `limits: { maxGeneratedRows }` alone removes the `rows` ceiling for `density` / `quantile`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/limits.ts:460-463`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854). Fixed: allot/allotUpTo compare the limit that replaces a ceiling at the site, before allocating; {maxGeneratedRows: 1000} alone refuses 5e7 density steps in 12 ms.
- **Area:** core / session, stream, limits (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-incr-2` — `core-incr/`

- **Where:**
  - `packages/core/src/limits.ts:460-463`: `checkGeneratedRows` calls `ceiling('rows', …)` then `active.checkRows`.
  - `limits.ts:310-315`: `checkRows` reads only `maxRows`.
  - `limits.ts:174-176`: `CEILING_KEYS.rows = ['maxRows', 'maxGeneratedRows']`, so either key "replaces" the ceiling.
  - Callers: `curve-fits.ts:432` (`density steps`), `transform-stats.ts:348` (`quantile`).
- **Claim:** `docs/LIMITS.md:66-67`: "Giving the matching limit replaces the ceiling by your number (your budget governs)".
- **Scenario:** `density` with `minsteps = maxsteps = 50000000` over two rows.
  - No limits: refused at once, `density steps 50000000 > 1000000 (built-in ceiling…)`.
  - `limits: { maxGeneratedRows: 1000, maxTimeMs: 500 }`: fatal OOM. The ceiling is skipped, there is no `maxRows` to compare, this helper never calls `generated()`, and the sampling loop has no clock tick.
  - At 3e6 steps the same limits allocate all 3 000 000 rows and only then fail (`maxGeneratedRows 2999991 > 1000 (transform density)`, 867 ms).
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN. `node --max-old-space-size=400 $S/t-genrows-only.mjs` (OOM); `$S/t-limits.mjs` section L2 shows the three outcomes.
- **Direction:** make `checkGeneratedRows` charge the cumulative budget (`active.rows(n, what)`), or keep the ceiling unless the replacing limit is one this call site actually compares.

#### C30 — High — A rejected evaluation or flush leaves its rows in the last good scene's datasets and runtime

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/incremental-engine.ts:128-148`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** core / session, stream, limits (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-incr-3` — `core-incr/`

- **Where:** the append fast paths write the committed step arrays in place before anything is accepted.
  - `packages/core/src/incremental-engine.ts:128-148` (`rowLocalAppendPulse`: `prev[i] = …`, `prev.push`)
  - `:160-164` (filter), `:187-191` (fold)
  - `:504-510` and `:563-585` (aggregate / joinaggregate state and rows)
  - `:734-738` (identifier)
  - `claim()` (`runtime.ts:4820-4826`) flags the committed state stale, so the next evaluation re-derives. But the arrays are the ones the previous scene published: `runtime.ts:3547` stores `ctx.datasets` by reference as `scene.__datasets`, and `scene.runtime.data()` reads the same arrays.
  - The session hands that scene out again from its no-op path (`session.ts:363-367`, `:370-375`).
- **Stream scenario (the documented recovery path):** a spec with `formula` on `table`, `limits: { maxItems: 8 }`, 3 initial rows, `flush()` ok. Then `push({ append: 27 rows })`, `flush()` throws `maxItems 30 > 8`, then `discard()`.
  - Expected: `stream.scene()` still describes 3 rows. Sources: `API.md:324-327` ("commits nothing until the evaluation succeeds … exactly as before the call"), `stream.ts:175-176` ("Never touches committed rows or the last scene"), and ARCHITECTURE ("Scenes are never observably mutated after they are returned").
  - Observed: the scene is the same object and draws 3 items, but `datasetsOfScene(stream.scene()).get('table').length === 30` and `stream.scene().runtime.data('table').length === 30`, before and after `discard()`.
  - Consequence: any signal handler bound to that scene (`length(data('table'))`, `indata`, a selection test) computes over the rejected batch.
- **Session scenario:** `evaluate(A)` ok → `evaluate(A + 4 rows, { limits: { maxItems: 5 } })` throws → `evaluate(A)` or an equal copy returns the cached scene with 7 rows in `datasetsOfScene` (fresh: 3).
  - With `joinaggregate` the retained rows also carry the rejected input's sums (`js: 52` where fresh has `17`, fuzz seed 5330).
  - `LIMITS.md:203-204`: "A failed evaluation leaves the session as it was."
- **Without any failure:** after a later append, `datasetsOfScene(firstScene)` has 4 rows where it had 3, and is the very array of the new scene. Its TSDoc (`runtime.ts:3584-3588`) says "the rows each of the spec's datasets ended with in the evaluation that made `scene`".
- **Drawn output is never affected:** `SVGONLY=1 node $S/fuzz.mjs 1200 7000` gave 60 000 SVG comparisons after interleaved failures, 0 mismatches.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
  - `$S/t-failed-flush-scene.mjs` (3 → 30 rows, runtime too)
  - `$S/t-after-failed-eval.mjs same|copy` (7 rows vs 3)
  - `$S/t-stream.mjs` S1/S2: formula, filter, joinaggregate and fold are affected; no-transform and aggregate are not
  - `node $S/fuzz.mjs 500 5000` (14 `H-mixed … DS` classes)
- **Test gap:** `published-scene.test.ts`, `session.test.ts`, `stream.test.ts` and `stream.property.test.ts` contain no `datasetsOfScene` / `runtime.data` assertion (grep count 0 each).
- **Direction:** stop the append paths writing arrays a published scene holds (copy-on-claim, or an undo record like `group.items` has), or have `scene.__datasets` and the scene runtime snapshot lengths when the scene is made. Pin it in `published-scene.test.ts` for a failed and a successful later evaluation.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `core-rt2-5`, scripts `core-rt2/`, CONFIRMED (run); `runtime.ts:3547`, `:3584-3595` (`datasetsOfScene`), `:4040-4045`):

**`runtime.ts:3547`, `:3584-3595` (`datasetsOfScene`), `:4040-4045`**: a returned scene keeps the engine's live dataset arrays, and a later pulse advances them in place.

Contradicted docs:
- TSDoc `:3584` and `docs/API.md:469`: "the rows each of the spec's datasets ended with in the evaluation that made `scene`".
- `ARCHITECTURE.md:221`: "Scenes are never observably mutated after they are returned".
- `LIMITS.md:203`: "A failed evaluation leaves the session as it was".

Observed:
- `t` = `src` + formula; evaluate with 3 rows gives scene#1; evaluate with `[...rows, r]` (plain auto-diff). `datasetsOfScene(scene#1).get('t')` now has 4 rows and is the same array as scene#2's. Same for `dataChanges` edits, `dataPulse` appends and a filter pipeline. No-transform and aggregate datasets are not affected.
- With `limits: {maxItems: 8}` the second evaluate throws `maxItems 9 > 8`. `session.last().scene` is still the accepted scene with unchanged SVG, but its `t` holds the 5 rejected rows and `scene.runtime.expr("length(data('t'))")` answers 5.

Scene nodes are protected by `supersedeItems`; datasets have no such snapshot. `published-scene.test.ts` never looks at `__datasets`.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**, `repro-old-scene-datasets.mjs`, `repro-rejected-leaks.mjs`.
Direction: lazily snapshot a superseded scene's datasets, or document both APIs as "the chart's datasets now" and stop a rejected evaluation from advancing arrays the accepted scene reads.

#### C31 — High — `item` is always `undefined` in the engine's expressions, including encode `signal` expressions where Vega binds the scenegraph item

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/expr-interpreter.ts:573-574`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (bdd4896,b514ce2). Fixed: encode expressions (marks, rule tests, nested groups, axes, legends) receive a facade of the scenegraph item being encoded; differential-encode-item.test compares canonical SVG with vega.

**`item` is always `undefined` in the engine's expressions, including encode `signal` expressions where Vega binds the scenegraph item.**

- **Observed:** `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'x')` goes to the logger and the mark has no text. `isDefined(item)` is `false`.
- **Expected (vega 6.3.1):** `row:3`, `row:text`, `row:100`, `row:1 row:2`; `isDefined(item)` is `true`.

- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p6.mjs`.
- **Direction:** pass the item being encoded as the frame's `item` (the `EngineExpression` signature has no slot for it today), or refuse `item` at encode sites at compile time and document the deviation.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `core-guides-3`, scripts `core-guides/`, CONFIRMED (run); `item` is accepted in encode expressions and is always `undefined`):

- `packages/core/src/expr-check.ts:31` lists `item` among the evaluator names, so it parses.

- The guide host cannot pass one: `guide-encode.ts:210` (`entry(spec, datum)`), `runtime.ts:7319`.

- Vega: three labels, coloured by position.
- Aster: logs `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'y')` and the pass stops. Label texts are `["0","",""]`, the domain line is missing, and the view is 210×110 (Vega 241×120).

The same expression in a plain text mark's `update` logs the same TypeError. `item.mark.role` in `encode.symbols` drops the legend's labels.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** — `repro.mjs` "G3" (two cases), `d2.mts`.

Direction: bind the item under construction into the encode frame (`EntryScope.item` already exists for the guide's own entry functions), or reject `item` at compile time in encode context with a typed error.

#### C32 — High — A regex literal with `g` or `y` is a single shared `RegExp`, so `test` advances `lastIndex` from row to row

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/expr-interpreter.ts:445-448`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (36c5d6b,fcae061,2eff9d0). Fixed: a g or y regex literal is a fresh RegExp per evaluation, as vega's code generator emits it (a non-g/y literal handed straight to test/replace/split, which has no lastIndex state and cannot escape, is shared); differential-expression-semantics.test covers every flag set over rows and repeated evaluations.
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-3` — `core-expr/`

**A regex literal with `g` or `y` is a single shared `RegExp`, so `test` advances `lastIndex` from row to row.**

- **Cause:** the parser constructs the regex once (`:547`), the tree lives in the process-wide `parseExpressionCached` map, and the `Literal` closure returns the same object on every evaluation. Vega's code generator emits the literal, so each evaluation gets a fresh regex. The engine mode is documented as the code generator's reading (`:173-178`).
- **Scenario:** four rows with `s: 'a'` and `{type:'filter', expr:"test(/a/g, datum.s)"}`.
- **Observed:** rows 1 and 3 are kept; as a formula the values are `true,false,true,false`.
- **Expected (vega):** all four rows; `true ×4`.
- **Cross-chart effect:** because the tree is cached by text for the life of the process, the first row's answer depends on earlier renders of the same expression text.
- **Not affected:** `replace` and `split`.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p5.mjs` (full `renderSpec` against vega) and `p2.mjs`.
- **Direction:** reset `lastIndex` on each read of a global/sticky literal, or hand out a fresh regex per evaluation. No test covers this.

- Row shape: vega's row is `{type:'MultiLineString', coordinates}`; Aster's is `{type:'GeometryCollection', geometries:[mesh]}` (`:58`). Neither is in the documented deviations (grep: no hit).
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `r09-topojson-vega.mjs` (last three output lines).

#### C35 — High — object-form field parameters are accepted and silently mis-read by almost every transform

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/row-keys.ts:35-36`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #194 (3b859f2,8077d40). Fixed: every transform parameter is resolved from the definition table (param-resolve.ts): {expr,as}, {field,as}, comparator {expr}, nested {signal}; differential over every field/computed/comparator param x every form vs vega.
- **Area:** core / compiler, transforms (also categories 4)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-xform-1` — `core-xform/`

- **Where:** `packages/core/src/row-keys.ts:35-36` (`fieldOf`: `if (typeof spec !== 'string') return field(spec)`), `util.ts:343-347` (`field` → `splitAccessPath(str)`; an object becomes the path `"[object Object]"`); `transform-extra.ts:282,285` (pie: `t.field as string` → `getField`), `transform-extra.ts:381-384` (dotbin), `raster-transforms.ts:45` (kde2d names: `String(g)`). The compile step does read these forms: `spec-expressions.ts:359-366` ("a field or a comparator may be written `{expr: text}`"), and `docs/ERRORS.md:263-266` says "a field or a value that takes `{expr: text}` is parsed".
- **Issue:** vega-parser accepts `{expr, as?}` and `{field, as?}` for every `field`-typed parameter (`vega-parser/src/parsers/transform.js:73-75`). Aster validates the expression, then the transform treats the object as a field name; the accessor returns the row itself or `undefined`.
- **Scenario:** `{type:'aggregate', groupby:['g'], fields:[{expr:'datum.v*2', as:'w'}], ops:['sum']}` over `v = 1,3 | 5,7` → Aster `[{g:'a','sum_[object Object]':NaN},…]`; Vega `[{g:'a',sum:8},{g:'b',sum:24}]`. `{type:'stack', field:{expr:'datum.v*2'}}` → Aster `y1: NaN`; Vega `0..2, 2..8`. `{type:'collect', sort:{field:{expr:'-datum.v'}}}` → Aster leaves rows unsorted. `joinaggregate` with an object `groupby` writes each row into itself (a cycle). `fold` puts the whole input row under `value`. No error.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `t2.mjs`: 41 of 43 differ (aggregate, joinaggregate, window fields/sort/groupby, bin, collect, countpattern, extent, flatten, fold, impute field/key/groupby, kde, lookup fields/values, pivot, project, quantile, stack field/groupby/sort, timeunit, regression, loess, pie, dotbin, kde2d). Only `dotbin.groupby{field,as}` and `identifier` agree.
- **Why not caught:** `packages/conformance/scripts/transform-cases.mjs` (3028 cases) has no object-form field parameter, and calls `applyTransforms` directly.
- **Direction:** resolve field parameters in one place (`fieldOf`/`fieldsOf`, given the expression runtime): `{field, as}` → accessor named `as`; `{expr, as}` → compiled-expression accessor. Route `pie`, `dotbin`, kde2d names, `fieldParam`, `geoAccessor` through it. Until then refuse an object field parameter with a typed error. Add both forms to the cases.

#### C37 — High — Canvas symbol batching changes the picture for translucent, blended or filled-and-stroked overlapping symbols

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/canvas.ts:1123-1178`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (647a044,abe8e82). Fixed: canvas symbol runs batch only when batchablePaint (opaque, unblended, fill xor stroke); otherwise painted per item.
- **Area:** core / SVG, DOM patcher, canvas, a11y
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-render-2` — `core-render/`

**Canvas symbol batching changes the picture for translucent, blended or filled-and-stroked overlapping symbols.**

- `renderSymbolRuns` puts a same-paint run in one path and paints it once (`paintPath(ctx, [], first, …)`, `:1151`/`:1168`). Only rotated and gradient runs are excluded (`:1128`).
- One fill at `globalAlpha = opacity` does not accumulate where symbols overlap. One fill then one stroke puts every outline above every fill.
- **Observed** (`canvas5.mjs`), 255 vs 256 overlapping symbols:

| Paint | 255 items | 256 items |
|---|---|---|
| fill + opacity 0.3 | `fill()` ×255 | `fill()` ×1 |
| fill + stroke | `(fill,stroke)` ×255 | `fill,stroke` once |
| blend multiply | `fill()` ×255 | `fill()` ×1 |

- The SVG batcher guards against this (`dom.ts:263-270`: "Translucent marks cannot batch … alpha would visibly change"). `PERFORMANCE.md:70` documents the canvas batch with no caveat, and it is not in "Deviations from Vega".
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN on recorded calls; the pixel consequence follows from canvas compositing, not from a browser run.
- **Direction:** batch only runs that are opaque, unblended, and have a fill xor a stroke.

#### C38 — High — A per-call text-metrics provider is not in force when the scene is serialised

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/index.ts:107-124`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (85ce62a,647a044,f075640,abe8e82). Fixed: the scene records its per-call text measurer and every renderer entry (SVG, DOM, canvas, append, hit, a11y) runs under it via withSceneOutput.
- **Area:** core / SVG, DOM patcher, canvas, a11y (also categories 4, 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-render-3` — `core-render/`

**A per-call text-metrics provider is not in force when the scene is serialised.**

- The provider is scoped around evaluation only (`runtime.ts:3344`). Truncation is recomputed at write time (`render.ts:623` `textLinesOf(it).map((l) => truncateToLimit(it, l))`), and `renderSpec` calls `renderSceneToSvg(scene)` (`index.ts:119`) outside that scope. `patchSceneDom` and `renderSceneToCanvas` are called the same way.
- **Scenario** (`textmetrics1.mjs`): provider = 3px per character; a 40-character axis label (120px, default `labelLimit` 180) and a text mark with `limit: 150`.
- **Observed:** `renderSpec(spec, { textMetrics })` → `['a category name of fo…', 'a category name …']`. `withTextMetricsProvider(provider, () => renderSpec(spec))` → both labels whole.
- The layout did use the provider (`padding.left` 127, vs 183 without), so the padding is sized for a label the output then cuts.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** resolve truncated lines once at encode/bounds time and store them on the item; or at least wrap serialisation in the same scope and carry the provider on the scene.

#### C39 — High — A canvas-mode hit index throws on a scene that crossed a structured clone and has an axis or legend

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/bounds.ts:783`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #200 (2ce7c3b). Stored guide boxes are read by their numbers (Bounds.copyOf); hit-canvas.test.ts indexes a JSON-round-tripped scene with an axis and a legend on both renderers and requires the same answers (bite: .clone() restored fails the canvas case).

- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-hit-1` — `core-hit/`

**A canvas-mode hit index throws on a scene that crossed a structured clone and has an axis or legend.**

- In canvas mode `walk` calls `boundsClip` → `layoutBounds` for every group item (`hit.ts:553`).

- Repro `S/clone2.mjs` (real `cloneableScene` from `packages/react/dist/worker.js` + `structuredClone`):
  ```
  no guides   canvas  ok, size 2
  one axis    svg     ok, size 18
  one axis    canvas  THROWS TypeError: meta.bounds.clone is not a function
  one legend  canvas  THROWS TypeError: own.clone is not a function
  a title     canvas  ok, size 3
  ```
  `S/clone.mjs` shows the same for a JSON round trip.
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** for `buildHitIndex` on the wire scene.
- Not traced: what `ChartCore` does with the throw (other lane). PLAUSIBLE: an SVG-mode index reaching the same path through a `noBound` scope group that holds an axis.
- No test covers canvas + worker scene (grep of `packages/react/src/*worker*.test.tsx` for `renderer="canvas"`: none).
- Direction: read stored boxes structurally (`new Bounds().union(meta.bounds)`, as `titleBounds`/`laidBounds` already do at `bounds.ts:1068-1071`), and add a clone round trip to the hit tests for both renderers.

#### C40 — High — Per-owner state (`{signal}`-handler memory, between/throttle/debounce state, timer streams) is keyed by text (`<scope>|<index>:<name>:<i>:<JSON events>`), not by chart

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/signals.ts:254`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (0604090). Fixed: all per-owner loop state (streams, timers, handler memory, scales, warnings) lives in one record keyed by the compiled chart and released with it; no text keys remain.
- **Area:** core / signal event loop, transitions (also categories 2)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-signals-4` — `core-signals/`

`packages/core/src/signals.ts:254`, `:262`, `:270`, `:384-390`, `:1189`, `:1349-1356`, `:1032-1034`

**Per-owner state (`{signal}`-handler memory, between/throttle/debounce state, timer streams) is keyed by text (`<scope>|<index>:<name>:<i>:<JSON events>`), not by chart.** A different chart bound to the same owner after `detach()` inherits it. Only the expression shell checks the chart (`:600`).

- **A, stale handler memory (`t8.mjs` §3):** `a` (click → 5), `n` on `{signal:'a'}` → `a * 2`, `m: update 'n + 1'`.
  - First chart: click gives store `{a:5, n:10, m:11}`.
  - Host detaches, binds a new chart from the same spec text with fresh signals, click: store is `{"a":5,"n":10,"\u0000held:m":true,"m":1}` and the next render shows `m = 1` (expected 11).
  - After `release()` instead of `detach()`, the second chart is correct.
  - `<Chart>` only detaches on a re-bind (`packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:980-981`) and releases only on unmount or a new host (`:922`, `:978`). Two Vega-Lite specs with a selection of the same name would collide.
- **B, timers (`t7-life.mjs` §B):** six specs with different `timer{N}` bound in turn on one owner with `detach()` between: `timers.pending()` is 6 with one live binding. INTERACTION.md:301-302 says "nothing is left scheduled".
- **C, `release()` (`t7-life.mjs` §D):** `releaseOwner` never deletes `persisted` (`:284-292`). mousedown, `release()`, bind again, mousemove → `[mousedown, mouseup] > mousemove` fires without a mousedown.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN in core; the `<Chart>` path is CONFIRMED-TRACE only, not run in React.
- **Direction:** key the per-owner record by the compiled chart, as the shell does, and drop the previous chart's record when a different one binds; delete `persisted` in `releaseOwner`.

#### C41 — High — `config.locale` is silently ignored

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:8022`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #194 (3e906ae). Fixed: config.locale is a per-chart locale read by axes, legends, captions, expression format functions and data parsing; @aster-charts/vl passes it through.

- Aster: `$0.00`, `$50.00`, `$100.00`; caption in dollars; view 273 px wide. No error, no warning.

A legend shows the same (`100.000,0` in Vega, `100,000.0` in Aster). I did not run a time-locale case, and I did not check the VL compiler, which would forward `config.locale` into the Vega config.

Direction: either honour it (a per-chart `Locale` built at compile time and threaded to `tickFormat` / `labelFormat` / captions / expression `format`), or refuse it with the typed unsupported-feature error and document it.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `core-scale-7`, scripts `core-scale/`, CONFIRMED (run); a spec's `config.locale` is silently ignored; the only locale is process-wide):

`packages/core/src/format.ts:432-447`, `time-format.ts:413-425`; cross-reference `locale.ts:139-153, 189-202` (outside my list, but the brief's "default locale — cross-chart leakage" lands here).

- **No per-chart locale exists:** `defaultLocale(...)` is the one switch, documented as "process-wide state: set it once at start-up" (`docs/API.md:409-410`). Two charts in different locales cannot coexist in one page or SSR process.

#### C42 — High — a fitted projection goes stale for every consumer whose own rows did not change

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:2116`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (feddea00). A fitted projection is a node of the dependency closure (projection edges), so every consumer is refreshed when the fit changes; pinned by incremental-shapes and by the incremental oracle seeds that reproduce C42 on the audited base. Earlier work: #196.
- **Area:** core / geo (also categories 2)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-geo-1` — `core-geo/`

`packages/core/src/runtime.ts:2116` (`datasetDepsOf`), `:2341` (`affectedDatasets`), `:2366` (`markDepsOf`). The reuse decision at `incremental-engine.ts:704-706` only looks at the transform's own pulse.

- **Issue.** Dependency tracking knows dataset→dataset (`source`, dataset names in transforms, `data()` in a dataset's expressions). It does not know dataset/mark → projection → `fit` → datasets. When the fitted data changes, the projection is rebuilt, but consumers reading another, unchanged dataset are reused with coordinates from the previous fit. Affected consumers: a dataset with `geopoint`/`geopath`, a mark with a `geoshape`/`geopoint` transform, an encode calling `scale('p', …)`.
- **Scenario (real Vega-Lite, the `<Chart>` session path).** `layer: [{data:{name:'regions'}, mark:'geoshape'}, {data:{name:'cities'}, mark:'circle', encoding:{longitude,latitude}}]`. The compiled projection is `fit: {signal: "[data('regions'), layer_1_geojson_0]"}`. Call `session.evaluate(spec, {data:{regions, cities}})`, then add one region and call `session.evaluate` again with the same `cities` array.
  - Observed: regions redraw under the new fit; circles stay at `52.05,150.96` / `247.95,51.37`.
  - Expected (fresh evaluation of the same input): `12.5,182.76` / `62.5,157.34`.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `node incr3.mjs regions` → `STALE/DIFF`. The reverse direction (`node incr3.mjs`, cities change) is fine. `incr2.mjs` isolates five hand-written Vega shapes, each under `session.change` and `session.evaluate`:
  ```
  DIFF  :: geopoint in data (layered map: regions + cities)   (regions re-fitted, cities stale)
  STALE :: geopoint as mark transform
  STALE :: encode reads scale(p)
  ok    :: signal reads geoScale(p)
  STALE :: geoshape of a second dataset
  ```
  `incr.mjs` shows the same for a text encode reading `geoScale('p')` (`exprFit` steps 1 and 3). It also shows that signal-driven projection parameters, same-dataset fits and `geojson`-signal fits are correct.
- **Traced.** `datasetDepsOf` builds `names` from `sourceNames(d)` and strings equal to a dataset name, and `allData` from `DATA_FN_EXPR` in the dataset's own transforms. A `projection: 'p'` string is neither.
- **Direction.** Put projections in the dependency closure: for each dataset/mark, the projections it names (transform `projection`, `scale()/invert()/geo*()` calls, `clip.sphere`); for each projection, `fitDatasets(def.fit)` plus the `geojson` signals it reads. Add the two-layer case to the incremental fuzz.

#### C45 — High — React hydration keeps the server's picture when the client scene differs

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:745-768`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #198 (3e4b8d1 750187f 959cf8b). Fixed: the hydration commit patches the adopted svg to the client scene and remounts the a11y overlay/bound inputs (each keyed on its own, so re-renders never duplicate a row of inputs: 959cf8b); tested with server markup from another time zone (child process) and another text measurer.
- **Area:** react / <Chart>, shells, SSR (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-chart-4` — `react-chart/`

`src/ChartCore.tsx:745-768` (markup), `:852-865` (layout effect: "the browser just parsed it, so the tree already matches").
- On hydration React keeps mismatching `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` content. The layout effect still records `domSceneRef.current = displayScene` and skips the patcher. Server and client scenes differ when (a) the server measures text with the headless estimate and the browser with a canvas (`packages/core/src/text-metrics.ts:1-12`), or (b) the server's time zone differs from the user's.
- Scenario (b), exact: server `TZ=UTC`, client `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`, a `time` x axis, fixed `width`/`height`. After `hydrateRoot` the axis reads `["2024","06 AM","12 PM","06 PM","Tue 02"]`; a client mount shows `["12 PM","06 PM","Tue 02","06 AM"]`. It stays wrong across parent re-renders.
- Scenario (a): band axis with a long label, autosize `pad`. The hydrated DOM has the plot at `translate(183,0)`; the scene the chart hit-tests and overlays with has `padding.left = 178`. Tooltips, clicks, the brush and the a11y boxes are offset from the pixels. The client canvas was a 9 px/char `measureText` stub in jsdom, not a real browser.
- A container-measured chart usually self-heals at the first ResizeObserver callback; a fixed-size static chart never does.
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `r8-hydrate.mjs` (a child process renders the server HTML under `TZ=UTC` with no DOM). `r8b-hydrate-converge.mjs` shows a later scene change (`setSignal`) repairs it. React logs one hydration-mismatch warning.
- `docs/adr/0003-ssr-async-worker.md:34` ("hydration has no layout flash and no measurement pass") and `chart-types.ts:106-107` do not hold across environments. `Chart.ssr.test.tsx` and corpus-parity hydrate in one jsdom process, so the guard cannot fail for this.
- Direction: patch the adopted `<svg>` to the client scene once after hydration (as `ssr.ts:56-58` does), or patch on a fingerprint difference.

#### C46 — High — A chart that mounts in its error state never measures its container and has no wheel zoom after it recovers

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:462-482`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #198 (f75cbb0). Fixed: the error state is drawn inside the chart's element, which persists through error and recovery, so measurement and wheel stay bound (Chart.error-channel recovery test).
- **Area:** react / <Chart>, shells, SSR (also categories 5)

`src/ChartCore.tsx:462-482` (ResizeObserver effect, deps `[needsMeasure, hasBinds]`), `:1145-1159` (wheel effect, deps `[zoomEnabled, zoomAxes, pointerMapper]`), `:1633-1638` (the error state is another element with no `containerRef`), `:586`.

- By the same reading, error then recovery after a healthy mount leaves the observers on the detached element (traced, not run).

- `src/useChart.test.tsx:42` ("surfaces render errors instead of throwing") covers an evaluation error only.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `docs-api-1`, scripts `docs-api/`, CONFIRMED (run); a VL spec without `/vl`, a VL compile error, or `spec={null}` throws out of render):

`R/packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:361`, `R/packages/react/src/useChart.ts:36`, `R/packages/react/src/spec.ts:7-13,22-24`; docs: `R/docs/ERRORS.md:44`, `:406-408`, `R/docs/API.md:1018-1019`, `:966-969`, `R/packages/react/README.md:27`.

This extends the known item "VL compile error thrown from render instead of `onError`" to the first-run path and to the docs that promise otherwise.

- **Cause.** `normalizeChartSpec` is called inside `useMemo` during render (`ChartCore.tsx:361`: `const spec = React.useMemo(() => normalizeChartSpec(stableSpec), [stableSpec])`; `useChart.ts:36` does the same), outside the `try` that produces the error state.
- **Scenario.** `<Chart spec={vlSpec} onError={report} />` with no `import '@aster-charts/react/vl'`, the first thing a Vega-Lite newcomer does.
  - Observed: render throws `Error: A Vega-Lite spec was passed but the compiler is not loaded. Add \`import '@aster-charts/react/vl'\` (side-effect import) before rendering Vega-Lite specs, or pass an already-compiled Vega spec. Vega specs need no extra import.`
  - With no error boundary the whole root is unmounted (container `innerHTML` length 0) and `onError` received nothing.
  - Expected an error state and a callback: ERRORS.md:44 says "`<div role="alert">` in `<Chart>` | the render failed ... `onError` receives the error", and :406-408 says "`<Chart>` renders `<div role="alert">` with `Chart render failed` ... and calls `onError`; `useChart` returns `{ error }`".
- **`useChart`.** `useChart(vlSpec)` without `/vl` throws from render. API.md:1018-1019 says "`error` is set (and `scene`/`svg` are `null`) when the evaluation throws". `useChartWorker(vlSpec)` in the same situation does return `{ error }` (observed), so the entry points disagree.
- **Compile error.** With `/vl` imported, `<Chart spec={{...vl, foo: 1}} onError>` throws `[aster/vl] <spec>: unknown top-level property "foo"` from render and `onError` is not called (the other lane's finding, reproduced).
- **Null spec.** `<Chart spec={null}>` (state not loaded yet) gives `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '$schema')` from render (`spec.ts:8`) and the root unmounts. `<Chart spec={undefined}>` does the same.
- **String spec.** `<Chart spec={'{"width":10}'}>` (a JSON string from `fetch().text()`) gives the same "A Vega-Lite spec was passed but the compiler is not loaded" message, which sends the reader to the wrong fix. `isVegaLiteSpec` reads `spec.concat` / `spec.repeat`, which every string has (`spec.ts:11-12`); arrays have `concat` too.
- **Doc wording.** API.md:966-969 calls this "the render-error stance of a missing Vega-Lite compiler", which a reader takes to be the `role="alert"` state. It is an uncaught throw.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** — `$S/ws/first-run-react.mjs` (sections 1, 3, 6). Output lines:
- `### <Chart spec={vegaLite} onError> WITHOUT /vl ... "html":0,"onError":[],"reactErrors":["act threw: A Vega-Lite spec was passed but the compiler is not loaded...`
- `### useChart(vegaLite) WITHOUT /vl ... "act threw: ..."`
- `### <Chart spec={null}/> ... "act threw: Cannot read properties of null (reading '$schema')"`

Direction: normalize inside the guarded evaluation, so the missing compiler, a `VLCompileError` and a non-object spec all reach the error state, `onError` and `useChart().error`. Make `isVegaLiteSpec` require a plain object and use own-property reads. Then make ERRORS.md and API.md say one thing.

#### C48 — High — failed `useSpecData` load refetches forever

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/useChart.ts:129-134`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #199 (d3bfa54). Fixed: a rejected useSpecData load stays cached and reaches the error boundary once (1 fetch, was 168/s); it is retried on an input change or resetSpecDataErrors() from the boundary's reset (DECISIONS Q19); a time-based drop was measured to refetch inside React's own retry.
- **Area:** react / hooks, streams, workers (also categories 5)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-1` — `react-hooks/`

`src/useChart.ts:129-134` (eviction), `:150` (`React.use`).
- **Cause:** the rejection handler deletes the cache entry before React retries. The retry render gets a new pending promise, fetches again and suspends again. The rejected promise is never read, so the error is never thrown.
- **Scenario:** `useSpecData(urlSpec, { fetch })` under `<Suspense>` plus an error boundary; `fetch` answers 500.
- **Observed** (`t07-usespecdata.mjs rejected 3000`): `fetches 514 | renders 515 | renders that got data 0 | DOM: loading`. The count is bounded only by the mock's 5 ms latency.
- **Expected:** one fetch, then the boundary shows the error.
- The comment at `:129-131` ("The rejected promise is still what this render sees") is false. `docs/API.md:1024` describes the loop as a feature.
- Continues prior **C92**: the fix over-corrected.
- **Test gap:** `src/registry.test.ts:26-45` checks only the resource function; nothing renders a failing load.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** keep the rejected promise cached so the retry render throws it; evict on boundary reset, unmount or a time-to-live. Add a component test with a fetch counter.

#### C49 — High — push before the start effect is accepted, then dropped

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:259-260`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #199 (dba96b7). Fixed: useChartWorkerStream has one ordered producer queue that exists before the stream; pushes before the start effect, during add-on load and across a restart are delivered in order; model-based test over generated op sequences.
- **Area:** react / hooks, streams, workers
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-3` — `react-hooks/`

`src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:259-260` (`batchesRef.current = []`), `:350-387` (`push`), contract at `:89-94` ("`true` means it will be delivered").
- **Cause:** before the start effect there is no stream, so `push` parks the batch; the effect then empties the buffer. A child's effects and any layout effect run before the hook's passive effect. The same applies between a spec-changing render and the restart effect.
- **Observed** (`t05-push-before-effect.mjs`, child pushes 3 rows in its mount effect):
  ```
  useChartStream                     push returned true | marks in svg 6 | flush requests -
  useChartWorkerStream(worker)       push returned true | marks in svg 3 | flush requests []
  useChartWorkerStream(no worker)    push returned true | marks in svg 3 | flush requests -
  ```
  6 means four rows drawn; 3 means only the spec's own row.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** do not clear the buffer on first start; replay parked batches once the stream exists. On restart, either keep them or answer `false`.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `docs-api-8`, scripts `docs-api/`, CONFIRMED (run); `useSpecData` reloads on every render for an inline spec or an inline `allow`/`fetch` function):

`R/packages/react/src/useChart.ts:102-110` (functions keyed by identity), `:118-128` (`RESOURCES` is a `WeakMap` keyed by the spec object, one entry per spec), `R/docs/API.md:1022-1024`.

#### C51 — High — Layer bin merging merges across unrelated sources and across differently filtered pipelines

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:976-1009`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #202 (225c702). layer bins before own transforms, MergeBins siblings only; binning a field the layer's own transform makes refused (Q9); vl-optimize-merges
- **Area:** vl / composition
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c1-2` — `vl-c1/`

**Layer bin merging merges across unrelated sources and across differently filtered pipelines.**

Bins are keyed by signal name with the layer prefix stripped (980, 985) over all datasets of the view. The later `extent` is dropped and the later bin's `signal` removed (1005-1007), with no check that the bins share a parent dataset.

- **(a) Different `data`:** two layers, both `x: {bin: true, field: "v"}`, values 1..9 and 100..900. Ours bins `source_1` with `layer_1_bin_maxbins_10_v_extent`, which is computed over `source_0`. Vega-lite keeps two extents.
- **(b) Same data, layer 0 filtered:** layer 0 has `filter: "datum.v < 10"`, layer 1 none (v includes 55). Ours takes the one extent after layer 0's filter and bins the unfiltered layer 1 with it. Vega-lite bins once on the unfiltered source and filters afterwards.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `t2-layer.mjs` (`layer-bin-diffdata`, `layer-bin-filter` are `DIFF`); datasets printed by `t3.mjs`.
- **Direction:** merge only bins that share the same parent and the same transform prefix; otherwise keep both extents and signals. The comment at 972-975 describes a rule that vega-lite does not follow in (b).

#### C53 — High — Two different binnings of one field: the aggregate groups by only the last one

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4176`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: the aggregate groups by every bin of a field (binNames carries the parameters); vl-scales-guides 'a field binned twice' (37 specs fail with the bug planted)
- **Area:** vl / scales, stacking, guides

**Two different binnings of one field: the aggregate groups by only the last one.**
`binSignals` is keyed by the raw field (`binSignals.set(f.field, …)`), so a second channel binning the same field with other parameters overwrites the first. The aggregate loop then pushes only that one's start/end into `groupby`.

Also reproduced with `size` binned, and with x `maxbins 10` + y `maxbins 4` (aria `b (binned): null`).
Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `t12.mjs` (3 of 4 cases DIFF).

#### C56 — High — Merging "identical" datasets drops a bin `signal` that scales still read, so the compiled spec does not run

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/optimize.ts:139-149`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #202 (225c702). literal-extent bins merged; a bin signal not shared is never merged away; vl-optimize-merges
- **Area:** vl / validate, optimize, predicates
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-rest1-2` — `vl-rest1/`

**Merging "identical" datasets drops a bin `signal` that scales still read, so the compiled spec does not run.**

`withoutBinDeclarations` strips every bin's `signal` before comparing pipelines, assuming MergeBins already renamed the readers. `mergeBins` skips bins without an extent signal (`optimize.ts:104`). A bin with a literal extent therefore keeps a distinct per-view signal, the two datasets compare equal, the second is dropped with its signal, and nothing renames the references.

- **Scenario (schema-valid):** `{data, hconcat: [hist, hist]}` with `hist = {mark: 'bar', encoding: {x: {field: 'b', type: 'quantitative', bin: {extent: [0, 30]}}, y: {aggregate: 'count'}}}`.
- **Observed:** aster declares only `concat_0_bin_extent_0_30_maxbins_10_b_bins`; scale `concat_1_x` reads `concat_1_…_bins`; real Vega throws `Unrecognized signal name: "concat_1_bin_extent_0_30_maxbins_10_b_bins"`.
- **Expected:** vega-lite keeps one dataset, declares the `concat_1` name, points every reader at it, and renders.
- **Also fails:** a `repeat` of heat maps with a binned colour and `resolve.scale.color: independent`, and two size-binned scatters (`opt2.mjs` O2a, O2f, O2h).
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `repro-optimize-bin-signal.mjs`, `opt2.mjs`.
- **Direction:** a transform that declares a signal is part of a dataset's identity unless the merge also renames that signal's readers. `mergeCommonPrefixes` already refuses `writesSignal` transforms; `mergeIdenticalDatasets` needs the same rule or the rename.

#### C57 — High — Two views that aggregate to the same output name with different ops or fields are merged; both views silently draw the same numbers

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/optimize.ts:217-223`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #202 (225c702). same 'as' with a different measure refused (Q9: vega-lite draws one in both); vl-optimize-merges
- **Area:** vl / validate, optimize, predicates
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-rest1-3` — `vl-rest1/`

**Two views that aggregate to the same output name with different ops or fields are merged; both views silently draw the same numbers.**

Measures are keyed by `as` only (`:221`: `if (!measures.has(String(as))) measures.set(...)`), and the group key is `[source, groupby]`.

- **Scenario (schema-valid):** `hconcat` of two bars over the same data; view 1 has `transform: [{aggregate: [{op: 'sum', field: 'b', as: 'v'}], groupby: ['a']}]`, view 2 the same with `op: 'mean'`; both use `y: {field: 'v'}`.

- **Direction:** pick the target (Open question 1). To match vega-lite, keep duplicates in its order. To be correct, do not merge aggregates whose `as` collides with a different `(field, op)`.
