#### C61 — High — Aster receives the spec object the oracle has already written its answers onto

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/run-sweep.ts:201-202`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (3df3102,cfcd65a,f7180a3). Fixed: forEngines gives each engine its own deep copy of every case in every gate and the vitest differentials copy per oracle parse; a vitest setup file and a static rule fail any harness that shares one object (shown to fail on planted fixtures).
- **Area:** conformance / harness (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `harness-src-1` — `harness-src/`

`src/run-sweep.ts:201-202,225-229,233-247`; `src/probe.ts:47`; `src/gallery/static.ts:42,61,71`; `src/sweeps/vega-schema.mjs:483-488,523-530`; `src/sweeps/signals.mjs:681`

- **Mechanism.** `runOneCase` renders the oracle first, then Aster on `ourVgSpec`, and for every non-Vega-Lite case `ourVgSpec === vgSpec`. Vega ingests inline `values` rows without copying and its transforms write onto them. `run.ts:63` clones for this reason; the sweep runner, `probe.ts` and gallery-static do not.
- **Observed** (`shared-spec-contamination.mts`): after the oracle ran, the rows Aster receives carry `y0,y1` (stack), `startAngle,endAngle` (pie), `bin0,bin1` (bin).
- **Consequence** (`shared-spec-contamination-verdict.mts`): an engine that runs no transform at all gets `differ` on clean rows and `OK` on the shared rows, for all five cases tried:
  - `linear-rect-stacked--plain`
  - `linear-rect-stacked--with-a-word`
  - `arc-theta--plain`
  - `arc-theta--with-a-null`
  - `binned--plain`
- **Value sweep.** Its "500 ok" cannot see a `stack`/`pie`/`bin` that skips a row or stops writing, which is what its header says it exists for.
- **Vega sweep, 17 `projection-*` families** (`shared-spec-projection.mts`): `PINS` is one module-level array used by every case. After the first oracle render, row 0 is `{"lon":-75,"lat":40,"px":21.46…,"py":14.22…}` for every later case and both engines. An engine with no `geopoint` gets `OK`.
- **Signals sweep (PR gate).** `spec: chart.spec` is one object for all cases of a chart, across 8 concurrent workers.
- **Gallery static, Vega specs.** `oracleSpec = src`, vega runs on it twice, then Aster gets a JSON copy taken after the mutation. Exposure is limited to examples with inline rows and a writing transform.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** deep-copy per engine before either runs, freeze generator tables, re-run the three sweeps and restate the numbers. Add a harness self-test where the engine side has its transform removed and must differ.

#### C62 — High — `scene-diff` compares nothing for marks inside a group mark

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/scene-diff.ts:172-183`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (f46e288). Fixed: scene-diff walks both trees at every depth (group marks, facets), compares scopes, scales, mark order and every encodeEntry channel, fails a spec whose oracle drew items and none were compared, and floors items 8211 (was 5524); 141 of 1063 corpus specs compared zero items before, 11 now (the oracle draws none either).

- **Lane ID / scripts:** `harness-src-2` — `harness-src/`

`src/scene-diff.ts:172-183,349-370,41-45,36-39,214`; `scripts/scene-diff.mts`; `docs/TESTING.md:123-125,165`

- **Mechanism.** `collectOurScopes` recurses only into children with `marktype === 'group'` or no marktype (:179-182). In Aster's scene, a group mark's child marks are typed nodes directly under the group node, so they are never collected. `sceneDiff` iterates only `ourScopes` (:349), so an empty list is a match.
- **Observed** (`scene-diff-vacuous.mts`):
  - two top-level rect marks: `groups=2 items=2`
  - the same two marks inside one group mark: `diffs=0 groups=0 items=0`
  - a 3-cell facet: `groups=0 items=0`

  - The runner passes on `diffs.length === 0` with no floor on items compared.

#### C66 — High — a prerelease tag publishes as npm `latest`

- **Location:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:103`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced; lines re-read by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (118b16a). release-publish.mjs passes --tag next/latest from the version; tested for 18 forms against a fake npm
- **Area:** tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks (also categories 5)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tooling-1` — `tooling/`

`.github/workflows/release.yml:8-9, 103`; `docs/RELEASE.md:25`; `scripts/check-release-tag.mjs:29`

- **Issue.** The workflow is triggered by `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+-*`. `check-release-tag.mjs` accepts `v1.2.3-rc.1`, and `release-workflow.test.mjs:148` asserts it. RELEASE.md documents "`vX.Y.Z` or `vX.Y.Z-prerelease`". The publish command has no `--tag`: `npm publish ./release-tarballs/aster-charts-"$pkg"-*.tgz --access public --provenance --ignore-scripts`. No manifest sets `publishConfig.tag` (only `access` and `provenance`).
- **Scenario.** The owner pushes `v0.5.0-rc.1` with the three packages at `0.5.0-rc.1`. With the npm that ships with Node 22 (npm 10; the job uses `node-version: 22` and never upgrades npm), all three go under the `latest` dist-tag, so `npm i @aster-charts/react` installs the release candidate. If the runner's npm is 11 or newer, `npm publish` of a prerelease without `--tag` is refused, so the documented path fails at the first package. Expected: a prerelease goes to `next` and `latest` stays on the last stable.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-TRACE for the workflow and manifests. npm's dist-tag behaviour is its documented behaviour; not run here (no network).
- **Direction.** Derive the dist-tag in the publish step from `$GITHUB_REF_NAME` (`--tag next` when it contains `-`) and assert it in `release-workflow.test.mjs`, or drop the prerelease trigger until that exists.

#### C67 — High — The hit comparison names items by first-encounter order on each side, so "compared by item identity" does not hold: a wrong-item bug is invisible

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/geometry-differential.testlib.ts:181`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #200 (2ce7c3b 855f5fb 3c22efa). The numbered old-vs-new hit comparison is gone; geometry-vs-vega.test.ts and conformance:geometry name items by their place (/g0[1]/m2[3]); bite: intersect reporting the next item of a mark fails 8 runs.
- **Area:** tests / core (legacy copies II … path)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core4-1` — `tests-core4/`
- **Lead's note:** The lead re-ran `j-identity.mjs` against the lane's clean and planted bundles: with the planted bug the new index picks item `b` where the legacy picks `a`, and `diffScene` reports no hit difference on that scene or on 300 random scenes.

`packages/core/src/geometry-differential.testlib.ts:181` and `:185` (one `ids` map per side), `:41-49` (`argText`), `:91` (`targetText`); the claim is at `:3-4`.

- Each side builds its own `const ids = new Map<object, number>()`, and `argText` gives an item the id `ids.size` the first time it is seen. The two logs are then compared as strings.
- Any bijective mix-up of items therefore produces identical text. Legacy hits `A,B,A` and new hits `B,A,B` both print `#0,#1,#0`.
- The intersect comparison shares one map (`:210`) and is sound. Only the hit consumer has this.

Scenario (`S/build-planted-hit.mjs` → `S/bundle-planted-hit.mjs`, then `S/j-identity.mjs`): `hit.ts` is planted so that `describe()` reports the next item of the same mark (cyclic) instead of the item under the pointer.

```
./bundle.mjs              | pick(20,30).datum.id legacy: a new: a
  random hand-built scenes seeds 1-150 (300 scenes), hit consumers only: scenes with a hit diff {} of 300
./bundle-planted-hit.mjs  | pick(20,30).datum.id legacy: a new: b
  diffScene hit diffs on this scene: []
  random hand-built scenes seeds 1-150 (300 scenes), hit consumers only: scenes with a hit diff {} of 300
```

Expected: every probe differs. Observed: 0 diffs over `query`, `queryMark`, `pick` and `tooltip`, in grid and "linear" mode.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

Direction: use one `ids` map for both sides, as `:210` does, or compare `t.item` with `===` since both indexes are built on the same scene object.

#### C68 — High — A signal that holds an event's `datum` is never identical to a row afterwards, so `reorderable-matrix` cannot highlight or reorder

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:4106-4108`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega examples II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery2-1` — `gallery2/`

`packages/core/src/runtime.ts:4106-4108` (`copyRows`: `rows.map((r) => ({ ...r }))`), reached from `runtime.ts:3987`. Spec: `vega/reorderable-matrix.vg.json:16` (`"update": "datum"`), `:25`, `:29`, `:48` (`dest >= 0 && datum === src ? dest : datum.order`), `:112`, `:158`, `:177`.

- **Scenario.** Press the 6th column label ("Geborand"), drag right to x=400 then x=600, release. Same DOM events to both engines; Aster resolves the item through the hit index, as `<Chart>` does.
- **Vega:** on press 1 label turns steelblue and 153 cells turn `#ddd`; the label moves from x=85 to 255 to 455 as the matrix re-sorts, and stays at 455 after release.
- **Aster:** 0 blue labels, 0 grey cells, label stays at x=85 throughout. `dest` is equal in both (26.5, 46.5), so the event loop works; only the identity tests fail. Log is empty.
- **Minimal form** (`S/i4.mjs min`): a rect mark with `fill: [{test: "datum === src"} → steelblue, {test: "datum.k === src.k"} → orange]`. Vega paints steelblue, Aster orange, with or without a transform on the dataset. With `datum === src` inside a `formula`, Vega moves the rect to x=100 and Aster leaves it at 0.
- **Cause** (`S/ident.mjs`, core only, no DOM): every evaluation hands marks fresh row copies. `item.datum === spec row` is false, and the second evaluation's datum is not the first's, although `scene.signalParams.src === d1` is true.
- **Docs.** "Deviations from Vega" (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:597`) covers by-value comparison only for `modify`/`remove`. Nothing says `===` between a signal-held datum and a row is always false. Not in the report (grepped `datum ===`, identity).
- **Why the gate passes.** `src` starts as `{}`; no pointer is ever pressed.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `S/i3.mjs reorderable`, `S/i4.mjs min`, `S/ident.mjs`.
- **Direction.** Keep row identity across evaluations for unchanged rows, or resolve a signal value that is a tuple to the current row by its tuple id before expressions run. Otherwise document it as a deviation and warn when a handler's `update` is `datum`.

#### C69 — High — `interactive_crossfilter`: a unit inside a `layer` bins after its own transforms; vega-lite bins before them, so any brush re-bins and re-scales the charts

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4296-4298`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** ALREADY FIXED in #211 (d30fab2,226c3a3). Fixed at base (leaf-first bins in the layer path); pinned by the brushed-store differential (bites when the order is swapped) and the gallery seeded path
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega-Lite examples I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery3-1` — `gallery3/`

`packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4296-4298` (user transforms pushed first, encoding nodes after); the comment at `compile.ts:972-975` describes a different rule from vega-lite's. Adds to `C51 (vl-c1-2)`.

- **Rule in the pinned vega-lite 6.4.3** (`packages/conformance/node_modules/vega-lite/build/index.js:18525-18531`, `18543-18545`):
  `const parentIsLayer = model.parent && isLayerModel(model.parent); … if (parentIsLayer) { head = BinNode.makeFromEncoding(head, model) ?? head; } … if (model.transforms.length > 0) { head = parseTransformArray(…) }`.
  A unit whose parent is a layer gets its encoding bins before its own `transform`.
- **Aster:** `pushAll(pipeline, userOut)` at `compile.ts:4297`, then the encoding's `extent` + `bin`.
- **Compiled output for the official spec:**
  - vega-lite: `source_0: [extent(delay), bin, extent(distance), bin, formula]`, then `data_1: [filter vlSelectionTest]`.
  - Aster: `data_3: [formula, filter vlSelectionTest]`, then `data_0: [extent(distance), bin, aggregate]`.
- **Why the gate is green:** with an empty `brush_store` the filter passes every row, so both orders give the same picture.
- **Scenario:** `interactive_crossfilter.vl.json` (repeat of `layer: [{params: brush, transform: [{filter: {param: "brush"}}], bar, x: bin maxbins 20}]`). Both engines rendered fresh with the tuple the example's own `brush_tuple` writes: `brush_store = [{unit: "child__column_distance_layer_0", fields: [{field: "distance", channel: "x", type: "R"}], values: [[1285.9, 2504.8]]}]`.
  - Vega: distance cell has 3 bars on an x axis "from 0 to 4,500"; delay cell 6 bars.
  - Aster: distance cell has 12 bars on an x axis "from 1,300 to 2,500"; delay cell 10 bars.
  - 45 canonical diff lines. A delay brush `[0, 60]` gives 46 diff lines.
- **Static consequence, no interaction needed:** `$S/single-layer-filter-bin.vl.json` (`layer: [{transform: [{filter: "datum.distance > 1285.9 && datum.distance < 2504.8"}], bar, x: {field: "distance", bin: {maxbins: 20}}, y: count}]`) is 357×347 with an axis 0–4,500 in vega-lite and 349×347, re-binned, in Aster.
- **Relation to `C51 (vl-c1-2)`:** that finding saw the two-layer form ("layer 0 filtered, layer 1 none") and attributed it to bin merging. The root cause is the ordering rule above; a single layer, with nothing to merge, shows it. `layer_histogram`, `concat_bar_layer_circle`, `interactive_concat_layer`, `interactive_layered_crossfilter(_discrete)` and `layer_circle_independent_color` pass only because their unfiltered layer comes first and the merge reuses its extent.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
  - `tsx one.mts interactive_crossfilter '{}' --data='{"brush_store":[…]}' --dump` → `FAIL (45 diff lines)`; the same command with no `--data` → `PASS`.
  - `tsx one.mts single-layer-filter-bin '{}' --spec=$S/single-layer-filter-bin.vl.json` → `FAIL (46 diff lines)`.
  - Found by `$S/probe-sel2.mts` (51 of 54 selection cases pass; this is the only fail) and independently by `$S/param-refs.mts`.
- **Direction:** for a unit whose parent is a layer, emit the encoding's `extent`/`bin` before that unit's own transforms, then let the merge share them; correct the comment at 972-975. Add the gap to `packages/vl/README.md` "Known compiler gaps": `gallery/TRIAGE.md:30-33` says the gaps the gallery cannot see are listed there, and this one is on a gallery spec.

#### C70 — High — After one legend click on the official `point_constant_legend_domain`, the legend loses its other entries; Vega keeps them

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:4651-4658`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega-Lite examples II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery4-1` — `gallery4/`
- **Lead's note:** The lead re-ran the legend click on both engines: Vega keeps `["USA","Japan","Europe"]`, Aster shows `["USA"]`. It falls inside the documented "a signal write is a fresh render" deviation, whose description does not mention scale domains or legend entries; if that deviation is meant to cover it, this is a Medium documentation gap.

- **Where:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:4651-4658` (`growsOnLookup`: "…it is never kept") and `:4900-4901` (`prevEntry === undefined || growsOnLookup(prevEntry.scale) ? undefined`). Test that claims the pattern: `packages/conformance/src/signal-react-false-vs-vega.test.ts:96-101`. Docs: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:594`, `docs/INTERACTION.md:134`, `:142-146`.
- **Scenario (the unmodified official spec, its url data inlined):** mount it, click the first legend symbol ("USA").
  - Real vega-lite + Vega (svg renderer, jsdom): legend labels `["USA","Japan","Europe"]` before and after; 245 points remain.
  - Aster `<Chart>` (built `@aster-charts/react`, jsdom, same DOM event): `["USA","Japan","Europe"]` before, **`["USA"]`** after; 245 points remain.
  - Expected: the legend stays constant. That is what the example and its `react: false` param are for; in Aster the user can no longer click or shift-click Japan or Europe.
- **Cause, isolated on a plain Vega spec** (`implicit-domain.mjs`): an ordinal scale with no domain feeding a legend, then the rows of two categories removed.
  - Vega keeps the scale object, so its implicit domain still lists them: `["USA","Japan","Europe"]`.
  - Aster rebuilds a grows-on-lookup scale on every evaluation: `["USA"]`.
  - In the VL example `color_domain` (`react: false`) is `undefined` in every evaluation, so the colour scale is exactly this kind of scale.
- **Why the gates are green:**
  - The gallery compares the first frame; the store is empty.
  - `signal-react-false-vs-vega.test.ts:96` is titled for this pattern and asserts only the first frame (`expect(want).toContain('Europe')`).
  - By the selections gate's own rule (`docs/INTERACTION.md:142-146`) the step would count as `retained`. My three-way probe shows vega-fresh-with-store equals Aster and differs from vega-updated, which is that rule's definition.
- **Documentation:** the `retained` deviation is described as "the autosize, padding and axis-tick order" Vega first computed (`INTERACTION.md:142`; `ARCHITECTURE.md:594` adds "and some other dataflow state"). Neither says that scale domains and legend entries change, or that `react: false` therefore has no effect after the first frame. `INTERACTION.md:134` says "The state is the one Vega computes for the same input".
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `react-interact.mjs legend` (Aster), `vega-interact.mjs legend` (oracle), `implicit-domain.mjs` (isolation), `probe-select.mjs` (3-WAY and STREAM lines for `point_constant_legend_domain`). Root cause **CONFIRMED-TRACE** from the lines quoted above plus the isolation run.
- **Severity note:** I rated this High because an official example's titular behaviour fails on the default `<Chart>` path. It sits inside a deliberate, documented deviation class, so the lead may prefer Medium plus a doc fix.
- **Direction:** either keep the implicit domain of an ordinal scale whose settings did not change (as Vega's scale object does), or state in "Deviations from Vega" that domain-less ordinal scales and `react: false` are first-frame only. Add this example's click step to `conformance:selections` without the `retained` exemption for legend content.

#### C110 — Medium — An update whose re-encode throws is not the fresh scene

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:5339-5400`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (0af54b9). Fixed (DECISIONS Q8): a pass cut short by a failure takes no pulse, so the update equals the fresh scene; recovered encode errors shape in incremental-shapes.test.ts.
- **Area:** core / runtime: state, signals, reuse keys
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt1-5` — `core-rt1/`

`runtime.ts:5339-5400` (core-rt3's range)

- **Scenario** (`s15-encode-error-update.mjs`; text `datum.o.label`, row 1 edited to `o: null`):
  ```
  incremental text/fill ["L0/#000","-/#000","L2/#000","L3/#000"]
  fresh       text/fill ["L0/#000","-/#000","-/-","-/-"]      svg equal: false
  ```
  Same via `evaluateChart` + `dataChanges`. The evaluation after it is correct.
- **Note.** The incremental result is arguably Vega's update behaviour and the fresh one its first-run behaviour; the documented guarantee has no exception for it.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-RUN. **Direction.** Re-encode the mark whole when a spliced encode logs an error, or document the exception.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `core-rt2-4`, scripts `core-rt2/`, CONFIRMED (run); `runtime.ts:5346-5404` (pulse branch of `evaluateMarkItems`)):

**`runtime.ts:5346-5404` (pulse branch of `evaluateMarkItems`)**: when the encode of a changed row throws (recovered, logged), the incremental scene matches neither a fresh evaluation nor Vega.

Spec: `labels` text mark with `text: {signal: 'datum.o.p'}`, then a `dots` symbol mark, both over `t`; rows A, B, C; row B changes to `o: null`.

| Evaluation | `labels` | `dots` |
|---|---|---|
| Session, and `evaluateChart` + `dataChanges` | A, no text, C | not made |
| Fresh `evaluateChart`, and a fresh Vega view | A, no text, no text | not made |
| Vega's running view after the same change | A, B, C | intact |

The other reuses refuse an unclean pass at entry (`cleanPass`); a pulse that fails midway keeps the items it did not visit. The evaluation is not committed as a base, so the next step is right again.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**, `repro-encode-error.mjs`; also `t-errors.mjs`.
Direction: on a failed pulsed encode, re-make the mark or pass without reuse; or state that a step with a recovered error is outside the Guarantee. The oracle generates no failing step.

#### C115 — Medium — A `source` dataset with `format` is built from the source's raw values, skipping the source's transforms; Vega ignores `format` there

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:3925-3933`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (0af54b9 4a5138b). Fixed (DECISIONS Q12): format on a source-derived dataset is ignored as in vega; source-format-vs-vega.test.ts.
- **Area:** core / runtime: datasets, scales, fit (also categories 3, 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt2-2` — `core-rt2/`

**`runtime.ts:3925-3933` (`buildDatasetsOf`)**: a derived dataset that also has `format` is built from the source's raw `values` (or `input.data[source]`) re-read with that format, and the source's own transforms are skipped. Not listed under "Deviations from Vega".
```ts
3925      if ((d as { format?: DataFormatSpec }).format && srcDef?.values != null) {
3931        rows = readData(given ?? inlineValues(ctx, srcDef.values), (d as { format?: DataFormatSpec }).format, ...)
3933        inPulse = ctx.inputPulses?.get(src) ?? null
```
Aster vs real Vega 6 `view.data('b')`:
- `a`: values + `filter datum.v > 1`; `b`: `source: a, format: {type: 'json'}`. Aster `b` has 3 rows, Vega 2.
- `a`: values + `formula … as w`; `b`: `source: a, format: {parse: {s: 'number'}}` + `formula datum.w`. Aster rows have no `w`/`w2` and `s` is a number; Vega has both and `s` is a string.
- Host rows for `a` with a filter on `a`: same loss.
- `:3933` also hands the source's row pulse to rows re-read through a format.
- No `corpus/*.vg.json` uses the combination, so no gate sees it.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**, `repro-source-format.mjs` (4/4 DIFFERENT).
Direction: match Vega (ignore `format` on a `source` dataset), or keep the extension only where well defined (source without transforms, no pulse), document it, and refuse the rest.

#### C131 — Medium — Sort ties in the hierarchy layouts follow row position; Vega follows tuple id

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/hierarchy-layout.ts:47-53`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (ac7a567). Fixed: hierarchy layouts break sort ties by the order rows were made in (tuple-order), as vega's stableCompare; pinned by a generated differential with collects before stratify.
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-7` — `core-layout/`

**Sort ties in the hierarchy layouts follow row position; Vega follows tuple id.**

- **Cause:** `byRow` falls back to `position.get(a.data)`, the index in the current rows. Vega uses `stableCompare(sort, d => d.data)`, which is ingest order. They differ whenever an earlier transform reordered the rows.
- **Scenario** (`hier-edges.mjs`, "sort ties after collect"): three children of equal `s: 5`; `transform: [{type: 'collect', sort: {field: 'n'}}, stratify, {type: 'treemap', field: 's', size: [100, 50], sort: {field: 'value', order: 'descending'}}]`.
- **Observed:** `row 1 x0: aster=0 vega=58.33…; row 2 x0: aster=58.33… vega=79.16…; row 3 x0: aster=79.16… vega=0`. Without the `collect`, the same spec matches.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN. Undocumented.
- **Direction:** break ties by the row's ingest identity, or document the deviation. The comment "Ties keep the order of the rows" holds only for rows nothing reordered.

#### C132 — Medium — calendar intervals that never return

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/time.ts:116-134`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (47836c0 cb33297). Fixed: filtered/stepped calendar intervals end with Invalid Date when a step leaves the Date range, a search past the items ceiling is refused, UTC weeks every(k) jump exactly; the d3-time filter differential now runs to the range ends (exclusion dropped).
- **Area:** core / scales, time, format, colour (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-scale-3` — `core-scale/`

`packages/core/src/time.ts:116-134` (`interval.filter`), used by `every(k)` (`time.ts:145-150`) for every unit except year and millisecond. That covers the tick ladder (`scale-calendar.ts:48-56`), `quarter` (`time.ts:504`) and `{interval, step}` tick counts (`scale.ts:243`).

```ts
floor(date) { if (date >= date) while (unit.floor(date), !test(date)) date.setTime(+date - 1) },
shift(date, n) { if (!(date >= date)) return
  ... do unit.shift(date, +1) while (!test(date)) ...
```
The validity guard is only at entry. Once a step leaves the Date range, `test` is false forever. Each case below ran in a child with a 10–20 s timeout; Aster and vega both time out.

| Input | Path |
|---|---|
| `utcOffset('quarter', datetime(2020,0,1), 4000000)` in a signal expression | `shift` walks past year 275760 |
| utc scale `domain: [8.64e15 - 60000, 8.64e15]` with an axis | default ticks pick the 5-second rung, a filter |
| axis `tickCount: {interval:'week', step:2e7}` on a 2020–2023 utc scale; `nice: {interval:'week', step:2e7}` on a pre-1970 domain | the next multiple of the week count is outside the Date range |

- **Under limits:** every case in the table still hangs. The `utcOffset` expression was still running after 12 s under `limits: {maxTimeMs: 300, maxItems: 1000}`; the scale and axis cases after 15 s under `maxTimeMs: 500`.
- **Expected:** an Invalid Date or a typed refusal. The project fixes upstream non-termination elsewhere (`time.ts:408`, ARCHITECTURE.md:610, LIMITS.md:256).
- **Known but parked:** `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-time-intervals.test.mts:69-73` says "near the ends of the Date range the search does not end (in d3-time as well); those instants are left out". It is not in `time.ts`'s header, LIMITS.md or the deviations table.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN — `hang-time.mjs` (5 cases), `hang-run.sh` + `hang-case.mjs`.
- **Direction:** leave both loops when the date turns invalid. No terminating result changes, so the differential stays green; then drop the test's exclusion.

#### C133 — Medium — `{signal: "true" | "false" | "null"}` in a scale property is refused as `Unrecognized signal name`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/scale-domain.ts:53-64`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (4d62704). Fixed: a scale {signal} that parses to a literal or constant is evaluated, only a free identifier is a signal name; generated differential over every scale property that takes a signal.
- **Area:** core / scales, time, format, colour
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-scale-5` — `core-scale/`

`packages/core/src/scale-domain.ts:53-64`:
```ts
const IDENTIFIER = /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/
const EXPRESSION_CONSTANTS = new Set(['NaN', 'E', 'LN2', …, 'MAX_VALUE'])
…
if (IDENTIFIER.test(reference) && !EXPRESSION_CONSTANTS.has(reference)) raise(`Unrecognized signal name: ${reference}`)
```
`true`, `false` and `null` are literals of the expression language, but they match `IDENTIFIER` and are not in the set.

- **Scenario:** `{"name":"x","type":"linear","domain":{"data":"t","field":"v"},"range":"width","nice":{"signal":"true"}}` with a symbol mark → Aster logs `Unrecognized signal name: true`, builds no scale, and draws no marks. vega draws the two symbols at x = 75 and 200.
- **Same for:** `zero`/`reverse`/`clamp`/`round` with `{signal:"false"}` or `"true"`, and `domainMax`/`domainRaw` with `{signal:"null"}` (first seven differing cases of `probe-spec.mjs`).
- **Related, outside this lane:** `{signal:"autosize"}` and `{signal:"background"}` are vega built-in signals; Aster says unrecognized (the signals map comes from `runtime.ts`).
- **Coverage:** no test or corpus spec uses a literal as a signal reference; `differential-scale-spec-gen` never generates one.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN — `probe-signal-names.mjs`, `probe-spec.mjs`.
- **Direction:** send `true`/`false`/`null` to `ctx.evaluate`, or decide by parsing (an Identifier node is a signal name). Add them to the generator's pool.

#### C135 — Medium — `renderSceneToCanvasAppend` returns true while a full repaint differs

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/canvas.ts:344-352`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (647a044,abe8e82). Fixed: the append compares the whole root paint (sameRootPaint) and paints under the same view frame (offset, clip) as a full repaint.
- **Area:** core / SVG, DOM patcher, canvas, a11y (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-render-6` — `core-render/`

**`renderSceneToCanvasAppend` returns true while a full repaint differs.**

- The append paints under `ctx.translate(pb.left, pb.top)` (`:420`); a full repaint uses `pad.left + (scene.frameX ?? 0)` (`:145`). The comparison covers only `frameStroke`, `frameFill`, `frameStrokeWidth`, `frameClip` (`:346-347`).
- **Scenario A** (`canvas1.mjs` 2): root `encode.update: {x: 30, y: 7}`, one appended row. Append returns true and paints `translate 0 0 | translate 50 50 | arc`; the full repaint paints `translate 30 7 | … | translate 50 50 | arc`. The random walk in `canvasfuzz.mjs` found the same (seeds 23, 140).
- **Scenario B** (`canvas4.mjs`): the root's `opacity`, `fillOpacity`, `cornerRadius`, `strokeOpacity`, `strokeDash`, `strokeCap` or `x` changes in the same update as an append → `append returned true` for all seven. Only `fill` returns false.
- The doc claim "returns `false` … unless the result equals a full repaint" does not hold.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** translate by `frameX/Y`, and compare the frame with `sameRootPaint` (already used by `paintsSameAs`).

#### C139 — Medium — A rect with a NaN position is drawn at 0 but left out of the bounds on that axis

- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)

- `S/bounds-diff.mjs 21 6000 rect`: 623 of 6000 generated rect marks differ from `vega.boundMark`, all with a NaN x or y.
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**.
- Direction: `|| 0`. The `x2`/`y2` fallback there is dead for engine scenes (the encoder writes `width`/`height`).

#### C149 — Medium — `geoshape` without a projection uses a second path writer that disagrees with the engine and with Vega

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/transform.ts:279-284`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (eb38636). Fixed: geoshape draws through the add-on's GeoPath with or without a projection (geoJSONPath deleted); per Q12 the geoshape mark type and a shape mark drawing a datum's path are removed; differential-geoshape vs vega.
- **Area:** core / geo (also categories 3)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-geo-3` — `core-geo/`

`transform.ts:279-284` (falls to `geoJSONPath(geo)`), `transform.ts:522-555`, `runtime.ts:5550-5552`. Contrast `transform-extra.ts:457-460`, where `geopath` with no projection uses `geoRegistry.defaultPath` (the engine).

- **Issue.** `geoJSONPath` handles only Polygon/MultiPolygon/LineString/MultiLineString. It drops the last ring vertex only when it equals the first, and writes nothing for an empty ring.
- **Observed (`spec1.mjs`, mark-level `{type:'geoshape'}`, no `projection`):**

  | Geometry | Vega `d` | Aster `d` |
  |---|---|---|
  | Point [50,60] | `M50,60m0,4.5a4.5,4.5 0 1,1 0,-9a4.5,4.5 0 1,1 0,9z` | nothing drawn |
  | MultiPoint | two circles | nothing |
  | GeometryCollection | `M0,0L20,20M0,0L10,0L10,10Z` | nothing |
  | FeatureCollection point + line | `M5,6m0,4.5…zM0,0L9,9` | `M0,0L9,9` |
  | unclosed ring (4 points) | `M0,0L100,0L100,100Z` | `M0,0L100,0L100,100L0,100Z` |
  | Polygon `[[]]` | `Z` | `""` |

  The same geometries through `geopath` with no projection match Vega exactly (`spec6.mjs`: `geopathNoProj`, `geopathNoProjPoint`).
- **Related, same code.** `runtime.ts:5550` accepts a mark `type: 'geoshape'`, which is not a Vega mark type (Vega fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'bound')`). A `shape` mark also draws a datum's `path`/`shape` string, which Vega cannot (`spec7.mjs`). Neither is in "Deviations from Vega".
- **Doc.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:326` says the geoshape transform routes geometry through the projection's `GeoPath` and that "a path with no projection draws coordinates as they are". For `geoshape` that is not the code path.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`spec1.mjs`, `spec7.mjs`).
- **Direction.** Delete `geoJSONPath`; route the no-projection case through `geoRegistry.defaultPath` and have `addonsNeeded` report it. Decide whether the `geoshape` mark type is an intended extension.

#### C152 — Medium — sphere `geoBounds` throws on an empty ring where d3/Vega answer

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/geo-sphere-measures.ts:200-204`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (b38d8b1). Fixed: a polygon of only empty rings adds no longitude range instead of throwing; differential-geo-empty-rings against d3 without the empty rings (deviation listed).
- **Area:** core / geo
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-geo-6` — `core-geo/`

`geo-sphere-measures.ts:200-204` (`closeRange` throws when `range` is null), reached from `:226` after `:233-238` skipped the empty ring.

- **Scenario.** `geoBounds(null, {type:'MultiPolygon', coordinates:[[[]], [square]]})`, or a FeatureCollection whose first feature is `Polygon [[]]`.
- **Observed (`emptyring.mjs`, fresh process):**
  ```
  MultiPolygon [[[]], [square]]   bounds d3 [[0,0],[10,10.037423045910709]]   aster throws
  FeatureCollection [[]] + square bounds d3 [[0,0],[10,10.037423045910709]]   aster throws
  spec: vega ['bounds=0,0,10,10.037423045910709'] | aster ['']
  ```
  Aster's error is `TypeError: Cannot set properties of null (setting '0')`.
- **Why.** In d3 an empty ring calls `boundsRingPoint(lambda00, phi00)` with whatever an earlier ring left there, which also pushes a range. So d3 never throws here, and its value is history-dependent. Aster's message imitates a TypeError d3 only raises for a polygon with no rings at all.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction.** At `POLYGON_END`, skip `closeRange` when the polygon produced no range.

#### C153 — Medium — a projection parameter whose signal throws is swallowed; the map is drawn with defaults

#### C154 — Medium — `graticule`: inverted extents, `precision: 0` and string precision differ from Vega

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/transform.ts:608-615`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (327a830). Fixed: graticule coerces values, swaps inverted extents, gives zero/NaN steps d3's empty range and applies params in vega's definition order; differential-graticule.
- **Area:** core / geo
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-geo-8` — `core-geo/`

`transform.ts:608-615` (`extentMajor`/`extentMinor` take the corners as given), `:632` (`typeof v === 'number'`), `:579-582` with `row-keys.ts:227-228` (`numberRange` refuses a zero step).

- **Observed (`spec2.mjs`, length of the projected graticule path):**

  | Parameter | Vega | Aster |
  |---|---|---|
  | `extent [[180,80],[-180,-80]]` | 38 908 chars | 0 (nothing drawn) |
  | `extentMajor [[90,45],[-90,-45]]` | 39 826 | 38 840 (different lines) |
  | `extentMinor [[90,45],[-90,-45]]` | 12 249 | 2 167 |
  | `precision: 0` | 5 011 | throws `[aster] limit exceeded: range length Infinity > 2147483647` |
  | `precision: '45'` | 8 985 | 41 007 (string ignored, default 2.5 used) |

  The other ten variants are identical (defaults, zero/negative/NaN steps, string extents, signals, one-element step, 0.5° steps).
- **Why.** d3's `extentMajor`/`extentMinor` coerce with `+` and swap when `x0 > x1` or `y0 > y1`. d3's `precision` coerces with `+`. d3's `range` with a zero step is empty.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction.** Port the two swaps and the coercions; give the graticule's `range` calls d3's zero-step result. The function header claims "reproduced operation-for-operation".

#### C158 — Medium — no-Worker fallback during add-on load reorders or drops a parked push

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:208-212`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #199 (dba96b7). Fixed: the no-Worker fallback drains the same ordered queue into its stream when it is created, and flush() sends the queue; covered by the model test's no-Worker runs (planted reorder caught).
- **Area:** react / hooks, streams, workers
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-7` — `react-hooks/`

`src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:208-212`, `:350-357`, `:390-396`.
- **Cause:** while `loadAddons` is in flight, pushes are parked. Once the local stream exists, later pushes bypass the buffer, and the next automatic flush applies the parked batch after them. An explicit `flush()` calls `sendFlush([])`, which empties the buffer unsent.
- **Observed** (`t09-fallback-order.mjs`, geo spec):
  ```
  mount effect: scene null | push(OLDER snapshot, 2 rows) -> true | depth() 1
  stream ready: scene rows 1 | depth() 0
  push(NEWER snapshot, 3 rows) -> true
  scene rows now 2 (expected 3: the newer snapshot)
  ```
  With the `flush` argument the parked snapshot is silently lost.
- The same parking occurs when local stream creation failed (`:280-283`), by trace.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** one ordered queue; drain parked batches into the new stream first; make `flush()` send the buffer.

#### C159 — Medium — `close()` leaves `scheduled` (rAF) and `paused` set for a rebuilt stream

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/useChartStream.ts:206-219`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #199 (dba96b7). Fixed: cancelling an animation frame clears the scheduled flag in both hooks, and close() closes the stream without pausing the hook; lifecycle test on every path, microtask and raf.
- **Area:** react / hooks, streams, workers
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-8` — `react-hooks/`

`src/useChartStream.ts:206-219`, `:238-244`; `src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:238-252`, `:409-424`, `:262`.
- **Cause:** `scheduled.current` resets only inside `run`; `close()` and the unmount cleanup cancel the frame, so it stays `true`. `close()` also sets paused, and a new stream after a spec change inherits it.
- **Observed A** (`t08-misc.mjs raf-stuck`: `raf`, `close()` with a frame pending, new spec, `resume()`, push 2 rows): both hooks show `push -> true | paused false | rows drawn 200 ms later 1 (expected 3)`. The `microtask` control draws 3.
- **Observed B** (`t08-misc.mjs close-sticky-pause`): `push -> true | paused true | rows drawn 100 ms later 1` in both hooks.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** clear `scheduled` wherever the frame is cancelled; reset both latches when a stream is created.

#### C160 — Medium — one throw from `post` on the queued path silences the worker for good

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/worker.ts:716-724`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #199 (dba96b7). Fixed: the worker dispatcher answers a request whose post throws with a wire error for that id and never rejects its chain; generated test over message shapes and failing positions (fresh module registry per case, queued path), also executes worker-entry.
- **Area:** react / hooks, streams, workers (also categories 5)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-9` — `react-hooks/`

`src/worker.ts:716-724`.
- **Cause:** `tail = tail.then(...)` has no catch. A throwing `post` rejects `tail`; callbacks queued behind it never run, `waiting` never returns to 0, and every later message queues behind the rejection. No `error` event reaches the main thread.
- **Observed** (`t03-dispatcher-poison.mjs`; message 1 needs geo and its `post` throws a simulated `DataCloneError`, message 2 arrives during the import, 3 and 4 later): `responses after the failed post: []`, expected `[2,3,4]`.
- **Reachability:** `worker-entry.ts:9` posts with `scope.postMessage`. I found no built-in spec with a non-cloneable response (`t04-clone-probe.mjs`), so today it takes a host-registered expression function or provider that returns a function.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN (simulated throw).
- **Direction:** `tail.then(job).catch(...)`, and answer the id with a wire error when `post` fails.

#### C168 — Medium — A one-dimensional view in a composition nested in another composition loses its grid

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:2909`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)

- **Area:** vl / composition

**A one-dimensional view in a composition nested in another composition loses its grid.**
- `axisSizeSignals` adds `{name: "height", update: hName}` only when `update !== name`.

- CONFIRMED-RUN, `t11-misc.mjs` `repeat-in-concat` and `t12.mjs`.

#### C169 — Medium — Every quantitative field gets a `toNumber` formula; vega-lite emits one only for `min`/`max` aggregates

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4226-4272`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: toNumber only for min/max and a path mark's quantitative dimension (getImplicitFromEncoding), valid predicates parse nothing; comparator now sees casts (C220); 78 specs fail with the old cast
- **Area:** vl / scales, stacking, guides (also categories 3, 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c2-3` — `vl-c2/`

**Every quantitative field gets a `toNumber` formula; vega-lite emits one only for `min`/`max` aggregates.** This is an undocumented deviation.
- **Empty string** (an empty CSV cell when `format.parse` names only the date column, or inline `""`): ours `toNumber('')` → `null` → row filtered. vega-lite keeps the row and plots it at 0. On a 5-row point chart, ours has 4 rows in `data_0` and vega-lite 5.
- **Non-numeric string in an aggregate:** ours draws the group where vega-lite's mean is NaN and the group is dropped (`line color agg`, `line nominal sort -y`: ours 4 points, vega-lite 3).
- **Not self-consistent:** `skipCasts` (`:4226-4233`) turns the casts off for bar/area with a discrete dimension, so the same rows draw as a bar and vanish as a point.
- **`data.format.parse: {e:'string'}`:** vega-lite honours it with a `toString` formula; ours emits `toNumber` instead.
- The comment "the oracle emits them around impute/stack pipelines" is false for vega-lite 6.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `casts.mjs` (rows printed for both), `t6-paths.mjs`.
Direction: follow `ParseNode.makeWithAncestors` (number only for min/max, date for temporal, explicit `format.parse` wins). Otherwise document the deviation in ARCHITECTURE.md and make bar/area agree with the rest.

#### C170 — Medium — Config assembly loses or misroutes title, font, style and autosize

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:3711-3750`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: config.title routed as extractTitleConfig (subtitle* stay in config.title, limit/angle are the title's, dx/dy reach the subtitle), font under title, styles merged by layer, composite autosize
- **Area:** vl / scales, stacking, guides (also categories 3)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c2-4` — `vl-c2/`

**Config assembly loses or misroutes title, font, style and autosize.** Each sub-case is CONFIRMED-RUN in `t20-config.mjs` (run with the case name to print both configs).
- **a. Subtitle props.** `config.title.subtitle*` (`subtitleColor`, `subtitleFontSize`, `subtitleFont`, `subtitlePadding`, …) are written into `style['group-title']` (`:3732-3736`), where Vega ignores them. vega-lite keeps them in `config.title`. Subtitle styling is silently lost. `limit`/`angle` also go to group-title (vega-lite: `limit` to group-subtitle only, no `angle`), and `dx`/`dy` miss group-subtitle.
- **b. Font order.** `config.font` overwrites `config.title.font` (`:3741-3745` runs after the title block): ours `serif`, vega-lite `monospace`.
- **c. Style replace.** A user `config.style[name]` replaces the derived style of that name (`:3747`); vega-lite merges.
  - `config.view.fill` + `config.style.cell` loses the fill.
  - `config.font` + `config.style['guide-label']` loses the font on axis labels.
  - `config.title.color` + `config.style['group-title']` loses the colour.
- **d. Autosize.** `config.autosize` is dropped: ours `config` undefined, vega-lite `{"autosize":"fit"}`, SVG 120 vs 208 wide.

Direction: merge at `:3747`, apply font before title, route `subtitle*` to `config.title`, forward `autosize`.

#### C171 — Medium — `config.scale` overrides what the encoding says, and expression values are coerced to booleans

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:3754-3767`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: config.scale.zero is the position default only (never an override), clamp/round/xReverse keep {expr}, xReverse any x type and undone by a descending sort, continuousPadding reaches bars/bins; config.scale.nice and {expr} zero are refused by the schema check (not Vega-Lite properties)
- **Area:** vl / scales, stacking, guides (also categories 3)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c2-5` — `vl-c2/`

**`config.scale` overrides what the encoding says, and expression values are coerced to booleans.**
- **a. `zero`.** `config.scale.zero` is written over every continuous x/y scale (`:3765`), including an explicit `scale.zero` and a custom domain.
  - `x:{scale:{zero:false}}` + `config.scale.zero:true` → ours `zero:true`, vega-lite `false`.
  - `x:{scale:{domain:[20,100]}}` + `config.scale.zero:true` → ours `zero:true` (domain widened to 0), vega-lite `false`.
- **b. `nice`.** `config.scale.nice` is not a vega-lite config property (absent from `ScaleConfig` in the installed schema; vega-lite ignores it). `validate.ts:427` accepts it and `:3764` applies it over an explicit `scale.nice:true` and onto binned scales, which must have none.
- **c. Expressions.** `Boolean(sc[k])` (`:3760`, `:3765`) turns `config.scale.clamp:{expr:'flag'}` and `zero:{expr:'flag'}` with `flag=false` into `true`; vega-lite emits `{signal:'flag'}`. `config.scale.xReverse:{expr}` is ignored by the `=== true` test at `:5050`.
- **d. `xReverse` + descending.** With `xReverse:true` and `sort:'descending'` on a continuous x, vega-lite un-reverses (`reverse:false`); ours gives `reverse:true`.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `t1-scales.mjs` ("cfg zero…", "cfg nice…"), `t19.mjs`, `t18-expr.mjs`.

#### C174 — Medium — Expression-valued scale properties that the schema allows are dropped or produce invalid Vega

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:5106-5113`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: {expr} band paddings, continuous padding, scheme and config.scale paddings compile to vega-lite's signals (paddingText/halfPadding)
- **Area:** vl / scales, stacking, guides (also categories 4)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c2-8` — `vl-c2/`

**Expression-valued scale properties that the schema allows are dropped or produce invalid Vega.**
- **Band paddings as `{expr}`.** `:5112` computes `userInner / 2` → `NaN` (emitted as `paddingOuter:null`). The step-size signal stringifies the object: `bandspace(domain('x').length, [object Object], NaN) * x_step`, which real Vega rejects with "Expression parse error". That signal is built at `:1387` (vl-c1). vega-lite emits `bandspace(…, p, p/2)`. Also reachable via `config.scale.bandPaddingInner:{expr}`.
- **Continuous `scale.padding:{expr}`.** `:5055` wants a number and `:5125` skips `padding` in the forward loop, so it is silently dropped.
- **`scale.scheme:{expr}`.** `schemeRange` reads it as `{name,…rest}` → `range:{"expr":"'viridis'"}` → Vega "Unsupported range type".

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `t18-expr.mjs`, `t19.mjs`.

#### C192 — Medium — the canonicalizer's painted boxes are not conservative

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/normalize.ts:943-947`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (ec8a395). Fixed: arc, S/T curve and multi-line text boxes are conservative; five planted pairs that passed as EQUAL now differ and the small cases still swap.
- **Area:** conformance / harness
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `harness-src-6` — `harness-src/`

`src/normalize.ts:943-947` (arc), `:954-970` (text)

- **Mechanism.** An arc segment is bounded as `endpoint ± r`, but an arc over 180° (or one with auto-scaled radii) reaches up to `2r` from its endpoint. Multi-line text is bounded at 1.6 em per extra line regardless of the tspans' `dy`. Records with disjoint boxes may swap in `paintOrderNormalForm`.
- **Observed** (`normalize-blind.mts`):
  - A1: a 270° wedge covering a rect, in both orders: `EQUAL (not flagged)`.
  - A2: two-line text with `dy=60` at font-size 10 over a rect, in both orders: `EQUAL`.
  - Control C1 (swapped overlapping rects): `DIFFER`.
- **Reach.** A pie or donut with one wedge over 180° and labels or symbols on it; `lineHeight` above 1.6 × `fontSize`. This is the zindex / mark-order class of defect.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** bound an arc by its true extrema or a `2·max(rx,ry)` disc; bound text by the tspans' own offsets; add both cases to `normalize.test.ts`.

#### C193 — Medium — `conformance:diff` counts any throw as "skipped"

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/diff.ts:228-238`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (21c7987). Fixed: conformance:diff runs each side on its own (one-sided throw or differing errors is a difference, nothing is skipped) and compares the accessibility structure; 941 changesets and 7346 steps compared, 0 skipped.
- **Area:** conformance / harness
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `harness-src-8` — `harness-src/`

`src/diff.ts:228-238,250`; `:153`; `src/diff-signals.ts:176-180`

- **Mechanism.** The per-datum phase wraps compile, first evaluate, incremental evaluate and fresh evaluate in one `try { … } catch { skipped++ }`. An incremental path that throws where the fresh one renders is a skip, with exit 0 and no ceiling. The row phase beside it does this correctly (`attempt` / "only the session threw").
- **Structure is not compared.** The Aster-vs-Aster phases compare `root` and `records` but never `structure`, so a stale `aria-label`, `role` or class on a kept node is not a mismatch in the per-datum and row phases.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE.
- **Direction:** reuse `attempt`; put a ceiling on skipped (TESTING.md:166 says 0 today); compare `structure`.

#### C194 — Medium — The canvas tolerance passes a missing 5×5 mark, a recoloured 6×6 mark and a 7×7 mark moved by a pixel; nothing asks for ink

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/canvas-pixels.mts:11`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #204 (860e237). Fixed: one comparePixels for every pixel gate adds an 8x8 locality limit measured per browser (Chromium 7, Firefox 6, WebKit 13) and an ink-on-both-sides rule; blank-vs-blank is counted apart, and network images are served so image marks are compared offline.
- **Area:** conformance / scripts and gates (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `harness-scripts-4` — `harness-scripts/`

**The canvas tolerance passes a missing 5×5 mark, a recoloured 6×6 mark and a 7×7 mark moved by a pixel; nothing asks for ink.**
- `CANVAS_LIMITS = { pixel: 48, ratio: 0.0005, mean: 0.05 }`. On a 410×310 canvas that allows 63 pixels over the limit and a summed difference of 25,420.
- `pixel-tolerance.mjs`, using the gate's own `pixelDiff`:
```
PASSES  a 5x5 steelblue mark present in vega, missing in Aster (white background)
PASSES  a 6x6 mark recoloured lightgray -> firebrick (a selection highlight not applied)
PASSES  a 7x7 mark moved by 1px
fails   a 7x7 black mark missing / a 60x1 black rule missing / a 20x20 mark missing
blank vs blank: null   hasInk: false
```
- `browser-canvas-parity.mts:257-258` says "a mark one pixel off is a difference"; for a small mark it is not.
- The same limits judge every canvas step of `browser-vl-selections.mts` (`:955-959`) and the animation frames of `browser-signals.mts:1029`. Signals and stores are compared exactly there and the SVG renderer strictly, so selection logic is covered; the canvas paint of a small change is not.
- The corpus phase never calls `hasInk`. An image mark whose URL fails resolves to `null` on both sides (`:280`), so offline every image entry is blank against blank.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** add a locality test (fail when any 8×8 window has more than N differing pixels) and require ink on both sides.

#### C195 — Medium — Phases 2–4 of the canvas gate count the path they exist to test but never require it to be taken

**Phases 2–4 of the canvas gate count the path they exist to test but never require it to be taken.**
- Append oracle: `if (snap != null && renderSceneToCanvasAppend(...)) { how = 'append path'; appended++ } else fullPaint(live, st.scene)`.
- If `renderSceneToCanvasAppend` starts always returning `false`, every step compares one Aster full repaint with another. It prints `120 scenarios, 0 append-path frames, 0 failing` and exits 0.

- Contrast `browser-intersect.mts:180-181` and `browser-signals.mts:1070`, which floor their counters.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE.

**Two React-gate assertions cannot fail for the reason they name.**
- `:455` checks `tip2.includes('cat') && tip2.includes('c')`. `'cat'` contains `'c'`, so any datum's tooltip passes. This is the check that the pointer maps correctly under `max-width` / a CSS transform for dense marks.
- `:521-531` ("capture must keep the gesture alive") is followed only by `countAfterDrag >= 3`. That count includes the two wheel zooms (`:515`, `:520`) plus the in-element drag steps, so a lost pointer capture still passes. The header (`:14`) lists pointer capture.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE.
- **Direction:** assert the datum exactly; require the view-change count to grow during the out-of-element leg.

#### C197 — Medium — the nightly browser floors pass on missing measurements, and are loose where they do bite

- **Location:** `packages/benchmarks/src/browser-floors.ts:52-57`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (2fe9114,13b00fa). every field validated, partners/rows required, faster-vega comparison, heap nightly; 227 tests
- **Area:** tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks (also categories 5)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tooling-7` — `tooling/`

`packages/benchmarks/src/browser-floors.ts:52-57, 62, 69-70, 113-134`; `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:96`

- **Missing measurement passes.** `checkStreamBench` compares in the positive form (`r.updates < …`, `perAppend > …`, `dense.nodes > …`), so `undefined` and `NaN` never fail. `checkBrowserBench` guards most fields with `num()` but not `fps.longShare`. The rows are built in an untyped `.mjs` driver from an in-page API, in a directory that is not typechecked (C303 (tooling-4)), so a renamed field is a real path.
- **Skipped comparisons.** A vega row with `frames: 0` is "not found" and the aster-vs-vega comparison is skipped (:122-124). The dense comparison is skipped when no per-item row exists (:130-131). A run with only canvas rows passes with no SVG check.
- **Loose where it bites.** Mount and update are compared with the slower of the two Vega embeds at 1.5x (:52-57). `reactVega` re-embeds on every update, so it is a soft baseline. With the documented bar numbers (aster 8.0 ms; react-vega 16.75, embed hook 8.3), aster's update can become 3.1x slower and pass; scatter 3.4x. Only `aster` is compared, never `asterDom` (moot today: C304 (tooling-6)). At 100,000 points the only append floor is "2 in 3 s" against a measured 18-19.
- **Dead floor.** `maxRetainedHeapMB` runs only with `--memory=true`. The nightly passes `--memory=false`, and `bench:memory` is in no workflow, so no automated run checks a leak.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-RUN: `$S/floors-repro.mjs` imports `browser-floors.ts` and feeds it rows. All of these return `[]` (pass): `updates undefined`; `updates/mutations/nodes NaN`; the 100k dense pair with `nodes/median/updates` undefined; a vega row with 0 frames next to an aster row at 500 ms median; canvas-only; "bar, aster update 3.1x slower (25 ms)"; "scatter, aster update 3.4x slower"; `fps longShare undefined / NaN`; "asterDom 10x slower than aster".
- **Direction.** Validate every row first (`Number.isFinite` on each field, else fail); fail when an expected comparison partner is missing; compare with the faster Vega embed or a stored aster baseline ratio; run the heap floor nightly. `browser-floors.test.ts` has no case for a missing field in a stream row.

#### C198 — Medium — Product defect shared by legacy and new: a rect with a numeric-string `width`/`height` is drawn zero-size (Vega draws it), while the hit index still treats it as full-size

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/geometry.ts:670-671`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #200 (2ce7c3b). rectData reads +(width || 0) as vega's rectangle builder: SVG text equals vega's for '30', '25px' and Infinity widths, and the hit index takes no pointer where nothing is drawn.
- **Area:** tests / core (legacy copies II … path)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core4-3` — `tests-core4/`

- New: `packages/core/src/geometry.ts:670-671` (`if (!Number.isFinite(w)) w = 0`).
- Legacy: `packages/core/src/legacy-render.testlib.ts:678-679`, identical.
- Not in the first-pass report (grepped `isFinite(w)`, "numeric string").

`Number.isFinite("30")` is false, so the size becomes 0. Vega's rectangle path coerces with unary plus (d3-path `rect`: `h${w = +w}`). The comment at `legacy-render.testlib.ts:675-677` justifies the guard for NaN only.

Scenario (`S/h2-string-width.mjs`): data `[{x:10,y:10,w:'30',h:'20'}, …]`, rect with `width:{field:'w'}`, `height:{field:'h'}`, `autosize:'pad'`.

```
aster dist renderSpec: 6025x4050 | M10,10h0v0h0Z | M60,40h0v0h0Z
vega                 : 6025x4050 | M10,10h30v20h-30Z | M60,40h25v50h-25Z
pick(25,20) legacy true new true
diffScene []
```

- The bars are silently absent from the drawing, yet `pick` reports a rect at a point where nothing is painted (`hit.ts` reads `+(item.width) || 0`).
- The bounds, and so the 6025×4050 view, agree with Vega: Vega string-concatenates there too.
- `S/h-string-width.mjs` shows the same with `{value: '30'}`.
- `S/i-wild-vs-vega.mjs` shows the same guard turns `width: 1/0` into `h0v10h0Z`, a 10 px stroked line. Vega writes `hInfinity`, which draws nothing. That part is trivial.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

Direction: coerce as Vega does (`+w || 0`). The random scenes do feed numeric strings (`geometry-scenes.testlib.ts:31`); both sides agree on 0, so the differential cannot notice.

#### C199 — Medium — `okResult` passes when the attack child crashes, so the "still renders" halves of the ceiling tests cannot fail on an out-of-memory

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/limits-attacks.test.ts:392-395`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #195 (8c00693). Fixed: attack() reports reported/exitCode/signal and expectReturned requires a report, exit 0 and the value, so a child that aborted on the heap cap no longer passes as 'still renders'.
- **Area:** tests / core (limits, loaders, locale, oracle vectors)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core5-2` — `tests-core5/`

`packages/core/src/limits-attacks.test.ts:392-395` (used at :414-415, :427-428, :443-444, :462-463, :480, :495-496); `packages/core/src/attack.testkit.ts:83-85`.

- When the child prints no `RESULT` line, the kit returns `{ threw: null, ms: Infinity, cpuMs: Infinity }` with `killed: false`.
- `okResult` asserts only `killed === false` and `threw === null`, so a child that aborted with a fatal OOM passes. It never looks at `r.value`, although `run` at :493-494 returns `…length > 0`.
- **Proof:** `okresult-vacuous.mjs` copies the kit's parsing and runs a child that exhausts its heap. Output: `child exit null SIGABRT … okResult passes on a child that crashed: true`.
- **Why it matters now:** `ok-cases.mjs axis150000` (the case at :428) renders 47 987 503 characters with `heapUsed 466 MB` under the kit's 512 MB cap. A small regression there becomes a crash the suite reports as green.
- `expectLimit` does fail on a crash, though with the message "no error thrown (the attack succeeded)".
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `okresult-vacuous.mjs`, `ok-cases.mjs`.
- **Direction:** have `attack()` report `exitCode`, `signal` and a `crashed` flag when there is no `RESULT` line. `okResult` should require a `RESULT` line and, where the body returns one, the value.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `tests-core1-12`, scripts `tests-core1/`, CONFIRMED (traced); `attack.testkit.ts`: a child that dies before reporting has `threw: null`, the same as a clean return):

`packages/core/src/attack.testkit.ts:83-85`.

- With no `RESULT` line (a 512 MB out-of-memory abort, a syntax error in the body), the result is `{ threw: null, ms: Infinity, cpuMs: Infinity }` and `killed: false`.
- `expectLimit` reports it as "no error thrown (the attack succeeded)", which misleads but still fails.
- A caller that asserts only `r.threw` is null would pass on a crash. The one such caller, `transform-safety.test.ts:190`, also checks `r.value`, so nothing is wrong today.
- The exit code and signal are not captured.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE.**
- **Direction.** Add `exitCode` / `signal` and a `reported: boolean`, and have `expectLimit` say "child died without reporting".

#### C201 — Medium — "a clock that jumps forward does not make an interval fire a burst" never jumps, and with a real jump the interval does burst

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/timer.test.ts:108-119`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #190 (7f0bf5e). Timer tests now jump the clock: frame-first stall is caught up at frame rate as d3-timer (63/62/21), the background-tab case where the 1 s poll fires first rebases the schedule; header worded as what happens; planted skew/poll removal fails.
- **Area:** tests / core (text … url)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core7-1` — `tests-core7/`

`packages/core/src/timer.test.ts:108-119`; `packages/core/src/timer.testlib.ts:56-59`; `packages/core/src/timer.ts:11-12, 187-194`

- The test calls `clock.advance(10_000)`. `advance` runs job by job (`timer.testlib.ts:68-81`), so the 100 ms interval ticks 100 times normally. Nothing stalls.
- `FakeClock.jump()` exists for exactly this ("a stall (a suspended tab)") and has 0 call sites in `packages/`.
- With a real stall (`jump(10_000)`, then run what is due), `timer.mjs` prints:
  - interval 500 ms: 1 tick at once, then 21 in the next second (no burst would be about 2);
  - interval 100 ms: 1, then 62 (about 10);
  - interval 20 ms: 1, then 62 (about 50).
- The test's own bound (`n - before <= 11`) would fail if it jumped.
- Real d3-timer 3.0.1 driven by the same fake clock gives 21 / 63 / 62 (`d3timer.mjs`). So the product matches upstream; it is the test title that is false.
- The header claim at `timer.ts:11-12` ("a 1 s poll notices a clock that jumped (a suspended laptop) and shifts the schedule by the jump instead of firing a burst") holds only when the poll's `setInterval` fires before the frame. If the frame fires first, `wake` resets `lastReading` (`timer.ts:174`) and the poll sees no gap.
- `checkJump` and `skew` have no test at all.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`timer.mjs`, `d3timer.mjs`).

Direction: rewrite the test with `jump()`. Add a case where the poll fires first (frames stopped, intervals running — the background-tab case the poll is for). Word the title and the header comment as what actually happens: catch-up at frame rate, as d3.

#### C202 — Medium — the `dsvFormatRow` vectors are recorded double-wrapped, and one pins a localised `Date#toString()`

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:837-847`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #190 (f34283d). dsvFormatRow vectors are real rows (null, undefined, Date as ISO, newlines, empty row); Date#toString and the double wrapping are gone; regenerated with gen-vectors.mjs; invalid-Date NaN now survives the codec (was null -> epoch).
- **Area:** tests / core (text … url)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core7-2` — `tests-core7/`

`packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:837-847`; `packages/core/testdata/vectors/d3-dsv.json:548-587`; replayed at `packages/core/src/oracle-vectors.test.ts:147`

- Each case is written as `[[1, 'x,y']]` and passed whole to `formatRow`. That is a row of one cell whose value is an array.
- Recorded wants:
  - `"\"1,x,y\""` — a real two-cell row gives `1,"x,y"`;
  - `"\"say \"\"\"\"hi\"\"\"\",\""`;
  - `"\"Mon Jan 01 2024 00:00:00 GMT+0000 (Coordinated Universal Time),z\""` — `Array#join` over a Date, not d3-dsv's ISO date formatting (`2024-01-01,z`).
- Consequences:
  - quoting between cells, null cells and Date cells of `formatRow` are pinned nowhere;
  - the third want depends on the host locale: under `LANG=de_DE.UTF-8` the port returns `(Koordinierte Weltzeit)` and the vector fails (`dsvlang.mjs`: en_US passes, de_DE fails).
- The port itself is right: `dsvrow.mjs` compares it with d3-dsv on 9 real rows, 4 parses including `.columns`, and 3 `format` calls — all the same.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`dsvrow.mjs`, `dsvlang.mjs`).

Direction: record `call(formatRow, [row])` with `row` as the row; add null, undefined and Date cells; pin `LANG`/`LC_ALL` or avoid `Date#toString` in vectors.

Topology fixtures are valid (two squares, a hole, a MultiPolygon), the quantized form is derived from the absolute one and the generator refuses unclosed rings or unequal decodes; interior (a!==b) and exterior (a===b) both recorded, duplicate topoMeshOuter dropped.

#### C206 — Medium — canonicalizer collapses NBSP and all Unicode spaces as if they were XML whitespace

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/normalize.ts:469-470`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** tests / conformance differentials II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confsrc2-1` — `tests-confsrc2/`

`packages/conformance/src/normalize.ts:469-470` (`decodeEntities(c).replace(/\s+/g, ' ')`), `:484` (`.trim()`); not pinned in `normalize.test.ts`.

- **Mechanism.** JS `\s` matches U+00A0, U+202F, U+2000–200A, U+3000, U+FEFF. SVG's default whitespace handling collapses only space, tab, CR and LF. The header's N-whitespace ("collapsed as SVG's default xml:space does") is therefore wider than what a browser does.
- **Observed** (`$S/nbsp.mts`): all `EQUAL` — `"1 000"` vs `"1 000"`, `"1   000"` vs `"1 000"`, `"1 000"` vs `"1 000"`, `"a  b"` vs `"a b"`, `"　x"` vs `"x"`, `"a﻿b"` vs `"a b"`, `"&#160;&#160;x"` vs `"x"`.
- **Through real Vega** (`$S/nod-and-space.mts`): text marks `"a b"` and `"a b"` give 0 diffs.
- **Expected.** A run of NBSPs is not collapsed and a leading NBSP is not trimmed by a browser, so these are different pictures.
- **Reach.** Every `canonicalizeSvg` differential (corpus gate, sweeps, all `*-vs-vega` files). An engine that turns a locale's NBSP group separator into a space, or trims or collapses NBSP padding, is not flagged.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** collapse only `[ \t\r\n]+`; add the pairs above to `PLANTED`.

#### C208 — Medium — raster fixtures: loose hand tolerances and a self-recorded baseline that accepts large disagreement (adds to C191 (harness-src-5))

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/raster-vs-chromium.test.ts:43-47`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** tests / conformance differentials II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confsrc2-4` — `tests-confsrc2/`

`packages/conformance/src/raster-vs-chromium.test.ts:43-47` (hand shapes), `:78-79` (ratchet); `packages/conformance/src/raster-fixtures.json`; `packages/conformance/scripts/raster-fixtures.mts:44-60`.

- **What is recorded from where** (`$S/raster-analysis.mts`, whole file analysed):
  - `browser`: "Chromium 151.0.7922.34".
  - `alpha`: 122 arrays (26 hand + 96 generated), from Chromium. All have length `w*h`, values 0–255, no orphan or missing names.
  - `baseline`: 96 `{mask, abs}` pairs, computed by Aster's own `AlphaCanvas` against that alpha at record time.
- **The ratchet is tight today.** 96/96 generated drawings sit exactly at baseline, so any regression fails.
- **What the baseline accepts:**

  | Drawing | Inked px | "Has any alpha" differs | Share | Max alpha diff |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | generated 79, stroked cubic w=0.5 | 34 | 11 | 32% | 92 |
  | generated 39, stroked cubic w=0.625 | 87 | 20 | 23% | 65 |
  | generated 46, stroke w=0.75 round bevel | 91 | 18 | 20% | 69 |
  | generated 95, stroked cubic w=0.5 | 71 | 10 | 14% | 87 |
  | generated 6, stroke w=4.25 square miter | 381 | 12 | 3% | 233 |

  - 25 of 96 generated drawings would fail the hand-shape tolerance.
  - "Has any alpha" is exactly what the label layout reads.
- **Hand-shape tolerance against planted faults:**
  - every alpha × 0.95: 25/26 still pass;
  - pixels with alpha < 8 dropped to 0: 24/26 pass;
  - 8 extra alpha-1 halo pixels beside the ink: 16/26 pass;
  - edge alpha ± 40: 0/26 pass, so that case is caught.
- **Actual margins.** "stroked circle" sits at nzdiff 8/8 and max 52/55; "closed stroked polygon" at ratio 0.9506 against a 0.94 floor.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:**
  - Record a per-shape baseline for the hand shapes too.
  - Treat the thin-stroke (w < 1) and square-cap-miter disagreement as a product lead in `raster.ts`.
  - State in "Deviations from Vega" that label avoidance of sub-pixel strokes differs from a browser canvas.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `w3-raster-c-1`, scripts `w3-raster-c/`, CONFIRMED (run); the generated-drawing ratchet is blind to the direction of disagreement (adds to `tests-confsrc2-4`)):

`packages/conformance/src/raster-vs-chromium.test.ts:75,78-79`; `packages/conformance/scripts/raster-fixtures.mts:53`

- **What the code does.** Line 75 is `if ((want[i] !== 0) !== (got[i] !== 0)) mask++`, and line 78 asserts `mask <= base.mask`. One counter sums two different errors:
  - the engine inks a pixel Chromium leaves empty (a halo: labels are kept slightly further away);
  - the engine leaves empty a pixel Chromium inks (a label may be placed over ink the browser shows).
- **Measured split, drawings 62–95** (`check.mts`): 167 differing pixels in total, 128 engine-only and 39 Chromium-only.
- **The two thin cubics run the other way.**

  | Drawing | Inked px | Chromium-only | Engine-only |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `generated 95 stroked cubic w=0.5` | 71 | 10 | 0 |
  | `generated 79 stroked cubic w=0.5` | 34 | 8 | 3 |

  `rows.mts` shows why: the engine puts the stroke in one pixel column (e.g. row 13 of drawing 95 is `0 132`) where Chromium spreads it over two or three (`13 113`, then `27 125 6`).
- **Scenario.** A `raster.ts` change that removes N halo pixels and drops N faint Chromium-inked pixels, with the summed alpha difference no larger, passes lines 78–79. By the test's own header ("a label is placed where no pixel under it has any alpha") that is a regression.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE** for the blindness (lines quoted above); **CONFIRMED-RUN** for the split. I did not plant such a change in `raster.ts`.
- **Direction:** record and ratchet the two counts separately in `baseline` (`maskMissing`, `maskExtra`), with the Chromium-only count the stricter one.

#### C209 — Medium — `dom-string-parity` does not exercise the path its header names, and its comparator is blind to mixed content

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/dom-string-parity.test.mts:5-9`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** tests / conformance generators and case tables II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confscripts2-2` — `tests-confscripts2/`

`packages/conformance/scripts/dom-string-parity.test.mts:5-9, 33-37, 89-93`

- **Header vs code.** The header says the motivating bug was "the first `patchSceneDom` over a string-rendered `<svg>` rewrote attributes". The test patches an empty element instead:
  `const patched = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'svg'); patchSceneDom(patched, scene)`
  The inline comment calls this "what `<Chart>` does after its first string mount". No case sets `innerHTML = renderSceneToSvg(scene)` and then patches, and no case patches with a second scene. C136 (core-render-7) lives exactly there (no `LAST` entry, element came from markup).
- **Comparator.** `canon` records text only for elements without element children:
  `return { tag, attrs, kids, ...(kids.length === 0 ? { text: el.textContent ?? '' } : {}) }`
  A text node beside `<tspan>` children is never compared.
- **Proof** (`dom-parity-blind.mjs`, the test's `canon`/`firstDiff` copied verbatim, jsdom):
  - Planted `<text>STRAY<tspan>one</tspan><tspan>two</tspan></text>` against the same without `STRAY`: `firstDiff` → `null`.
  - The C136 (core-render-7) sequence (string-mount `'one'`, `patchSceneDom` to `'one|two'`): patched `<text>` is `#text(one) <tspan>one <tspan>two`, fresh is `<tspan>one <tspan>two`, and the test's `firstDiff(fresh, patched)` → `null`.
- So C136 (core-render-7) needs two fixes in this file before it can fail.
- **C550 (core-render-17)** (non-numeric `angle`): the comparator would see `rotate(a&quot;b)` against `rotate(a"b)`, but the pool is the 1063 valid corpus scenes, none with a non-numeric angle.
- Attribute namespaces (`setAttributeNS` vs `setAttribute`) are also not compared: `a.name` only.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction.** Compare `childNodes` (text nodes included), not `children`. Add a third arm that string-mounts and then patches with the same scene, and a small set of scene pairs (one line to several, item count changes) patched over a string mount. Add hostile attribute values (quotes, `<`, `&`) to the pool.

#### C216 — Medium — `vlx-hdr-label-expr` is inert in the oracle, and it is the only `labelExpr` in the corpus

#### C218 — Medium — `translatePathData` gives wrong or `NaN` output for valid SVG path strings

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/dom.ts:122-172`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #188 (a55f4f9). Fixed: translatePathData walks the engine's own path reader (vega's grammar), a first m is absolute, packed flags and .5.5 are read right; 2000 generated paths against vega pathRender.
- **Area:** leftovers / budgets, declarations, demo data, gallery lists
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gaps-misc-b-3` — `gaps-misc-b/`

`packages/core/src/dom.ts:122-172` (declaration `packages/core/dist/dom.d.ts:15-22`; documented at `docs/API.md:618-619`)

| Input (dx 100, dy 200) | Output | Expected geometry |
|---|---|---|
| `m10,10l5,5` | `m10,10l5,5` (unchanged) | `moveTo(110,210) lineTo(115,215)` |
| `M1e1,.5.5-1` | `M110,NaN,99` | `moveTo(110,200.5) lineTo(100.5,199)` |
| `M.5.5L1-1` | `MNaNL101,199` | `moveTo(100.5,200.5) lineTo(101,199)` |
| `M0 0A5 5 0 01 5 5` | `M100,200A5,5,0,01,5,105` | arc endpoint `(105,205)` |

- **Causes.**
  - `:151` treats every lowercase command as relative, including a leading `m`, which SVG defines as absolute.
  - `:145` consumes any run of digits and dots as one number, so `.5.5` is one token.
  - The `A` case (`:157-160`) counts tokens, so compact flags `01` shift the endpoint index.
- **Reach.** The engine's own caller (`dom.ts:358`) passes normalised geometry and is unaffected: a dense symbol mark with shape `m-1,-1l2,0l0,2z` or `M-.5-.5.5-.5.5.5Z` batches correctly (`$S/dense-shape.mjs`). The defect is in the documented public export.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `$S/translate-path.mjs` compares with the engine's own `parsePathData` + `tracePath`.
- **Direction.** Implement it over `parsePathData`, or document the accepted subset and reject the rest.

#### C219 — Medium — `firstDiff` skips any left-hand object it has met before, so the force comparison is blind to a wrong link endpoint and to node row order

- 84 of the 220 generated force cases have a link force (`$S/force-hier-tally.mjs`), plus the two big-graph cases. The header's "bit for bit" claim does not cover which node a link resolves to, nor the order of linked nodes.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`$S/product-three.mjs`, item 3).
