#### C223 — Medium — `scale.rangeMin` / `rangeMax` are applied to scale types where vega-lite drops them

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4917-4922`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: rangeMin/rangeMax rows in scaleprops.ts consulted by withRangeLimits at every site; forwarding differential asks them on every channel and type (13 cells fail with the bug planted)
- **Area:** closure / conformance suites, line by line II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-conftest-b-1` — `w3-conftest-b/`

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4917-4922` (`withRangeLimits`) and `:5132-5138`; `packages/vl/src/scaleprops.ts:51-53` (no row for `rangeMin` / `rangeMax`, so `scalePropApplies` answers `true`). Pinned by `packages/conformance/test/vl-scale-props.test.ts:43-44` (`'*'` for all 16 scale types).
- **Scenario:** `{mark:'point', encoding:{x:…, y:…, opacity:{field:'q', type:'quantitative', scale:{type:'quantize', rangeMax:50}}}}`.
  - vega-lite 6.4.3: `"range":[0.3,0.8]`.
  - Aster: `"range":[0.3,50]`.
- **Same for:**
  - `strokeWidth` on a `threshold` scale with `rangeMin: 3`: vega-lite `[1,4]`, Aster `[3,4]`.
  - `size` on an explicit `ordinal` scale with `rangeMax: 50`: vega-lite `[4,361]`, Aster `[4,50]`.
  - `quantile` likewise; channels opacity, strokeWidth, angle, size (26 differing cells in `probe2.out`).
- **Controls that agree:** `linear` and `point` scales (the default for an ordinal field) honour the property in both compilers.
- **Reaches the picture:** with `rangeMax: 1` on a quantize opacity, vega-lite draws `opacity="0.8"` and Aster `opacity="1"`; the ordinal size case changes the SVG's width and height (391×146 against 380×142).
- **Why:** vega-lite only applies them when `scaleTypeSupportProperty(scaleType, 'rangeMin')` holds, i.e. continuous-to-continuous, `point` or `band` (`vega-lite/build/index.js:2566-2569`), and drops them silently otherwise. Aster's two sites have no scale-type condition:
  ```
  if (user.rangeMin !== undefined) r[0] = user.rangeMin
  if (user.rangeMax !== undefined) r[1] = user.rangeMax
  ```
- **Why no test sees it:** the pinned table records Aster's own answer; the vega-lite half's `ASK` (`vl-scale-props.test.ts:76-79`) and `vl-scale-forwarding.test.ts:21-24` (`PROPS`) both omit `rangeMin` / `rangeMax`. Corpus specs with these properties use linear and band scales only.
- **Not documented:** `packages/vl/README.md:80` lists `rangeMin` / `rangeMax` as supported, with no deviation noted.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `probe2.mjs` (output in `probe2.out`), `probe3.mjs`, `probe4.mjs`.
- **Direction:** add `rangeMin` / `rangeMax` rows to `scaleprops.ts` (`only(...CONTINUOUS, ...BANDED)`), consult them at both sites, correct the two pinned rows, and add both properties to `ASK` and `PROPS`.

#### C224 — Medium — an explicit `scale.reverse` on a discrete `theta` or `radius` is deleted

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:5272-5273`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #210 (53ccb41e,285c395e). Fixed: only the sort-derived reverse of a discrete theta/radius is dropped; theta/radius added to the forwarding differential
- **Area:** closure / conformance suites, line by line II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-conftest-b-2` — `w3-conftest-b/`

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:5272-5273`:
  ```
  // (a discrete scale is ordered by its domain's sort, not reversed)
  delete sc.reverse
  ```
- **Scenario:** `{mark:'arc', encoding:{theta:{field:'n', type:'nominal', scale:{reverse:true}}, color:{field:'n', type:'nominal'}}}` (default scale type; no explicit `type` needed).
  - vega-lite: `{"name":"theta","type":"band",…,"reverse":true}`.
  - Aster: the same scale without `reverse`.
- **Reaches the picture:** the first arc is `M-150,0A150,150,0,0,1,0,-150L0,0Z` from vega-lite and `M0,-150A150,150,0,0,1,150,0L0,0Z` from Aster.
- **Same for `radius`:** a nominal radius with `reverse: true` draws its first ring at radius 112.5–150 in vega-lite and 0–37.5 in Aster.
- **Control:** without `reverse` the two SVGs are identical.
- **Why:** the comment's rule is right for `sort: 'descending'` (vega-lite does not reverse a discrete scale for that) but the line also removes a `reverse` the spec wrote. Position and colour scales in the same file keep an explicit reverse (`:5050`, `:5316`, `:5342-5344`).
- **Why no test sees it:**
  - `vl-scale-props.test.ts:45` pins `reverse: '*'`, and its vega-lite half confirms the table says "applies" for band on theta — but it asserts on `scalePropApplies` only (`:112`), not on what the compiler emits.
  - `vl-scale-forwarding.test.ts:27-30` (`TYPES`) has no `theta` or `radius`.
  - `vl-polar-ranged.test.ts` has no `reverse` case.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `probe2.mjs` ("reverse on band", "reverse on point", theta and radius), `probe3.mjs`, `probe4.mjs`.
- **Direction:** drop only the sort-derived reverse on a discrete polar scale; keep `polarDef.scale.reverse`. Add `theta` / `radius` to `TYPES` in `vl-scale-forwarding.test.ts`.

#### C225 — Medium — A numeric top-level `width`/`height` beats the spec's own `width`/`height` signal `update`; vega/horizon-graph renders a wrong frame for any non-default `layers` given as `signals` (adds …

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:870`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega examples I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery1-1` — `gallery1/`

`packages/core/src/runtime.ts:870`, `:1003-1008`, `:1012`

- **Cause.** Line 870 takes the frame height from the top-level number: `let height = signed?.height ?? resolveSize(chart.height, viewOverride(chart, input, 'height'), signals)`. The `height` signal's resolved value is adopted only at line 1004: `if (height === DEFAULT_SIZE && hasHeightSignal && typeof ctx.signalParams.height === 'number')`, i.e. only when no top-level height was given (or it happens to be 500). Line 1012 does the same for `width`.
- **Vega.** The top-level number is just the signal's initial value, and the signal's `update` wins.
- **Relation to the report.** `C112 (core-rt1-8)` has the same sentinel for a host-supplied height. This is the spec-only trigger, with no host size at all.
- **Minimal scenario** (`height-split.mjs`):

  | spec | Vega 6.3.1 | Aster |
  |---|---|---|
  | `{width:100, height:100, signals:[{name:'height', update:'40'}]}` | svg 100x40 | svg 100x100 (signal reads 40) |
  | `{width:100, height:30, signals:[{name:'width', update:'40'}]}` | svg 40x30 | svg 100x30 |
  | same as row 1 without the top-level height (control) | 100x40 | 100x40 |

- **Official example.** `horizon-graph.vg.json` has `"height": 100` (line 5) and `{"name":"height","update":"floor(200 / layers)"}` (lines 14-16), with `layers` bound to a select and cycled by `pointerdown!`. At the default `layers=2` both are 100, so the gate cannot tell.
- **Observed** (`horizon-static.mjs`, also `sweep-binds.mts horizon-graph`), `renderSpec(spec, {signals:{layers:N}})` against a fresh Vega view with `view.signal('layers', N)`:

  | layers | Vega svg | Aster svg | Aster `height` signal |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 512x217 | 512x117 | 200 |
  | 3 | 512x83 | 512x117 | 66 |
  | 4 | 512x67 | 512x117 | 50 |

  The gate's canonical diff reports 42 differences per case; the axis ticks are at y=100 instead of 200/66/50 and the root size is wrong. The y scale spans `vheight`, and the group mark sizes and clips itself to the view height (`{"field":{"group":"height"}}`, `clip: true`), so by reading the spec `layers=1` shows only the upper half of the value range.
- **Why interaction hides it** (`horizon-interactive.mjs`, `horizon-setsignal.mjs`). A real `pointerdown`, or `binding.setSignal('layers', 1)`, gives the right 217. The event loop writes the derived value into the store (`{"layers":1,"height":200,"opacity":1}`), and a numeric `signals.height` is treated as explicit. `evaluateChart({signals:{layers:1}})` gives 512x117; `{layers:1, height:200}` gives 512x217.
- **Affected path.** `RuntimeInput.signals` on `renderSpec`/`evaluateChart`, for a chart whose controls live in the host. I did not mount `<Chart signals>`; whether it shares this path is traced no further than the type's doc.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** Not listed in "Deviations from Vega".
- **Direction.** Decide the frame from the size signal whenever the spec declares one with an `update`/`init`, not from `=== DEFAULT_SIZE`. This is the same fix `C112 (core-rt1-8)` asks for; make it cover the spec's own number.

#### C226 — Medium — `bar_axis_orient`: an `axis.orient: {expr}` does not drive the label alignment; with "top" the rotated labels point into the plot

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:5878-5892`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #209 (3bc5fbd). Fixed: defaultLabelAlign / Baseline take the orient as a signal; driven through the bound parameter for both axes and 6 label angles.
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega-Lite examples I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery3-2` — `gallery3/`

`packages/vl/src/compile.ts:5878-5892`

- **Cause:** `labelOrient` is taken only from a string orient: `isObject(def.axis) && typeof (def.axis as Record<string, unknown>).orient === 'string' ? … : … def.channel === 'x' ? 'bottom' : 'left'` (5878-5884). An `{expr}` orient falls back to `bottom`, and `defaultLabelAlign(270, 'bottom', 'x')` is frozen to `"right"` (5885-5887).
- **Compiled x axis:**
  - vega-lite: `"labelAngle":270,"labelBaseline":"middle","encode":{"labels":{"update":{"align":{"signal":"xAxisOrient !== \"bottom\" ? \"left\" : \"right\""}}}}`
  - Aster: `"labelAngle":270,"labelAlign":"right","labelBaseline":"middle"`
- **Scenario:** `bar_axis_orient.vl.json`, the user picks `top` in the example's own `xAxisOrient` select (both engines fresh with `xAxisOrient = "top"`).
  - Vega: 236×345; labels `text-anchor="start" transform="translate(9.5,-7) rotate(270) …"`, running up, above the axis.
  - Aster: 236×337; labels `text-anchor="end" transform="translate(10,-6.5) rotate(270) …"`, running down across the ticks into the bars.
  - 42 canonical diff lines. `bottom` and `yAxisOrient = "right"` pass.
- **Why the gate is green:** the default is `bottom`, where both agree. `axis.orient: {expr}` occurs in 0 of the 672 corpus `.vl.json` (`$S/corpus-has.mjs`), so no PR gate holds it either.
- **Prior mention:** the report's Appendix C has "`axis.orient:{expr}`: the grid axis keeps `bottom`, but the grid pixels are the same; not pursued". The label rule was not looked at.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `tsx one.mts bar_axis_orient '{"xAxisOrient":"top"}' --dump`. Found by the bound-param sweep `$S/probe-fresh.mts` (60 of 61 non-default values of every `bind` param in the range pass; this is the one) and by `$S/param-refs.mts` (`bar_axis_orient xAxisOrient axes: oracle 2 / aster 1`).
- **Direction:** when the orient is an expression, emit the align (and, for the angles where it depends on orient, the baseline) as vega-lite's signal expression. `defaultLabelAlignSignal` already does this for a signal angle and takes a constant orient.

#### C227 — Medium — A `select` bind whose options are arrays renders "undefined" seven times and writes `undefined`

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:190-192`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #198 (2d95532 f97895c). Fixed: select options of any type (arrays, null, booleans) are labelled as vega labels them and written back as themselves; differential vs vega-view bind (conformance/react-binds-vs-vega), with the a11y tree on and off, controls re-found before every edit, and Vega-Lite selections bound to inputs.
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega-Lite examples II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery4-3` — `gallery4/`

- **Where:** `packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:190-192`: `if (o != null && typeof o === 'object') { const rec = o …; return { value: rec.value, label: String(rec.label ?? rec.value) } }`. An array option is read as a `{value, label}` record.
- **Scenario:** `line_params.vl.json:31-35` and `rule_params.vl.json:17-21` bind `strokeDash` to `options: [[1,0],[8,8],[8,4],[4,4],[4,2],[2,1],[1,1]]`.
  - Vega: `<select name=strokeDash>` with options `"1,0","8,8",…`, value `"1,0"`. Choosing `8,8` gives `stroke-dasharray="8,8"`.
  - Aster: options `["", "undefined" ×7]`, blank selection. Choosing any option sets the signal to `undefined`; the line's dash goes from `1,0` to none. No dashed line can be produced.
- Not in `C295 (react-chart-14)`, which covers `bind.labels` and clearing a number input.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `CTRL=4 VAL=2 node react-interact.mjs lineparams` against `CTRL=4 VAL=1 node vega-interact.mjs lineparams`; `ruleparams` with `CTRL=6`.
- **Direction:** treat only plain non-array objects as `{value,label}` records; label an array as Vega does (`String(array)`).

#### C411 — Low — Mark boxes are approximations, though the module comment promises "a node lies exactly over the mark"

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/a11y.ts:118`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (85ce62a,fa54a10,abe8e82). Fixed: a11y boxes are the hit index's item bounds (boundItemOfKind), finite and >=2x2, path-mark items are their point, ids derive from the datum not the position.
- **Area:** core / SVG, DOM patcher, canvas, a11y (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-render-14` — `core-render/`

**Mark boxes are approximations, though the module comment promises "a node lies exactly over the mark".**

- Text uses `align ?? 'center'` (`render.ts:583` defaults to start) and width `length × fontSize × 0.6`, with no `dx/dy/angle/baseline`. `a11y1.mjs` 5: text at x=100 → box x 35, width 138.
- A NaN `width` gives a NaN box (`box 14 14 NaN 5`). A line mark is one 2×2 node per point.
- Mark ids are positional: inserting a row renames later nodes (`mark-0=A mark-1=B` → `mark-0=NEW mark-1=A mark-2=B`).
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.

#### C442 — Low — smaller compile differences found in passing

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:4268-4270`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** vl / validate, optimize, predicates
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-rest1-19` — `vl-rest1/`

- A param `value: {expr: "x"}` (a plain object value) is read as an expression; the same for `{expr}` in `lookup.default` and `impute.keyvals` (`misc.mjs`, `mut-trans.txt`).
- A typeless field with `scale: {type: "linear"}` on a bar with `cornerRadius`: vega-lite emits the `stack_group` clip group, Aster a flat rect (`notype.mjs`).
- An aggregate over a field named `valueOf` and a `timeUnit` transform over `constructor` fail in Aster's output where vega-lite's runs (`cls.mjs` B1–B8).
- A field with an escaped backslash (`x\\y`): the chart is 348 px wide vs 355; cause not investigated (`names.mjs` N13).

- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.

**Brief premise.** `embed.ts` is not a vega-embed counterpart. It only renames child-local names for composition; the package has no HTML, DOM, URL, theme or embed-option handling. `index.ts` exports `compile`, `compileUnit`, `VLCompileError` and type `VLSpec`; `compileUnit` is not in the README.

**Sound, said once.**
- **`predicate.ts`:** 68 of 68 runnable forms render identically to vega-lite — all comparisons, `range` with nulls, `oneOf`, `valid`, and/or/not, ExprRef operands, DateTime with names / utc / quarters, time-unit predicates. Values containing `"`, `\`, `'` are JSON-escaped. `range: {expr}` is refused by both.
- **`timeunit.ts`:** 108 units × 7 forms identical.
- **`scaletype.ts` / `scaleprops.ts`:** 162 of 162 combinations identical (`st.mjs`).
- **`expr-tokens.ts` / `renameExpr`:** across 74 expressions, every one vega's parser accepts is tokenised losslessly and renamed exactly where vega sees a free identifier (`tok.mjs`).
- **`names.ts`:** `a\.b` / `a_b` / `a b` / `a-b` do not collide; vega-lite emits duplicate signals for `a-b` vs `a+b`.
- **Generated-looking user dataset names** (`data_0`, `source_0`, `row_domain`) work in aster and fail in vega-lite.
- **Type-confusion sweep:** no raw `TypeError`.

#### C480 — Low — `intersect()` moves the box into every nested group without the bounds check Vega makes, so a group at a huge x loses later sibling hits

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/scene-intersect.ts:282-290`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #189 (fbefcc3,e33eb9a). Fixed: intersect() enters a nested group only if its mark-style bounds meet the box, as vega visitMark; differential vs vega.intersect over 14 magnitudes (8/29 failed before); CPU cold/warm neutral to faster
- **Area:** closure / gallery lists, small recorded vectors
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-lists-1` — `w3-lists/`

`packages/core/src/scene-intersect.ts:282-290` (the walk; `:288` recurses with no bounds test; the bounds test at `:262` only applies to `marktype: 'group'` marks, which `:252` says Aster scenes do not have).

- **Scenario:** a spec with marks `[group at x = 1e300 containing one rect, rect "sib" at 10..30]`, then `intersect([[5,5],[40,40]])`.
- **Observed:** Aster returns 0 hits; real Vega 6 returns 1 (the sibling rect). With the group listed last, both return 1. With group x = 0, both return 2.
- **Cause:** `box.translate(-x, -y)` … `box.translate(x, y)` is not an exact inverse for large x. Vega has the same pair, but its `visitMark` skips a group mark whose bounds miss the box, so it never translates here. Aster translates for every group.
- **Expected:** the same hits as Vega, independent of mark order.
- **Reach:** only degenerate coordinates (the error is about one ulp of x, so roughly |x| ≥ 1e16 before it shows). Hence Low.
- **Related:** this path is what the committed fixture `packages/core/testdata/intersect-stall-scene.json` actually exercises (see C762 (w3-lists-2)). There x is `Infinity`, the box comes back as `NaN 20.8 NaN 58.2`, and Vega also translates in that case (infinite bounds meet the box).

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `boxrestore.mjs`:
```
group x=1e+300 group first  aster hits=0  vega hits=1
group x=1e+300 group last   aster hits=1  vega hits=1
```
Direction: skip a group item whose bounds miss the box, as Vega does, and restore the box from saved values instead of translating back.

#### C481 — Low — the quarter-pixel test's pattern records that a grid repeats an earlier one, not which one

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/raster-vs-chromium.test.ts:54-59`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #189 (b7d2b6e). Fixed: pattern compares first-equal grid index (0,1,1,3,3,5,5,7) and the one-row shift; planted grid swap fails
- **Area:** closure / raster fixtures I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-raster-a-1` — `w3-raster-a/`

`packages/conformance/src/raster-vs-chromium.test.ts:54-59`

- **How it should behave.** The title says a circle "moves in steps of a quarter pixel … as in the browser", so the assertion should fail if the engine snaps a circle to the wrong quarter.
- **What it does.** `pattern` maps each of the eight grids to `'n'` or `'r'` by `grids.findIndex(equal) === i`. An `'r'` means "equal to some earlier grid".
- **Recorded truth.** In the fixture, cy=5.125 equals 5.250, 5.375 equals 5.500, 5.625 equals 5.750, and 5.875 is 5.000 moved down exactly one row. That gives `nnrnrnrn`.
- **Scenario.** An engine that draws cy=5.250 as cy=5.000 (snapping down, not up) yields grids `[g0,g1,g0,g3,g3,g5,g5,g7]`. Its pattern is also `nnrnrnrn`, and `expect(engine).toBe(chrome)` passes.
- **Mitigation that keeps this Low.** The per-shape test for `circle r=2.5 cy=5.250` catches the same planted grid: max alpha difference is 73 against the 55 ceiling. So the planted fault fails the suite today, only through the loose tolerance of C208 (tests-confsrc2-4), not through the test named for it.
- **Also unasserted.** The one-row shift between cy=5.000 and cy=5.875 is true in the data and in the engine, but nothing checks it.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `~/.cache/aster-review/audit-2026-11-22/w3-raster-a/pattern.mts` (output in `pattern.out`):
  - `chromium nnrnrnrn engine nnrnrnrn planted nnrnrnrn planted passes the pattern assertion: true`
  - `cy=5.250 drawn as cy=5.000 against the hand tolerance: { on: 28, nz: 2, allow: 8, max: 73, ratio: 1.0205 } passes: false`
- **Direction.** Compare the index of the first equal grid per position (e.g. `0,1,1,3,3,5,5,7`) between engine and Chromium, and assert the 5.875 grid is the 5.000 grid shifted one row.

#### C482 — Low — the engine's stroker puts a miter join on the vertices of a flattened curve, so a tight turn in a stroked curve grows a spike the browser does not draw; the baseline pins it

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/raster-stroke.ts:158-188`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** closure / raster fixtures II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-raster-b-1` — `w3-raster-b/`

`packages/core/src/raster-stroke.ts:158-188` (join loop over every vertex of the flattened polyline; miter branch `:174-185`); pinned by `packages/conformance/src/raster-fixtures.json` `baseline["generated 31 stroked cubic w=2.75"]` = `{mask:7, abs:1296}`.

- **Scenario:** drawing 31 is `moveTo(6.125,39.75)`, `bezierCurveTo(9.875,4.125, 2.375,68.25, 25.75,39.875)`, `lineWidth 2.75`, `lineCap round`, `lineJoin miter`, `miterLimit 4`, on a 32x75 canvas.
- **Observed:** Chromium's first inked row is row 27 (`89,179,66`). The engine inks rows 25 and 26 as well (`11,18` and `83,159`), where Chromium has nothing. That is 6 engine-only pixels, alpha up to 159, about 2 px beyond the browser's outline at the curve's sharp turn.
- **Expected:** no ink above row 27. A browser does not apply `lineJoin` inside a single curve segment.
- **Cause, checked by changing only the join:**

  | `lineJoin` | Engine's top inked row | Engine-only pixels | Max engine-only alpha |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `miter` (as recorded) | 25 | 6 | 159 |
  | `round` | 27 | 2 | 14 |
  | `bevel` | 28 | 2 | 14 |

  `outline()` applies the pen's join to every vertex of the flattened polyline, including the vertices flattening created (`const joins = closed ? n : n - 2`, then `if (join === 'miter') { … out.push(orient([[vx, vy], [ax, ay], [vx + mx * k, vy + my * k], [bx, by]])) }`).
- **Reach:** `packages/core/src/label-draw.ts:50-51` sets `pen.lineJoin = item.strokeJoin || 'miter'` and `pen.miterLimit = item.strokeMiterLimit ?? 4`. So the default pen for every stroked mark that `label` avoids is the affected one. The effect is conservative: a label is kept off a few pixels the mark does not cover. On this curve, raising `miterLimit` to 10 gave the same spike.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** Scripts: `~/.cache/aster-review/audit-2026-11-22/w3-raster-b/cusp.mts` (join swap against the fixture), `cusp2.mts` (same curve at `miterLimit` 4 and 10), `diff-grid.mts 31` (both grids and the difference).
- **Direction:** apply the join only at vertices the path itself has (between segments or curves), and join flattening vertices round or bevel. Then re-record the baseline; drawing 31's mask should fall from 7.

#### C231 — Medium — a partial publish cannot be finished by the workflow, and exact pins make version skew costly

- **Location:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:99-104`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (118b16a). idempotent publish script, RELEASE.md recovery and lockstep rationale (Q21)
- **Area:** tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks (also categories 5)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tooling-5` — `tooling/`

`.github/workflows/release.yml:99-104`; `packages/react/package.json:58-59`; `docs/RELEASE.md` (no recovery section)

- **Issue.** The publish step is `set -euo pipefail` over `core vl react`. If `vl` fails (registry 5xx, token scope, OTP), `core@X` is live and immutable. Re-running the job fails at `core` every time, so `vl` and `react` at X can never come from this workflow, and the tag cannot be reused. RELEASE.md has no step for this. The ways out are a manual `npm publish` outside the protected environment (no verified tarball, no provenance) or burning the version.
- **Compounding.** `@aster-charts/react` depends on `"@aster-charts/core": "workspace:*"`, which `pnpm pack` rewrites to the exact version. README:23-24 tells apps to install `@aster-charts/core` too when they import it directly. Any skew (a partial publish, or an app that updates one of the two) gives two copies of core: the app's and react's nested one. Core keeps module-level registries (`transformRegistry`, `geoRegistry`, `dataFormatRegistry`, visible in `scripts/check-bundle-shaking.mjs:479-481`), so `import '@aster-charts/core/geo'` in the app registers into a copy `<Chart>` does not read.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-TRACE for the loop and the manifests. The duplicate-instance consequence is PLAUSIBLE (not run; it needs a registry install).
- **Direction.** Make the loop idempotent (`npm view "$name@$version" version`, skip when present), document recovery in RELEASE.md, and weigh `workspace:^` or a peer dependency on core against the lockstep rule of ADR 0004.

#### C78 — High — `config.events.view` / `.window` / `.selector` / `.timer` are ignored by the event loop

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/signals.ts:349-353`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (0604090,90d30c8). Fixed: config.events view/window/selector/timer permits are applied as vega's permit applies them; event-permit-vs-vega.test checks which listeners each config installs.
- **Area:** core / signal event loop, transitions (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-signals-2` — `core-signals/`

`packages/core/src/signals.ts:349-353`, `:582`, `:1073-1083`; compare `packages/core/src/cursor.ts:70-74`

**`config.events.view` / `.window` / `.selector` / `.timer` are ignored by the event loop.** `eventDefaults` reads only `config.events.defaults`. The cursor tracker does honour the `view` rule (`cursor.ts:72`), so one config is honoured in one module and ignored in the other.

- **Scenario (`t12-permit.mjs`):** `config: { events: { view: false, window: false, selector: false } }` with handlers on `click`, `window:keydown`, `{source:'body', type:'mousedown'}`, `window:mousemove`.
- **Vega:** warns `Blocked view click event listener.` (and the others); signals stay `[0,0,0,0]`.
- **Aster:** `[1,2,2,2]`, nothing logged. With `{ window: ['keydown'], selector: [] }` Vega blocks the body and `window:mousemove` listeners; Aster binds them.
- This is the control a Vega embedder uses to confine a spec to its own surface, so -1 cannot be mitigated by config. It is not documented as a deviation (INTERACTION.md:290-293 and API.md:549 mention only `defaults`).
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** port `permit(view, key, type)` into `rootFor` for all four sources, with vega's warning.

#### C80 — High — `config.style.<mark type>` is dropped from the emitted Vega config

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:3747`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #209 (3bc5fbd). Fixed: config.style.<mark> is merged over config.<mark> into the one style Vega gets (as vega-lite redirects it), Vega-Lite-only keys are stripped per mark, and the compiler reads styles for every property; the mark x property x place sweep (about 15 000 drawings) fails on the base.
- **Area:** vl / mark encoding (also categories 4, 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c3-2` — `vl-c3/`

**`config.style.<mark type>` is dropped from the emitted Vega config.**
- Cause: `if (!MARK_TYPE_BLOCKS.includes(name) && isObject(block)) style[name] = block` skips blocks named after a mark type, and they are not merged into the `style[type]` built from `config.<mark>`. Only what the compiler reads itself through `styleConfigProp` survives (paint, `orient`, `filled`, `timeUnitBand*`).
- `config: {style: {bar: {opacity: 0.4}}}`: aster emits no `config` at all and opacity is undefined; vega-lite renders 0.4.
- `config: {style: {text: {fontSize: 17}}}`: 11 vs 17.
- Breadth (`out_cfgstyle.txt`): opacity, fillOpacity, strokeOpacity, strokeWidth, strokeDash, strokeCap, cornerRadius*, angle, blend, font*, dx/dy, limit, size, shape, width/height, align/baseline, description, aria, invalid, clip, tension, on every mark.
- Contradicts `packages/vl/README.md:93` (`style` listed as supported) and 133-135 ("nothing is silently ignored … a feature that vega-lite supports and is not here compiles to the same Vega").
- Status: CONFIRMED-RUN (F2, `t2.mjs`).
- Direction: merge `user.style[type]` under `user[type]`, and let the builder's explicit defaults yield to it.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `gallery4-6`, scripts `gallery4/`, CONFIRMED (run); adds to `vl-c3-2` and `vl-c3-3`: the one official example in this lane with `config.style` passes only on the subset that works):

- **Where:** `parallel_coordinate.vl.json:100-103` (`style: {label: {baseline, align, dx}, tick: {orient: "horizontal"}}`); `packages/vl/src/compile.ts:3747`.
- `tick` is both a named style and a mark-type style. The gate passes because `orient` is one of the properties the compiler reads itself.
- One property added to the official spec (`perturb-style.mjs`):
  - Diverge from vega-lite: `style.tick.opacity: 0.3`, `style.tick.thickness: 4`, `style.tick.size: 20` (with `mark.size` removed). Vega-lite applies them; Aster keeps opacity 0.7, thickness 1, size 8.
  - Equal: `style.tick.color`, and on the text style `label`: `fontSize`, `opacity`, `angle`, `fontWeight`, `dy`, `color`.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

#### C82 — High — `import { ChartStream }` pulls the whole synchronous engine up front (244.4 vs 188.6 kB gzip); no budget row or shaking pattern covers it

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/ChartStream.tsx:23-26`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** docs / ARCHITECTURE, ADRs, CHANGELOG, demo (also categories 4, 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `docs-arch-1` — `docs-arch/`

- **Issue:** `ChartStream.tsx` defines both `ChartStream` and `ChartWorkerStream`. The latter statically imports `useChartWorkerStream.ts`, which imports the full `@aster-charts/core` barrel. `core/dist/index.js` is in `sideEffects`, so its bare `import './parts-evaluate.js'` survives tree-shaking.
- **Scenario:** an app imports only `ChartStream`. Expected: the lean engine plus on-demand parts, as for `<Chart>`. Observed:
  ```
  Chart           up front 188.6 kB gzip; part-legend: false | part-aggregate: false | incremental-engine: false | react worker.js: false
  ChartStream     up front 244.4 kB gzip; part-legend: true  | part-aggregate: true  | incremental-engine: true  | react worker.js: true
  useChartStream  up front 161.1 kB gzip; part-legend: false | ...
  ```
  My figures sum the gzip of every statically reached chunk, so absolutes differ from `budget.mjs`; the comparison is the point. `ChartStream` costs about what the `Chart + all` row does (ceiling 247.7).
- **Second effect:** such an app never suspends for a part. The built `apps/demo/dist` shows it: `legend:()=>Promise.resolve().then(...)` is in the main chunk, and only pulse/intersect/modify/timer/canvas/signals are separate chunks.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `stream-bundle.mjs` (esbuild, `conditions: ['browser']`, splitting; one-off bundle, not the gate).
- **Direction:** move `ChartWorkerStream` to its own module; have the worker hooks import from `core/lean` or a non-side-effect entry; add a `ChartStream` budget row and a shaking pattern asserting no `part-*` up front.

#### C281 — Medium — `maxGeneratedRows` is metered per pulse, so a session accepts appends a fresh evaluation rejects, then throws on the next signal change or resize

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:4036-4045`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #201 (0af54b9 430d489). Fixed (DECISIONS Q17): maxGeneratedRows meters the rows an evaluation produces; kept steps are not charged; LIMITS.md documents the session-vs-fresh consequence; runtime-state-contracts.test.ts.
- **Area:** core / runtime: datasets, scales, fit
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt2-6` — `core-rt2/`

**`runtime.ts:4036-4045` (pulse path, taken under `limits` when `prevDS.fp === passFp`) vs `:4495-4502` (`keepStep`)**: `maxGeneratedRows` is charged per pulse on the pulse path, but in full by a fresh evaluation and by the session's own next non-pulse evaluation.

`t` = `src` → `flatten` (3 rows per source row) → `formula(… * s)`, `limits: {maxGeneratedRows: 10}`:

| Step | Session | Fresh |
|---|---|---|
| 5 source rows | 15 rows | 15 rows |
| append → 6 | 18 rows, accepted | throws `maxGeneratedRows 12 > 10 (transform flatten)` |
| append → 7 | 21 rows, accepted | throws `… 14 > 10` |
| same rows, signal `s` 1→2 | throws `… 14 > 10` | throws |
| same rows, width 200→300 | throws | throws |

`maxRows` is checked on the pulse path and rejects at the same step as fresh. `LIMITS.md:123` calls the budget "cumulative rows produced by transforms/emitters in one evaluation".

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**, `repro-generated-rows-pulse.mjs`, `t-limits-pulse.mjs`.
Direction: one accounting rule: the pulse path charges what a run from scratch would, or datasets do not take the pulse path under `limits`.

#### C284 — Medium — `limits.regex: 'refuse'` does not see expressions in the view's own `layout` and `encode`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/spec-expressions.ts:222-231`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (7b4fa17,04188f5). Fixed: the view's own layout, encode and config.legend.layout are walked, so limits.regex 'refuse' sees them; covered by the schema-site differential's regexSites check.
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-8` — `core-expr/`

**`limits.regex: 'refuse'` does not see expressions in the view's own `layout` and `encode`.**

- **Documented promise:** every expression is read at compile, "also those in branches that never run".
- **Cause:** `objectProperty(m.layout)` and `encode(m.encode)` are called only from `mark()` (`:539, :549`), never for the root. The runtime evaluates both.
- **Scenario:** top-level `layout: {columns: {signal: "false ? test(/(a+)+$/, 'aaaa') : 1"}}`, or the same text in root `encode.update.opacity`, with `{regex:'refuse'}`.
- **Observed:** rendered; `compileChart(spec).regexSites` is `undefined`. The same text in a signal `update` is refused.
- **Scope of the hole:** a regex on a live branch is still refused by the run-time guard, so this is the compile-time guarantee failing, not an execution path.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p10.mjs`.
- **Direction:** read the root's `layout` and `encode` in `view()` as `mark()` does for a group.

#### C285 — Medium — The interpreter-shaped entry points have a weaker sandbox than the file header states, and only tests use them

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/expr-interpreter.ts:14-20`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (36c5d6b). Fixed: the interpreter-shaped entry points call native methods only (NATIVE_METHODS), never hand out prototypes, and refuse Function/eval in engine mode; expression-sandbox.test.
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-10` — `core-expr/`

**The interpreter-shaped entry points have a weaker sandbox than the file header states, and only tests use them.**

- **Header claim (`:18-19`):** no function value is handed to a built-in, so one reached by member read cannot be invoked.
- **What the code does in that mode:**
  - `guardArgs` (`:331-339`) inspects top-level arguments only.
  - Default `join`/`indexof`/`lastindexof`/`slice` are `viaMethod` with no cast (`:70-73`).
  - `callMethod` does `obj[method].apply(obj, args.slice(1))` on any object (`:38-39`).
  - Object literals may hold function values under non-`Object.prototype` keys (`:412-429`), and member reads yield function values (`:279-285`).
  - So a function nested in an object-literal argument is invoked with spec-chosen arguments.
- **Production is not affected:** `createBuiltinFunctions` shadows all of these with versions that require a real array or string (`expression.ts:184-190, 468-477`), and `host[name] || DefaultFunctions[name]` (`:350`) never falls through for them.
- **Users of the weak path:** `expression-limits.test.ts`, `expr-call-paths.test.ts` and two conformance differentials.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE; not run, because the entry points are not in `dist/index.js`.
- **Direction:** move the interpreter mode and its duplicate table to a test helper, or give `callMethod` the engine's receiver checks.

#### C286 — Medium — `baseURL` is WHATWG-resolved for data and the policy check, but string-prefixed for the drawn image

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/url-policy.ts:159-169`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (ede341e,f075640,1b08c14). Fixed: image urls are resolved by vega's prefix rule first and allow is asked once about the drawn url (protocol/credential checks still apply to the text as written); TSDoc/LIMITS say baseURL is a prefix.
- **Area:** core / loading, URL policy, add-ons (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-load-11` — `core-load/`

**`baseURL` is WHATWG-resolved for data and the policy check, but string-prefixed for the drawn image.**
- The TSDoc gives `location.href` as the example. With `baseURL: 'https://app.example.com/dash/page.html?id=3'` and image `url: 'logo.png'`:
  - `allow` is called with `https://app.example.com/dash/logo.png`, then with `https://app.example.com/dash/page.html?id=3/logo.png`, which is what is drawn.
  - `loadSpecData` with the same base requests `…/dash/logo.json`.
- `DATA:image/png;…` (upper case) is drawn as `https://app.example.com/DATA:image/png;…`.
- No policy bypass: the drawn string is re-vetted (`runtime.ts:5575`) and stays on the base host.
- `docs/LIMITS.md:487-489` describes the concatenation; the TSDoc does not.
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `r11-image-policy.mjs`.
- Direction: resolve once with `new URL(raw, baseURL)` and draw `url.href`, or document the image base as a prefix and remove `location.href` from the TSDoc.

- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-c3-5` — `vl-c3/`

**Config precedence differs from vega-lite.**

| config | mark | aster | vega-lite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config.mark.size: 50` | line | strokeWidth 50 | 2 |
| `config.mark.size: 50` | text | fontSize 50 | 11 |
| `config.mark.fontSize: 17` | text | 11 | 17 |
| `config.rule.size: 6` | rule | default | 6 |
| `config.mark.strokeWidth: 4` | point / circle / square | 4 | 2 |
| `config.mark.outerRadius: 70` (also `radius2`) | arc | 150 | 70 |

- The comment at 6756 ("a config value reaches Vega through config.style") is wrong for `config.mark.*`: Vega's own `text.fontSize` shadows `config.mark`, which is why vega-lite encodes the value.
- Status: CONFIRMED-RUN (F6, `t3.mjs`).

#### C299 — Medium — The rename cannot tell compiler-written expressions from the user's, and is asymmetric about which keys it rewrites

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/embed.ts:71-93`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #202 (0f80de5). user labelExpr (axis/legend/header) excluded from renames; stray labelExpr key dropped; key asymmetry documented; vl-user-expressions.test.ts (60)
- **Area:** vl / validate, optimize, predicates
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-rest1-8` — `vl-rest1/`

**The rename cannot tell compiler-written expressions from the user's, and is asymmetric about which keys it rewrites.**

- **(a) It rewrites user expressions.** An axis `labelExpr` mentioning `width` in a concat, facet or repeat child: vega-lite emits `datum.value + '/' + width`; aster emits `… + concat_0_width` (`child_width` in a facet), so labels differ. The same axis also carries a stray `"labelExpr"` key, which is not a Vega axis property.
- **(b) It skips `expr` and `test`.** `EXPRESSION_KEYS` in the same file (`embed.ts:110`) lists `signal, update, init, expr, test`, but `renameFragment` handles only `signal` and `update` / `init`. `tok.mjs` shows `{"type":"filter","expr":"datum.v < width"}` and `{"test":"width > 3 && scale(\"x\", 1)"}` unchanged while a sibling `{"signal":"width"}` is renamed. `optimize.ts:63-77` patches `expr` by hand for top-level datasets only.
- **Status:** (a) CONFIRMED-RUN (`emb.mjs`: `hconcat / labelExpr`, `facet / labelExpr`, `repeat / labelExpr`, `concat-indep / labelExpr`). (b) CONFIRMED-RUN at function level (`tok.mjs`); reachability from `compile` is PLAUSIBLE — I found no compiled spec with a renamed name inside a `test`.
- **Direction:** one definition of "expression-bearing key" for both walks; keep user-authored expressions out of the walk.

#### C302 — Medium — Why no gate caught `in` throwing and `/g` regexes alternating

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-expression-engine-gen.test.mts:107-111`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #204 (749682a). Fixed: the engine generator draws every operator (in, instanceof, bitwise, shifts, != !== > <=, unary), stateful g/y regex literals over 12 rows, and a generated encode differential that reads item; it fails on this base for C32/C125/C31 (fixed by a04 36c5d6b/fcae061/bdd4896: stack a04 first).
- **Area:** conformance / scripts and gates (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `harness-scripts-6` — `harness-scripts/`

**Why no gate caught `in` throwing and `/g` regexes alternating.**
- `leads-expr.mjs` (formula over 4 rows, real `vega.View` against `evaluateChart`):
  - `test(/a/g, datum.s)`: vega `[true,true,true,true]`, Aster `[true,false,true,false]`.
  - `"a" in datum`: vega `[true,…]`, Aster `ERR TypeError: Ops[n.operator] is not a function`. `datum.a in [1,2,3,4,5]` likewise.
  - `|`, `<<`, `>>>`, `~`, `!=`, `!==`, `<=`, `>`, `^`, `&` and unary `+` agree.
- The engine generator's operators are `['+', '-', '*', '/', '%', '<', '>=', '===', '==', '&&', '||']` (`:142`): no `in`, `instanceof`, bitwise, shifts, `!=`, `!==`, `>`, `<=`.
- Its regexes are `/a/`, `/^\d+$/`, `/l+/i` (`:171`) and `/a/` (`:110`): no `g` or `y`, although each expression is evaluated over 12 rows.
- `differential-vega-interpreter-gen` does generate `in` and `/x/g` (`expression-gen.mts:41, 133`), but its oracle is vega-interpreter, which has no `in`/`instanceof`.
  - `vega-expression-cases.mjs:73` pins that on purpose: `'a in b', // Binary has no 'in' op upstream; pin the resulting throw`.
  - Aster reproduces the message (`packages/core/src/expr-interpreter.ts:263-265`). Vega's default code generation evaluates `in`.
  - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:281` says "the semantics of `vega-interpreter`"; the deviation list names neither `in`/`instanceof` nor the regex statefulness.
- Encode expressions reading `item`: `item` is in the identifier pools (`expression-gen.mts:27, 130`) but is evaluated only through interpreter entry points with a hand-made `event.item`. No generator renders an encode expression that reads `item`.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN for the two defects; CONFIRMED-TRACE for the pools.
- **Direction:** give the engine generator the full `OPS` list and regex flags `g`/`y`; add an encode-site evaluation differential; decide and document `in`.

#### C304 — Medium — the benchmark's `aster` and `asterDom` embeds are the same configuration

- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced; lines re-read by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (fa2ed6d). aster=incremental false, asterDom=true explicit, probe test; exposed and fixed blank string-mode dense charts

#### C305 — Medium — `ci.yml` runs on every pull request although the convention is CI on `main` only

- **Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-7`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (a7b4374). ci.yml triggers on push to main only, tested
- **Area:** tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tooling-11` — `tooling/`

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-7`

- **Issue.** `on: push: branches: [main]` and `pull_request: branches: [main]`, with no `concurrency` group. Each push to a PR branch starts the whole gate list plus three `unit` jobs, and the merge starts them again on `main`. The convention (CI on `main` only) is enforced by hand, not by the file. `gates.test.mjs` asserts the trigger of `release.yml` only.
- **Scenario.** A five-branch stack with three pushes each: 60 jobs to cancel by hand.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-TRACE.
- **Direction.** Decide it in the file: drop `pull_request`, or keep it with `concurrency: { group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`, and assert the choice in `gates.test.mjs`. CONTRIBUTING.md:14-15 ("CI runs exactly `pnpm check`, so a green local run is a green CI run") should also name the Node-matrix `unit` job, which a local run does not reproduce.

#### C306 — Medium — an undeclared dataset name in `data` is silently ignored (Vega throws)

- **Location:** `docs/API.md:358-359`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** docs / README, API, ERRORS (also categories 5, 8)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `docs-api-4` — `docs-api/`

`R/docs/API.md:358-359`, `:829-834`, `R/packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:585-591` (only `dataChanges` is validated).

- **Scenario.** The README names its dataset `data0`; API.md's examples use `table`. A reader writes `<Chart spec={spec} data={{ tabel: rows }} />` or `renderSpec(spec, { data: { tabel: rows } })`.
- **Observed.** No error and no log; the output is byte-identical to passing no data at all. Real Vega for the same call: `view.data("tabel", rows)` throws `Unrecognized data set: tabel`.
- **Inconsistency.** The neighbouring input is validated: `dataChanges={{ nosuch: [0] }}` reports `[aster] dataChanges["nosuch"]: no "nosuch" array in the data prop` through `onError` (observed).
- **JS callers.** `data={[{...}]}` (a bare array; API.md:830 only says it "does not typecheck") renders the spec's inline rows with no report. `data={{ t: null }}` and `data={{ t: { x: 1 } }}` also render with no report.
- **Not documented.** ARCHITECTURE.md, API.md and ERRORS.md have 0 hits for `Unrecognized data set`.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**.
- `$S/ws/unknown-dataset.mjs`: `vega view.data("tabel", rows) THROWS: Unrecognized data set: tabel` / `aster ... output identical to no data at all: true`.
- `$S/ws/misuse-core.mjs` and `$S/ws/first-run-react.mjs` section 3.

Direction: refuse, or at least report through `logger`/`onError`, a `data` key that no scope of the spec declares, as `dataChanges` already does. Document whichever is chosen.

- **Expected:** either the same refusal or a documented "Aster renders where Vega's parser fails" entry, with the test asserting which.
- **Dead branch:** the `non-finite transform` alternative in the regex at `:184`, and the "or a NaN transform" comment, are never hit (0 occurrences).
- **Ceilings:** 14 against 11 actual; 4 against 2 actual.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `e4b-guide-null.mjs` (`11 unanswered of 1983`, each `aster: RENDERED a readable document`), `e5-e6.mjs` (`title.group two styles: vega threw … "nullnull" | aster RENDERED`).

**Direction:** in both tests run Aster on the unanswered cases and assert the intended outcome; set the ceilings to the exact counts; add the deviation to ERRORS.md or refuse.

Relates to C424 (core-guides-12), which reports the same skip for `guide-compare.ts`. These are two further copies of the pattern, with a concrete divergence behind them.

#### C311 — Medium — An unknown `interpolate` logs Vega's error and still draws the line; the test that covers the names patches its oracle

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/shape.ts:278-285`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** tests / conformance generators and case tables I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confscripts1-1` — `tests-confscripts1/`

- `packages/core/src/shape.ts:278-285` (`resolveCurve` returns `LINEAR` for an unknown name; `CURVE_NAMES` at `:266-269` includes `monotone-x` / `monotone-y`)
- `packages/core/src/bound-failure.ts:23-30` (`measureCurve` throws for the same names; comment: "The renderers here draw such a mark in the linear curve")
- `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-d3-shape-generated.test.mts:334-342`

Scenario: a line mark with `interpolate: {value: X}`, followed by a rect mark.

| `interpolate` | Vega | Aster |
|---|---|---|
| `nonsense` | logs `TypeError: curve is not a function`; `toSVG` rejects | logs the same error; returns an SVG with `<path d="M0,5L20,30L40,10">` |
| `monotone-x` | same as above | logs the same error; draws the monotone-x curve (`M0,5C6.667,17.5,…`) |
| `toString` | `vega.parse` throws `Operator not defined: undefined` | logs the TypeError; draws linear |
| `monotone` | draws | draws, identical |

- Aster reports "not a function" and draws with that very curve. The two modules disagree about whether `monotone-x` is a curve.
- Not in `docs/ERRORS.md` or "Deviations from Vega". ERRORS.md:473 documents the opposite policy for axes: where Vega's renderer cannot draw, Aster refuses the view.
- The test titled "every interpolate x orient x tension draws what vega's pathCurves draws" builds its oracle as `pathCurves(...) ?? aliases[name] ?? d3Shape.curveLinear`. For 7 of its 18 names the expected value is chosen by the test, not by Vega.
- No differential in this range compares the whole-spec picture for an unknown curve.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `curve.mjs`, `curve2.mjs`.
- Direction: pick one rule. Either refuse or leave the mark undrawn when `measureCurve` fails, or drop the alias from one side and document the fallback. Remove the `??` patches from the test and assert the divergence explicitly.

#### C316 — Medium — 13 specs whose named property is inert: deleting or flipping it leaves real Vega's SVG unchanged

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/bar-clip.vg.json:1`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #206 (24f7a7d5,1b00c821). every inert property now bites (mark-level clip over a clamped domain, sort with op, domainRaw differing, nice on a non-nice max, zero with min>0, domainMin 1, domainMid 4, extent 0.25, expr filter dropping rows, config.group.stroke); bar-stack-zero-explicit and bar-align-center are kept as the default written out and say so, next to bar-align-left/right where align bites
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 1
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus1-4` — `corpus1/`

Mutation probe: `inert.mjs inert-cases.json` and `inert2.json`. Each line printed `INERT (vega SVG identical) | aster identical`.

| File | Property | Why it is inert |
|---|---|---|
| `bar-clip.vg.json:1` | `encode.update.clip:{value:true}` on a rect | `clip` is a mark property (or a group's encode channel); no bar leaves the frame anyway. SVG identical to `bar-nice-false`. |
| `bar-x-ordinal-sort.vg.json:1` | `domain.sort:{field:"val",order:"descending"}` | no `op`, so Vega does not sort (`probe-sort.mjs`: domain stays `["Banana","Apple","Cherry","Date"]`; with `op:"max"` it becomes `["Date","Apple","Banana","Cherry"]`). The ordinal scale with `range:"width"` also puts bars at 0/400/0/400. |
| `bar-domain-raw.vg.json:1` | `domainRaw` signal `[0,10]` | equals the explicit `domain:[0,10]`. This is the only raw-Vega spec in the corpus that names `domainRaw`. |
| `bar-nice-false.vg.json:1` | `nice:false` → `true` | domain is already `[0,5]`. |
| `area-zero-domain.vg.json:1` | `zero:true` → deleted or `false` | data minimum is 0. |
| `bar-align-center.vg.json:1` | `align:0.5` | the default. |
| `color-diverging-domainmid-scheme.vl.json:46` | `domainMid:6` | data is 3..9, so 6 is the centre; `probe-geo.mjs` shows identical colours without it, different with `domainMid:4`. |
| `color-hcl-three-stop-range.vl.json:50` | `interpolate:"hcl"` | Vega-Lite's default; `rgb` differs. |
| `bar-domain-min-max.vg.json:1` | `domainMin:0` | `zero` already gives 0 (`domainMax` is observable). |
| `bar-stack-zero-explicit.vg.json:1` | `offset:"zero"` | the default. |
| `box-plot-full.vl.json:1` | `extent:1.5` | the default. |
| `expr-time-fns.vg.json:16` | filter `utcyear(..) >= 2021 && quarter(..) < 5` | keeps every row. |
| `config-style.vg.json:9` | `config.view.stroke` | a Vega-Lite config key in a Vega spec. |

- **Scenario:** an engine that ignored mark `clip`, sorted (or failed to sort) an op-less domain sort differently, or dropped `domainRaw` would still pass these.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** give each a value or dataset where the property bites — bars past a clamped domain with mark-level `clip:true`, a `sort` with `op`, `domainRaw` different from `domain`, data whose minimum is above 0 — and keep a second spec only where the default-equals-explicit case is the point.

#### C317 — Medium — 11 specs whose named feature is absent

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/force.vg.json:1`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #206 (d7347aa8,1b00c821). force (real force transform), crossfilter, box-plot, gnomonic, mercator-default, bar-interpolate, color-scheme, canvas-arc-radius-scale, funnel, dot-plot, expr-function-geo-only now contain the named feature
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 1
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus1-5` — `corpus1/`

- `force.vg.json:1`: no `force` transform. The `rule` mark reads `source.x` from link rows whose `source` is a number, so both rules have no coordinates (`probe-misc.mjs`: rule items `{}` `{}`, drawn as `<line x2="0" y2="0">`). It compares three static symbols and two zero-length lines.
- `crossfilter.vg.json:1`: an `aggregate`, no crossfilter. It also carries an inert `"type":"ordinal"` in an encode entry, and bars at x = 1,2,3,4 px with width 30 overlap almost fully.
- `box-plot.vl.json:8`: `"mark": { "type": "bar", "opacity": 0.3 }`. It compiles to one `rect` mark.
- `geo-vlout-gnomonic-clip.vg.json:179`: `"type": "azimuthalEqualArea"`. Switching to `gnomonic` changes the SVG, so gnomonic is not what is tested (gnomonic is covered by `vlx-geo-proj-gnomonic*`).
- `geo-vlout-mercator-default.vg.json:149`: `"type": "equalEarth"`.
- `bar-interpolate.vg.json:1`: a `quantize` colour scale, no interpolate.
- `color-scheme.vl.json:1`: an explicit `range`, no scheme.
- `canvas-arc-radius-scale.vg.json`: radii are raw fields, no scale.
- `funnel.vl.json:1`: a plain bar chart.
- `dot-plot.vl.json:1`: every `y` is 1, so six circles land on three points.
- `expr-function-geo-only.vg.json:1`: both polygons are wound clockwise, so d3-geo reads them as the sphere minus a rectangle. Both rows render "big" at the same off-canvas point (-480, 730) on a 200×100 view. A `geoBounds` returning a constant 180, or any positive `geoArea`, would pass.

- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`probe-misc.mjs`, `inert.mjs`) for force, crossfilter, box-plot, gnomonic and geo-only; CONFIRMED-TRACE for the rest.
- **Direction:** rename or replace. For `force.vg.json`, either add the transform or delete it, since `force-layout-marks.vg.json` covers force.

- **Product check:** with `path` encoded, all 15 combinations of shape (line, arc, curve, orthogonal, diagonal) × orient (horizontal, vertical, radial) match Vega (`repaired.mjs`, 55 records each).
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`inert.mjs`, `repaired.mjs`).
- **Direction:** add `"path":{"field":"path"}`; consider one group per shape.

#### C325 — Medium — Four errorbar/errorband specs draw nothing; both engines agree on an empty chart

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-ebx-eb-stdev-ticks.vl.json:73-77`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #206 (1b00c821,f1dd19ca). the four errorbar/errorband specs get three rows per group and draw; the per-entry floor on data items is the corpus-no-items.json check
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 3
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus3-2` — `corpus3/`

`vlx-ebx-eb-stdev-ticks.vl.json:73-77`, `vlx-ebx-eb-timeunit.vl.json:76`, `vlx-ebx-ebd-2d.vl.json:72-73`, `vlx-ebx-ebd-2d-interp.vl.json:72-75`.

- **Cause:** the shared 6-row dataset has exactly one row per group (per `c`×`g`, per month, per `x`). The stdev/stderr of one value is undefined, and Vega-Lite's validity filter drops every row.
- **Observed (`render-all.mjs`):**
  - `vlx-ebx-eb-stdev-ticks items=0/0` and `vlx-ebx-eb-timeunit items=0/0`, with Vega warning `Infinite extent for field "lower_v"`. The only axis label is `0.000000` (`misc.mjs`).

- **Inertness (`inert.mjs`):** deleting `mark.extent`, `mark.ticks.size` and `mark.rule` (stdev-ticks), or `mark.interpolate` and `mark.borders.strokeDash` (2d-interp), leaves the canonical SVG identical.
- **Expected:** specs named for stdev ticks, timeUnit error bars, and 2-D bands with interpolation and borders should draw them.
- **With real data:** given several rows per group, the same four specs draw 18/3/3/6 items and Aster matches (`probes.mjs`, "several rows per group": `check3=0 check4=0`).
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** give the `vlx-ebx-*` dataset at least 3 rows per group, and add a per-entry floor on data-driven items to the gate.

#### C327 — Medium — Bin specs whose named parameter does not change the bins

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-bin-nice-false.vl.json:122`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)

#### C328 — Medium — Three `config.scale` specs where the config has no effect in real Vega-Lite

#### C329 — Medium — Tooltip specs are invisible to the corpus gate

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-chan-tooltip-mark-true.vl.json:118`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #206 (f1dd19ca). conformance-vl compares every item's tooltip between vega-lite's Vega and ours; planted tooltip strip fails all five specs
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 3
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus3-6` — `corpus3/`

`vlx-chan-tooltip-mark-true.vl.json:118`, `vlx-chan-tooltip-content-data.vl.json:118`, `vlx-chan-tooltip-field.vl.json:126`, `vlx-chan-tooltip-array.vl.json:126`, `vlx-cfgf-number-format.vl.json:134`; `packages/conformance/src/run-vl.ts:102-110`.

- **Why:** the gate compares canonical SVG, and neither engine's SVG carries tooltips.
- **Planted bug (`planted.mjs`):** I stripped every `tooltip` from the Vega our compiler emits. For all five specs: `tooltip encodings removed from our Vega=1; check3 diffs=0; check4 diffs=0`. The control (view width +7) gives 33–42 diffs, so the comparison itself can fail.
- **Partial visibility:** `encoding.tooltip` fields leak into `aria-label`, so `-field` and `-array` are seen indirectly. `mark.tooltip: true`, `{content:"data"}` and the tooltip in `cfgf-number-format` are fully inert.
- **Today's state:** tooltip values are equal between our Vega and Vega-Lite's when both run in real Vega (`probes.mjs`: `tooltipsEqual=true` for all five). Tooltips are also exercised in `packages/conformance/test/vl-compiler-parity.test.ts:141-200`.
- `href` and `description` are fine: the canonicalizer compares them.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** have `run-vl.ts` also compare per-item `tooltip` from the two scenegraphs, or move these specs to a test that does.

#### C330 — Medium — 42 `vlx-invalid-<mark>-<mode>` specs are 15 distinct tests; the `*-domains` modes are never distinguished

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-invalid-point-break-paths-show-domains.vl.json:41`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #207 (57b5824b). vega-lite collapses the modes at the mark, config.mark.invalid keeps two apart: those specs set the mode there; every spec has its own data; aliases say so in their description; corpus-identical.json holds no invalid group
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 5
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus5-4` — `corpus5/`

`vlx-invalid-{area,bar,line,point,text,trail}-{default,filter,break-paths-filter-domains,break-paths-show-domains,break-paths-show-path-domains,show,null}.vl.json` (e.g. `vlx-invalid-point-break-paths-show-domains.vl.json:41`)
- **Observed:** hashing vega-lite's own compiled Vega per mark gives these classes (`probe2.mjs`):
  - area, line, trail: `{default, bp-filter-domains, bp-show-domains, bp-show-path-domains}`, `{filter}`, `{show, null}`.
  - bar, point, text: `{default, filter, bp-filter-domains, bp-show-domains, bp-show-path-domains}`, `{show, null}`.
- That is 3+3+3+2+2+2 = 15 distinct compiled specs for 42 entries. The identity is at compile level, so no data could separate them.
- **Why the names mislead:** `break-paths-show-domains` vs `-filter-domains` promises a scale-domain difference. For the point specs the compiled scale domains are identical (`data_0` in both), and moving the invalid row's x to 40 still gives the same output in both engines (`probe4.mjs`).
- **Consequence:** 27 of the "1063" are restatements. They do pin that Aster's mode parsing collapses the same way, but the gate count overstates the coverage of invalid-data handling.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`probe2.mjs`, `render.mjs` hashes).
- **Direction:** keep one spec per distinct class per mark, and add specs where the modes really differ in vega-lite 6 (if any configuration does — see open question 1).

#### C331 — Medium — React budget rows are the gzip of concatenated chunks and stop at the first `import()`; the "whole bundle" label is no longer true

- **Location:** `packages/benchmarks/scripts/budget.mjs:24`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #188 (0e65f18,6a88509). Fixed: each file gzipped on its own, React rows gate up front + on demand, useChartWorker / hydrateChart / ssr have rows; ceilings re-set in their own commit.
- **Area:** leftovers / budgets, declarations, demo data, gallery lists
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gaps-misc-b-5` — `gaps-misc-b/`

`packages/benchmarks/scripts/budget.mjs:24`, `:413` ("the whole bundle of the app"), `:632-634`, `:653-665`, `:675`

| Row | Row figure (kB) | Per-file gzip of the same eager chunks (kB) | Eager chunks | On-demand, ungated (kB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `useChart` | 146.14 | 152.80 | 21 | 142.05 |
| `Chart` | 181.70 | 188.60 | 23 | 137.15 |
| `SvgChart` | 168.13 | 173.89 | 19 | 121.32 |
| `SvgChart + interaction` | 181.39 | 188.30 | 23 | 126.25 |
| `Chart + all` | 247.69 | 259.48 | 44 | 67.46 |
| `Chart + VL` | 288.18 | 294.97 | 23 | 137.15 |

- **Understated.** `:663-664` gzips one concatenated buffer. A browser fetches 19-44 separately compressed files, so the published figure is 5.8-11.8 kB (3.4-4.8%) under what is transferred. `lazyKb` (`:662`) is summed per file, so the two numbers on one output line use different methods.
- **Ungated.** The on-demand total is printed (`:675`) and has no ceiling. Code moved behind an `import()` that every chart triggers lowers the row. The stack-8 note records `<Chart>` going 235.0 → 209.1 that way.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `$S/budget-replica.mjs`; the `Chart` figure equals CHANGELOG 0.4.2's 181.7.
- **Direction.** Sum per-file gzip for the eager set; add a ceiling on eager + on-demand for the React rows; reword `:24` and `:413`.
- **Adds to C82 (docs-arch-1).** The same cause reaches two more unbudgeted imports (`EXTRA=extra-entries.json`):
  - `useChartWorker` from the root: 193.2 kB eager (`useChart`: 146.1).
  - `hydrateChart` from the root: 206.5 kB; `@aster-charts/react/ssr`: 199.5 kB. Both exceed `<Chart>`'s 181.7.

#### C332 — Medium — The Vega sweep never sweeps scale `reverse` or legend `type`; the skip reasons are false for those families

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/sweeps/vega-schema.mjs:939`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (0bf91e3,56101b3). Fixed: scale reverse and legend type are swept (reverse in every scale family, legend type gradient and symbol).
- **Area:** closure / gallery, sweeps, canvas helpers, corpus-tz
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-confsrc-2` — `w3-confsrc/`

`packages/conformance/src/sweeps/vega-schema.mjs:939` (`reverse: 'covered by the boolean sweep of the scale family'`), `:921` (`type: 'the scale type; sweeping it rebuilds the chart rather than varying it'`), applied by `skipReason` at `:1014-1019`.

- **Mechanism.** `SHARED_SKIP` applies to every family unless `FAMILY_SKIP` mentions the property. `FAMILY_SKIP.scale` (`:1023-1032`) lists only `interpolate`, and `FAMILY_SKIP.legend` (`:1043-1051`) does not list `type`.
- **Observed** (`$S/gen.mjs`):
  - `reverse`: skipped in 15 families (`scale` and all 14 `scale-*`), swept in 0. The family the reason points to is itself skipped. The comment at `:772-773` names `reverse` as a reason the `scale` family targets the band scale.
  - `type`: skipped in `legend` and `config-legend` with the scale-type reason. The schema declares `legend.type` as `enum ["gradient","symbol"]`, so both words are available and never tried.
- **Expected.** `reverse` true/false on each scale type, and `legend.type` gradient/symbol on the base chart.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `$S/gen.mjs`.
- **Direction:** add `reverse: null` to `FAMILY_SKIP.scale` and `type: null` to `FAMILY_SKIP.legend`. This adds to `C301 (harness-src-9)`, which lists other stale skip reasons but not these two.

#### C566 — Low — `tsc` never cleans `dist`: this tree holds a built module that has no source

- **Location:** `scripts/bundle-shaking.test.mjs:24-27`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (50b953e). build cleans dist; budget refuses orphans
- **Area:** tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tooling-15` — `tooling/`

`packages/*/package.json` (`"build": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json"`)

On this freshly built tree `packages/core/dist/svg-path.js` exists and `packages/core/src/svg-path.ts(x)` does not. A local `pnpm pack` would ship it. `check-deps`, `verify-publish`, `check:bundle` and `bundle-shaking.test.mjs:24-27` ("dist paths that exist") all read `dist`, so an `exports` or `sideEffects` entry whose source was deleted stays green locally and goes red in CI on a clean checkout. `budget.mjs:578-596` checks src → dist only, never dist → src. CONFIRMED-RUN (a shell loop over `dist/*.js` against `src/`; one orphan). Direction: remove `dist` before each build, or have the budget's staleness check also refuse orphans.

`packages/core/src/canvas.ts:64` (`fillText(text, x, y, maxWidthOrMulti?: number | boolean)`), `packages/core/src/canvas.test.ts:101-104` (`if (multi) return`).

#### C589 — Low — The structural half of `check()` is root-level and set-based, so its labels promise more than it compares

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/test/vl-compiler-parity.test.ts:867-881`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Area:** tests / conformance suites I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-conftest1-8` — `tests-conftest1/`

`packages/conformance/test/vl-compiler-parity.test.ts:867-881`; `packages/conformance/test/vl-expressions.ts:135-160`

- `SIZE_KEYS` and `AXIS_STEPS` read `vg.signals`, `vg.scales`, `vg.axes` at the root only; in a concat, facet or repeat the scales and axes live in child groups, and only signals are compared.
- `DATA_NODE_KINDS` is a set of transform types. For C53 (vl-c2-1) the full node lists are equal on both sides while the aggregate's `groupby` is wrong.
- `expressionsOf` is a set over the whole spec, with no location or multiplicity. An expression dropped at one site and kept at another is equal by construction.

The render assertion is the real gate and did catch every probe; this matters for diagnosis and for the ~259 cases that never render (expressions block, legend matrix, spacing, cell, URL formats).

**Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE** (lines above), with the C53 (vl-c2-1) node lists from `miscompiles.mts`. Direction: walk groups in `SIZE_KEYS`/`AXIS_STEPS`; compare expressions as a multiset keyed by dataset or mark role.

- **What still works:** the comparison sees the clip attribute and its rect. Stripping `clip-path` from the oracle SVG gives 8 canonical diffs, and so does shrinking the clip rect.
- **What is weak:** at 3-decimal comparison, a 3 px shape hides relative projection errors that a 300 px one would show.
- **Covered by siblings:** `explicit-scale-translate` (bbox y up to 407 in a 300 frame) and `explicit-translate-only` (negative x/y) do cross the frame.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN (`render.out` bboxes, `probes.mjs` item 1).
- **Direction:** raise the scales to roughly 500 and 200.

#### C617 — Low — the "by a list of values" sort names values no field holds

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/test/vl-sort-channels.test.ts:26`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** closure / conformance suites, line by line II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-conftest-b-5` — `w3-conftest-b/`

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/test/vl-sort-channels.test.ts:26` — `['by a list of values', ['b', 'a', 'c']]`.
- **Issue:** the space's fields (`vl-honoured-space.ts` `DATA` over `TIME_DATA`) are `v` (0–4, 9), `k` (0, 1, 2) and `t` (ISO instants). No row holds `'a'`, `'b'` or `'c'`, so every row gets the same sort index.
- **Evidence:** for `x: {field:'k', type:'ordinal'}` the running domain is `[0,1,2]` with no sort and `[0,1,2]` with `sort: ['b','a','c']`, in both compilers. With `sort: [2,0,1]` it is `[2,0,1]`. Same on `color`.

- **Covered elsewhere:** sort arrays with matching values exist in `vl-real-vega.test.ts:49`, `vl-compiler-parity.test.ts` and seven corpus specs, but on nominal x / colour only — not across this file's space (binned, temporal, time-unit fields).
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `probe1.mjs` part A.

#### C77 — High — worker-stream backpressure bounds one tick, not the worker

- **Location:** `packages/react/src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:238-252`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #199 (dba96b7). Fixed: one request in flight to the worker; pushes queue under the stream's policy until it is answered, so a silent worker holds one flush and the queue its bounds (t06: 2 of 2000 accepted); the model test asserts never two unanswered flushes.
- **Area:** react / hooks, streams, workers (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-4` — `react-hooks/`

`src/useChartWorkerStream.ts:238-252`, `:205-236`; claims at `:61-67`, `:89-94`; `docs/API.md:320-321`.
- **Cause:** the buffer is posted every tick whether or not the previous flush was answered. Nothing counts flushes in flight. The worker's own stream is flushed right after each push, so its queue never fills either.
- **Observed** (`t06-worker-backpressure.mjs`; `drop-newest`, `capacity: 2`, `maxQueuedRows: 10`, one push per tick, silent worker): `pushes accepted: 2000 of 2000 | depth(): 0 | flush messages in flight: 2000 | rows in flight: 2000`.
- **Expected** from the docs ("A paused or slow consumer therefore cannot grow the queue past `capacity` batches or `maxQueuedRows` rows"): at most 2 batches / 10 rows outstanding, then `false`.
- **Test gap:** `src/worker.protocol.test.tsx:300-340` pushes within one tick against a fake that answers at once.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** one flush in flight; keep buffering under the policy until the worker acknowledges.

#### C269 — Medium — `method: 'resquarify'` is accepted but always lays out as `squarify` after an update

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/treemap-tiling.ts:160-182`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (bf3dbdc). Documented: resquarify across evaluations lays out afresh (ADR 0005: a scene is a pure function of its inputs), listed in Deviations from Vega and pinned by a session test.
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer (also categories 3)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-8` — `core-layout/`

**`method: 'resquarify'` is accepted but always lays out as `squarify` after an update.**

- **Cause:** the remembered rows live in a `WeakMap` keyed by tree nodes, and `stratify` builds new nodes on every evaluation. The memo can only hit when two treemap transforms run over one tree in one evaluation.
- **Observed** (`resquarify.mjs`: 7 leaves, size signals `[600, 400]` then `[200, 900]`):
  - Vega keeps the first layout's rows: `0,0,100,450 | 0,450,100,900 | 100,0,157.1,525`.
  - Aster at the new size: `0,0,200,225 | 0,225,200,450 | 0,450,114.3,712.5`, identical to `squarify`.
  - `resquarify-session.mjs`: a session's second `evaluate` equals a fresh evaluation and differs from Vega.
- This follows from ADR 0005, but `resquarify` appears nowhere in `docs/`.
- **Test note:** `treemap-tiling.test.ts:21` pins a replay path the engine does not reach across evaluations.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** document it as a deviation (and consider removing the memo), or carry the rows across evaluations by row identity.

#### C271 — Medium — An `owner` that is not a DOM node kills the timers it was meant to keep

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/signals.ts:1040-1045`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (0604090). Fixed: liveness is the owner's isConnected only when the owner is a DOM node, otherwise the element of the binding that last took the timer; a non-node owner keeps its timers while that element is shown.
- **Area:** core / signal event loop, transitions
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-signals-10` — `core-signals/`

`packages/core/src/signals.ts:1040-1045`; doc at `:184-188`

**An `owner` that is not a DOM node kills the timers it was meant to keep.** `(owner as Partial<Node>).isConnected ?? el.isConnected` falls back to the `el` of the binding that created the timer. A host that replaces its element disconnects that `el`, and the next tick calls `releaseOwner`.

- **Scenario (`t14.mjs`):** `timer{10}`, element replaced each render. With `owner = container`: 20 ticks in 300 ms. With `owner = new EventTarget()`: `tick = 1`, then `timers.pending() = 0` for good.
- The doc says "its container (or any stable object)".
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** track the live binding's element in the timer state, or type `owner` as `Node`.

#### C274 — Medium — the README's first React chart does not draw at the spec's `width`/`height`

- **Location:** `README.md:83-109`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** docs / README, API, ERRORS (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `docs-api-3` — `docs-api/`

`R/README.md:83-109` (no size prop, no word about size), `R/docs/API.md:813`, `R/packages/core/src/runtime.ts:3721-3730` and `:3756-3759`, `R/packages/react/src/ChartCore.tsx:466-476`.

- **Rule in code.** `viewOverride` returns the measured container for any spec that has no `{signal}` size, declares no `width`/`height` signal, and whose autosize is not `none` (`runtime.ts:3729`: `return drivesSize(chart, 'width') || drivesSize(chart, 'height') ? undefined : measured`). A literal `width: 400, height: 300` is not "driving".
- **Scenario.** The README spec (`width: 400, height: 300`) in `<Chart spec={spec} />`, with ResizeObserver stubbed to report the container:

  | Situation | Rendered `<svg>` size |
  |---|---|
  | container 1000x600 | 1000x600 |
  | block parent with no height (reports the chart's own height, 341) | 1000x341 |
  | `width={400} height={300}` props | 423x322 |
  | `autosize: 'none'` | 400x300 |
  | container 1000x0, or no ResizeObserver | 423x322 (the spec's own size) |

  `ChartCore.tsx:474` ignores a measurement unless `w && h > 0`, so a zero-height parent also discards the width.
- **Expected.** A reader of README, and anyone who knows vega-embed or react-vega, expects 400x300 plus padding everywhere.
- **Wording.** API.md:813 says the measured container "only sizes a spec that has no `width` / `height` signal of its own". In Vega every spec's `width` is a signal, so the sentence reads as "a spec with a width is not resized". The code means "declares one in `signals` or writes `{signal}`".
- **SSR consequence, also unstated.** The server and the first client render draw 423x322, then the first measurement redraws at the container's size, so a hydrated page shifts layout once.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** — `$S/ws/first-run-react.mjs` section 2 (`"svg":"1000x600"`, `"1000x341"`, `"423x322"`, `"400x300"`). The behaviour is deliberate (issue #128 comments); the finding is the documentation and the first-run surprise.

Direction: add one short "Size" paragraph next to the README example and at the top of the `<Chart>` section. It should say the chart fills its container, that `width`/`height` props or `autosize: "none"` keep the spec's size, what a zero-height parent does, and that SSR shifts once. Reword API.md:813 to "declares no `width`/`height` in `signals`".

- **Resolution:** FIXED in #188 (37c91dc). Fixed: dataPulse and StreamBatch.pulse accept diffRows' RowDiff (read by addedRanges/removedRanges); PulseChangeInput and PulseRange exported; compile and stream tests.
