#### C21 — High — The escaping suite's patcher coverage skips the cached-descriptor path and every encode-level channel name; its "every channel" table omits at least nine channels the renderer reads (adds…

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/svg-escaping.test.ts:50-67`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** tests / core (render … stream)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core6-1` — `tests-core6/`

`packages/core/src/svg-escaping.test.ts:50-67` (table), `:119-123` (`withChannel`), `:330-344` (DOM tests); `packages/core/src/dom.ts:483-496`.

- **How the suite builds a hostile scene:** `withChannel` evaluates a fresh `baseScene()` and assigns a value to a field of every node after evaluation. The patch test builds DOM from one such scene and patches with another, unrelated, fresh scene.
- **Why C1 (core-render-1) is out of reach:** `isClean` needs `it.__gen !== CURRENT_GEN` (`dom.ts:483-485`). Every item of a freshly evaluated scene carries the current generation, so `cachedDesc` (`dom.ts:488-496`, `if (isClean(it) && cached) { cached.clean = true; return cached }`) never returns a cached descriptor in this file. No test here uses a session or a string-render-then-patch mount.
- **Values are always strings** (or `[h, h]` for dash). No object-valued channel is tried.
- **The table's claim is false:** the comment at `:50-51` says "Every channel the string renderer (render.ts) and the descriptor builder (dom.ts) read". `render.ts` also reads `href` (`:1088`), `strokeDashOffset` / `strokeMiterLimit` (`:1191-1192`), `fontStyle` (`:1320`), `fontVariant`, `description` (`:1511`), `ariaRole` / `ariaRoleDescription` (`:1518-1519`) and `cssName` (`:1601`). `image` and `__domDesc` are absent too.
- **Run (`svg-gap.mjs`):** I replayed the harness over 17 omitted names, string + fresh DOM + patched.
  - All omitted channels escape correctly today; `href: 'javascript:alert(1)'` drops the `<a>`. No new product defect.
  - Adding `__domDesc` (a descriptor object with `xlink:href="javascript:…"` and `onclick`) to this harness reports "same" structure on all three paths. So the harness as designed would stay green with C1 (core-render-1) present even if the channel were listed.
- **Also:** `describeDiff` (`:171-183`) compares tags, child counts and attribute names only, never values. A `javascript:` value in an existing attribute is invisible to it.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`svg-gap.mjs`) and CONFIRMED-TRACE (lines above).
- **Direction:** add a mode that injects through `encode` in a spec, renders with the string renderer, then patches a second evaluation of the same session. Include object-valued hostile values. Derive the channel table from the renderer rather than by hand.

#### C22 — High — A `tickCount` ≥ 2^32 on a time/utc axis or legend skips the built-in ceiling and exhausts the heap

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/limits.ts:200`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** tests / conformance generators and case tables II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confscripts2-1` — `tests-confscripts2/`
- **Lead's note:** The lead re-ran the `{signal: "1/0"}` form: fatal heap out-of-memory without `limits`; `AsterLimitError` (time ticks) with them. Same family as C9.

`packages/core/src/limits.ts:200`, `packages/core/src/scales.ts:362`, `packages/core/src/time.ts:99-115`; the excluding test is `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-scale-helpers-gen.test.mts:59-61`.

- **Cause.** `ceiling()` returns early for large counts:
  `if (!(n > cap) || (kind !== 'latticeTests' && n >= 4294967296) || ceilingReplaced(...)) return`
  The comment above it says such a count "already fails natively and at once, `Invalid array length`". A tick count is not an array length: on a time scale it selects the finest interval, and `interval.range` (metered only under `limits`) then lists every millisecond of the domain.
- **Scenario** (plain JSON text, no `limits`):
  `{"width":300,"height":40,"scales":[{"name":"x","type":"utc","domain":[1577836800000,1609459200000],"range":"width"}],"axes":[{"orient":"bottom","scale":"x","tickCount":4294967296}]}`

| `tickCount` | Where | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `4294967295` | axis | `AsterLimitError: tickCount 4294967295 > 100000 (built-in ceiling that applies even without limits…)` in 10 ms |
| `4294967296` | axis | `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit … JavaScript heap out of memory` (SIGABRT, 600 MB child) |
| `1e308` | axis | same fatal OOM |
| `1e400` (parses to `Infinity`) | axis | same fatal OOM |
| `1e400` | legend (`"legends":[{"fill":"x","tickCount":1e400}]`) | same fatal OOM |
| `{signal:"1/0"}` | axis, `time` and `utc` | same fatal OOM |

- `0/0` and `-1/0` return normally, and a `linear` scale returns normally for all three non-finite values.
- With `limits: {maxTimeMs: 500, maxItems: 1000}` the `{signal:"1/0"}` case is refused in 13 ms (`maxItems 1024 > 1000 (time ticks)`); the 2^32, `1e308` and `1e400` literals were not run under `limits`.
- **Expected.** The refusal that `docs/LIMITS.md:74` promises ("`items` 100 000 — counts a spec sets: `tickCount` of axes and legends") without `limits`.
- **Vega** dies the same way on 4294967296 and `1e400` (`tickcount-vega.mjs`), so this is Aster's own guarantee failing, not a parity gap.
- **Why no test saw it.** `differential-scale-helpers-gen.test.mts:59-61` removes exactly these inputs: "A NaN or infinite tick count sends d3-time into a loop that allocates without end; the oracle itself does not answer". Like the C132 (core-scale-3) exclusion, it is written down only in the test.
- **Adds to C89 (core-expr-6)** (same early return in `ceiling`). This is a different sink with a worse outcome: process death rather than a wrong length.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `tickcount-time.mjs`, `tickcount-time2.mjs` (accepts a JSON list of `[count, where]`), `tickcount-vega.mjs`.
- **Direction.** Refuse non-finite and ≥ 2^32 counts in `ceiling` for every kind that is not an array length, or drop the early return and let callers that really allocate rely on the native error. Give `interval.range` a ceiling when no meter is active (also C132 (core-scale-3)'s direction). Then remove the test's `unbounded` exclusion and assert the refusal.

- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854). Fixed: scale bins/range, utcSequence, graticule positions, cross, fold, flatten, impute, pivot cells, aggregate cross, kde groups x steps and the regression order are under the built-in ceilings (what they add beyond their input), with or without limits (Q18).

#### C89 — Medium — `sequence()` with a count ≥ 2^32 skips the built-in ceiling and then wraps via `count | 0`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/expression.ts:33-40`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #197 (36c5d6b,fcae061). Fixed: sequence() applies the count ceiling before any wrap (len = ...|0 then boundedCount, negative is RangeError as vega); the finding's claim that vega throws on 2^32+5 is wrong (vega returns 5 items), scratch/fix-a04-expr-signals/seq-vega.mjs.
- **Area:** core / expressions, regex screen
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-expr-6` — `core-expr/`

**`sequence()` with a count ≥ 2^32 skips the built-in ceiling and then wraps.**

- **Cause:** `ceiling` returns early for `n >= 4294967296` on the assumption that such counts fail natively. `numericSequence` then does `const len = count | 0`, which truncates instead of failing.
- **Observed:**
  - `length(sequence(0, 4294967296 + 5))` gives `5`; vega throws `RangeError`.
  - `length(sequence(0, 4294967296 + 3e7))` allocates 30 000 000 elements with no limits and also under `{maxTimeMs: 5000}` (RSS up about 480 MB). The documented ceiling is 1 000 000.
  - With `maxRows` set it is refused.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN, `p1.mjs` and `p4.mjs seq`.
- **Direction:** refuse a non-finite or ≥ 2^32 count explicitly in `numericSequence`; check other `ceiling` callers that truncate afterwards.

#### C93 — Medium — `label` meters only its occupancy bitmap; the canvases and loops around it are unbounded

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/label.ts:168-171`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854). Fixed: AlphaCanvas allots its pixels (pixels ceiling, 16M), label placement labels x spots is bounded as work, and every label loop ticks (field rows, labels, searched cells).
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-4` — `core-layout/`

**`label` meters only its occupancy bitmap; the canvases and loops around it are unbounded.**

- **Cause:** `new AlphaCanvas(width, height)` allocates `width * height` bytes, up to three times, with no meter. `drawField` then loops every pixel. The only meter is `Grid`'s `meterRows` (`label.ts:46`), and the grid is capped near 1e6 cells by its `ratio`.
- **Observed:**
  - `dos.mjs label-size-40k`: `size: [40000, 40000]`, 3 labels, `maxTimeMs: 200` → "ok" after 8 311 ms. RSS stays low on Linux only because untouched zero pages are not committed.
  - `dos.mjs label-size-huge`: `size: [70000, 70000]`, same limits → killed at 100 s.
  - `label-time.mjs 20000 20000 200 nobase`: 20 000 labels, 20 000 `anchor`/`offset` entries, `avoidBaseMark: false` → "ok" after 7 503 ms.
  - In two other runs the overrun was caught only by the bitmap's meter (`maxTimeMs exceeded during label bitmap` after 427 ms and 1 936 ms), which shows the clock is read there and nowhere else.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN.
- **Direction:** meter `width * height` as `cells` before the canvases are made, or draw at the grid's own resolution; `meterTick` per pixel row and per label.

#### C94 — Medium — A round join or cap of a very wide stroke builds millions of points per disk

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/raster-stroke.ts:101-106`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #193 (c93ceb3 04c0854 af50f2f). Fixed: a round join/cap of an immense pen is made as the slice of the disk that faces the canvas (exact inside it, pinned by raster-stroke.test.ts); strokeWidth 1e11/1e17 complete in milliseconds.
- **Area:** core / layout transforms, rasterizer
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-layout-5` — `core-layout/`

**A round join or cap of a very wide stroke builds millions of points per disk.**

- **Cause:** the point count is `PI / acos(1 - TOL / r)`. It is `Infinity` once `1 - TOL / r` rounds to 1 (r above about 4.5e14).
- **Observed:** `dos.mjs wide-round-1e11` (base rect, `strokeWidth: 1e11, strokeJoin: 'round'`, under `label`, `maxTimeMs: 200`) → fatal heap out-of-memory at 1 GB, exit 134. The control `dos.mjs wide-butt` (`strokeWidth: 1e17`, miter joins) is ok in 37 ms.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN for 1e11; CONFIRMED-TRACE for the infinite case (`Math.acos(1 - 5e-17) === 0`).
- **Direction:** cap the disk's segment count and clip the pen radius to the canvas diagonal.

#### C98 — Medium — The parse caches are module-level and bounded by 4096 entries, not by size

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/path-data.ts:130-141`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #200 (2ce7c3b). The path parse caches are bounded by the characters they hold (2^21 per cache) as well as by count; the repro's heap after release fell from 763 MB to 2 MB.
- **Area:** core / hit index, bounds, geometry
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `core-hit-7` — `core-hit/`

**The parse caches are module-level and bounded by 4096 entries, not by size.**
- They keep the path text, its segments and, through WeakMaps keyed on the segments, the flattened polygons.
- Repro `S/cache-mem.mjs` (3000 distinct shape paths × 2000 vertices, one hit-test pass, then everything dropped and `gc()`):
  ```
  path text 88MB (chars) | build+1000 picks 7256ms | heap with the chart alive 861MB
  heap after the scene, the index and every item are unreachable: 763MB
  ```
- A county map (3142 shapes) stays under the 4096 limit, so nothing is ever evicted.
- Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN**. Reading itself is linear: one `L` with 1e6 pairs parses in 751 ms.
- Direction: a byte budget, or per-scene (WeakMap) ownership with the string cache kept for short shared texts.

#### C104 — Medium — the dependency boundary still has holes (continues C40)

- **Location:** `scripts/lib/scan-imports.mjs:70-83`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #187 (1ada289). scanner+classifier+manifest+files checks cover all 7 audit cases; generated table tests
- **Area:** tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tooling-3` — `tooling/`

`scripts/lib/scan-imports.mjs:70-83, 119-126, 146-152, 157-159, 165-171`; `scripts/check-deps.mjs:110-116, 123, 134`

- **Issue.** C40's cases (bare `vega`/`d3`, template literals) are fixed and tested. The header still promises more than the code does ("every import form is covered … A specifier that cannot be resolved statically is itself an error"; ADR 0004: "a forbidden oracle import can never be published"). These pass `check-deps` with exit 0:
  1. `import * as m from 'node:module'; m.createRequire(import.meta.url)('vega')` and `process.getBuiltinModule('module').createRequire(…)('vega')`. `createRequire` as a property name is "name only" (`isNameOnly`, :119-126), and the outer call's callee is a call, not a loader. The header (:14-17) lists `createRequire` as flagged; only the bare identifier is.
  2. `globalThis['require']('d3')` and `module['require']('d3')`. `isLoaderCallee` (:70-83) handles property access, not element access.
  3. `import('https://esm.sh/vega@6')` and `import … from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7/+esm'`. `packageName` returns `null` for `http(s):` (:167). This is the form a browser library would really use to pull Vega at run time.
  4. An npm alias or git dependency: `"dependencies": { "chart-rt": "npm:vega@^6" }` plus `import 'chart-rt'`. The manifest check reads dependency names only (`check-deps.mjs:110-116`), never the ranges.
  5. A relative import into the oracle (`'../../conformance/node_modules/vega/build/vega.js'`): `packageName` returns `null`.
  6. `/// <reference path="…/vega-typings/…d.ts" />` and `declare module 'vega' { … }` in a shipped `.d.ts`. Only `typeReferenceDirectives` are read (:158-159), although the comment on :157 says "and `/// <reference path>`".
  7. Any shipped file outside `dist`: only `src` and `dist` are walked (`check-deps.mjs:123, 134`). `files` is `dist` today, so this is latent (a `bin/` added to `files` would not be scanned).
- **Scenario.** Each case planted in a three-package fixture gives `[deps] dependency boundary holds`, exit 0; expected exit 1.
- **Status.** CONFIRMED-RUN. `$S/scan-imports-repro.mjs` feeds strings to `scanSource`; `$S/check-deps-repro.mjs` runs the real CLI with `--root <fixture>`. The control `import 'vega'` exits 1; cases 1-7 exit 0.
- **Direction.** Treat `createRequire` under any access path and `x['require']` as loaders; ban non-relative URL specifiers in the three packages; resolve `npm:`/git/`file:` ranges in the manifest check; scan every path in `files`; flag relative specifiers that leave the package directory; add each case to `check-deps.test.mjs`.

#### C105 — Medium — the linearity guard for the untrusted-text readers accepts quadratic growth

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/expr-text.test.ts:33-37`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #195 (4f5c42e). Fixed: the linearity guard of the expression-text readers measures per-character cost growth above the timer's noise (bound 8x over 32x the size), with a permanent planted-quadratic case; the old guard passed a quadratic reader.
- **Area:** tests / core (data … hit)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core2-2` — `tests-core2/`

`packages/core/src/expr-text.test.ts:33-37`

- **The guard:** `small = Math.max(at(100_000), 1)` and `expect(big / small).toBeLessThan(40)`.
- **The problem:** the denominator is floored at 1 ms. A reader that takes under 0.4 ms at 100k characters and grows quadratically takes under 40 ms at 1M, which gives a ratio under 40 and passes.
- **Observed** (`expr-text-times.mjs`, built readers, same 14 units × 5 readers):
  - 49 of 70 cases are under 1 ms at 100k; 42 of 70 are under 0.4 ms.
  - The slowest case is 5.7 ms; the largest real `big/small` is 22.3.
  - Planted example: 0.2 ms at 100k → 20 ms at 1M (100×) gives a guard ratio of 20, which passes.
- For the other 28 cases, a 40× bound for a 10× input still accepts growth up to about n^1.6.
- These readers run on spec text (`lexedText`, `namesIn`, `identifiersIn`, `datasetsReadIn`, `scalesReadIn`); the file header calls the bound a safety property.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** measure at sizes where every reader is well above timer noise (for example 1M and 8M), drop the 1 ms floor, and bound the ratio near the size ratio; or count work (a step counter) instead of time.

`packages/core/src/limits.ts:547-585` (`checkSpecLimits` walk; `visited` at :569 feeds only the clock), `docs/LIMITS.md:79`, `packages/core/src/limits.test.ts:37-39`.

**The README says the "Throws" list is complete; at least nine schema-valid features are refused and not on it.**

README: "The list is what `compile` refuses today … a feature that vega-lite supports and is not here compiles to the same Vega." Each row below is schema-valid, compiles and renders in vega-lite, and is absent from the list:

| Feature | Refusal | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Any selection (brush, `bind: "scales"` zoom, point, legend) whose projected field is escaped or nested (`sepal\.length`, `o.k`) | `a selection cannot be projected over the nested or escaped field` | `validate.ts:701-707`, `compile.ts:8792` |
| `order` as an array of field defs | `order cannot be an array` (false: the schema allows `OrderFieldDef[]`) | `validate.ts:960` |
| `resolve.scale` / `resolve.legend: independent` for colour, size and similar in a facet | `not supported yet (independent x and y scales are)` | `validate.ts:776-779` |
| `resolve` on a plain unit spec (vega-lite ignores it) | `` `resolve` has no meaning on a single unit spec `` | `validate.ts:770` |
| `align` / `bounds` / `center` / `spacing` on a plain unit | `only meaningful on composition specs` | `validate.ts:288-292` |
| Param names that are not identifiers (`"my-param"`, `"my brush"`) | `parameter names must be identifiers` | `validate.ts:584` |
| `bind: {element: "#slider"}`, `bind.event`, any `bind.input` outside the fixed list | `unsupported input type undefined` / `unknown bind property "event"` | `validate.ts:621-624` |
| `lookup.from.data` that is a generator (`sequence`, `sphere`, `graticule`) | ``needs `values`, `url` or `name` `` | `validate.ts:1446-1449` |
| `config.axisQuantitative`, `axisTemporal`, `axisDiscrete`, `axisPoint`, typed `axisX*` / `axisY*`, `config.locale`, `config.params` | `valid Vega-Lite but is not supported` | `validate.ts:420-434` (the README never states the supported list) |

- **Most consequential row:** the first. Zoom/pan or a brush on a scatter of a dotted column is refused while the README lists "dotted/escaped/bracketed field names" as supported.
- **Also refused but not schema-valid:** `type: "Quantitative"` / `"q"`, which vega-lite's compiler accepts (`validate.ts:978`).
- **Guard is one-directional:** `readme-refusals.test.ts` checks that phrases in a hand-written table appear in the README and are refused. Nothing enumerates what `validate.ts` refuses, so an unlisted refusal cannot fail it, although its header comment claims otherwise.
- **Two smaller holes in the guard:** `LIST` is sliced up to `## Known runtime gaps`, so a phrase in "Known compiler gaps" satisfies it; and `toThrow(VLCompileError)` passes on a refusal for an unrelated reason.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `valid.mjs`, `valid2.mjs`, `x2.mjs`, `names.mjs` (lines print `schema-valid | VL-OK | ASTER-THROW(…)`).
- **Direction:** weaken the sentence, or tag every `fail()` that refuses valid vega-lite and have the test diff the tags against the README. Fix the `order` message.

  ```
  <SvgChart> bars + legend    SUSPENDED (fallback rendered)
  ```
  Without the `browser` condition all four render synchronously.
- **Dev/prod divergence:** `suspend-parts.mjs` imports `react/dist/index.js` unbundled under the same condition and nothing suspends. `index.js` re-exports `session.js`, which imports `@aster-charts/core/dom`, which fills every slot. That this is what Vite dev does is my inference, not run: PLAUSIBLE.
- **No ADR** records the engine-parts decision, which reverses 0007's rationale. ADR 0003 decision 1 ("serializes the full SVG on its first render, on both server and client") is stale for the same reason.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-RUN for the Node observations.
- **Direction:** a new ADR that supersedes the "nothing loads asynchronously" clause of 0007; fix ARCHITECTURE:355 and :438; state in API docs that a browser build needs a `<Suspense>` boundary or `@aster-charts/react/all`.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `docs-api-6`, scripts `docs-api/`, CONFIRMED (run); "outside a browser build every part is always there" is false under the `browser` condition without bundling):

`R/docs/API.md:803-804` ("Outside a browser build (a server render, a test runner) every part is always there and none of this changes anything"), `R/packages/react/README.md:30-35`, `R/packages/core/package.json` (`./lean` → `browser: ./dist/lean.js`).

- **Scenario.** `import { SvgChart } from '@aster-charts/react/lite'` in a runtime that resolves with the `browser` export condition but does not bundle, then `renderToString(<Suspense><SvgChart spec={spec with a legend and a log scale}/></Suspense>)`.
- **Observed with `node --conditions=browser`.** `<!--$!--><template data-msg="Switched to client rendering because the server rendering aborted due to: ...` (the chart suspended on a part). With default conditions: full svg markup.
- **Why `<Chart>` is unaffected.** `<Chart>` from the root entry is fine only because `dist/index.js` also loads `ssr.js`, which imports the full `@aster-charts/core` and fills the slots as a side effect. Observed: svg markup under both conditions.
- **Which tools do this.** From their documentation, `jest-environment-jsdom` sets `customExportConditions: ['browser']` by default, and edge/worker SSR toolchains resolve `browser`/`worker` conditions. I did not run Jest or such a toolchain, so that part is **PLAUSIBLE**.

Status: **CONFIRMED-RUN** for the mechanism — `$S/ws/browser-condition-lite.mjs` and `$S/ws/browser-condition.mjs`, each run with and without `--conditions=browser`.

Direction: say "a resolver that applies the `browser` condition" instead of "a browser build", and name the remedy for tests and edge SSR (`import '@aster-charts/react/all'`, or `await preloadParts()`). Alternatively, key the lean/full split on something other than `browser`.

- **Location:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:328`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #196 (eb38636). Fixed (docs): ARCHITECTURE lists the empty-ring, string-coordinate, copy-handle and deep-signal deviations and rewords 'No state outlives a call' to what holds.

`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:328,331`; `geo-path.ts:253-258`; `geo-sphere-measures.ts:47-50,233-238,362-364`; `geo-events.ts:25-29`; `geo-path.ts:43-45`; `geo-projections.ts:143`.

- **Exceptions found.**
  - C149 (core-geo-3) (a different writer) and C154 (core-geo-8).
  - Empty rings. The planar measures of an identity or absent projection, and the three spherical measures, give a clean deterministic result. d3 instead closes the ring onto state left by an earlier ring or call. This is the only residue in `fuzz.mjs` (`centroid:identity`, `measure:identity`, `area:identity`).

- **State.** The buffer pool (`free`, `keptEvents`), the circle-text cache, the shared `scratch` and `GeoPath.sink` (left set when `feed` throws) all outlive a call. None caused a wrong result in testing, and I found no double release. The sentence is still wrong as written.

#### C376 — Medium — The demo app mis-describes itself and models patterns a newcomer should not copy (no `<Suspense>`, ref-derived `dataChanges`, legacy brush props, stale hero figures)

- **Location:** `apps/demo/README.md:9`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Area:** docs / ARCHITECTURE, ADRs, CHANGELOG, demo (also categories 8)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `docs-arch-10` — `docs-arch/`

- **Wrong description:** `README.md:9` and `VegaPane.tsx:10-11` say Vega-Lite is compiled by `@aster-charts/vl` for both columns. `App.tsx:116` hands `spec={s.raw}` to vega-embed, which compiles with official vega-lite. `App.tsx:374` says so correctly. The `compiled` field of `SPECS` (`App.tsx:454-473`) is never read.
- **No `<Suspense>` around any `<Chart>`:** the page works in a production build only because of C82 (docs-arch-1). A newcomer who copies a card without the streaming section gets a legend chart that suspends with no boundary.
- **Fragile `dataChanges` pattern:** `App.tsx:397` derives it from a ref read during render. If `data` ever differs at a row the hint does not name, the chart silently keeps the stale row:
  ```
  2 rows changed, dataChanges names only [4] -> [50,50,50,50,22,50] (fresh would be [50,50,11,50,22,50]) warnings: 0
  ```
  That is the documented contract (API.md:109-111), but the example gives no warning, and a new array without the hint would be safe. Reachability in the demo itself is low.
- **Legacy props on a spec with its own selection:** `App.tsx:443` uses `onSelect`/`brush` (INTERACTION.md:78 calls them legacy) on a spec with its own `brush` interval param; INTERACTION.md:124 says the two do not talk. Not run in a browser: PLAUSIBLE.
- **`width={0}`:** `showcase.tsx:28-36` compiles each Vega-Lite spec a second time for its size and passes `width={0}` (and `height={0}`) for concat/facet specs. Harmless for those layouts (`demo-zero-size.mjs`: same 409×151 and 557×202 SVG), but a bad pattern to copy.
- **Stale comment:** `main.tsx:3-5` says geo is not used; `showcase.tsx:3` and `App.tsx:27` import it. Continues prior D43.
- **Stale hero figures:** `App.tsx:560-564,574` say "1,055/1,055", "205 kB", "400+ spec corpus"; the corpus is 1063 and CHANGELOG 0.4.2 says `<Chart>` is 181.7. Continues prior D2; the README now disclaims them.
- **Clean:** no deep imports into `src`/`dist`, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no CDN (vega-embed is an npm dependency in a lazy chunk), `wrangler.toml` has no account id, `vite.config.ts` has no alias.
- **Status:** CONFIRMED-TRACE, plus `demo-datachanges.mjs`, `demo-sizes.mjs`, `demo-zero-size.mjs`.

#### C380 — Medium — A derived dataset that opens with a sort re-orders its source in Vega; Aster does not, and the deviation is recorded only in a test comment

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-sort-ties.test.mts:53-55`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Area:** tests / conformance generators and case tables II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confscripts2-3` — `tests-confscripts2/`

`packages/conformance/scripts/differential-sort-ties.test.mts:53-55`; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:583-612` (not listed)

- **The exclusion.** "a dataset made from another that opens with a sort sorts the rows of its source in place: vega's own aliasing, which is not reproduced; a step before the sort avoids it". The generator then unshifts a `formula` before every derived dataset's transforms, so the shape is never drawn.
- **Scenario** (`source-sort-alias-line.mjs`): `d0` = `[{x:0,y:90,k:3},{x:50,y:10,k:1},{x:100,y:50,k:2}]`, an unused dataset `{name:'sorted', source:'d0', transform:[{type:'collect', sort:{field:'k'}}]}`, and a `line` mark over `d0`.
  - Vega: `M50,10L100,50L0,90`
  - Aster: `M0,90L50,10L100,50`
  - Without the derived dataset both give `M0,90L50,10L100,50`.
- `source-sort-alias.mjs` shows the same for text marks: document order `1,2,0` in Vega, `0,1,2` in Aster.
- **Why it matters.** Deriving a sorted copy of a dataset is a common idiom, and a line, area or trail over the source then differs from Vega. Aster's result is the saner one, but `ARCHITECTURE.md:585` says every deliberate difference "is listed here". The "Input mutation" row names only `joinaggregate` and `window`.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction.** Add the row to the Deviations table. Check whether any corpus or gallery spec has this shape; if one does, the pixel gate is silently pinning one side.

#### C735 — Low — a trail with a negative `size` throws a bare `Error` from every renderer and the hit index; not in `docs/ERRORS.md`

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/geometry-differential.testlib.ts:152-165`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)

- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core2-5` — `tests-core2/`

This is a product behaviour revealed by `packages/core/src/geometry-differential.testlib.ts:152-165`, where `tryBoth` counts "both throw the same message" as no difference.

- **In the differential:** 63 of the 800 hand-built scenes (seeds 1–400, both variants) throw `negative radius: …` in svg, dom, dom-dense, canvas, hit and label-draw; only bounds runs (`throws-entry.ts` → `throws-bundle.mjs`). Those scenes compare an error message and nothing else. All 63 trace to a trail item with a negative `size` (`negrad-entry.ts`).
- **Through the public API** (`negative-trail.mjs`): a trail with rows `s: 6, -2, 4` and `size: { field: 's' }`:
  - `aster renderSpec: THROWS Error: negative radius: -1`
  - `aster hit index: THROWS Error: negative radius: -1`
  - `vega toSVG: REJECTS Error: negative radius: -1`
- Aster matches Vega here, so this is not a deviation. The error is a plain `Error`, not an Aster error class; nothing is logged; `docs/ERRORS.md` has no "negative radius" entry. In Aster the hit index throws too.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** add the row to `docs/ERRORS.md`, and pin it with a named test instead of leaving it implicit in a fuzz. Whether to keep Vega's crash is the owner's call.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `tests-core4-9`, scripts `tests-core4/`, CONFIRMED (run); 7.9% of the random scenes throw `negative radius` in the renderers: for those, SVG, hit and label-draw compare only an error message):

`packages/core/src/geometry-differential.testlib.ts:152-162` (`tryBoth`: equal messages → no diff); `packages/core/src/geometry-scenes.testlib.ts:72` (trail `size` from `wild(r, 20)`, negative 10% of the time).

Observed (`S/g-vacuity.mjs`): 63 of 800 scenes throw in `renderSceneToSvg`, `buildHitIndex` and `drawMark` alike, every time with `negative radius: <n>` from `ArcPathWriter.arc`. 31 of those in `S/c-workload.out` are "finite" scenes.

- One negative trail size voids the whole scene for those consumers.
- The throw itself matches d3-path and Vega.
- The remaining scenes are not vacuous: 31% of probes hit an item and 55% of intersect boxes are non-empty.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

Direction: keep one dedicated negative-size case and clamp the generator elsewhere; count "both threw" and bound it.

#### C763 — Low — the "DST-straddling" date set never crosses either 2024 transition and has no fractional second, so the `%Z`, `%L` and `%f` groups are inert for what they suggest

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:301-308`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #189 (d275b19,ffde8e6). Fixed: dstDates gains post-gap, second-01:30, gap/repeat-landing and ms instants, comment corrected; %Z varies within both transition days, %L/%f not constant, skipped/repeated hour parsed
- **Area:** closure / vega-format vectors
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-vecfmt-b-2` — `w3-vecfmt-b/`

`packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:301-308` (comment and `dstDates`); evidence in `packages/core/testdata/vectors/vega-format.json:2811-2920` (`%Z`), `:4131-4240` (`%L`), `:4241-4350` (`%f`).

- **Scenario:** the generator says "Timestamps chosen to straddle the 2024 US transitions (2024-03-10 02:00 local, 2024-11-03 02:00 local) plus an ambiguous/absolute pair for each".
- **Observed for the March pair:** `05:30Z` and `06:30Z` are 00:30 and 01:30 EST. Both are before the spring transition at 07:00Z.
- **Observed for the November pair:** `04:30Z` and `05:30Z` are 00:30 and 01:30 EDT. Both are before the fall-back at 06:00Z, and neither is the repeated 01:30 EST.
- **Consequence in the file:** `%Z` is `-0500, -0500, -0500` for the three March dates and `-0400, -0400, -0400` for the three November dates. The offset never changes within a transition day; DST is seen only through January versus July.
- **Fractional seconds:** all 11 dates have a zero millisecond part, so `%L` is `"000"` ×11 and `%f` is `"000000"` ×11. These are constant-want groups, like `%%` and `%C`.
- **Planted bugs** (`mutant.mjs`):
  - M3, which takes the offset from the local day's midnight: 0 of 352 fail, yet it prints `-0500` instead of `-0400` at `2024-03-10T07:30Z` and `-0400` instead of `-0500` at `2024-11-03T06:30Z`.
  - M2, where `%L`/`%f` drop the fraction: 0 of 352 fail, yet it prints `"000"` instead of `"123"`.
- **Parse side:** the only `localeTimeParse` case after a transition is `:5763-5772` (`2024-03-10T14:30:45` → EDT, correct). There is no parse of the skipped hour (`02:30` on Mar 10) or of the repeated hour (`01:30` on Nov 3).
- **Mitigation:** `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-time-format.test.mts` (live) covers `%L`, `%f` and DST. The port matches upstream on my post-transition, repeated-hour and non-zero-millisecond probes in four zones.
- **Shared cause:** the same `dstDates` feed `vega-time.json`, which belongs to the `w3-time-*` lanes. The comment is wrong for those suites too.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`verify.mjs` prints the local time and offset of each date; `mutant.mjs`).
- **Direction:** add `2024-03-10T07:30:00Z`, `2024-11-03T06:30:00Z` and one instant with milliseconds (e.g. `…:00.123Z`) to `dstDates`; add the skipped-hour and repeated-hour strings to `localeTimeParse`; fix the comment.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `w3-time-b-2`, scripts `w3-time-b/`, CONFIRMED (run); the "DST-straddling" dates all sit before the transitions; no vector input is after the spring gap or in the repeated autumn hour):

`packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:301-308`; consumed by `timeFloor` (`vega-time.json:16645-23638` in my range), `dayofyear` (`:15961-16066`) and `week` (`:16067-16172`).

- **The comment.** "Timestamps chosen to straddle the 2024 US transitions (2024-03-10 02:00 local, 2024-11-03 02:00 local) plus an ambiguous/absolute pair for each."
- **Observed in New York (`verify.mjs`).**
  - `2024-03-10T05:30Z` is 00:30 EST and `06:30Z` is 01:30 EST; the spring transition is at 07:00Z, so both are before it.
  - `2024-11-03T04:30Z` is 00:30 EDT and `05:30Z` is 01:30 EDT; the autumn transition is at 06:00Z, so both are before it. `05:30Z` is the first occurrence of 01:30; the second (`06:30Z`) is absent.
- **Consequence.** No `timeFloor`, `dayofyear` or `week` vector takes an input on a transition day after the offset changed. The upstream quirk that a floor in the repeated hour lands before the transition is not pinned: `timeFloor(['year','month','date','hours'])(2024-11-03T06:30Z)` → `05:00Z`, 90 minutes back.
- **What does cross the transitions.** The `timeSequence` vectors (hours over 2024-03-08…13 at `:12708-13205`, date step 2 at `:13976-14015`, hours step 6 over 2024-11-01…06 at `:14016-14111`) and the `timeOffset` suite. Those are sound.
- **No product defect.** `dst-sweep.mjs` compared 18,894 floor / offset / sequence / dayofyear / week calls in a ±4 h window around both transitions, with 22 unit lists and steps undefined/2/3/5: 0 differences between the built `packages/core/dist/time.js` and vega-time 3.2.1. The repeated-hour quirk above is reproduced identically.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `verify.mjs`, `dst-sweep.mjs`.
- **Direction.** Add `2024-03-10T07:30:00Z` and `2024-11-03T06:30:00Z` to `dstDates`, or correct the comment.

`packages/conformance/src/raster-shapes.ts:18` (cross-reference; it is the source of the first eight fixture entries)

- **Comment:** "a circle moved down by a sixteenth of a pixel at a time: its vertices move a quarter of a pixel at a time".

#### C334 — Medium — The canvas/SVG corpus parity test silently skips 42 of 391 specs, covers no Vega-Lite spec, and has no floor on passes

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/canvas.test.ts:626-631`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #190 (a98fe89 d26d040). canvas, geometry-differential, geometry-no-parse and hit corpus loops load the add-ons, skip only the two url-data specs (named, asserted) and rethrow the rest; counts and per-mark floors added; Vega-Lite corpus declared out of scope for core (banner corrected).
- **Area:** tests / core (a11y … curves)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core1-1` — `tests-core1/`

`packages/core/src/canvas.test.ts:626-631` (the `catch { continue }`), `:612` (the only floor: `names.length > 250`), `:652` (`failures.length === 0`), `:535-536` (the banner says "vega + vega-lite corpus scenes"), `:543` (only `.vg.json` is listed).

- **Scenario.** The test evaluates each spec with `sceneOf(spec)` and continues on any throw. The vitest setup installs `parts-all` and `part-canvas` but no add-on, so every spec needing geo, the transforms add-on or a loaded URL is dropped without being counted.
- **Observed** (`a-corpus-skips.ts`): `corpus files 1063; .vg.json 391; .vl.json 672; evaluated 349; skipped by catch 42`. Breakdown of the 42:
  - 20× "uses a geo projection; load the addon first"
  - 18× "uses the <q> transform; load the addon first" (force, geopath, kde2d/isocontour, label, …)
  - 2× URL datasets not loaded
  - 2× add-on expression functions
- A further 3 specs are excluded by name (`:619`, `:623`).
- **Expected.** A test titled "matches across the vega corpus" should either load the add-ons or assert how many specs it compared. As written, `pass` is computed and never asserted: if `compileChart` threw for every spec, the test would still pass with `pass = 0`.
- **Consequence.** No geoshape, contour, label or force scene, and no Vega-Lite-compiled scene, gets unit-level canvas-vs-SVG parity. Only the Chromium gates cover them.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `a-corpus-skips.ts`, output above.
- **Direction.** Import the add-ons in this file (or use `loadAddonsFor`), catch only the "no data was loaded" case by name, assert `pass >= N`, and either include `.vl.json` through the compiler or correct the banner.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `tests-core2-3`, scripts `tests-core2/`, CONFIRMED (run); corpus loops skip every geo and add-on spec, and never read the Vega-Lite corpus):

- `packages/core/src/geometry-differential.test.ts:42-59` (`try { … } catch { continue }` at `:55`; the only floor is the file count at `:46`)
- `packages/core/src/geometry-no-parse.test.ts:63-77` (`catch { continue }` at `:70` and `:72`)
- `packages/core/src/hit.test.ts:182-200`

**What happens:**
- `scripts/vitest-core-parts.setup.mjs` loads `parts-all` and `part-canvas` but no add-on, and these files import none. Every spec that needs one throws "load the addon first" and is skipped without a count.
- `geometry-no-parse.test.ts` has `vi.mock`, so the setup skips it; it loads the two part files itself.
- The filter is `.vg.json` only, so the 672 `.vl.json` specs are never read.
- `corpus-vega-only` holds only a README, so that half of the `CORPUS` list is empty.

**Observed** (`corpus-skips.mjs`, same parts, no add-ons): `{ files: 391, thrown: 42, emptyIndex: 1, checked: 348 }`.
- 20 of the 42 are "this spec uses a geo projection".
- The rest are geopath, force, label, pack, kde2d, contour, tree, treemap, sunburst, the `t-*` add-on transforms and the two `data-url-*` specs.

**Consequence:** the legacy-vs-new geometry differential, the no-parse guard and the hit test compare no projected `shape` mark, no geoshape and no label-transform output from the corpus, while their headers say "the vega corpus". A change that made 300 more specs throw would still pass `geometry-differential.test.ts`.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

**Direction:** import `./addon-transforms.js` and `./addon-geo.js` in these files (as `escaped-names.test.ts:9-10` does), assert `evaluated === CORPUS.length` minus a named allow-list, and compile the `.vl.json` specs through `@aster-charts/vl` or state plainly that they are out of scope.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `tests-core4-4`, scripts `tests-core4/`, CONFIRMED (run); The corpus half of the differential skips 42 of 391 specs silently, including every geo and add-on spec, and nothing floors what was compared):

`packages/core/src/geometry-differential.test.ts:55` (`catch { continue }`), `:46` (the only floor: `CORPUS.length > 300`, a count of files).

Observed (`S/c-workload.mjs` → `S/c-workload.out`): `corpus: 391, corpusSkipped: 42, corpusNoLeafItems: 5`.

| Skip reason | Specs |
|---|---|
| "uses a geo projection; load the addon first" | 20 |
| "uses the … transform; load the addon first" | 18 |
| "calls the expression function …; load the addon first" | 2 |
| "has a url but no data was loaded" | 2 |

- The vitest setup installs engine parts, not add-ons, so every projection, force, contour or voronoi scene is dropped.
- Corpus items actually compared: area 636, rect 527, line 500, symbol 202, text 59, arc 53, rule 22, trail 8, **shape 2, path 2, image 2**, geoshape 0.
- Only `.vg.json` files are read: 391 of the 1,063 corpus cases.
- The same silent `catch` is at `:83`, `:88` and `:110`. Those skipped nothing today (`randomSpecSkipped: 0`, `transitionSkipped: 0`), but nothing asserts that.

Expected of "the vega corpus … every consumer": geo paths, the main producer of `shape` marks, are compared, or the skip is counted and bounded.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**

Direction: load the add-ons (`loadAddonsFor`) before evaluating, count skips, and assert a ceiling and a per-marktype floor.

#### C335 — Medium — The parity recorder in `canvas.test.ts` is blind to eight kinds of paint difference and rejects a correct rotated symbol

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/canvas.test.ts:50-53`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #190 (a98fe89). Parity recorder keeps full graphics state, clip, rotation, strokeText, drawImage and every line property; SVG side reads transform lists, clipPaths, cap/join/miter/dashoffset, blend, stroked text, images; a pair test shows all eight blind spots are now seen and a correct rotated symbol is no difference.
- **Area:** tests / core (a11y … curves)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core1-2` — `tests-core1/`

`packages/core/src/canvas.test.ts:50-53` (the transform is a translation only), `:85` (`clip()` is a no-op), `:100` (`rotate` is recorded only for text), `:108` (`drawImage` is a no-op), `:127-129` (cap, join and miter limit are plain fields nobody reads), `:166-170` (`parseTranslate` matches only a transform that is exactly `translate(...)`), `:504` (the test "applies group translates and clips").

- **Scenario.** I copied the helpers verbatim (lines 19-394) and compared the SVG of scene A with the canvas records of scene B, where A and B paint differently. A result of zero diffs means the helper cannot see the difference.
- **Observed** (`f-parity-blind.ts`):

| Pair (A vs B) | SVG(A) vs canvas(B) diffs | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| path mark angle 0 vs 40 | 0 | blind |
| group clip on vs off | 0 | blind |
| mark-level clip on vs off | 0 | blind |
| strokeCap butt vs round | 0 | blind |
| strokeJoin miter vs bevel | 0 | blind |
| strokeDashOffset 0 vs 3 | 0 | blind |
| blend none vs multiply | 0 | blind |
| text stroke none vs red | 0 | blind |
| image present vs absent | 0 | blind |
| rect fill colour (control) | 2 | seen |
| rect cornerRadius 0 vs 4 (control) | 2 | seen |
| text baseline, text angle, gradient stops | 2 each | seen |

- **False positive.** A single correct rotated symbol compared with itself gives 2 diffs: the SVG's `translate(..) rotate(..)` is not parsed, so the helper places the SVG path at the origin.
- **Why the corpus still passes** (`h-corpus-features.ts`): of the 349 scenes evaluated, none has a rotated symbol or path, blend, dash offset, non-default cap or join, or stroked text. Four have a clip (`bar-clip`, `group-nobound`, `group-paint-clip`, …) and one has an image; the test cannot see either.
- **Name that lies.** "applies group translates and clips" (`:504`) checks only the translate.
- **Expected.** A parity oracle either records the full graphics state, as `canvas-record.testlib.ts` largely does, or states what it excludes.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `f-parity-blind.ts`, `h-corpus-features.ts`.
- **Direction.** Replace `makeRecordingCtx` with the testlib recorder once C336 (tests-core1-3) is fixed, parse the full SVG transform, record the clip on both sides, and rename the clip test or make it assert the clip.

#### C336 — Medium — The paint recorder behind the append and same-pixels oracles cannot see text rotation, blend, dash offset, stroked text or images

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/canvas-record.testlib.ts:128`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #190 (9bb0e46). Testlib recorder keys text on the full matrix and records blend, dash offset, strokeText and drawImage; canvas-record.test.ts shows 10 pairs unseen by the old recorder are seen.
- **Area:** tests / core (a11y … curves)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core1-3` — `tests-core1/`

`packages/core/src/canvas-record.testlib.ts:128` (`fillText` keys on the device anchor plus `styleKey`; the matrix's rotation is not in the key), `:80-86` (`styleKey` has no `globalCompositeOperation` and no `lineDashOffset`). The context has no `strokeText` or `drawImage` method, so the painter's `if (ctx.strokeText)` guard at `canvas.ts:1048` skips stroked text.

Users: `canvas-append-oracle.test.ts`, `canvas-same-pixels.test.ts`, `canvas-regressions.test.ts`.

- **Scenario.** Two scenes that paint differently are rendered through `makeRecorder` and compared both ways the tests compare: `diffPaintMultisets` (append oracle) and `JSON.stringify` (same-pixels).
- **Observed** (`g-recorder-blind.ts`):

| Pair | Multiset (append oracle) | JSON (same-pixels) |
|---|---|---|
| fill colour (control) | seen | seen |
| text angle 0 vs 30 | blind | blind |
| blend none vs multiply | blind | blind |
| strokeDashOffset 0 vs 3 | blind | blind |
| text stroke none vs red | blind | blind |
| image present vs absent | blind | blind |
| strokeCap, gradient direction, group clip, symbol angle | seen | seen |
| paint order of two overlapping rects | blind | seen |

- **Why it matters.** Text rotation is in the generated input: `scene-fuzz.testlib.ts:65` gives 40% of text marks `angle: datum.v * 3`, and `edit` operations change `v`. A stale rotation after an in-place edit, or an appended label painted at the wrong angle, is therefore invisible to "canvas append paint === full repaint".
- **Mitigation already in the product.** `paintsSameAs` compares every key except a deny-list (`canvas.ts:449`), so I found no product bug hiding here. The gap is in the oracle's power.
- **Paint order** is a documented exclusion (file header of the append oracle); the others are not.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `g-recorder-blind.ts`.
- **Direction.** Put the rotation (or the full matrix) into the text record; add `globalCompositeOperation` and `lineDashOffset` to `styleKey`; give the recorder `strokeText` and `drawImage` that emit records.

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/hit.test.ts:181-219`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #195 (0923f0f fdcd40c b938cad). Fixed: HitIndexOptions.strategy ('auto'|'scan'|'grid') lets the corpus test and the legacy differential build the grid by name; 348 scenes x 3 grids vs the scan, 13 531 probes, planted grid bugs fail.

`packages/core/src/hit.test.ts:181-219`

#### C339 — Medium — The shrinker prints a "minimal" step list that does not reproduce a final-audit failure

- **Location:** `packages/core/src/incremental-oracle.test.ts:752`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Area:** tests / core (incremental oracle, legacy copies I)
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-core3-7` — `tests-core3/`

`packages/core/src/incremental-oracle.test.ts:752`, `:1060-1061`.

**Scenario.** A retained scene from step 2 is mutated by step 9 and caught only by `finalAudit`.
- `finalAudit` reports `fail(old.step, 'final audit', …)`, so `f.step` is 2.
- `checkSeed` shrinks `steps.slice(0, f.step + 1)`, which cuts off steps 3..9, including the one that mutated the scene.
- No trial fails, so `shrink` returns the truncated list unchanged.
- `run(minimal).failure ?? f` silently falls back to the original failure.

The report then shows "minimal steps (3): …" next to "minimal failure: step 2 (final audit)" for a list that passes. `ASTER_ORACLE_SEED=<seed>` still reproduces.

Two smaller effects:
- `fails` accepts any failure, so a shrink can end on a different bug (both lines are printed, so it is visible).
- Step indices drive `stepNo % 3` (read order, `:734`) and `i % 3 === 1` (re-evaluate, `:860`), so dropping a step changes what later steps do.

**Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE** (lines quoted above).

**Direction.** Report the detecting step for the final audit; require the same `where` during the shrink; print whether the minimal list was re-verified.

#### C350 — Medium — every worker fake answers at once; four skip the clone boundary; none holds a stream flush (adds to the test-gap notes of C77 (react-hooks-4) / C244 (react-hooks-6) and report line 7160)

Fixed: one testing/fake-worker.ts (clones both ways, later-turn answers, hold/release fifo or reverse, silent, error/messageerror, terminate) replaces the seven fakes; new tests for out-of-order answers, a held stream flush and a silent worker with unmount (planted apply-last-arrival fails).
- **Area:** tests / react II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-react2-3` — `tests-react2/`

Seven separate `FakeWorker` classes:

| File | Lines | `structuredClone` | Can hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Chart.stream.test.tsx` | 34-48 | yes | no |
| `ChartStream.test.tsx` | 24-35 | no | no |
| `hooks.spec-swap.test.tsx` | 104-116 | no | no |

| `worker.protocol.test.tsx` | 27-52 | yes | yes (`hold`/`release`) |
| `worker.test.tsx` | 44-57 | no | no |

- Each runs the real handler synchronously inside `postMessage` and delivers in one `queueMicrotask`. The worker therefore always acknowledges before the next tick, never reorders, and is never slow or silent.

#### C353 — Medium — The spec-level scale differentials draw no literal-as-signal, no case variant of `type` and no hostile `bins`/tick count (adds to C133 (core-scale-5), C288 (core-scale-6))

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-scale-spec-gen.test.mts:112-145`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (traced)
- **Area:** tests / conformance generators and case tables II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-confscripts2-5` — `tests-confscripts2/`

`packages/conformance/scripts/differential-scale-spec-gen.test.mts:112-145`, `differential-scale-spec.test.mts:20`, `scale-spec-cases.mjs:543-610`, `differential-scale-helpers-gen.test.mts:187-198`

- **`{signal: "true"|"false"|"null"}` (C133 (core-scale-5)).**
  - `scale-spec-cases.mjs` has 29 distinct `signal:` texts: 27 declared names plus `'[5, 6]'` and `'0/0'`. No literal.
  - Its 700-case seeded section ("any type x domain form x range form x option set", `:541-542`) writes every option as a literal value: `s.zero = chance(0.5)`, `s.nice = pick([true, 3, 8, …])`, `s.clamp = true`. Never `{signal}`.
  - `scale-spec-gen` draws `domainImplicit` and `padding` as literals; its signals appear only in domain and sort positions and are always declared names.
  - Had one been drawn it would have failed: Vega builds the scale, Aster returns no scale, which the test reads as `{$:'throw'}`.
- **Upper-case `type` (C288 (core-scale-6)).**
  - Both pools take types from fixed lower-case lists (`scale-spec-cases.mjs:553`, `scale-spec-gen:113`). The only unknown type is `'cubic'`.
  - `scale-helpers-gen:187-198` does test `'LINEAR'`, `'Linear'`, `'band '` against vega-scale, but at the registry, where both sides return `undefined`. The defect is in the spec reader (`scales.ts:421,431`), so that check is true and beside the point.
  - `differential-transform-names` does this properly for transform types; there is no counterpart for scale types (nor for projection or mark types).
- **`bins: {step}` and tick counts.** The `bins` suite uses steps 1.5 to 20 over domains ≤ 100. A differential cannot assert the unbounded case because Vega dies too, and none of the 29 files runs either engine under `limits` or asserts a ceiling.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-TRACE** (pools read; `signal:` texts enumerated by grep).
- **Direction.** In the seeded section wrap each option in `{signal: <literal text>}` with some probability, including `'true'`, `'false'`, `'null'`, `'1/0'`. Draw `type` through the four spellings `transform-names` uses. Add a ceiling test (Aster-only, expected refusal) fed by the inputs these files exclude.

#### C355 — Medium — `check()` cannot see interaction wiring: event types, `bind`, `interactive`, `cursor`

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/test/vl-compiler-parity.test.ts:903-916`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** tests / conformance suites I
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-conftest1-4` — `tests-conftest1/`

`packages/conformance/test/vl-compiler-parity.test.ts:903-916`; `packages/conformance/test/vl-expressions.ts:22`

39 `GROUPS` cases have `params` (18 with `select`, 6 with `bind`), several of them about selections (`:741-743`, `:766`, `:1056-1147`). I planted differences in vega-lite's own output for a point selection + slider spec and ran `check()` on them:

| Planted difference | Result |
|---|---|
| every object-form event stream listens to `dblclick` | passes |
| the slider `bind` removed | passes |
| the slider `bind` given another range | passes |
| the mark set `interactive: false` | passes |
| the `cursor` changed | passes |
| control: a constant changed in an expression | caught |
| selection `on` handlers dropped, tooltip dropped, `href` changed, store values dropped | caught |

Cause: `EXPR_KEYS` compares `events` only when it is a string; vega-lite writes object-form streams. `value`, `bind`, `interactive` and `cursor` are neither expressions nor in a first-frame SVG.

In this file only the three "input bindings" cases (`:1331-1348`) and the geo-interval signals test (`:1131-1141`) compare these; the selection suites are in the next lane's range.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`probes.mts`, section d).

Direction: add signals (`on` in full, `bind`, `value`) and each mark's `interactive`/`cursor` to the structural part of `check`, or say in the header that selection wiring is out of this file's reach.

#### C358 — Medium — "scalePropApplies is what vega-lite does" checks the table, not the compiler, and leaves properties out

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/test/vl-scale-props.test.ts:96-121`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** closure / conformance suites, line by line II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-conftest-b-3` — `w3-conftest-b/`

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/test/vl-scale-props.test.ts:96-121` (assertion at `:112`), `ASK` at `:76-79`; `packages/conformance/test/vl-scale-forwarding.test.ts:21-30`.
- **Issue:** the test compiles with vega-lite only, then asserts `scalePropApplies(channel, type, prop)` equals what vega-lite did. `@aster-charts/vl`'s `compile` is never called in that file. It therefore passes while the compiler disobeys or bypasses the table — findings 1, 2 and 4 are three live instances.
- **Gaps in what is asked:**
  - `ASK` omits `rangeMin`, `rangeMax`, `domainRaw`, `domain`, `range`. For the first two vega-lite can be asked and disagrees with the pinned `'*'` (finding 1).
  - The companion that does compile both (`vl-scale-forwarding.test.ts`) omits the same properties plus `scheme` and `bins`, and omits `theta`, `radius`, `fill`, `stroke`; on `color` it omits `point`, `band`, `sequential`, `bin-ordinal`.
- **Evidence:** running the forwarding test's own helpers over the wider space gives 173 differing cells of 2,520 asked (`probe2.out`). Of these, 143 are the `domainRaw` literal-array refusal (discarded, see §6); the other 30 are findings 1, 2 and 4.
- **The "PINNED" half is a self-oracle by design** (the header says so), but the header also says the un-askable cells are the only ones held there. `rangeMin` / `rangeMax` are askable.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `probe2.mjs`; lines quoted above read in full.
- **Direction:** make the forwarding differential the one that covers the whole table (every `Scale` property of the schema, every channel that has a scale), and keep the table test as the cheap unit check.

#### C359 — Medium — 104 of the 480 `timeFloor` vectors (and the same 104 in `utcFloor`) cannot fail: sub-minute units, sub-hour steps and millisecond truncation are never exercised

- **Location:** `packages/core/testdata/vectors/vega-time.json:19450-20649`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run; re-run by lead)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #189 (d275b19,ffde8e6,471bf8e). Fixed at the generator: floors use every dstDates instant (non-zero seconds/ms, minutes not multiples of 3 or 5), vectors-coverage fails if a step or unit goes inert; mutants (seconds/ms reader 0, trunc) now fail the replay
- **Area:** closure / vega-time vectors II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-time-b-1` — `w3-time-b/`

`packages/core/testdata/vectors/vega-time.json:19450-20649` (`["minutes"]`, `["seconds"]`, `["milliseconds"]`), `:21946-22369` (`["hours","minutes"]`), `:22370-22889` (`["year","month","date","hours","minutes","seconds"]`). Cause: `packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:349-354` with `:303-308`.

- **Cause.** `floorCases` uses `dstDates.slice(0, 8)`. All eight instants have seconds = 0 and milliseconds = 0, and minutes of 0 or 30. The slice drops `1999-12-31T23:59:59Z`, the only date in the list with a non-zero second.
- **What the data shows (`verify.mjs`, per unit list, 24 cases each):**
  - `["seconds"]`: 1 distinct want (`1325394000000` in all 24); 16/16 step cases equal the no-step want.
  - `["milliseconds"]`: 1 distinct want; 16/16 step cases inert.
  - `["minutes"]`: 2 distinct wants; 16/16 step cases inert (0 and 30 are multiples of both 3 and 5).
  - `["hours","minutes"]`: 16/16 step cases inert.
  - `["year","month","date","hours","minutes","seconds"]`: all 24 wants equal the input, and 16/16 step cases are inert.
- **Planted bugs that pass.** Three mutants of the oracle's own `timeFloor`/`utcFloor`, replayed against the recorded wants:
  - seconds and milliseconds units dropped (floored to 0): caught by 0/480 in `timeFloor`, 0/480 in `utcFloor`;
  - `step` ignored when the last unit is minutes, seconds or milliseconds: 0/480 and 0/480;
  - identity when the unit list is y-m-d-H-M-S: 0/480 and 0/480.
- **These are real behaviours upstream.** On `1999-12-31T23:59:59.123Z`:
  - `utcFloor(['seconds'])` → `2012-01-01T00:00:59.000Z`;
  - `utcFloor(['milliseconds'], 5)` → `…00.120Z`;
  - `utcFloor(['minutes'], 5)` → `…00:55:00.000Z`;
  - the y-m-d-H-M-S floor is not the identity.
- **Expected.** The replay header (`packages/core/src/oracle-vectors.test.ts:5-8`) says these vectors are "what licenses dropping the upstream dependency"; a floor suite should pin seconds, milliseconds and their steps. The generator comment at `gen-vectors.mjs:355-356` calls the hours/minutes steps "the interesting ones", yet the minutes steps are inert.
- **Mitigation.** The live differential `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-time-intervals.test.mts:256-272` does generate unit lists, steps and instants against the pinned vega-time. The gap is in the recorded suite only. The port itself is correct here: aster matches the oracle on all 480 cases and in the sweep under finding 2.
- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** — `verify.mjs`.
- **Direction.** Add instants with non-zero seconds and milliseconds and minutes that are not multiples of 3 and 5 (e.g. `…T12:37:41.123Z`) to the floor inputs; use the full `dstDates` list, not `slice(0, 8)`.
- **Overlap.** The `utcFloor` half is in w3-time-c's range, and the generator is shared, so expect the same finding there.

**Independent report of the same defect** (lane ID `w3-time-c-1`, scripts `w3-time-c/`, CONFIRMED (run); the floor vectors never use an instant with non-zero seconds or milliseconds, so the `seconds`/`milliseconds` units and any step on `minutes`/`seconds`/`milliseconds` cannot fail):

`packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:351` (cause); `packages/core/testdata/vectors/vega-time.json:28289-29088`, `:30809-31328`, `:27889-28288`, `:30385-30808` (effect in my range; `timeFloor` has the same shape in the other lanes' ranges).

- **Cause.** `floorCases` is built from `dstDates.slice(0, 8)`. The slice drops `1999-12-31T23:59:59Z`, the only instant in `dstDates` with non-zero seconds, along with 1970 and the 2000-02-29 leap day. All 8 remaining instants are on `:00:00.000` or `:30:00.000`.
- **Effect in `utcFloor`, as read:**
  - `['seconds']` (lines 28289-28688): all 24 wants are `1325376000000`.
  - `['milliseconds']` (lines 28689-29088): all 24 wants are `1325376000000`.
  - `['year','month','date','hours','minutes','seconds']` (lines 30809-31328): all 24 wants equal the input.
  - `['minutes']` and `['hours','minutes']`: step `undefined`, `5` and `3` give the same want for all 8 dates, because minutes are 0 or 30.
- **The generator comment is wrong.** `gen-vectors.mjs:355-356` says "'hours'/'minutes' steps are the interesting ones under DST". The minutes step is unobservable in both suites.
- **Proof (`mutants.mjs` → `mutants.out`).** Each mutant is a patched copy of `packages/core/dist/time.js`, replayed over all 2,028 cases of the file with the test's dispatch. These survive with 0 failing cases:
  - the `seconds` reader returns 0;
  - the `milliseconds` reader returns 0;
  - the `seconds` reader returns `minutes % 30`;
  - the step is ignored when the finest unit is minutes, seconds or milliseconds.
- **Controls.** The unpatched copy fails 0 of 2,028. A mutant where the `hours` reader returns 0 fails 232.
- **Mitigation, which is why this is Low.** `packages/conformance/scripts/differential-time-intervals.test.mts:256-272` runs `timeFloor`/`utcFloor` live against vega-time over generated unit lists, steps and instants. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:103` runs `scripts/differential-` together with `oracle-vectors.test`. I did not run that differential, so I have not confirmed it kills these mutants.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`~/.cache/aster-review/audit-2026-11-22/w3-time-c/mutants.mjs`, `check-range.mjs`; outputs `mutants.out`, `check-range.out`).

Direction: use all of `dstDates` in `floorCases`, or add instants such as `…T05:29:59.999Z` and `…T12:07:13.456Z`, then re-record. Fix the comment at `:355-356`.

  - a `<path>` with no `d` equals no element (N-degenerate);

- **Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
- **Direction:** move the 70-pair table into `normalize.test.ts`.

#### C683 — Low — corpus-tz: two inert specs and three uncovered zone behaviours

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/corpus-tz/enter-update.vg.json:1`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Area:** tests / conformance suites II
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `tests-conftest2-8` — `tests-conftest2/`

`packages/conformance/corpus-tz/*`

Measured by rendering every spec with real Vega (and Aster) under different `TZ` values (`$S/tz.mjs`, `$S/tz-dst.mjs`):

- **15 of 28 change with the zone** in real Vega, so they would fail if local time were treated as UTC.
- **13 are byte-identical in UTC, New York, Kolkata and Lord Howe:**
  - 10 are UTC-scale or `formatType: "utc"` specs. These are legitimate inverse guards: they fail if UTC output leaks into local time.
  - `bar-year-axis.vl.json` is a local year time unit on 1 June dates, so the zone cannot move it.
  - `enter-update.vg.json` and `signals-update.vg.json` contain no date, time scale or time function. They are copies of `corpus/` files and compare nothing zone-related.
- **Real DST rules are needed by 11 specs:** their New York output differs from both `Etc/GMT+5` and `Etc/GMT+4`, because the domains span winter and summer.
- **Aster's text matched Vega's** for all 28 specs in all four zones.
- **Not covered:**
  - a `timeFormat()` expression — only `utcFormat` appears (`expr-time-fns.vg.json`);
  - hour-level ticks or labels across a transition day — the two hour-level specs are 1970-01-01 and 1–4 January 2024; the 2024-03-10 and 2024-11-03 values sit in gradient legends whose ticks are months;
  - local time units finer than month — the three `timeUnit` specs use month and year;
  - `timeOffset`, `datetime()`, and the `timeunit` transform.
- 9 of the 28 are JSON-identical to `corpus/` specs. That is intended (same spec, other zones), but it means only 19 are tz-specific.
- The corpus is runtime-only: `.vl.json` is compiled by vega-lite (`src/run.ts:54-58`).

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN.**
**Direction:** drop the two inert specs; add a `timeFormat` text, an hours axis across 2024-03-10 and 2024-11-03, and a `timeunit` transform with `hours` / `day`.

- **Area:** closure / gallery lists, small recorded vectors
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-lists-3` — `w3-lists/`

`packages/core/testdata/vectors/d3-dsv.json:467-477` (`dropOdd`), `:154-197` (Semi / Tab); generated at `packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:816`, `:781-797`; replayed at `packages/core/src/oracle-vectors.test.ts:362`, `:143-144`.

- **`dropOdd`:** the input is `"a,b\n1,2"` — one data row, index 0 — and the converter drops only odd indices. The recorded want `[{a:"1",b:"2"}]` equals a parse with no row function at all.
  - A port that keeps rows whose converter returns `null` passes: `vectors.mjs` prints `planted "keeps null rows" impl matches the recorded want: true`.
  - So d3's "a null/undefined row is skipped" contract is pinned by no vector.
  - The port itself is right: on `"a,b\n1,2\n3,4\n5,6"` port and d3 both give `[{1,2},{5,6}]`.
- **Semi / Tab:** both suites hold arrays of arrays (`[["a","b"],["1","2"]]`). `parse()` to objects with a non-comma delimiter is recorded nowhere, nor is the duplicate-header case `a\ta` as objects. Port and d3 agree on both when checked directly.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`vectors.mjs`). Direction: record `dropOdd` on three or more rows; rename the two suites or add `parse` cases for `;` and tab.

#### C694 — Low — 8 of 108 `formatPrefix` cases are exact duplicates, and 12 record the same degenerate `"NaN"`

- **Location:** `packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:548-553`
- **Status:** CONFIRMED (run)
- **Resolution:** FIXED in #189 (d275b19,471bf8e,ffde8e6). Fixed: refs y..Y, clamp, zero and non-finite, more specs, de-duplicated triples; no suite may record a case twice (test); V8-pow-dependent cases avoided
- **Area:** closure / d3-format vectors
- **Lane ID / scripts:** `w3-vecfmt-a-1` — `w3-vecfmt-a/`

`packages/conformance/scripts/gen-vectors.mjs:548-553`; `packages/core/testdata/vectors/d3-format.json:7503-7526, 7527-7550` (repeated for `s` at 7719-7766, `.0s` at 7935-7982, `.3s` at 8151-8198).

- The generator builds `[ref, ref * 0.5, 1]` for each ref.
  - For ref 0 the first two triples are identical: `(".2s",0,0)` at 7503 and 7511.
  - For ref 1 the first and third are identical: `(".2s",1,1)` at 7527 and 7543.
  - That is 2 duplicates × 4 specs = 8, leaving 100 distinct cases of 108.
- All 12 ref-0 cases record `"NaN"`, whatever the applied value (`(".2s",0,1)` → `"NaN"`, line 7525). This is what d3-format 3.1.2 does, since `formatDecimalParts` returns null for ±0.
- Refs are only `0, 1, 999, 1000, 1500, 1e6, 2.5e9, -3.7e12, 7e15`. The suite therefore never records:
  - a sub-unit prefix (m, µ, n, p, f, a, z, y);
  - E, Z or Y, or the clamp beyond 1e24 / 1e-24;
  - a non-finite ref;
  - a spec other than plain `s` with a precision.
- The port is right on all of these: `gaps.mjs` compares 19 specs × 36 refs × 9 values of `formatPrefix` against d3-format 3.1.2 with 0 differences.

**Status: CONFIRMED-RUN** (`verify.mjs` prints `formatPrefix … cases 108 distinct 100 dups 8`).

Direction: use refs `[1e-24, 1e-9, 0.001, 0.5, …, 1e24, 1e27, NaN, Infinity]`, and replace the `1` in the value triple with a value that cannot collide (e.g. `ref * 3`).

---

## 4. Design tensions

These are structural: fixing the cited findings one by one leaves the mechanism that produced them in place.

### T1 — Safety is enforced per call site, so every new site is unsafe by default

URL vetting, the built-in ceilings, the cooperative clock, error-to-abort conversion, `Object.prototype`-safe lookup and "this structure is claimed" are each a helper that a call site must remember to invoke. This audit found the forgotten site for every one of them: title links and the `image` channel for the URL policy (C8, C20); legends, interval ranges, scale `bins`, data-supplied grids, `cross`/`fold`/`graticule` for ceilings (C9, C19, C17, C88); force, label, raster stroker, contour, geo, heatmap, the regex screen for the clock (C239, C93, C242, C15, C10); mark items for claims (C2). Three different helper tiers (`ceiling`, `checkGeneratedRows`, `boundedCount`) make "which protection does this site have" a matter of which name was typed, and one limit can silently *remove* a ceiling it does not replace (C29).

**Alternative to weigh.** Move each guarantee to the single place the thing is produced: vet URLs in one pass over the finished scene (or in the attribute sink); have the allocating primitives (`AlphaCanvas`, `Grid`, `contourPolygons`, `Events.grow`, `sequence`, `interval.range`, the tick generators) take their budget themselves and apply the ceiling unconditionally, with an explicitly named unbounded variant for parity tests; give every loop sized by spec or data a tick through a lint rule or a gate that flags unticked loops in the transform, layout and geo files. For the hard guarantee, own the worker deadline and restart in the hooks (C244) rather than describing it.

### T2 — A bounded round loop and ~29 hand-keyed reuse rules stand in for a dataflow graph

The runtime resolves signals, scales and datasets by iterating to a fixed bound, and decides what to keep by comparing hand-assembled keys (`readsKey`, `ctxFpOf`, `markKeyOf`, `groupMarkKeyOf`, `guideKeyOf`, `pipelineKey`, `datasetKey`…). Each key must be a superset of what its result reads, and each mechanism has its own prose list of refusals. The failures are of three kinds: order (C23, C25, C113, C144), a missing dependency edge (C42, C26, C280, C282), and identity standing for content in an engine that mutates in place (C24, C30, C229). `datasetRanksOf`, `signalsInDataflowOrder`, the propagation graph in `signals.ts`, the add-on detector's walk and `spec-expressions.ts` are five partial copies of "what reads what".

**Alternative to weigh.** Build one dependency graph per compiled chart (signals, datasets, scales, projections, marks, guides as nodes; reads as edges) from the single expression enumerator the compile check already has, run it in rank order, refuse cycles with Vega's message, and derive invalidation from it. Short of that: record a *read set* while a node evaluates and key reuse on the recorded set instead of a hand-written one; and never compare an engine-written array by identity — give arrays a version stamp checked through one helper, or stop mutating published arrays (copy-on-append, or persistent/chunked arrays so no returned object is ever written).

### T3 — "Accepted" and "implemented" are two separate lists, in both the engine and the compiler

`spec-expressions.ts`/`guide-model.ts`/`transform-params.ts` say what Vega *parses*; the runtime decides separately what it *reads*. `validate.ts` says what Vega-Lite keys are *allowed*; `compile.ts` decides separately what it *consumes*. Everything in the gap compiles, renders, and is silently different: `encode.hover`, colour objects, `zindex`, `key`, data triggers, object-form field parameters, `config.locale`, `config.events`, `config.legend.layout` signals (C76, C27, C28, C120, C73, C35, C41, C78, C147); layer `resolve`, wrapped-facet `header`, layer child sizes, `config.style.<mark>`, `parse: null` (C79, C52, C161, C80, C181). The project's own rule — "unsupported or unknown features throw a typed error … no silent wrong charts" — is the right one; the structure cannot keep it.

**Alternative to weigh.** Make consumption observable: compile functions *take* properties from the validated clone (delete-on-read or a `take()` accessor) and a final pass refuses anything left unread, so the refusal list is generated rather than remembered — and becomes the README's "Throws" list (C83). For the engine, resolve every parameter from the per-transform/per-guide table the compile check already holds, so `{expr}`, `{field, as}` and nested `{signal}` are handled once (C35, C148). For the validator, generate key *and value* checks from the Vega-Lite JSON schema at build time and keep by hand only a "valid but unsupported" list.

### T4 — The verification system measures agreement on what it happens to generate, and reports it as coverage

Counts ("1063/1063", "500 ok", "68 corpus symbol specs") stand for coverage, but no gate floors what was actually *compared*, exclusions are prose plus `delete` in generators, tolerances are global scalars, and gates have no test of their own failure path. Hence a gate with no exit code (C64), a sweep whose oracle pre-computes the engine's answer (C61), a differential that compares zero items (C62), an exclusion that hides a live defect while its stated reason is stale (C63), and two oracles for one expression language that disagree on `in` (C302). The incremental oracle, which carries the engine's central guarantee, generates none of the inputs that break it: reading its generator for what it never draws led directly to a stale-mark defect on the default session path (C7), and its default sweep reaches 33 of its 58 pipelines (C75). The same holds one level down: reference copies that share code and cache slots with their subject (C67, C106), loops that skip what throws (C334), and a corpus whose count includes 86 render-identical specs (C318).

**Alternative to weigh.** One `runGate` harness that owns the exit code, the zero-case rule and required counters, with a planted-difference self-test per gate (as `run-sweep.test.mjs` and `verify-publish.test.mjs` already do). One `forEngines(spec, fn)` helper that deep-clones or freezes per engine. Comparators return a coverage vector (items, attributes, channel forms) and gates floor it. Known gaps live in an expected-differences table whose entries a test requires to *still differ*. Site and property lists are derived from the pinned Vega / Vega-Lite JSON schemas and fail on an uncovered position. And a relational layer in the generators: per-item variation, nesting, `enter`+`update`, hover, selections under update — the inter-item behaviours a one-literal-per-case sweep cannot reach.

### T5 — Three identity regimes and four error exits at the React boundary

Some inputs are compared by content (`spec`, `limits`), some by identity (`signals`, `data` in the worker hook, option functions, the spec in `useSpecData`), and the rule is documented piecemeal or not at all; props are copied into stores by effects, which makes "changed" mean "identity changed" and cannot express removal. Errors leave through `onError`, a throw from render, `onStreamError` or the logger depending on which line raised them. The loops (C48, C72, C50), the snap-back of `signals` (C292), the double `onError` (C157), and the unmounted root on a Vega-Lite typo (C47) are all this seam. A third axis compounds it: which engine an app gets depends on the `browser` export condition, tree-shaking and which React export it touches (C82, C84).

**Alternative to weigh.** One stated rule — JSON-shaped inputs by content, functions through a latest-ref — applied in every hook and component; keep only event-written values in stores and merge with content-stable props at read time. One error channel: normalise and compile inside the guarded evaluation so every failure reaches the error state and `onError`/`error`. Always render the container and put the alert inside it, so effects never have to know about an element swap (C46). Make the lean/full choice explicit in the import (`@aster-charts/react` full and synchronous, `/lean` opt-in) or enforce the import-graph invariant with a test over every React export.
