## 5. Expectation gaps

"Expected X, found Y", from the point of view of a first-time consumer following the docs. Each line cites the finding that carries the evidence.

### Safety and limits

- Expected `urlPolicy` to cover every URL in the output; found title/subtitle links, the `image` channel and `cursor` outside it, and a refused update still present in later scenes (C8, C20, C97, C2).
- Expected "`javascript:` produces no link, whatever the spec says"; found `file://javascript:…` written as `javascript:…` on the no-policy path (C3).
- Expected the built-in ceilings to stop "a few hundred bytes of spec" from exhausting the process; found fatal out-of-memory from a legend `tickCount`, scale `bins`, `utcSequence`, a tiny `strokeDash`, a wide CSV header, `cross`, `graticule` (C9, C19, C16, C12, C88).
- Expected any `limits` object to be at least as safe as none; found `{ maxGeneratedRows }` alone less safe for `density`/`quantile` (C29).
- Expected `maxTimeMs` to bound an evaluation; found 9–30 s runs and never-returning loops under a 100–500 ms budget, some returning normally with no error (C239, C15, C132, C14).
- Expected `limits` to add checks; found it also turns off incremental reuse, a 30–60× cost per signal write on a 20k scatter, documented only in ARCHITECTURE internals (C277).
- Expected the default loader policy to refuse internal hosts; found `http://metadata/`, `*.svc`, `.lan` fetched (C13).
- Expected `regex: 'refuse'` to be a property of the spec; found it a property of the sites the compile walk reads, and the heuristic screen itself hangs on one valid pattern (C284, C10).
- Expected "Aster's stricter sandbox" to confine a spec to its chart; found handler expressions hold the native event and can listen on `window` or any selector, with `config.events` ignored (C4, C78).

### Vega parity and "no silent wrong charts"

- Expected an unsupported Vega feature to throw a typed error; found `encode.hover`, colour objects, item `zindex`, mark `key`, data triggers, `{field: {group}}`, object-form field parameters, `config.locale`, unknown mark types and misspelt scale properties accepted and ignored (C76, C27, C28, C120, C73, C119, C35, C41, C238, C333).
- Expected "Deviations from Vega" to be the list; found fourteen confirmed deviations in no list (C372).
- Expected `item` in an encode expression to be the item; found `undefined` (C31).
- Expected "resolved to a fixed point"; found a three-round bound whose exit test precedes the scales (C23).
- Expected a label, rule or voronoi drawn from another mark to follow a data edit; found the previous items kept on every same-length update through a session (C7).
- Expected a numeric string for a rect's `width`/`height` to draw as in Vega; found a zero-size rect that is still hit-testable (C198).
- Expected a derived dataset and `graticule` to treat source rows as Vega does; found the source order and existing rows differ, undocumented (C380, C210).
- Expected `zindex` to mean the same inside a group as at top level (C118).
- Expected `datasetsOfScene(scene)` to be that scene's rows; found the engine's live arrays, including rows of a rejected evaluation (C30).
- Expected "pass a new array" to be a sufficient remedy for mutated rows; found the rows must be new objects, and nothing warns (C266).

### Vega-Lite compiler

- Expected "never compiles a wrong chart silently" and an exhaustive "Throws" list; found silent mis-compiles of mainstream shapes and nine unlisted refusals (C6, C53, C54, C83).
- Expected `resolve` to work at every layer level or be refused; found it accepted everywhere and honoured for a subset at the top layer (C79).
- Expected `facet: {field}` and `facet: {row/column}` to treat `header` alike; found two implementations (C52).
- Expected `rangeMin`/`rangeMax` and `reverse` to follow vega-lite's per-scale-type rules; found the first applied to discretizing scales and the second deleted on discrete polar scales (C223, C224).
- Expected an area over a pre-binned position, and a bar from a datum to a field, to compile as in vega-lite; found an empty path and a missing axis title (C221, C222).
- Expected `config.style.bar` to act like `config.bar`; found it dropped (C80).
- Expected `config.scale.zero` to be a default; found it overrides the encoding (C171).
- Expected compile cost independent of row count, as the README says; found deep comparison of equal arrays across layers (C364).
- Expected only `VLCompileError`; found `RangeError` on deep or cyclic input and Vega-time failures for raw names (C493, C102, C182).

### React

- Expected `onError` to be the one place errors arrive; found a Vega-Lite typo, a missing `/vl` import or `spec={null}` unmounts the root (C47).
- Expected the README's first `<Chart>` to draw at the spec's `width`/`height`; found it fills its container (C274).
- Expected inline literals to be safe everywhere, as they are for `spec`; found a render loop in `useChartWorker`, an endless refetch in `useSpecData`, and `signals` snapping back (C72, C50, C292).
- Expected `diffRows`' result to be accepted as `dataPulse`, as API.md says; found a type error (C278).
- Expected `setTextMetricsProvider` to take effect on the next evaluation; found kept marks sized by the previous measurer (C217).
- Expected a failed `useSpecData` load to reach the error boundary; found 500+ fetches in three seconds (C48).
- Expected "`true` means it will be delivered" for a stream push; found pushes accepted and dropped before the start effect, during add-on load, and after unmount (C49, C158, C506).
- Expected `capacity`/`policy` to bound a slow worker; found they bound one tick (C77).
- Expected time-series charts to zoom and brush on x, and log axes to pan; found time axes skipped and log treated as linear (C44, C155).
- Expected SSR + `hydrateRoot` to equal a client mount; found the server's time zone and text metrics kept (C45).
- Expected `style={{ height: 300 }}` to size the box; found it overridden unless `a11y={false}` (C294).
- Expected "first paint is synchronous"; found a Suspense fallback for any chart with a legend or time scale in a production browser build, and none in dev (C84).
- Expected `<ChartStream>` to cost about what `<Chart>` does; found the full synchronous engine (C82).
- Expected `hydrateChart` to hydrate; found a one-shot static patch whose `tooltips` option writes row JSON into the DOM and shows no tooltip (C276).
- Expected a `data` key the spec does not declare to be reported, as `dataChanges` is; found it ignored (C306).

### Gates, release and onboarding

- Expected `pnpm conformance:browser` to fail when entries differ (C64).
- Expected the scene differential to be the stricter check; found it empty for grouped marks (C62).
- Expected the value sweep to test Aster's `stack`/`pie`/`bin`; found their outputs pre-written by the oracle (C61).
- Expected a filter typo to fail a gate everywhere, as in the sweeps; found `0/0 passed`, exit 0 (C247, C230).
- Expected "1063/1063" to mean 1,063 distinct checks; found 54 groups of render-identical specs, composite specs drawn into a 10-pixel root, and spec names that do not match their content (C318, C255, C313).
- Expected the incremental oracle to hold "for any spec, any update sequence"; found 33 of 58 pipelines run by default and a whole mark shape never generated, behind which a session keeps stale items (C75, C7).
- Expected the old-versus-new geometry differential to be an independent reference; found shared modules, a shared descriptor cache and per-side item numbering (C67, C106).
- Expected a ceiling test's "still renders" half to fail when the child process dies; found a crash counted as a clean return (C199).
- Expected `pnpm typecheck` to cover tests and runner scripts (C303).
- Expected a `vX.Y.Z-rc.1` tag to publish under a prerelease dist-tag, and the documented release commands to push the tag (C66, C367).
- Expected CONTRIBUTING's Node minimum to run the suite, and TypeScript's `moduleResolution` requirement to be stated (C369, C371).
- Expected the benchmark's `aster` vs `asterDom` rows to compare two modes; found one configuration measured twice (C304).
- Expected every published number to sit next to a command that reproduces it; found five PERFORMANCE sections measured by probes kept outside the repository, and bundle tables that disagree with the budgets in code (C370, C368).

## 6. Open questions

What the code alone cannot resolve. Each is a decision for the maintainer; the findings named depend on the answer.

**Threat model**

- **Q1. Is an interactive `<Chart>` meant to be safe for untrusted specs?** `docs/LIMITS.md` describes an untrusted-spec path (limits + loader allowlist + worker), but the signal event loop always runs on the main thread with the native DOM event. If yes, C4 needs an event facade and C78 is its companion; if interactive charts are for trusted specs only, LIMITS.md should say so and the finding becomes a documentation gap.
- **Q2. Is an untrusted *spec* (not only untrusted data) in the threat model for the DOM patcher?** C1, C20 and C97 need the spec to name the channel. LIMITS.md says "data and specs are untrusted input", which reads as yes.
- **Q3. Should `href` vetting be on by default,** given Vega's own sanitizer is bypassable (C3)? And should server-side `loadSpecData` require an explicit allowlist rather than "any public URL" (C13)?
- **Q4. Should the hooks own the worker deadline,** or is terminating a runaway worker deliberately the host's job (ADR 0010 reads that way)? With `workerFactory` the host holds no reference to terminate (C244).
- **Q5. Should the regex screen fail closed** under limits on syntax it cannot read, at the cost of refusing syntax newer than its parser (C11)?

**Parity vs intent**

- **Q6. Are `encode.hover`/`exit`, data and mark `on` triggers, item `zindex`, mark `key` joins and `item` in encode expressions out of scope on purpose?** None is in ROADMAP, ERRORS or the deviations table (C76, C73, C28, C120, C31).
- **Q7. `in`/`instanceof`:** the cases file pins the throw (vega-interpreter's behaviour); default Vega evaluates them. Which is the contract (C125)?
- **Q8. After an update whose encode throws, is the target Vega's running-view picture or the fresh scene?** The incremental result is neither today (C110).
- **Q9. Where vega-lite is itself wrong** (duplicate aggregate outputs, upstream crashes), is the rule "render like vega-lite" or "never a wrong chart silently"? Aster currently does neither for C57.
- **Q10. Is the `toNumber` cast on every quantitative field deliberate?** It changes rows on a default path and is undocumented (C169).
- **Q11. Is "fill the container" meant to stay the default for a spec with a literal `width`/`height`,** given the aim of matching Vega's observable behaviour (C274)?
- **Q12. Is the `geoshape` mark type, a `shape` mark drawing a datum's `path` string, a literal `domainRaw` array, `config.scale.nice`, extension-based format inference, and `format` on a `source` dataset each an intended extension?** Each is accepted where Vega or vega-lite refuses or ignores it (C149, C287, C115, C171).
- **Q13. Is matching an upstream hang ever intended?** Several unbounded loops are parity with d3/Vega (C132, C92); if so LIMITS.md should list the inputs.

**Contracts**

- **Q14. Is `datasetsOfScene` meant to be historical (its TSDoc) or live** (`scene.runtime` is documented as live)? The failed-evaluation half of C30 is a defect either way.
- **Q15. May one injected `random` source be shared by several charts** (ADR 0006 compares it to Vega's global `setRandom`) or is it one per chart (API.md) (C124)?
- **Q16. Is one `CompiledChart` shared by several `evaluateChart` callers supported?** The per-chart state is a module `WeakMap`.
- **Q17. `maxGeneratedRows`: per evaluation's work or per evaluation's state** (C281)?
- **Q18. Should `cross`/`fold`/`pivot` amplification be under a built-in ceiling?** LIMITS.md says data-sized input is deliberately uncovered, but n×n is not data-sized (C88).
- **Q19. Is `signals` on `<Chart>` controlled or initial?** The docs say both in one sentence (C292). Should a rejected `useSpecData` load retry automatically or only after a boundary reset (C48)? Should a push made before a worker stream starts be kept or refused (C49)?
- **Q20. Which symbols are public (semver) surface?** `@aster-charts/core/lean*` (exported, typed, called internal), `registerVegaLiteCompiler` (`@internal` in TSDoc, documented in API.md), `compileUnit`, `ChartSession.last()`, `HydrateChartOptions.tooltips`, `checkChartRows`, `buildPulseGraph`.
- **Q21. Is the lockstep rule exact pins (`workspace:*`) or compatible ranges?** Exact pins make a partial publish or a one-package update yield two copies of core with separate registries (C231).
- **Q22. Is Node 20 a supported runtime for `@aster-charts/react`?** Nothing executes `dist` or React there.

- **Q28. Why is Vega-Lite `nearest` (voronoi over a mark) unaffected by C7?** The lane observed it correct and did not trace why; if it is an accident of `identifier` forcing the conservative path, Vega-Lite hover selection is one optimisation away from the same staleness. Do the other reuse records hold arrays that are later advanced in place?
- **Q29. Is a false `appendOnly` pulse tolerated by contract or by accident?** A regression test feeds two and passes (C510).
- **Q30. Should the legacy geometry differential outlive the refactor it guarded,** given that it is edited with each fix (C307)?
- **Q31. Is the corpus meant to be a set of distinct checks or a regression archive?** The answer decides whether render-identical and misnamed specs are defects (C318, C313).

**Facts not checkable offline**

- **Q23.** Do the pinned action SHAs match the versions in their comments; is the `npm-release` environment protected; which npm major runs the publish job (decides which half of C66 applies)?
- **Q24.** Did `browser-conformance` ever gate? `git log -S"process.exit"` on the script shows no commit adding or removing an exit (C64).
- **Q25.** How many sweep cases pass today only because of the shared spec object (C61), and how many of the 1,063 corpus specs does `scene-diff` compare with zero items (C62)? Only a re-run of those gates with the harness fixed answers this; gates were out of bounds for this audit.
- **Q26.** Real-browser behaviour this audit could only infer: whether a `<script>` inserted through C1 executes (the `onclick` handler did, under jsdom), pointer hit-testing in dash gaps, touch brushing, opaque-redirect handling in `loadSpecData`, canvas pixel effects of symbol batching, and whether charts sharing a content-addressed clip id lose it when the first chart unmounts.
- **Q27.** Which of the ~10% browser label-layout differences are understood, and is there a list (C191)?

## Appendix A — Coverage ledger

### A.0 Evidence from the tool logs (independent of what lanes reported)

Every lane ran as a recorded session, and so did the lead. The recordings hold each tool call and the text it returned, so what was actually displayed to a reader can be measured without relying on any ledger. Three scripts in the audit scratch directory do that over all 65 lane transcripts plus the lead's own (`readlog.py`, `contentlog.py`, `contentlog2.py`):

- **Source, tests, scripts, documents, configuration (1,031 tracked files outside the corpus).** For each file, every substantive line (12 or more characters after whitespace is collapsed) was looked up verbatim in the text returned by any tool call. Result: for 1,029 files every such line was displayed; the other two are single-line data files measured by character range below. Before the lead's own reads the same measure exposed real gaps that the ledgers had hidden: `packages/core/src/dataset-reuse.test.ts` (219 of 456 substantive lines displayed, although its lane's ledger listed it as read), `packages/conformance/gallery/swap-pairs.txt` (12 of 223; checked by script only), `packages/conformance/src/d3-color.d.ts` (3 of 9), and six lines longer than the lanes' display width in `color-schemes.ts` and two benchmark files. The lead read each of these in full; the two long colour ramps were also compared with Vega's at their end stops.
- **Single-line data files.** `packages/conformance/src/raster-fixtures.json`: 561,150 of 561,183 characters fall inside a 40-character window that occurs verbatim in tool output; the remainder are runs of at most ten characters at the seams between consecutive display chunks, an artefact of the windowing. `packages/core/testdata/intersect-stall-scene.json`: 13,040 of 13,044.
- **Corpus (1,063 specs).** The corpus lanes read re-serialised dumps, so lines cannot be matched; instead every object key, string value and number of each parsed spec was looked up in the tool output. Before the lead's reads, 1,009 specs had every token displayed and 54 did not; the lead read those 54 in full from a lossless compact dump. Afterwards 1,055 were complete and 8 lacked exactly one token each, where the lead's dump had folded a line inside a string; the lead then read those 8 unfolded. The token script still reports them (its quote-pairing regex loses alignment in the unfolded print), so the lead checked the tokens it names by direct substring search of the session's tool output: each is present. All 1,063 specs have therefore been displayed in full.

- **Gallery specs (720 upstream files, outside the repository).** The same line measure over the four gallery lanes' recordings: all 24,445 substantive lines (8 or more characters) of all 720 specs were displayed.

What this establishes is that the text of every tracked file was put in front of a reader. It cannot establish how carefully each line was considered; the findings, and the planted-fault and differential scripts behind them, are the evidence for that.

### A.1 Per-file coverage table

Generated by `coverage3.py` (in the audit scratch directory) from the lanes' ledgers, under the strictest rule that could be checked mechanically: a file is credited to a lane only when that lane's coverage ledger names the file followed by the file's **true line count** (`wc -l`, ±1) or by the range `1-<count>`, with no partial qualifier ("lines a-b", "in part", "grep", "header") attached to that entry; a file whose name occurs in more than one package must be named with its path. Fourteen files were read over several stated ranges (a large file split between lanes, or paged within one lane); for those the table quotes each range and the script checks that the ranges are contiguous from the first line or character to the last. The script asserts that no tracked file is left uncredited. An earlier, looser version of this check accepted any mention of a file name in a ledger and so overstated coverage; the files it wrongly passed were then read line by line by the third wave or by the lead, and appear here under `w3-*` or `lead`. ### A.2 Ledgers as reported by each lane

What each lane read in full, read in part, and did not read. A lane's ledger is reproduced as it reported it. The first 26 ledgers are the first pass (non-test source, scripts, documents); where one of them says a test file, the corpus or a leftover was "not read in full", a second-wave lane (`tests-*`, `corpus*`, `gaps-misc-*`) read it in full afterwards and its ledger below says so file by file. A third wave (`w3-*`) then read line by line, with page ranges recorded in each ledger, every file an earlier ledger had checked "by script", read "in part" or named ambiguously; the `lead` ledger lists files read by the lead; the tool-log measure in A.0 covers the lead's later reads (the two case tables, `dataset-reuse.test.ts`, `swap-pairs.txt`, 54 corpus specs and others) that are not in that ledger. Nothing tracked remains unread. Two qualifications, stated once: seven third-party licence texts in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` were read but have no local source to verify against (C687); and where a large file was split between lanes (`vega-time.json` in three, `d3-color.json` in two, `raster-fixtures.json` in three by character range) each lane's ledger covers its own range and the ranges are contiguous. The fetched gallery cache is untracked and absent from the checkout; a previously fetched copy that verifies against `gallery/manifest.json` was read by the `gallery*` lanes (720 specs, 37,689 lines by their ledgers) and used for the gallery gate run in Appendix B. `node_modules` was opened only for oracle code a finding cites. **Not exercised**: a real browser (touch, real canvas text metrics, real `ResizeObserver`, browser-build lazy chunks), a real `Worker`, the network, npm.

### corpus / specs, range 1 (`corpus1`)

All 277 files in the range were read in full (7,403 lines, 287,869 bytes).

**How they were read:** as compact JSON via `show.mjs` (key order kept; whitespace is the only thing dropped). Five families were read as one base file in full plus an exhaustive deep diff of every sibling against it: `area-curve-*` and its area siblings, `bar-color-*`, `geo-vlout-*`. Every differing path was printed; non-differing content is identical to the base that was read. Some diff output was column-capped; I checked no line was cut short of its content, and the one family of lines filtered out was the repeated `-20/-10/10/20` data row. ### corpus / specs, range 4 (`corpus4`)

**How the files were read.** The first four files were read raw, line by line. For all 71, `compact.mjs` first verified that each file is byte-identical to `JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(text), null, 2) + "\n"` (true for every file, so there are no duplicate keys or hidden content). I then read every file in a lossless compact rendering: primitive arrays inline, and a repeated `values` blob printed in full at first occurrence and replaced by a hash reference afterwards. Every line of every file on my list was read.

**Top 5:**
1. `firstDiff`'s identity-only `seen` set hides a wrong link endpoint and reordered node rows in the "bit for bit" force comparison (run).
2. `vl-expressions.ts` drops in-place casts from both sides, so a missing or different cast compares equal; this hides `C169 (vl-c2-3)` from the parity suites (run).
3. Product: `area` over a measure and a pre-binned position without a second channel draws nothing; vega-lite draws it (`compile.ts:4376-4379`, run).
4. Product: a ranged mark from a datum to a field (`y: {datum}`, `y2: {field}`) has no axis title; vega-lite titles it with the field (run).
5. `vl-orient` cannot see the no-orient answer for tick and line (4,246 of 8,190 combinations), and its 84 per-case tests cannot fail; no orientation defect was found in the gap, only findings 3 and 4 and more of `C436 (vl-c3-11)`.

**Top findings:**
1. C480 (w3-lists-1) — `intersect()` translates the box into every nested group without Vega's bounds check; a group at x = 1e300 makes a later sibling hit disappear (Aster 0, Vega 1).
2. C762 (w3-lists-2) — the stall fixture's refusal comes from a NaN box left by a sibling group and depends on mark order; the test comment describes a different scene.
3. C693 (w3-lists-3) — the `dropOdd` vector never drops a row (a "keep null rows" port passes); the Semi/Tab suites record `parseRows`, not `parse`.

**Top findings, one line each**
1. C225 (gallery1-1) (Medium): top-level `width`/`height` beats the spec's own size-signal `update`; horizon-graph is wrong for any non-default `layers` passed as `signals` (117 px against Vega's 217/83/67).
2. C73 (gallery1-3) (adds to `C73 (core-signals-3)`): interactive-legend, global-development and force-directed-layout lose their core interaction silently.
3. C76 (gallery1-2) (adds to `C76 (core-rt3-3)`, `C28 (core-rt3-6)`): hover highlight and raise are dead on 12 official examples.
4. C766 (gallery1-4): the documented fresh-render deviation resizes bar-chart on every hover and widens crossfilter-flights during a brush drag.
5. Positive: 250 of 253 non-default bound-signal values and seven scripted pointer sequences equal real Vega exactly.

## Appendix B — Lead verification log

The lead rebuilt the packages at `d30ead9`, then re-ran each lane's headline repro scripts from the lane's scratch directory and compared the printed output with the lane's claim. Findings so checked carry "re-run by lead" in their status. Not re-run, to keep memory safe on this machine: the 4 GB `isocontour` case of C17 (the 15-second variant was re-run), the geo amplification of C242, and the uncapped hang/out-of-memory cases of C19, C132 and C96. For four findings whose evidence is a gate or workflow that may not be run here (C64, C66, C304, C85) the lead re-read the cited lines instead. No lead re-run contradicted a lane's claim.

Second wave: the lead re-ran each lane's headline scripts as they reported (the corpus lanes' render-and-compare probes on the specs their findings name, the planted-value proofs of vacuous tests, and every product repro that is safe on this machine). The `tickCount` out-of-memory case of C22 was re-run for the `{signal: "1/0"}` form only. The bundle-budget figures of C331 and C757 come from the lane's replica of `budget.mjs` (the real script writes into the repository) and were not re-run by the lead. Third wave: the lead re-ran the product repros (C223, C224, C221, C222, C482, C480, C620) and the planted-bug replays over the recorded vectors (C698, C697, C359, C219); it did not repeat the lanes' re-derivation of every recorded vector from the pinned upstream, nor the Chromium re-recording of the raster fixtures. The lead did not repeat the corpus lanes' full 1,063-spec render sweep, nor run any vitest file; statements of the form "this test passes on a planted wrong value" were reproduced from the lanes' extracted copies of the test helpers, not by running the suite.

Gates run by the lead after the last lane reported, each once, under `TZ=UTC` and the gate lock, logs in `gates/` of the audit scratch directory:

- `pnpm check`: all 26 gates PASS (build, deps, knip, typecheck, test, tz-matrix, verify-publish, incremental-append, conformance, conformance-vl, scene-diff, incremental-diff, a11y-parity, transform-matrix, canvas, batch, signals-browser, selections-browser, intersect-browser, react-browser, browser-conformance, sweep-signals, fuzz-replay, bundle-shaking, budget, probe). The unit suite inside it: `Test Files 465 passed (465)`, `Tests 42332 passed (42332)`, which re-confirms that `docs/TESTING.md:161` ("319 files, 33665 tests") is stale. The budget gate printed `Chart + all gzip= 247.7 kB budget=247.7 kB`, the zero headroom C757 describes.
- Nightly-only checks, with the flags `nightly.yml` uses:

  - `pnpm sweep-vl … --vega-check`: 27452 ok, 47 both-refused, 14 node-error, 0 engine-error, 0 differ, 0 vega-differ / 27513; exit 0.

The 720 upstream gallery specs are fetched third-party inputs, not part of the repository; four lanes (`gallery1`–`gallery4`) also read every one of them in full, with ledgers below.

## Appendix C — Considered and discarded; what is sound

Each lane tried to disprove its candidates before keeping them. These are the ones that did not survive, with the reason, reproduced per lane so a later reader does not re-derive them. Items stated as "sound" were checked and hold.

### core / runtime: state, signals, reuse keys (`core-rt1`)

- Prototype-named signals, datasets, fields: handled. A text `field: 'constructor'` prints the native `Object` function, an inherited read in `util.ts` (other lane).
- Separator collisions in `paramFpOf` / `readsKey` with crafted signal names: sorted keys make the sides differ.
- `contentKey` aliasing of shared references: tried, no collision (`s21-misc.mjs`).
- Object key order sharing a key: no expression function exposes it (`keys`, `toJSON` are refused).
- `now()` / `datetime()` marks kept: not comparable with a fresh evaluation, and Vega does not re-run them.
- `dataPulse: { t: {} }` for a changed dataset: the hint says nothing changed.
- Out-of-range or negative indices, wrong `baseLength`, wrong-length `from`: all equal the fresh scene.
- `-0`, `NaN`, valid Dates in signals: typed correctly.
- `signalsInDataflowOrder` is quadratic: 4000 reversed signals take 0.42 s.
- Retained scenes under ordinary updates (axes, legend, facet): 0 problems in 60 seeds × 12 steps (`s13b-nofail.mjs`).
- `fitBuilding` module-global set (`runtime.ts:1299`): synchronous, cleared in `finally`.
- `evaluateChart` twice with an in-place change and no hint: equals fresh.

### core / runtime: datasets, scales, fit (`core-rt2`)

- Census wrong for `1` vs `"1"`, same-second Dates, null / NaN / Infinity, shrink or removal: refuted by fuzz.
- Published signal lost when a kept step's record has no `published`: the first round re-publishes.
- In-place item append left half-done after a later throw: `supersedeItems` plus undo are correct.
- Two passes appending to one live array: the getter materialises a private copy first.
- Dataset failure ordering vs Vega: identical.
- Prototype names, including `ROW_READING_TRANSFORMS[t.type]` at `:2870`: handled or unreachable.
- Group title `{...ctx.signalParams, parent}` plain object (`:3654`): inherited names are rejected at expression compile.
- `{signal, extraKey}` parameter objects: consistent with `resolveSignalParams`.
- `datasetKey` treating `#` in content as an identity key (`:4454`): costs a re-run only, never a stale hit.
- `valueKey` collisions: length-prefixed.
- Generation number reused after a failed evaluation: items are new objects.
- Malformed `dataPulse` shapes: re-derive, equal fresh.
- `-0` vs `0` census minimum: no observable difference found.
- `sample` vs Vega: documented deviation.
- Fit non-convergence: by design, one pass.

### core / runtime: marks, encode, groups (`core-rt3`)

- Spec-given gradient `id` collisions: Vega does the same.
- Plain-before-signal channel order: the catch block replays in spec order.
- `undefined` vs `null` for `{}` or an unmatched rule: no rendered difference.
- Test-less rule first, `band:'abc'`, `field:0`, top-level `{parent}`: Vega refuses or crashes.
- Kept marks surviving a `urlPolicy` change: invalidated correctly.
- A mark transform writing `href` to dodge the policy: no link is emitted without an encoded href, and vetting runs after transforms.
- Positional key in `runScopedData`: validated by array identity.
- `mergeVegaConfig` `recurse[k]` hitting the prototype: harmless.
- Array-valued layout option: not reachable sanely.
- Deep nesting stack overflow: blocked by the ceiling.
- Shape mark `datum.path`: Vega crashes there.
- SVG attribute order and clip-id text: representation only.

### core / session, stream, limits (`core-incr`)

- Session commits before the scope's exit rethrow: unreachable. Violations surface before `commit()` with and without limits (traced; 18 swallow-site probes threw on both calls).
- `change()` skips the pre-flight, so two datasets each under `maxRows` pass: documented (`LIMITS.md:142`).
- Re-entrant `session.evaluate` from a logger callback: commits in order, later results correct (`t-session2.mjs` section 8).
- `dataPulse` with a wrong-length `from`, `appendOnly` on a shrunk array, `dataChanges` on a longer array: all equal fresh (`t-session.mjs` section 6).
- `autoChanges: false` with replaced arrays: equals fresh.
- In-place mutation of an array handed back unchanged is invisible: documented ("Rows are treated as immutable").
- `identifier` numbers differ from a fresh evaluation: documented (`ARCHITECTURE.md:596`).
- `modify` / `remove` with a tuple read back from `data()` matched by value: documented (`ARCHITECTURE.md:597`).
- `valueKey` collisions in `metaKeyOf`: typed and length-prefixed; none found.
- Uncacheable-spec key uses `Date.now()`: needs a spec JSON cannot write that still compiles; no reachable harm.
- Items ceilings when `maxItems` replaces them (colour scheme count, contour levels): still checked (`t-items-replaced.mjs`). The isocontour case in that script was inconclusive (the transform likely never ran).
- Rows pushed to a stream under a derived dataset's name count toward `maxRows` though unused: errs on the safe side.
- `setTextMetricsProvider` not in the session key: could not show a scene difference; dropped.
- Time-interval tick counts over a century, `nice` counts, log bases, `dotbin` step, `window` frames, `impute` with a 900k `keyvals`: bounded or cheap (`probe.mjs`).
- `contentKey` (64-bit non-cryptographic hash) as tape identity: a collision replays the wrong tape; no practical route found.

### core / expressions, regex screen (`core-expr`)

- Raw `RangeError` from deep nesting: not reproducible.
- `format` width and precision: bounded, or no allocation.
- `pad` with huge, NaN or fractional counts: metered before building.
- `toDate` with a callable argument (prior C1): fixed; the builtin is unary.
- Pollution via `merge`, object literals, `pluck`, or `values:{signal}` + `formula`: not reproducible (`p7.mjs`).
- `datum.constructor.constructor`: `undefined`; `Function`, `eval` and timers are never returned.
- `_constructor` and `__test` call names: blocked or unknown.
- `replace` with a function replacement: refused.
- Data-trigger text built by unescaped concatenation (`spec-expressions.ts:376`): no boundary is crossed.
- The string `"if"` parsed as an identifier: pinned vega-expression behaviour.
- `isTuple`, `inScope`, `data`, `indata`, `modify` differences in `p2.mjs`: stub-runtime artefacts.
- `sortSlice`, `truncate`, `splitAccessPath` oddities: vega parity, vector-pinned.
- `timeUnitSpecifier`'s `extend` with an own `__proto__` key: affects one local table only.
- `lambdas()` depth 64 and `holdsExpression` depth 8 cuts: vega refuses such nesting earlier.

### core / loading, URL policy, add-ons (`core-load`)

- Prototype pollution via a csv `__proto__` header, `parse: {"__proto__": …}` or `inferTypes`: none pollutes (`r12`).
- `format.property: '__proto__'` or `'constructor.prototype'`: blocked by `util.getter`'s guard (`r12`).
- A limits scope leaking between renders: an artefact of my own harness (a default parameter); retested clean.
- Topojson amplification without limits: the built-in 2 000 000 ceiling applies (`r08`).
- Decompression bombs and lying `Content-Length`: the stream is counted in decoded bytes.
- Image policy bypass via the resolver differential: the drawn string is re-vetted (`r11`).
- CSS / `url()` injection via `font`, `strokeCap`, `opacity`, `cursor`, `blend`: presentation attributes only (`r02`).
- The csv `header` option quoting differs from vega: Aster's is the correct csv.
- `dsv` with no `delimiter` defaults to `,` where vega throws: a benign superset.
- A failed add-on import cached forever: it is not (`addons.ts:552`).
- An add-on cache keyed by spec identity: none in core.
- `walkSpec` stopping silently at depth 1000: the engine refuses that spec itself (`r10`).
- Semaphore over-admission: the hand-off is correct by reading.
- `callFetch`'s `/signal/i` fallback double-sending: I could not construct a case.
- A spec mutating the locale: no path.

### core / compiler, transforms (`core-xform`)

- Window frame signed vs `Math.abs`: installed vega-transforms 5.2.1 is signed; matches.
- Window frame wholly outside the partition: covered by the "Oracle crashes" deviation row.
- `sample` without `size` samples nothing: same in Vega 6.3.1.
- `sample` diff in `t8.mjs`: my seeding order; identical in `t8b.mjs`.
- `stack` keyed by `JSON.stringify`: identical output to Vega on every key mix tried.
- `aggregate cross` on nested group-by fields: both engines fail alike.
- Cross-fill key with `''` first value: same quirk, same output.
- `impute` method `toString` refused: deliberate (prototype-less tables).
- Pivot/lookup/countpattern keys named `constructor`: documented deviation.
- Duplicate signal/scale names accepted: documented as unchecked (`ERRORS.md:298-299`).
- `flatten` of null, `countpattern` of a non-string, fractional `order`, `lookup` without `as`: both fail with the same messages.
- timeunit `interval: false` signal: same as Vega.
- Window `median` over `[null,null]` quadratic: Aster 5.4 s, Vega 12.0 s at 8000 rows.
- `Adder` 32 partials: identical to d3.
- `planTicks`, `binStep`, `sampleCurve` loops: bounded (traced).
- Host/spec/upstream rows written: not found.
- Prototype pollution via `config.__proto__` etc.: none.
- `frameStyleValue` with `style:'constructor'`: output equals Vega's.
- Title `text: 5`, subtitle arrays/signals: rendered as Vega.
- `maxGeneratedRows` over-count via `evaluateChart`: not reproducible.
- `kde2dIso` failures in `t5.mjs`: my spec.
- Axis `labelFontWeight` style fallback under a signal `orient` (`compiler.ts:492` vs vega-parser `axis-config.js`): very narrow, not run.

### core / layout transforms, rasterizer (`core-layout`)

- Force/pack determinism under an injected source: by design (ADR 0006 §4), equal to d3's LCG.
- Force mutating host link rows: not so; the runtime hands copies.
- Stale link ends on a second evaluation: equal to a fresh one.
- `node not found` / null link end: same message and recovery as Vega.
- Quadtree leaving out NaN bodies where d3 adds them at (0, 0): the NaN-position force cases match Vega.
- Voronoi with a 1e308 outlier differs from Vega: documented ("coordinates beyond 1e150"); 1e6 to 1e300 match.
- `Grid` with a negative product is a raw `RangeError`: identical in vega-label.
- "Unrecognized Treemap/Tree layout method" logged, not thrown: Vega logs it too.
- Label time quadratic in labels: measured linear (2 000 / 8 000 / 32 000 labels: 260 / 911 / 3 185 ms).
- Checkerboard isocontour quadratic: it has no holes (326 ms at 700²).
- `paintAlpha('none')` painting opaque: a canvas ignores an invalid `fillStyle`, so Vega fills too.
- `arcConics` reading `ring[8]`: only when `full`, which skips that branch.
- PNG writer in `raster-image.ts`: header, stored blocks, Adler and CRC read correct.
- `nest` with a `__proto__` key: Aster handles it; Vega throws `values.push is not a function`.
- `sizeOf` on a non-array `size`: NaN boxes in both engines.

### core / scales, time, format, colour (`core-scale`)

- `nice: "constructor"` and `timeOffset('constructor', …)` differ from vega — documented (`time.ts:20`).
- Scheme `constructor`/`__proto__` refused where vega returns junk — better than upstream.
- Scheme `count: 200000` refused — documented ceiling.
- `interpolate: 'transform-css'|'transform-svg'` missing — undocumented in Vega and needs a DOM.
- `scale.tickFormat()` ignoring `defaultLocale` — vega behaves the same (ran both).
- `format('s')` prefix leak across locales — d3 does the same; documented at `format.ts:15-16`.
- `timeUnits` sorting the caller's array — `util.array` copies first.
- DST, week numbering, `%Z %f %L %s %Q`, parse strictness, years < 100 and negative — no mismatch across the runs above.
- Band/point padding extremes, log with 0 or sign-crossing domains, base ≤ 1, pow exponent 0, `padding` ≥ half range, config range cycles — equal to vega.
- `interpolateObject` writing a `__proto__` key — same as d3, and object ranges are refused earlier.
- `tickCount: 99999` refused at 100 001 ticks — documented ceiling.
- `blend-mode.ts`, `LEGEND_SCALES`, `luminance`/`contrastRatio` — sound.
- Prior audit C10, C26, C61, C62, C95 — not reproduced. C9 is fixed for the sites it named; C19 (core-scale-2) and -4 continue it.

### core / SVG, DOM patcher, canvas, a11y (`core-render`)

- Injection through ordinary channels in the string renderer: sound (`inject1.mjs`, 12 marks × 78 channels × 12 hostile strings × value/field, HTML and XML parse, 0 problems).
- `url(https://…)` through a gradient `id` or stop colour: written, but the first reference is always `#…`, so it is not a valid external paint.
- Stale `__domDesc` after an unpatched evaluation: `domparity.mjs` "skipped patch" cases pass.
- Mark type change at one position, clip on/off, group ↔ leaf, zindex reorder, `denseMarks` threshold both ways, text multi → single → multi: patched DOM equals a fresh build.
- `paintsSameAs` returning true for a different picture: 572 checks over random session walks, none.
- Canvas clip path offset twice (`canvas.ts:559`): the content-clip scope has x = y = 0 (`runtime.ts:6122`).
- `scene.plotWidth` vs `width - padding` on canvas: equal on every scene tried.
- Non-gradient object stroke keeping the previous `strokeStyle`: believed same as Vega's canvas, not re-run.
- Clip id hash collisions within a render: detected and suffixed (`svg-defs.ts:48-57`).
- `truncateToLimit` vs Vega's `truncate`: same search by reading.
- A text-metrics provider change with clean text items (`domprovider.mjs`): inconclusive as a patcher test, because serialisation ignores the per-call provider (finding 3).
- Unbounded width cache: bounded at 8000.
- `sceneHasCursor` recursion: bounded at depth 256.
- `GUIDE_PARTS[part]!` prototype lookup: not reached when `g.parts` is set.
- Memory growth in the first injection run: jsdom windows, not the engine (`leak.mjs`: 400 `renderSpec` calls, +1 MB).

### core / hit index, bounds, geometry (`core-hit`)

- Prior C41 (grid OOM), C46 (area baseline), C47 (arcs not hit): fixed and verified.
- `readNumbers` quadratic on a long command: measured linear.
- Vega dropping `Z` before a command letter: not in this Vega; the parsers agree.
- Line bounds lacking Vega's miter: Vega uses it too.
- Text bounds diffs: my harness passed `{}` as Vega's `mode`; 0 once fixed.
- Line bounds double Vega's with no `strokeWidth`: the engine's default width 2, a harness artifact.
- Symbol with no x/y/size bounded as a point: the encoder always writes `size`; equal through the pipeline.
- NaN/Infinity scene size making `buildGrid` loop: it terminates.
- Catmull-Rom division by zero on coincident points: guarded, equals d3.
- `inStroke` per-vertex allocation and `big` scan cost: milliseconds at 1e5 items.
- Picks off by pixels in my first probes: `autosize: pad` had moved the plot.
- Root group identity in `intersect()`: equivalent for the expression's uses.

### core / signal event loop, transitions (`core-signals`)

- Selector grammar differences: none in 800k cases; `constructor:click` is hardening.
- Empty-message errors (`","`): identical to Vega.
- `markname` interpolated unescaped into filter text (`stream-defs.ts:28-33`): same as Vega, and only reaches the sandboxed language.
- Function values reachable by member read (`event.target.remove`): not callable (`Illegal callee`) and refused as arguments. No call gadget found. The object-literal `toString` block was traced at `expr-interpreter.ts:415`, not run.
- Prototype pollution via signal, unit or field names: own keys only.
- Listener leaks after `detach()`: none (window listeners 2 → 0); a debounce after detach is dropped.
- Handler order, `force`, update + on, between/filter/marktype/markname/merge, object stream defs, throttle and debounce timing, `preventDefault`/`consume`, scope + `push: "outer"`: equal to Vega (`t4-loop.mjs`, `t6-misc.mjs`, `t13.mjs`).
- The `['svg','click']` difference in `t4-loop.mjs`: a jsdom artefact (picker by point vs Vega's DOM target).
- Regex screen, `regex: 'refuse'` and row meters in handlers: hold.
- `timer:500` ticking once: documented parity. The frame re-request at clock 0 and the 1 s poll: same as d3-timer.
- `setTimerClock` being global: documented.
- `vlSelectionResolve` on mixed id/field stores or array-valued `E` tuples with `isMulti`: key order and aliasing differ from Vega; not reachable from Vega-Lite output.
- Transition planner (NaN endpoints, duplicate keys, enter/exit, reorder, colour to `none`, interrupt from a frame, `at(NaN)`, bad `maxItems`, unknown easing): as documented (`t11-trans.mjs` §4-6).
- Doc file and gate references (ADR 0005; INTERACTION.md sweep numbers vs `scripts/gates.mjs:80`): exist and agree.

### core / axes, legends, titles (`core-guides`)

- `labelBound` without `labelOverlap` does nothing: Vega's Overlap also exits early on a falsy method (source read).
- `thinOverlaps` resets a user `opacity` to 1: Vega's `reset` does the same.
- `stepsOf(..., done)` skipping an `update` entry identical to `enter`'s: only guide-built entries are shared and none reads `item`.
- `contentKey` collisions sharing marks between specs: length-prefixed and type-tagged; only `-0` / `0` collide, harmlessly.
- `SHARED` map growth: cleared at 300 entries.
- Kind-3 cached step values going stale: `isStaticEntry` admits only primitives.
- `tickCount()` `while (--wanted)` running 1e9 times: bounded by `span/minStep + 1` first.
- Prior C25, C55, C58, C51: all fixed. 1 408 time cases each in UTC, America/New_York and Australia/Lord_Howe differ only in the categories of findings 5 and 6, plus the documented ceiling.
- Missing scale name: same message as Vega (`Unrecognized scale name: "nope"`, `Missing valid scale for legend.`).
- Hostile label / title text (`<script>`, `]]>`, control characters, `__proto__`, objects): same text as Vega, escaped.
- `offset: '10'` (string) with a grid: garbage in both engines, different garbage.
- `tickCount: 'seconds'` over 3 days throws the ceiling where Vega draws 259 201 ticks: documented deviation.
- `encode.<part>.name` with a space, or `interactive: false` with `name: ''`: both engines throw the same error.
- Incremental guide reuse: 2 021 steps over signal-driven axis / legend / title properties and scale domains equal a fresh evaluation.
- `pointer-events` on guide parts, with and without `interactive`: identical to Vega.

### core / geo (`core-geo`)

- Sphere through an identity or null projection throws `this.stream.sphere is not a function`: same in Vega.
- Empty ring under a spherical projection throws: same in d3/Vega.
- Clockwise ring fills the complement; pole-containing and antimeridian-crossing polygons: identical to Vega (`spec3.mjs`).
- NaN/Infinity coordinates hanging or recursing: about 150 000 NaN-seeded checks, no hang, no slow case, identical output.
- Quadratic `rejoin`: real but identical to d3; folded into C242 (core-geo-2).
- Deep GeometryCollection nesting overflows the stack: same `RangeError` in d3.
- Unknown, differently-cased, missing, null or numeric projection type: matches Vega. `type: 'constructor'` throws in Aster while Vega picks `Object` off the prototype; Aster is right.
- `identity` with reflect, ignored `center`/`rotate`/`clipAngle`, fit with reflect: identical.
- `fit` to empty data, non-GeoJSON rows, a number or string, zero size, with a clip extent, albersUsa: identical.
- albersUsa `project` outside the insets → null; `invert` in and out of insets: identical.
- `pointRadius` on the projection, on the transform, as `{expr}` or `{signal}`, negative, non-numeric, 0: identical; the transform's radius does not leak.
- Duplicate projection name or projection–scale clash accepted: documented in `ERRORS.md` ("What the compile does not check").
- A feature that throws mid-pipeline leaves buffers unreleased: they are garbage-collected; no double release.
- d3's `digits(null)` corrupting its own append cache: a d3 bug that affected my harness; Vega never calls it.
- `geopoint` with null, string, out-of-range or infinite coordinates, one-name `as`, missing `fields`, unknown projection: identical.
- `geojson` transform (fields, no fields, missing field): identical, including the failure.
- Group-scoped fit projection under session updates: correct (`incr4.mjs`).
- Prototype pollution through `type` names: guarded and tested.

### react / <Chart>, shells, SSR (`react-chart`)

- Keyboard `+`/`-` not clamped by `maxZoom`: documented (`docs/INTERACTION.md:227`).
- Wheel zoom-out never returns to base: refuted by run (`r11` (e)).
- Canvas at twice its size after a DPR change: refuted by run; kept only as C505 (react-chart-24).
- Stale tooltip under a stationary pointer after a data change: discarded as pointer-event-driven by design; not compared with Vega.
- `React.use` of an unstable `spec` promise loops: React's contract.
- Remembered add-on failure: documented (kept as T7).
- `markupBox.__html = ''` confusing React: prop compared by identity; remount paths refill the host (traced).
- `onSignal` → `setState` → `signals` loop: refuted by run (`r2`).
- StrictMode double binding or leaked timers: refuted (`r12`). The four window/document listeners left after unmount match no literal in `packages/{core,react}/src`.
- `href` → `javascript:` or `window.open`: none in React; core sanitizes (`render.ts:1088-1090`).
- Tooltip HTML injection: content is React text nodes (`ChartCore.tsx:1907-1916`).
- Prior C28/C29/C33/C64/C66/C68: not re-reported (assumed fixed per the brief; current code reads so; not re-run).
- VL registry invisible across copies (prior C92): fixed with `Symbol.for`.
- Dev `checkChartRows` throwing in render: it only warns.

### react / hooks, streams, workers (`react-hooks`)

- StrictMode breaks the worker stream: my fake built a stream map per message; fixed, it works.
- `useChart` re-evaluates per render with inline options: the session returns the cached scene.
- A stale one-shot reply is committed: the listener is removed and the id checked.
- A built-in spec yields a non-cloneable response: none found.
- `<ChartStream view>` with Vega-Lite loses its initial view: not confirmed.
- `mergeBatches` dropping pulses is wrong: it is used only on the Worker path, where a snapshot diff is correct.
- `useChartWorker` pending on the server: documented.
- A slow add-on import blocks later worker messages: by design and documented.
- `useSpecData` cache leak: it is a `WeakMap`.
- The main thread trusts worker replies: the worker is the host's own script, and replies are matched by id.

### vl / composition (`vl-c1`)

- **User dataset named `data_0`, `source_0`, `row_domain`:** guarded by `makeCtx`; ours renders.
- **User dataset named `cell`, `marks`, `concat_0_group`; params named `child_width`, `concat_0_x_step`, `x_step`; duplicate view names; duplicate or `varName`-colliding repeat values:** Vega rejects both outputs loudly, so parity.
- **Prototype pollution via spec keys:** refused; `Object.prototype` is clean after compile.
- **Input mutation and non-determinism (prior C73):** not reproduced.
- **Field names with quotes, brackets or dots in facet, repeat and sort arrays:** escaped or refused as vega-lite does. A backslash field renders where vega-lite's does not. A newline field fails in Vega for both.
- **`title: {repeat: "repeat"}`:** ours substitutes the value; vega-lite emits the object (upstream bug).
- **`labelExpr` textual substitution (2452):** same as vega-lite.
- **`config.headerRow.labels: false` not read by `labelsOn`:** output is `SAME`.
- **Layer children's `background`, `autosize`, `config`; `resolve` or `columns` on a unit:** refused loudly.
- **View name `""` hang in the fuzz:** the hang is in real Vega running vega-lite's output; ours renders.
- **Deep nesting cost:** linear (500-deep hconcat gives 1.25 MB in 250 ms).

### vl / scales, stacking, guides (`vl-c2`)

- Field names with dots, brackets, quotes, backslashes, spaces, unicode, `datum.x + 1`, braces, `%` (`t7-names.mjs`): no injection. Unbalanced quotes/brackets are refused as vega-lite refuses them; bracket paths and `\\` render where vega-lite's output gives undefined/NaN.
- `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString` as repeat variable, type or config key: refused by validation; no pollution. As a dataset name it compiled, and I did not confirm the render.
- `config.axisY.labelAngle:-30` → ours `rotate(330)`, vega-lite `rotate(-30)`: same picture.
- `legend.type:'gradient'` on a nominal colour, `scheme.count:{expr}`, `interpolate:{expr}`, newline in a field name: broken in vega-lite too.
- `axis.orient:{expr}`: the grid axis keeps `bottom`, but the grid pixels are the same; not pursued.
- `legend.title:{expr}`: vega-lite renders no title, ours renders it; unclear which is intended upstream.
- Integer-like field name (`"123"`) reorders the aria description parts relative to vega-lite (JS key order); aria only.
- Typed refusals (layer scale type conflicts, differing layer sorts, `unionWith` in a layer, DateTime sort arrays, empty repeat/concat): the documented policy.
- `hashString` 32-bit collisions for anonymous lookup sources: a collision of different data throws (`:4047`), never mixes.
- `prefixFree` / `fresh` loops (`:4010-4038`): bounded by the longest user name.
- `dataSource` URL extension sniffing (`:4086`): same rule as vega-lite.
- Same as the oracle in the batteries: `domainLimit`, label baseline/align signals, tickCount defaults, timeUnit axis formats, every sort form, impute variants, offset scales, polar stacks, conditional axis properties.

### vl / mark encoding (`vl-c3`)

- Hostile field names in `datum[…]`, `isValid`, tooltip values, stack extents, midpoint signals: all `JSON.stringify`d or renamed; aster equals or beats vega-lite.
- `__proto__` field (aster 0 items vs 3): vega-lite loses its own invalid filter and Vega's ingest treats the key specially; an upstream quirk.
- `binnedEndExpr` not escaping `\`: unreachable with a hostile name.
- `customFormatExpr` splicing `formatType`: same as vega-lite, gated on `customFormatTypes`.
- `applyLegendSelections` interpolating the raw param name: identical to vega-lite.
- `interpolate` / `tension` missing on trail items: Vega's trail ignores them.
- `config.bar.cornerRadiusEnd` leaf radius 0 vs undefined: SVGs are equal (`t4.mjs`).
- `clip: false` + bound scales (false vs undefined): equivalent.
- ExprRefs in mark properties, channel values and conditions (about 800 specs): all match.
- Mark-def `x/y/x2/y2`, `timeUnitBand*`, lat/long on bar / rect / area / tick / arc, half lat/long pairs: refused loudly and listed in the README.
- Layer-level `bind: 'scales'`: refused; vega-lite's output is rejected by Vega.
- Dataset-name differences in scale domains: naming only.

### vl / validate, optimize, predicates (`vl-rest1`)

- `range: {expr}` refused — vega-lite throws too.
- String-value injection in predicates — JSON-escaped, identical to vega-lite.
- "Identical pipelines with `sample`" diff — compiled Vega is identical; `sample` is random.
- `ci0` / `ci1` diff — bootstrap randomness.
- User datasets named `data_0` / `source_0` / `row_domain` — aster correct, vega-lite fails.
- `removeUnusedDatasets` deleting a user dataset — only generated header-domain names are removable.
- Same url with csv vs tsv merged — vega-lite merges identically; same render.
- Nested `a.b` and flat `a\.b` in one chart — vega-lite's flattening collides; aster's output is the saner one.
- `safeKey` / `signalSafe` hash collisions — not constructible in practice.
- Tokenizer gaps (template literals, comments, `?.`, `\u{…}` names) — vega's parser rejects all of them.
- `LEGEND_SCALE_PROPS` renaming a literal colour — no CSS colour is a scale name.
- Raw `TypeError` from type confusion — none in 9,240 + 4,128 mutations.
- Validation cost on huge inline data — rows not walked (3.7 ms at 400k).
- `datum: {expr}` rule in a layer refused oddly — vega-lite throws too.
- `animation.ts`, `orient.ts`, `titles.ts`, `scaleconfig.ts`, `channels.ts` — read in full, no defect found. The `channels.ts` table matches upstream `getSupportedMark` from memory; it was not diffed against the oracle.

### vl / composite marks, selections, transforms (`vl-rest2`)

- errorbar / errorband `extent:"ci"` scene differences — Vega's `ci0`/`ci1` use `Math.random`; the compiled specs are identical.
- Interval `value` for `x` only with `encodings:["x","y"]` — compiled specs identical; both views log the same Vega error.
- `extent` transform `param` equal to a declared parameter (duplicate signal) — identical in vega-lite.
- Default-`_vgsid_` point selection with an input `bind` (`Unrecognized signal name: "p_tuple_fields"`) — identical in vega-lite.
- `params:[p, p_tuple]` duplicate signal — identical in vega-lite.
- Columns named `constructor` / `toString` / `__proto__` / `hasOwnProperty` on a channel — real Vega fails for both compilers' output.
- A selection named `__proto__` — vega-lite's output fails in Vega; aster/vl's runs.
- Variable params declared on a concat / layer / facet child — vega-lite's output fails; aster/vl's runs.
- `impute` over an escaped field, and projection `rotate:[{expr},0,0]` — vega-lite's output fails in Vega; aster/vl's runs.
- `config.selection.point.nearest:false` overriding `select.nearest:true` (`selection.ts:65`) — same quirk in vega-lite.
- `withVoronoi`'s `name.includes("voronoi")` (`selection-marks.ts:163`) — same test upstream; a view named `voronoi_view` matched.
- `mark.opacity: 0` dropped by the truthiness test in `part()` (`composite-marks.ts:214-215`) — same upstream; scene matches.
- `joinaggregate` / `window` fields not passed through `replacePathInField` (`transforms.ts:279`, `:293`) — same upstream; scenes match.
- `lookup.default` forwarded only when truthy (`transforms.ts:380`) — commented; matches vega-lite.
- Ranged `line` → `rule` keeping `interpolate` on the scene item upstream — no visual effect.
- Empty composites (`band:false`, boxplot with every part off): root width 0 vs 20 — nothing is drawn in either.
- `config.boxplot.size:null` with `config.mark.size` — a one-off offset on a contrived config.
- A field with a bare double quote (`w"x`) refused where vega-lite's errorbar accepts it — `names.ts`, another lane; the error is clear.
- Expression injection through `quotedRef` as a security issue — a spec can already carry arbitrary expressions; kept as correctness finding C390 (vl-rest2-13).
- Event-selector differences for `Object.prototype` qualifiers — deliberate.

### conformance / harness (`harness-src`)

- C38 attribute drops: fixed; controls confirm.
- C39 upstream compile in `run.ts`: now intentional, since `run-vl.ts` is a gate.
- C76 error reclassification in sweeps: fixed (`run-sweep.ts:250-254,315`).
- "Both throw = pass" in `run.ts`: no, any error is FAIL (`run.ts:71-73`).
- `N-bg` hiding a missing background: no, it is compared via `root bg=`.
- `N-paint-none`, `N-degenerate`, `N-paintless` hiding pixels: sound for pixels.
- S/T curve boxes: my planted case was flagged, and vega does not emit S/T.
- Text measurer injected into vega in the Node runners: no, only the label stand-in does this.
- `floors.json`, passing lists and manifest inconsistent: they agree.
- Probe floor silently lowerable: it is a literal in `gates.mjs`.
- Sweep concurrency hiding failures: no; the real issue is shared objects (C61 (harness-src-1)).
- ADR 0009 versus practice: consistent.
- Gallery `unverifiable` counted as pass: no, it is capped and listed.

### conformance / scripts and gates (`harness-scripts`)

- `gallery-fetch` path traversal: names come from the committed manifest; regenerate filters to one level.
- Fetched content executed: JSON only.
- `--no-sandbox`: not used anywhere.
- Stale esbuild bundles: rebuilt every run (the dist/src mix is -14).
- `--min-cases` floors loose: they equal current counts.
- Signals animation cases comparing Aster with Aster: no; both engines get `@aster-charts/vl`'s Vega (stated at `:901`), then real vega against Aster.
- `canon()` dropping RegExp content: the parser differential's `same()` compares source and flags.
- Mark `on` triggers missing from sites: present, and agree.
- `dropOnCrash` hiding transform cases: bounded by an exact count.
- `transform-cases.mjs:295` omitted `bin` extent case: a documented extension with its own unit test.
- `dom-string-parity` floor `> 300` of 1063: build errors are pushed as failures.
- Pick "edge" allowance: capped at 1 per 2000.
- React gate `press('0')` without focus making the pan check vacuous: it only weakens it (folded into -12).
- `SEL_DUMP_DIR` in the OS temp dir: opt-in debugging aid.
- Secrets in env: none read.
- Leftover servers or browser in the React gate: closed in `finally` (`:1033-1036`, `:1075-1077`).

### tooling / gates, CI, release, benchmarks (`tooling`)

- Script injection in workflows: none; refs are read from quoted environment variables.
- `pull_request_target` or secrets on PRs: not used; fork PRs get a read-only token and no secret.
- Summary step missing a skipped step: skipped steps are in the `steps` context and count as failures.
- Gate exit-code propagation: `status !== 0` (including `null` on a signal or spawn error) is a failure.
- A vitest glob that drops test files: none dropped (compared with `git ls-files`).
- Missing export targets or `sideEffects` files in `dist`: none. Source maps or test files shipped: none.
- `react-dom` not declared as a peer: documented and deliberate.
- Budget passing on a missing row: it throws ("no budget for …") and exits 1.
- On-demand chunks unbudgeted: the add-ons are covered by the marginal rows and the engine parts by the `Chart + all` row.
- `incremental.bench.tsx` round-ratio indexing with alternating order: correct.
- `spawnAsync` sends SIGTERM only on timeout: bounded by the test's own timeout.
- JSDoc `import('vega')` in a shipped `.js`: a comment, with no runtime or type dependency for consumers.
- `check-release-tag` regex: rejects every malformed tag tried in its test; leading zeros fail the version comparison.
- Gallery cache poisoning: `gallery:fetch` verifies every file against the manifest whether or not the cache hit.
- `--root` without a value in `check-deps` (falls back to the current directory): harmless.
- NOTICES prose against the code: nothing contradictory found in the derivation notes; licence texts not compared (the test does that against `node_modules`).

- **Symbol shape message.** "incorrect parameter count" (ERRORS.md:322) vs "incorrect parameter type" seen for `hexagonn`: both are Vega's, which one depends on the string, and Vega agrees case by case (`misuse-oracle.mjs`).

- **"An unknown stream `policy` disables backpressure."** No: it falls through to drop-newest and is still bounded (Low, in C645 (docs-api-16)).
- **Leftover `@aster/*` scope** in the nine docs: none (grep).
- **Subpath or export parity.** No documented subpath is missing from `exports`, and no runtime export is missing from API.md (`parity.mjs`).
- **Props and field lists.** The `ChartProps` list in API.md:812-816 matches the type exactly: 39 public props, plus the 2 internal ones described at :820-827. I also compared `ChartHandle` (:836-837), `StreamBatch` (:277), `RuntimeInput` (:356-358), `A11yOptions` (:504-505), `StreamStats` (:266) and the hook returns (:1018, :283-286, :1085) against the `.d.ts`; all match.
- **`keyboardView('-')` zooming out past the base domain.** Documented (INTERACTION.md:227 "not clamped").
- **`<SvgChart>` runtime report texts** vs API.md:972-977: match. The first reads "tooltip need hit testing", a grammar slip only.
- **`compileUnit(layerSpec)` raw `TypeError`.** Documented (API.md:1249-1250).
- **Dev warning for rows changed in place** (API.md:127-129): fires as described under an unset `NODE_ENV` (`misc.mjs`).
- **SSR placeholders.** `<ChartWorkerStream>` placeholder and `<ChartStream>` markup (API.md:1077-1079): as described.
- **3 px drag/click thresholds.** `ChartCore.tsx:1238` (hypot) and `:1285` (per-axis) can disagree for a diagonal 2.5 px move. That is the interaction lane's file; not pursued.

### tests / core (a11y … curves) (`tests-core1`)

- `canvas-draw.test.ts:252` pins a default `miterLimit` of 4 on canvas — matches vega-scenegraph 5.2.1 (`strokeMiterLimit != null ? … : 4`); my recollection of 10 was wrong.
- `canvas-same-pixels` records `prev` lazily, after the next evaluation — the session does not mutate the earlier scene (`b-same-pixels.ts`: `mutated: 0`, `sameWrongEager: 0`, `differLazy 502 == differEager 502`, `freshDiffers: 0`).
- `bind-leaves` counter never installed — it is installed and counts (`d-bind-leaves.ts`).
- A group-scoped `events: 'dblclick'` does not fire off-item in `bind-leaves` — matches Vega, where a bare selector in a subscope has source `scope`, i.e. `inScope(event.item)`; `view:dblclick` and `window:keydown` do fire (`d2-scoped.ts`).
- `derived-incremental` `ask()` could be comparing `'-'` with `'-'` everywhere — answers are non-trivial on both surfaces: 152 of 390 points on SVG and 169 of 390 on canvas answer, and 17 points differ between the two renderers as the spec comment intends (`d3-derived.ts`). There is still no floor in the test.
- `dataset-reuse` `usable()` hiding most seeds, or both-sides-throw visits counted as checked — 0 unusable, 0 both-error (`c-reuse-usable.ts`).
- `cursor.test.ts` `['', null, null]` versus Vega's `''` — the same observable result (cursor property cleared).
- `process.env.TZ ??= 'UTC'` leaking across files — each file is its own fork under vitest's default isolation, and the first test asserts the offset took.
- `dom-canon` compares attribute names without namespaces — `xlink:href` keeps the same qualified name on all three routes.
- `a11y.test.ts:102` early `return` — the hit-test assertions precede it; the containment check is deliberately conditional.
- `dom-guide-keep.test.ts:197` loop possibly empty — the following `not.toBe(first2)` would then fail, so it is not vacuous.
- `bind-shell` `vi.mock` counting only `compileExpr` — `signals.ts` compiles through that export only (`signals.ts:44`).
- `paintsSameAs` ignoring blend or dash offset (a lead from the recorder's blindness) — it compares all keys minus a deny-list (`canvas.ts:449`); not probed further.

### closure / d3-format vectors (`w3-vecfmt-a`)

- `c` rows use ASCII `-` (`"-1"`, `"-Infinity"`, lines 6116, 6227) while every other type uses U+2212: this is upstream behaviour, and the port matches.
- `#x` / `#o` on NaN and Infinity give `"0xNaN"`, `"0oInfinity"`, `"0xINFINITY"` (4801-4819, 4977-4995, 5153-5171): upstream behaviour, port matches.
- `08.3f` with 1e21 gives `"0001e+21"` and NaN gives `"00000NaN"` (3633, 3649): upstream, port matches.
- `%` with 987654321.123 gives `"98765432112.300003%"` (1921): binary float through `toFixed`, specified and deterministic.
- `precisionFixed(0)` gives NaN (9386-9392): upstream 3.1.2 behaviour, port matches.
- `tickStep(1, 0, 10)` gives `-0.1` (9524-9530): upstream behaviour for a reversed range.
- `tickStep` sitting in `d3-format.json` under oracle `d3-array`: explained by the generator comment at line 568.
- `-0` formats as `"0"` everywhere: upstream.
- Width specs such as `99999999d` (allocation bound): outside what this file records, so not probed.
- The `'+$, .2f'` throw rows: already `C461 (tests-core7-5)` (C461 (tests-core7-5)).

### closure / vega-format vectors (`w3-vecfmt-b`)

- `formatFloat("%")` → `"12345678.9012345001%"` looked like recorded float noise that could vary by V8 version: it matches upstream on Node 26 and is `toFixed`-defined, so it is deterministic.
- `%C` → `"C"` looked like a defect pinned by the vectors: it is upstream behaviour (d3-time-format has no `%C`) and the port matches.
- `localeFormatSpan(0, 100, 5, "")` → `"5e+1"` looked wrong: it is upstream's `precisionRound` path and was recomputed identically.
- `%H:%M` parsed in New York as year 1900 with a −5:00 offset (possible LMT or ICU-version dependence): the zone was on standard time by 1900, so the value is stable; recomputed identically.
- The object specifier's key order (`date, month, year` in the file versus `year, month, date` in the generator): `enc` sorts keys, and the result does not depend on order.
- `process.env.TZ` left behind by the replay: already reported as `C576 (tests-core5-14)` / `C576 (tests-core7-11)`; nothing to add.
- Byte-reproducibility of this file: already established by `C577 (tests-core7-4)` and confirmed here case by case; nothing to add.

### closure / d3-color vectors I (`w3-color-a`)

- Recorded values wrong against upstream — none; re-recording is identical.
- Entries recorded as throws — none in the range (0 occurrences of `throw`).
- Duplicate `args` within a suite — none (`verify.mjs` checks). Identical `want` across different inputs (`#f00`, `#ff0000`, `#F00`, `red`, `red `, `red\t`) is intended.
- Engine-dependent strings — none. Formats are shortest-round-trip numbers; apart from `brighter2`, the arithmetic is + − × ÷ only.
- Odd-looking values that are faithful d3 behaviour, not pinned defects:
  - `rgb(-5,0,0)` formats as `hsl(180, 0%, 0%)`;
  - `hsl(0,0%,50%)` keeps `s: 0` while `h` is NaN;
  - `rgb(255.7,…)` has `displayable: false`;
  - `rgb("#ff")` gives all-NaN channels with NaN opacity, while `clamp` gives opacity 1;
  - `hsl("rgb(-5,10,300)").rgb()` gives `-4.999999999999925`.
- The tolerance letting a wrong colour through — already discarded by an earlier lane (report line 15186); the port is bit-exact anyway.
- The TZ leak for suites without `tz` — already `C576 (tests-core5-14)` / `C576 (tests-core7-11)`; colour is unaffected by time zone.
- Prototype-key lookups (`constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf` as colour names) — the port returns `null`, as d3 does (`probe.mjs`).

### closure / d3-color vectors II (`w3-color-b`)

- Tolerance letting a wrong colour through — already discarded by tests-core7. Integer and text tokens are exact, and the closest rounding boundary in my range (`r: 127.49999732730035` → `#7f8080`, `:10244-10253`) sits 2.7e-6 from .5, well outside floating-point noise.
- Near-grey hues such as `194.325…` (`:10246`) being engine noise — no. They come from the deterministic ~4e-6 channel spread of d3's matrices, and match bit-exactly here.
- `"#f000"`, `"transparent"` and `rgba(0,0,0,0)` giving NaN channels with opacity 0 — this is d3's `rgba()` (`a <= 0` → NaN channels), correctly recorded.
- `"red "`, `" steelblue"`, `"red\t"` parsing as valid — d3 trims; correct.
- `darker.l` of `1.0499999999999998` (`:8810`) and `l: -18`/`-12.149…` — plain upstream arithmetic.
- Suites lacking a `tz` field — already `C576 (tests-core5-14)`.

### closure / vega-time vectors II (`w3-time-b`)

- `["day"]` step 5 on a Saturday giving a Friday: upstream's `step * floor(f/step)` on the weekday index; recorded faithfully.
- `timeUnitSpecifier` `"%H:%MS"` looking like a typo: it is upstream's composite `hours-minutes` followed by the overridden `S`.
- `timeSequence` week starting 2024-01-07 rather than 2023-12-31: `ceil` of Sunday 19:00 local is the next Sunday; correct.
- `utcweek(0) = 0` and `week(0) = 52` in New York: correct (1970-01-01 is a Thursday; local time is 1969-12-31).
- Step-inert cases for `["quarter"]` (11/16) and `["day"]` (10/16): partly inert but each has cases that bite; not reported separately.
- Invalid-Date loss in the codec and the unrestored `process.env.TZ` are already in the report (C445 (harness-scripts-17); tests-core7, C576 (tests-core5-14)). Nothing in my range adds to them: there are no invalid dates here.

### closure / vega-time vectors III (`w3-time-c`)

- **`utcFloor(['day'], 5)` returns a Friday for a Saturday input** (for example `1325808000000`). This is upstream's stepped day-of-week semantics. The port and the pinned oracle agree, so it is not an Aster defect.
- **`['quarter']` step 3: July → 2012-01-01 but November → 2012-10-01.** Upstream arithmetic on the quarter index; matches.
- **`timeDay.every(3)` restarting each month** (Jan 31 → Feb 1 at lines 34430-34436). This is d3's day-of-month phase, pinned correctly.
- **`timeYear.count` = 1 and `timeWeek.count` = 52 for 2024-01-01Z..2025-01-01Z in New York.** Correct: both ends are the previous local evening.
- **Engine-version-dependent strings.** None: the range holds only integers, dates and unit names.
- **TZ leak after `utcIntervals`.** Already reported (tests-core5/tests-core7, report lines 6852 and 6860); not repeated.

### closure / raster fixtures I (`w3-raster-a`)

- **Chromium version drift between recording and pinned Playwright:** refuted, both are 151.0.7922.34 and the replay is identical.
- **Duplicate JSON keys silently collapsed by `JSON.parse`:** none; 122 raw keys, 122 unique.
- **`generated 0` peak alpha 117 where 204 expected, as a bad recording:** no; a 0.75 px radius circle never covers a whole pixel, and Chromium reproduces it.
- **Vertical asymmetry in `circle r=2.5 cy=5.000`** (top row 58,114,62 against bottom row 5,65,114,69,5): Skia behaviour, reproduced on replay; the engine differs by 2 mask pixels, within tolerance.
- **Fill drawings leaking ink to column 0 or the last column** (suspected by eye in `generated 20 quads`, 24 px wide): refuted, 0 border ink pixels.
- **Alpha above the globalAlpha cap where a stroke overlaps itself** (`generated 22`, alpha 128): none; one `stroke()` call gives a union.
- **`line width 2, slope 0.25` "touching the edge" as clipping:** no; the ink reaches the last row but lies inside the canvas.

### closure / raster fixtures II (`w3-raster-b`)

- Drawing 30 (closed sliver triangle, bevel join), difference of 128 on row 13: Chromium records about twice the engine's alpha (255/237/225… against 127/120/119…) where the two nearly collinear stroke bodies overlap. The engine's value is the geometric area; the doubling is Skia summing overlapping coverage, which the test header already allows for ("Skia's analytic coverage is not an area"). Not an engine defect.
- Drawing 42 ellipse, abrupt-looking top and bottom rows (`39,173,221`, `218,213,78`): a thin, steeply tilted ellipse, not clipped (bbox 28-42 by 23-41 on 71x65, no edge pixels).
- Drawings 55 and 60, rows capped at 64 under full-alpha ink: quarter-pixel coverage of a horizontal edge, consistent with the quarter-pixel y snapping the test describes.
- Drawing 57, a row of 128 above rows of 255 with no `globalAlpha`: a half-covered row (the arc's chord sits on a half-pixel y).
- Drawings 40 and 48, both named "circle r=2.625": different drawings (different canvas, position and alpha); the index in the name keeps the keys unique.
- Drawing 32 with only 8 inked pixels: legitimate; the `on > 10` floor applies to hand shapes only.
- Arc sweeps above 2π: none in my range (sweeps are 3.82, 1.94, 2.01, 0.51).

### closure / raster fixtures III (`w3-raster-c`)

- **Interior dips in `generated 87`** (60, 56, 61 inside a field of 64): the engine reproduces them (58, 57, 61); it is real overlap geometry.
- **Row sums of about 215 for a 0.5-wide stroke in `generated 95`**: the cubic doubles back on itself, and both renderers show it.
- **Stale fixture after editing `raster-shapes.ts`**: a renamed drawing throws on `want.length`, and a changed drawing under the same name moves `mask`/`abs`; either way the test fails.
- **Playwright caret range `^1.62.1` drifting from the recorded Chromium**: the fixture is a snapshot and the versions match today.
- **Baseline keys missing or out of order**: read by eye and checked by script; all 96 present and ordered.

### gallery / official Vega examples I (`gallery1`)

- **airport-connections stuck title after pointerout:** artefact of passing `HitIndex.query` as `pick` (the route paths are `interactive: false`). With `pick`, which `<Chart>` uses (`ChartCore.tsx:972`), it is equal. The TSDoc that recommends `query` is already in the report (C392 (corpus2-13)).
- **edge-bundling picks the neighbouring label; global-development hover dead:** my pointer was off by the view padding. Equal once origin + padding is used.
- **earthquakes-globe differs at init in the jsdom harness:** unseeded `random()` in that harness only. Equal with the seeded sweep.
- **crossfilter `delayRange` jumping on a zero-length drag:** identical in Vega (`xmove` starts at 0).
- **global-development initial `trackCountries` row in Vega only:** no visible effect; covered by `C73 (core-signals-3)`.
- **Tooltip/description values:** equal.
- **Unknown channels/properties (`zIndex`, `strokeSize`, mark `index`/`shape`):** ignored by both engines.
- **`autosize.resize` unimplemented:** subsumed by the documented fresh-render deviation; Aster always re-fits.
